chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Severity. Origination. Love. The Throne. Whatever He wills.
center.note: The theological core from which everything radiates. The hinge between the human plane and the cosmic plane. Al-Wadud at the center of a surah about unanswered suffering.
center.label: The Divine Attributes

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah's opening and closing pair forms one of the Quran's most striking architectural arcs

sectionJourney.title: The Vertical Ascent

sections.desc: The sky with its constellations, the promised Day, the witness and the witnessed. The surah assembles its courtroom at the highest possible vantage point. The root sh-h-d — to witness, to testify — appears at the threshold and governs everything that follows.
sections.title: The Cosmic Oath

sections.desc: Believers burned alive for no reason other than faith. The horror is not in the flames but in the posture of the persecutors: they sat and watched. The root sh-h-d returns — they were witnesses to their own crime. Their spectatorship becomes their testimony.
sections.title: The Trench

sections.desc: Fire answered by water. The persecutors receive Hell and the Burning. The believers receive gardens with flowing rivers. But the door of repentance remains open — thumma lam yatubu, 'then did not repent.' Even after burning believers alive, the door is not shut.
sections.title: The Warning & Promise

sections.desc: Severity, then creative power, then — unexpectedly — love. Al-Wadud, among God's most intimate names. In a surah about believers burned alive, the declaration of divine love lands with particular force. Then the Throne. Then the keystone: fa''alun lima yurid — He does whatever He wills.
sections.title: The Divine Attributes

sections.desc: Pharaoh and Thamud — two names, no elaboration, a lineage of organized persecution that ends in destruction. Then the final altitude: the Preserved Tablet, where these words were written before the trench was dug. The persecutors could destroy bodies. They could not touch the Tablet.
sections.title: The Ascent to the Tablet

sectionJourney.subtitle: Five movements: oath → trench → warning → attributes → Tablet

deductiveFunnel.title: The Triangle of Witness

layers.desc: The witness and the witnessed — cosmic, unnamed, sworn by at the surah's threshold. The courtroom is being assembled. Whether the witness is the Day, the Prophet, or the angels, the structural function is clear: something is about to be testified to.
layers.label: Cosmic Witness

layers.desc: The persecutors as witnesses to their own crime. They sat by the trench and watched. The same word that opens a courtroom now produces the evidence. They saw what they did. They cannot claim ignorance.
layers.label: Criminal Witness
layers.arabic: وَهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَفْعَلُونَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌ

layers.desc: God Himself is the final witness. The root completes its arc: cosmic witness, criminal witness, divine witness. The triangle holds the surah's argument together. Witnessing is the central concern — who sees, who is accountable, who holds the final testimony.
layers.label: Divine Witness

layers.desc: The Preserved Tablet — where the witnessing is made permanent. The testimony is not oral. It is inscribed in something no force can alter. The word mahfuz — preserved, guarded — is the final answer to the trench.
layers.label: The Record

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The root sh-h-d (to witness) appears four times — each occurrence reshapes its meaning

content_nodes.concept: Al-Wadud — divine love in a surah of fire
Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz — the Preserved Tablet
Buruj-Inshiqaq pair — the sky that obeys and the sky that testifies
Shahid — the triangle of witness across the surah

why_this_surah: Tells the story of believers thrown into a burning trench for their faith — and the people who sat and watched. A surah about persecution and the courage it takes to hold onto belief when the cost is your life. It also carries one of the most reassuring verses: God's forgiveness and love are real, and He does what He intends.

name: Al-Infitar
thesis: Nineteen ayahs: four cosmic fractures (sky splits, stars scatter, seas burst, graves overturned), then the pivot question — what deceived you about your Generous Lord? — then the recording angels, then the final sorting. The surah traces a line from cosmic collapse to personal accountability.

heart_verse.why: The surah's fulcrum. Everything before it is cosmic demolition — sky, stars, seas, graves. Everything after it is the answer: creation, surveillance, two destinations, sovereignty. The question is placed only five ayahs in because Al-Infitar does not build slowly — it confronts immediately. And the word that ends it — al-Karim, the Generous — is the door left open inside the rebuke.
heart_verse.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ
heart_verse.translation: O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?

full_text.arabic: إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انفَطَرَتْ
full_text.translation: When the sky breaks apart,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الْكَوَاكِبُ انتَثَرَتْ
full_text.translation: and when the stars scatter,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ فُجِّرَتْ
full_text.translation: and when the seas erupt,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ
full_text.translation: and when the graves are overturned —

full_text.arabic: عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا قَدَّمَتْ وَأَخَّرَتْ
full_text.translation: every soul will know what it has sent ahead and what it has held back.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ
full_text.translation: O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?

full_text.arabic: الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ
full_text.translation: He who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you,

full_text.arabic: فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَّا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ
full_text.translation: and assembled you in whatever form He willed.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا بَلْ تُكَذِّبُونَ بِالدِّينِ
full_text.translation: But you deny the Judgment.

full_text.arabic: وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكُمْ لَحَافِظِينَ
full_text.translation: And indeed, over you are guardians —

full_text.arabic: كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ
full_text.translation: noble ones, recording.

full_text.arabic: يَعْلَمُونَ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ
full_text.translation: They know what you do.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ
full_text.translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss,

full_text.arabic: وَإِنَّ الْفُجَّارَ لَفِي جَحِيمٍ
full_text.translation: and indeed, the wicked will be in hellfire.

full_text.arabic: يَصْلَوْنَهَا يَوْمَ الدِّينِ
full_text.translation: They will burn therein on the Day of Judgment,

full_text.arabic: وَمَا هُمْ عَنْهَا بِغَائِبِينَ
full_text.translation: and they will not be absent from it.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ
full_text.translation: And what will make you realize what the Day of Judgment is?

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ مَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الدِّينِ
full_text.translation: Then — what will make you realize what the Day of Judgment is?

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ لَا تَمْلِكُ نَفْسٌ لِّنَفْسٍ شَيْئًا ۖ وَالْأَمْرُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلَّهِ
full_text.translation: The Day when no soul will have power over another soul in any way — and the command that Day will belong entirely to Allah.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: At-Takwir has scrolls spread open, souls paired, the buried girl's testimony. Al-Infitar skips all courtroom procedure — it moves straight from 'what deceived you?' to the two outcomes. The concern is the defendant's state of mind, not the trial.
No destroyed nations, no narratives, no historical examples. The surah's only example is the reader's own behavior.
No commands, no prohibitions, no instructions to the Prophet. The surah is not telling you what to do — it is showing you what is already true about the architecture of accountability.

absences.item: No bridge between cosmos and question
absences.note: The transition from four cosmic disruptions to 'O mankind, what deceived you?' has no 'therefore,' no connector. Cosmic destruction and personal confrontation are presented as the same event — simultaneous, not sequential.
Ar-Rahman asks 'which of your Lord's favors will you deny?' thirty-one times. Al-Infitar asks its question once. The single question, unrepeated, hits harder for its solitude.

absenceMap.subtitle: Every absence sharpens the surah's focus — intimacy, not spectacle

left.desc: Sky splits, stars scatter, seas erupt, graves overturn — the physical order dissolves
left.label: Creation Undone

right.desc: All authority collapses into one point: the command belongs entirely to Allah
right.label: Sovereignty Declared

left.desc: Every soul knows what it sent forward and held back — both columns in full light
left.label: The Ledger Opens

right.desc: Righteous in bliss, wicked in fire — the ledger's two sides become two destinations
right.label: The Two Fates

chiasticRing.title: The Frame

center.desc: What has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?
center.note: Placed only five ayahs in — the surah confronts immediately. The k-r-m root threads through: al-Karim (the Generous Lord, v.6) and kiraman (the noble angels, v.11) share one root, linking generosity with accountability.
center.label: The Question

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah opens with creation dissolving and closes with sovereignty revealed — the surface giving way to what was always underneath

sectionJourney.title: The Three Stages

sections.desc: Four conditional clauses unmake the visible world — sky splitting, stars scattering, seas erupting, graves overturned. Then the response: every soul will know what it sent ahead and what it held back. The reckoning includes both action and inaction — the two columns of the ledger.
sections.title: The Four Fractures

sections.desc: The surah's hinge: a direct address to the human being by name. What deceived you about your Lord, the Generous? Four verbs of creation answer the question. Then kalla — the sharp rebuke — and the revelation of the kiraman katibin, noble recording angels who know everything you do.
sections.title: The Question & the Witnesses

sections.desc: Two parallel declarations — the righteous in bliss, the wicked in fire. The question 'what will make you realize?' is asked twice, intensified by thumma. The answer: a Day when no soul can help another, and all command belongs to Allah alone.
sections.title: The Two Destinations

sectionJourney.subtitle: Cosmic demolition → personal confrontation → absolute sovereignty

deductiveFunnel.title: The Thread of K-R-M

layers.desc: Allah names Himself by His generosity at the exact moment He questions human ingratitude. The deception was made possible by divine generosity — because He was patient, you assumed He was absent.
layers.label: The Generous Lord

layers.desc: Four verbs of creation answer the question: created (khalaqa), proportioned (sawwa), balanced ('adala), assembled (rakkaba). Each verb adds specificity — the progression from general creation to particular form.
layers.label: The Fourfold Making

layers.desc: The angels share the k-r-m root with al-Karim: the generosity of the Lord and the nobility of His witnesses are the same quality at two scales. The ones recording your deeds carry the attribute of the One whose generosity you exploited.
layers.label: The Noble Witnesses

layers.desc: The generosity was real. So is the sovereignty. Total, unshared authority. No soul helping another. The surah holds both without explaining away either.
layers.label: The Sole Command

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The root k-r-m weaves through the surah, linking generosity to accountability

content_nodes.concept: Ma gharraka — the question between rebuke and invitation
Kiraman katibin — the noble recording angels
At-Takwir / Al-Infitar twin pair
Qaddamat wa akhkharat — the two columns of the ledger

why_this_surah: When the sky breaks apart — and it will — every soul will know what it sent ahead and what it left behind. This surah is short and sharp: it takes apart the world you know (sky, stars, seas, graves) and asks what made you careless about your Lord, who created you, shaped you, and proportioned you in whatever form He willed.

name: Ash-Sharh
thesis: Eight ayahs, three rhetorical questions ('Did We not expand your chest? Remove your burden? Raise your reputation?'), then the doubled promise of ease, then two commands: when you finish, stand up; and to your Lord, turn. The structure moves from what God already did to what the servant must now do.

heart_verse.why: The gravitational center of the surah. The preposition ma'a — 'with,' not 'after' — changes everything. Ease is not waiting on the other side of difficulty. It is already present inside it. And the Arabic grammar yields a celebrated insight: the hardship is definite (one), the ease is indefinite (new each time). One hardship, two eases.
heart_verse.arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
heart_verse.translation: For truly, with hardship comes ease.

full_text.arabic: أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ
full_text.translation: Did We not open for you your chest?

full_text.arabic: وَوَضَعْنَا عَنكَ وِزْرَكَ
full_text.translation: And remove from you your burden —

full_text.arabic: الَّذِي أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ
full_text.translation: the one that was breaking your back?

full_text.arabic: وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ
full_text.translation: And raised for you your name?

full_text.arabic: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
full_text.translation: For truly, with hardship comes ease.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
full_text.translation: Truly, with hardship comes ease.

full_text.arabic: فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَانصَبْ
full_text.translation: So when you have finished, then rise to labor.

full_text.arabic: وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَارْغَب
full_text.translation: And to your Lord, turn in longing.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No reckoning, no consequence for disobedience, no mention of disbelievers, no destroyed nations, no Day of Judgment. In a Quran where warning (indhar) is one of the primary modes of speech, this surah contains none of it.

Six of the eight ayahs are addressed to 'you' — second person singular, intimate, direct; only the two at the centre (5–6) state the general law. Allah is speaking to His prophet the way a healer speaks to someone who has forgotten they were already healed.
The closing imperatives do not ask for patience or perseverance. They ask for effort (insab) and desire (irghab). Relief is not an invitation to stop — it is fuel for what comes next.

absences.item: No separation between hardship and ease
absences.note: The preposition is ma'a — 'with,' not ba'da — 'after.' The surah refuses the common consolation that things will get better later. The ease is already here, inside the hardship, simultaneous.

Some early reciters joined Ash-Sharh to Ad-Duha without a basmala, treating them as one revelation. The surah arrives as the second half of a conversation — the internal evidence of care after Ad-Duha's external reassurance.

absenceMap.subtitle: A surah of pure mercy — every absence confirms the register

left.desc: Three past-tense verbs — opened, removed, raised. Allah is the subject, the Prophet is the recipient. Every line ends with the possessive -ka: your chest, your burden, your name.
left.label: Allah Acts Upon Him

right.desc: Two imperative verbs — rise, desire. The Prophet is now the subject, and the motion is toward Allah (ila rabbika). The grammar has flipped completely.
right.label: He Acts Toward Allah

left.desc: Completed gifts — what has already been done. The question form (alam) invites the listener to remember and affirm.
left.label: Past Evidence

right.desc: Forward commands — what to do next. The imperative form (fa-insab, fa-irghab) pushes toward what has not yet been reached.
right.label: Future Orientation

chiasticRing.title: The Mirror

center.desc: With hardship comes ease. With hardship comes ease.
center.note: The universal principle that connects past evidence to future command. The only part of the surah not addressed to 'you' — a truth larger than any individual.
center.label: The Hinge

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah opens with divine action upon the Prophet and closes with the Prophet's action toward Allah

sectionJourney.title: The Conversation

sections.desc: Three completed acts in ascending order. First an internal transformation — the chest opened, made spacious enough to carry revelation. Then the removal of a burden so heavy the back was making the sound of wood about to break (anqada). Finally the raising of the Prophet's name — joined to Allah's in every shahada, every adhan, every prayer across every century.
sections.title: The Three Gifts

sections.desc: The same sentence spoken twice, word for word. With hardship comes ease. The definite article on 'hardship' (al-'usr) means it is one and the same. The indefinite 'ease' (yusr) means each mention is a new instance. One hardship, two eases. The repetition is not emphasis — it is a mathematical claim embedded in grammar.
sections.title: The Doubled Promise

sections.desc: Two imperatives that reframe everything. When you finish, rise into the next effort. And turn your deepest wanting — irghab, from a root meaning appetite, longing, desire — toward your Lord. The surah that began with gifts ends with a command not to rest but to desire. The relief is fuel, not destination.
sections.title: The Forward Command

sectionJourney.subtitle: Three movements: gifts already given → promise at the center → forward command

deductiveFunnel.title: The Ascent

layers.desc: The chest (sadr) is the seat of spiritual perception in the Quran. When constricted, the person cannot receive. When opened, they can hold revelation, suffering, the weight of a mission, and the vastness of the divine. This is the foundational gift — without it, nothing else is carriable.
layers.label: Internal Transformation

layers.desc: The burden (wizr) is set down — not endured, not lightened, but placed on the ground. The verb anqada means 'to make a cracking sound' — the sound a wooden beam makes under a load it can barely bear. Allah is saying: I heard the sound your back was making. I put the load down.
layers.label: Removal of Suffering
layers.arabic: وَوَضَعْنَا عَنكَ وِزْرَكَ ۝ الَّذِي أَنقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ

layers.desc: The name is raised. Every shahada, every adhan, every prayer across every century joins Muhammad's name to Allah's. Interior → burden → name. Each gift is larger than the last. The movement is from what only you can feel, to what pressed upon you, to what the entire world will hear.
layers.label: Public Elevation

layers.desc: The three gifts become evidence for a universal law. Because We did all of that — know this: hardship and ease are bound together. The evidence came first. The principle comes second.
layers.label: The Principle

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: Three gifts arranged in ascending order — each larger than the last

content_nodes.concept: Sharh al-sadr — the opened chest and Musa's prayer in Taha
Ma'a vs. ba'da — the grammar of simultaneous ease
The Duha-Sharh diptych — outer and inner care
Irghab — the Quran's vocabulary of desire and longing

why_this_surah: With hardship comes ease. The Quran says it twice in this surah — and scholars say the repetition is the point: for every single hardship, there are two eases. Eight ayahs of direct reassurance. If you are going through something difficult right now, this is the surah to read.

name: Al-Jathiyah
thesis: The surah that performs an autopsy on spiritual blindness and finds that the cause of death is not ignorance but the quiet enthronement of the self — desire made god, senses sealed, and every nation kneeling before its own record.

heart_verse.why: The surah's central diagnosis. The person has not abandoned worship — they have redirected it. The faculty of devotion is intact; its object has been replaced. The phrase 'with knowledge' is devastating: the sealing happens after knowledge has arrived, because of a choice made in full awareness. Every channel of perception — hearing, heart, sight — is shut.
heart_verse.arabic: أَفَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُ هَوَاهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمْعِهِ وَقَلْبِهِ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِ غِشَاوَةً
heart_verse.translation: Have you seen the one who takes his own desire as his god, and Allah has left him astray with knowledge, and sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a cover over his sight?

full_text.arabic: حمٓ
full_text.translation: Ha, Mim.

full_text.arabic: تَنزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ
full_text.translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.

full_text.arabic: وَفِي خَلْقِكُمْ وَمَا يَبُثُّ مِن دَابَّةٍ آيَاتٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ
full_text.translation: And in your creation and what He scatters of creatures are signs for people of certainty.

full_text.arabic: وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِن رِّزْقٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ آيَاتٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ
full_text.translation: And in the alternation of night and day and what Allah sends down from the sky of provision and revives thereby the earth after its death and in the directing of the winds are signs for people who reason.

full_text.arabic: تِلْكَ آيَاتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا عَلَيْكَ بِالْحَقِّ ۖ فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَ اللَّهِ وَآيَاتِهِ يُؤْمِنُونَ
full_text.translation: These are the signs of Allah which We recite to you in truth. So in what discourse after Allah and His signs will they believe?

full_text.arabic: وَيْلٌ لِّكُلِّ أَفَّاكٍ أَثِيمٍ
full_text.translation: Woe to every sinful liar,

full_text.arabic: يَسْمَعُ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُصِرُّ مُسْتَكْبِرًا كَأَن لَّمْ يَسْمَعْهَا ۖ فَبَشِّرْهُ بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
full_text.translation: who hears the signs of Allah recited to him, then persists in arrogance as though he did not hear them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا عَلِمَ مِنْ آيَاتِنَا شَيْئًا اتَّخَذَهَا هُزُوًا ۚ أُولَـٰئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ
full_text.translation: And when he learns anything of Our signs, he takes them in mockery. Those will have a humiliating punishment.

full_text.arabic: مِّن وَرَائِهِمْ جَهَنَّمُ ۖ وَلَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُم مَّا كَسَبُوا شَيْئًا وَلَا مَا اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ ۖ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ
full_text.translation: Behind them is Hell, and nothing they earned will benefit them, nor those they took as allies besides Allah. And for them is a great punishment.

full_text.arabic: هَـٰذَا هُدًى ۖ وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مِّن رِّجْزٍ أَلِيمٌ
full_text.translation: This is guidance. And those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord will have a punishment of painful torment.

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الْبَحْرَ لِتَجْرِيَ الْفُلْكُ فِيهِ بِأَمْرِهِ وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِهِ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
full_text.translation: It is Allah who subjected the sea for you so that ships may sail upon it by His command and that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.

full_text.arabic: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُم مَّا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا مِّنْهُ ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
full_text.translation: And He has subjected for you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth — all from Him. Indeed, in that are signs for people who reflect.

full_text.arabic: قُل لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَغْفِرُوا لِلَّذِينَ لَا يَرْجُونَ أَيَّامَ اللَّهِ لِيَجْزِيَ قَوْمًا بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ
full_text.translation: Tell those who believe to forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah, so that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn.

full_text.arabic: مَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلِنَفْسِهِ ۖ وَمَنْ أَسَاءَ فَعَلَيْهَا ۖ ثُمَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ تُرْجَعُونَ
full_text.translation: Whoever does righteousness — it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil — it is against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ وَرَزَقْنَاهُم مِّنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَفَضَّلْنَاهُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ
full_text.translation: And We gave the Children of Israel the Book, judgment, and prophethood, and provided them with good things, and favored them over the worlds.

full_text.arabic: وَآتَيْنَاهُم بَيِّنَاتٍ مِّنَ الْأَمْرِ ۖ فَمَا اخْتَلَفُوا إِلَّا مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَقْضِي بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ
full_text.translation: And We gave them clear proofs of the matter. They did not differ until after knowledge had come to them — out of mutual envy. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَاكَ عَلَىٰ شَرِيعَةٍ مِّنَ الْأَمْرِ فَاتَّبِعْهَا وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: Then We placed you on a clear path of the matter, so follow it, and do not follow the desires of those who do not know.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهُمْ لَن يُغْنُوا عَنكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا ۚ وَإِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ ۖ وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, they will never avail you against Allah at all. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, and Allah is the ally of the righteous.

full_text.arabic: هَـٰذَا بَصَائِرُ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ
full_text.translation: This is insight for mankind, and guidance, and mercy for a people who have certainty.

full_text.arabic: أَمْ حَسِبَ الَّذِينَ اجْتَرَحُوا السَّيِّئَاتِ أَن نَّجْعَلَهُمْ كَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَوَاءً مَّحْيَاهُمْ وَمَمَاتُهُمْ ۚ سَاءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ
full_text.translation: Or do those who commit evils think We will make them like those who believed and did righteous deeds — equal in their life and their death? Evil is their judgment.

full_text.arabic: وَخَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ وَلِتُجْزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.

full_text.arabic: أَفَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلَـٰهَهُ هَوَاهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ سَمْعِهِ وَقَلْبِهِ وَجَعَلَ عَلَىٰ بَصَرِهِ غِشَاوَةً فَمَن يَهْدِيهِ مِن بَعْدِ اللَّهِ ۚ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
full_text.translation: Have you seen the one who takes his own desire as his god, and Allah has left him astray with knowledge, and sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a cover over his sight? Who then will guide him after Allah? Will you not then remember?

full_text.arabic: وَقَالُوا مَا هِيَ إِلَّا حَيَاتُنَا الدُّنْيَا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيَا وَمَا يُهْلِكُنَا إِلَّا الدَّهْرُ ۚ وَمَا لَهُم بِذَٰلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ ۖ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ
full_text.translation: And they said, 'There is nothing but our worldly life — we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.' They have no knowledge of that. They are only guessing.

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ مَّا كَانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا أَن قَالُوا ائْتُوا بِآبَائِنَا إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ
full_text.translation: And when Our clear signs are recited to them, their only argument is that they say, 'Bring back our forefathers, if you are truthful.'

full_text.arabic: قُلِ اللَّهُ يُحْيِيكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يَجْمَعُكُمْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: Say, 'Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you to the Day of Resurrection about which there is no doubt — but most of the people do not know.'

full_text.arabic: وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَخْسَرُ الْمُبْطِلُونَ
full_text.translation: And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And the Day the Hour arrives — that Day the followers of falsehood will lose.

full_text.arabic: وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جَاثِيَةً ۚ كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ تُدْعَىٰ إِلَىٰ كِتَابِهَا الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
full_text.translation: And you will see every nation kneeling. Every nation will be called to its book: 'Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.'

full_text.arabic: هَـٰذَا كِتَابُنَا يَنطِقُ عَلَيْكُم بِالْحَقِّ ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنسِخُ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
full_text.translation: This is Our book that speaks against you in truth. Indeed, We were having transcribed whatever you used to do.

full_text.arabic: فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَيُدْخِلُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْمُبِينُ
full_text.translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear triumph.

full_text.arabic: وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آيَاتِي تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ فَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ وَكُنتُمْ قَوْمًا مُّجْرِمِينَ
full_text.translation: But as for those who disbelieved: 'Were not My signs recited to you, and you were arrogant, and you were a criminal people?'

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا قِيلَ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَالسَّاعَةُ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَا قُلْتُم مَّا نَدْرِي مَا السَّاعَةُ إِن نَّظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنًّا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ
full_text.translation: And when it was said, 'Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth and the Hour is beyond doubt,' you said, 'We do not know what the Hour is. We think it is only speculation, and we are not convinced.'

full_text.arabic: وَبَدَا لَهُمْ سَيِّئَاتُ مَا عَمِلُوا وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ
full_text.translation: And the evils of what they did will appear to them, and they will be enveloped by what they used to mock.

full_text.arabic: وَقِيلَ الْيَوْمَ نَنسَاكُمْ كَمَا نَسِيتُمْ لِقَاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هَـٰذَا وَمَأْوَاكُمُ النَّارُ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن نَّاصِرِينَ
full_text.translation: And it will be said, 'Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours, and your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers.'

full_text.arabic: ذَٰلِكُم بِأَنَّكُمُ اتَّخَذْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ هُزُوًا وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا ۚ فَالْيَوْمَ لَا يُخْرَجُونَ مِنْهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ
full_text.translation: That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery, and the worldly life deluded you. So that Day they will not be removed from it, nor will they be asked to make amends.

full_text.arabic: فَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ رَبِّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبِّ الْأَرْضِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
full_text.translation: To Allah belongs all praise — Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of all the worlds.

full_text.arabic: وَلَهُ الْكِبْرِيَاءُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
full_text.translation: And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Mighty, the Wise.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No story of a messenger confronting a tyrant, no scene of ruins, no extended dialogue. The Children of Israel appear as a structural reference, not a narrative. The evidence is not in the past — it is above you, beneath you, inside you, falling as rain right now.

A single instruction to the believers: forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah. Otherwise, no legislation, no ritual, no social conduct. The surah is not about what you should do but what has gone wrong with the mechanism that would let you see why.
The believers are mentioned but never addressed with comfort or reassurance in this world. The surah's gaze is fixed on the diagnosis. The verdict is the only comfort offered.

absences.item: No escape clause for the sealed
absences.note: The question in ayah 23 — 'Who will guide him after Allah?' — is rhetorical. No path back is offered within the surah's frame. Once desire sits on the throne, the surah does not pretend another court can remove it.

Paradise is mentioned in a single phrase (ayah 30). Hell receives slightly more — but the surah is not interested in the furniture of the afterlife. It is interested in the moment every nation kneels. The posture is the verdict.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah is pure diagnosis — what it excludes reveals what it is examining

left.desc: The Book from the Mighty, the Wise. Signs in heavens, earth, creatures, rain, winds — three categories for believers, the certain, the reasoning
left.label: The Mighty, the Wise — Signs

right.desc: Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, Lord of all the worlds. Grandeur in the heavens and earth. The same two names close the frame
right.label: The Mighty, the Wise — Praise

left.desc: The person who hears signs recited and persists in arrogance 'as though he did not hear them.' Behind them is Hell.
left.label: Warning to the Mocker

right.desc: Believers admitted to mercy. Deniers confronted: 'Were not My signs recited to you?' Today We forget you as you forgot this Day.
right.label: The Two Verdicts

left.desc: The sea, the heavens, the earth — all placed in your service. Command to forgive. Righteousness is for your own soul.
left.label: Cosmos Subjected for You

right.desc: Called to its book. The transcription of everything you did. The cosmos that served you now testifies against you.
right.label: Every Nation Kneeling

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: The one who takes desire as his god. Sealed in hearing, heart, and sight. Their philosophy: nothing but time destroys us. They are only guessing.
center.note: The gravitational center of the surah. Everything converges on why the signs are refused. Everything radiates from the answer.
center.label: Desire  — Senses Sealed

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah spirals toward and away from a single diagnosis at its center

sectionJourney.title: The Prosecution

sections.desc: Signs in the heavens and earth (for believers), in your creation and creatures (for people of certainty), in night and day and rain and winds (for people who reason). Three categories of evidence, three qualities of audience. The sea subjected, the cosmos placed in your service. Then the question: in what discourse after Allah and His signs will they believe?
sections.title: The Cosmic Exhibition

sections.desc: The Children of Israel received the Book, wisdom, prophethood — and divided anyway, not from ignorance but from mutual envy. The Prophet is placed on a shari'ah — a clear road to water. Follow the road. Do not follow desires. The word 'desire' threads from this section into the next.
sections.title: The Historical Precedent

sections.desc: The surah's center: the person who has taken desire as god. Knowledge was present. The sealing happened anyway. Hearing sealed. Heart sealed. A cover over the sight. Their philosophy: nothing destroys us except time. The universe speaks. Desire deafens. The record awaits.
sections.title: The Diagnosis

sections.desc: Every nation on its knees, called to its book. The record is a transcription — nastansikhu — everything exactly as it was done. Today We forget you as you forgot this Day. The surah closes with threefold praise: Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, Lord of all the worlds. The Mighty, the Wise — the same names from the opening.
sections.title: Every Nation Kneeling

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: evidence → precedent → diagnosis → verdict

deductiveFunnel.title: The Autopsy

layers.desc: Signs placed in creation — heavens, earth, creatures, rain, winds. Visual, tactile, experienced in the natural world. The word ayat appears three times in three ayahs, each addressed to a different quality: believers, the certain, the reasoning.
layers.label: Cosmic Signs

layers.desc: Signs recited aloud — the Quran being read to someone who persists in arrogance 'as though he did not hear them.' The same word ayat has moved from nature to revelation. The evidence has been delivered in a second form.
layers.label: Recited Signs

layers.desc: The mechanism of refusal exposed. Desire installed as god. Hearing sealed, heart sealed, sight covered. The signs — cosmic and recited — cannot reach a person whose every faculty of reception has been closed by self-worship.
layers.label: Sealed Reception

layers.desc: The same word ayat, now spoken by Allah on the Day of Judgment: 'Were not My signs recited to you?' Cosmic signs became recited signs became courtroom evidence. The defendant was surrounded by ayat in every form and still the verdict arrives.
layers.label: Courtroom Evidence

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The surah tracks the word 'ayat' (signs) from evidence through refusal to courtroom

content_nodes.concept: Desire as god — the deification of the self
Jathiyah — the kneeling of nations
The ayat escalation: cosmic → recited → courtroom
Shari'ah — the clear road to water (45:18)

why_this_surah: Have you ever met someone who made their own desires their god? This surah names that condition: a person who hears the truth but turns away as if they never heard it, who treats the signs of God as a joke. It's a surah about spiritual deafness — and the consequences of choosing to stay comfortable over choosing to listen.

name: Al-Qadr
thesis: Five ayahs that open a window onto a single night: the Quran descended in it, it surpasses a thousand months, angels descend in it with every matter, and it is peace until the rising of dawn. The surah names the night three times — Laylat al-Qadr — as if the name itself is the point.

heart_verse.why: A single night set against eighty-three years of human life — and declared greater. The comparison restructures the mathematics of hope. The night's value does not come from what the worshipper brings to it. It comes from what God has placed in it.
heart_verse.arabic: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
heart_verse.translation: The Night of Al-Qadr is better than a thousand months.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ
full_text.translation: Indeed, We sent it down in the Night of Al-Qadr.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ
full_text.translation: And what will make you know what the Night of Al-Qadr is?

full_text.arabic: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
full_text.translation: The Night of Al-Qadr is better than a thousand months.

full_text.arabic: تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ
full_text.translation: The angels and the Spirit descend in it, by the permission of their Lord, with every matter decreed.

full_text.arabic: سَلَامٌ هِيَ حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ
full_text.translation: Peace it is, until the emergence of dawn.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: This is the night his life changed forever — yet he is not named, not addressed. No cave, no Jibreel squeezing, no trembling descent. The surah views the event from heaven's side, not earth's.

There is no command to pray, to fast, to stay awake, to seek this night. The surah describes what the night is and what happens in it — and leaves the response entirely to the listener. The description is the motivation.
No mention of disbelievers, no warning of punishment, no destroyed nations. The surah is not making a legal case or issuing a warning. It is showing you something.

absences.item: The word Allah does not appear
absences.note: The surah uses rabb — 'Lord' — folded into the possessive rabbihim, 'their Lord.' Intimate language. The angels descend by the permission of their Lord, not by the command of a distant authority.
A surah about the night the Quran descended does not quote the Quran. It does not describe what was revealed. It speaks only of the night itself — the container, not the contents.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah views the event from heaven's side, not earth's

left.desc: Inna anzalnahu — a completed past action. God acted. The Quran descended. The event is historical, singular, finished.
left.label: We Sent It Down

right.desc: Hatta matla'i al-fajr — dawn's emergence, an ongoing, cyclical, recurring event. The descent happened once; the night returns every year.
right.label: Until Dawn

left.desc: The question that implies the reality of this night exceeds what human cognition can contain
left.label: What Will Make You Know?

right.desc: The answer made visible — the sky does not close. Angels in continuous procession carrying every decree by divine permission.
right.label: The Angels Descend

chiasticRing.title: The Frame

center.desc: The Night of Al-Qadr is better than a thousand months.
center.note: The turning point. Everything before it builds to this claim. Everything after it unfolds from it. Why do the angels descend in multitudes? Because the night warrants it. Why is it entirely peace? Because a night that exceeds a thousand months cannot contain turbulence.
center.label: The Measure

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah opens with divine action and closes at the horizon of light

sectionJourney.title: The Unveiling

sections.desc: We sent it down. The pronoun 'it' has no antecedent in the surah — the Quran assumes you know what 'it' refers to, because what else could warrant a surah about the night of its descent. The word al-qadr carries decree, power, and precise measure all at once.
sections.title: The Declaration

sections.desc: The rhetorical formula wa ma adraka ma — 'what will make you know what it is?' — pauses the listener before they can absorb the first claim. The answer: a single night set against eighty-three years of human life. The comparison has no ceiling — 'better than,' not 'equal to.'
sections.title: The Question and Answer

sections.desc: The angels do not simply descend — the intensive verb tanazzalu means they keep descending, in waves, continuously. Jibreel among them. Every decreed matter carried from unseen to seen. And the whole of it is salam — peace — until dawn emerges over the horizon.
sections.title: The Atmosphere

sectionJourney.subtitle: Three movements: declaration → question-and-answer → atmosphere

deductiveFunnel.title: The Layers of Knowing

layers.desc: Revelation happened, and it happened here. The unnamed 'it' creates a gravitational pull — the Quran is so central it needs no introduction.
layers.label: The Event

layers.desc: Where the night stands relative to human time. A thousand months — eighty-three years — a full human lifespan. This single night exceeds it. The mathematics of hope restructured.
layers.label: The Rank

layers.desc: What is happening in the night — an unending procession of angels, Jibreel among them, carrying every decreed matter. The sky as highway. The gates of heaven remaining open from dusk to dawn.
layers.label: The Activity

layers.desc: What it feels like to be inside the night — peace. Salam placed first for emphasis. The night is peace before it is anything else. A nominal sentence conveying permanence: the night is peace.
layers.label: The Experience

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: Each ayah answers at a different level — rank, activity, experience

content_nodes.concept: Laylat al-Qadr — the triple root of decree, power, and measure
Tanazzalu — the continuous descent of angels
Al-'Alaq to Al-Qadr — first command and first night
Salam as atmosphere — peace as identity, not event

why_this_surah: One night, better than a thousand months of worship. Muslims search for it every Ramadan in the last ten nights — praying, reciting, asking. This surah tells you what happens on that night: angels descend with every matter decreed, and it is peace until the dawn. Five ayahs that explain why millions stay awake every year.

name: Al-Inshiqaq
thesis: Twenty-five ayahs tracing the split: the sky cracks and submits, the earth flattens and empties, then humanity divides. Right-hand recipients return to their families in joy. Behind-the-back recipients call for destruction but receive fire. The oath at the end — by the twilight, the night, the full moon — seals it.

heart_verse.why: The surah's most direct address. The word kadih — to toil with strain — describes every human life. The meeting is not optional. The labor is not wasted. Everything before this verse is cosmic obedience; everything after is what that meeting looks like for two different kinds of people.
heart_verse.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ
heart_verse.translation: O human being, you are laboring toward your Lord with great effort — and you will meet Him.

full_text.arabic: إِذَا السَّمَاءُ انشَقَّتْ
full_text.translation: When the sky has split open —

full_text.arabic: وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ
full_text.translation: and listened to its Lord, as it must —

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ
full_text.translation: and when the earth has been extended —

full_text.arabic: وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ
full_text.translation: and has cast out what is within it and become empty —

full_text.arabic: وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا وَحُقَّتْ
full_text.translation: and listened to its Lord, as it must —

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنسَانُ إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًا فَمُلَاقِيهِ
full_text.translation: O human being, you are laboring toward your Lord with great effort — and you will meet Him.

full_text.arabic: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ
full_text.translation: As for the one given his record in his right hand —

full_text.arabic: فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا
full_text.translation: he will be judged with an easy accounting —

full_text.arabic: وَيَنقَلِبُ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا
full_text.translation: and return to his family in happiness.

full_text.arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ
full_text.translation: But as for the one given his record behind his back —

full_text.arabic: فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُو ثُبُورًا
full_text.translation: he will cry out for destruction —

full_text.arabic: وَيَصْلَىٰ سَعِيرًا
full_text.translation: and will burn in a blaze.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهُ كَانَ فِي أَهْلِهِ مَسْرُورًا
full_text.translation: He used to be among his people in happiness —

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَن لَّن يَحُورَ
full_text.translation: he thought he would never return.

full_text.arabic: بَلَىٰ إِنَّ رَبَّهُ كَانَ بِهِ بَصِيرًا
full_text.translation: But yes — his Lord was watching him.

full_text.arabic: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالشَّفَقِ
full_text.translation: I swear by the twilight —

full_text.arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ وَمَا وَسَقَ
full_text.translation: and by the night and what it gathers —

full_text.arabic: وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا اتَّسَقَ
full_text.translation: and by the moon when it becomes full —

full_text.arabic: لَتَرْكَبُنَّ طَبَقًا عَن طَبَقٍ
full_text.translation: you will surely travel from stage to stage.

full_text.arabic: فَمَا لَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
full_text.translation: So what is the matter with them that they do not believe?

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقُرْآنُ لَا يَسْجُدُونَ
full_text.translation: And when the Quran is recited to them, they do not prostrate?

full_text.arabic: بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُكَذِّبُونَ
full_text.translation: Rather, those who disbelieve deny.

full_text.arabic: وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ
full_text.translation: And Allah knows best what they contain.

full_text.arabic: فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
full_text.translation: So give them tidings of a painful punishment —

full_text.arabic: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ غَيْرُ مَمْنُونٍ
full_text.translation: except those who believe and do righteous deeds — for them is a reward uninterrupted.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No Musa, no Ibrahim, no mediating example between the listener and the judgment. You hear about the sky's obedience, then you hear about your own reckoning. There is no buffer.

absences.item: No direct address to the Prophet
absences.note: The word qul ('say') does not appear. The surah addresses humanity in the second person plural — la-tarkabunna, 'you will surely travel.' The message is unmediated.
The person who receives the record behind the back is unnamed. The universality is the point — a type, not a person, described by an assumption: he thought he would never return.
No halal, no haram, no command structure. The surah operates entirely in the register of witness and warning — the sky that obeys, the human who does not, the stages that continue regardless.
Unlike most Makkan surahs, the oaths appear in the third quarter (ayahs 16-18), after the judgment scenes. The structural reversal creates contemplative rest between drama and final warning.

absenceMap.subtitle: Every absence sharpens the surah's architecture — no buffer between you and the reckoning

left.desc: The sky splits in obedience — adhinat li-rabbiha. The action is reflexive, willing, natural.
left.label: Sky Heard & Obeyed

right.desc: The Quran is recited and they do not prostrate — la yasjudun. The same act of hearing, opposite response.
right.label: They Hear & Refuse

left.desc: The earth extends, empties its contents, listens — the refrain repeated for both witnesses of creation.
left.label: Earth Obeys

right.desc: Allah knows what they harbor inside — yu'un. The earth emptied itself; they refuse to open.
right.label: God Knows What They Contain

left.desc: Right hand: easy accounting, family, happiness. Behind the back: destruction, fire, the assumption of no return.
left.label: The Two Fates

right.desc: Those who believe and do good — a reward uninterrupted. The humans who responded the way the sky did.
right.label: The Exception

chiasticRing.title: The Inversion

center.desc: You will surely travel from stage to stage — tabaqan 'an tabaq.
center.note: The hinge that universalizes everything. The splitting sky is a future event. The movement from stage to stage is happening now, in every twilight that yields to night.
center.label: The Stages

chiasticRing.subtitle: The opening's cosmic obedience frames the closing's human refusal — and the final exception resolves the tension

sectionJourney.title: The Four Registers

sections.desc: The sky splits itself open — the reflexive verb means the action comes from within, not from an external force. Then the refrain that governs the entire surah: wa-adhinat li-rabbiha wa-huqqat — it listened to its Lord, as it must. Sky and earth both obey with the ease of natural necessity. The human being is about to be measured against this standard.
sections.title: The Cosmic Prelude

sections.desc: Every human being is laboring toward a meeting — kadih, toil with strain. The record in the right hand brings an easy accounting and return to family in happiness. The record behind the back — not the left hand, but behind, where the person spent their life keeping it — brings a cry for destruction. The root error: he thought he would never return.
sections.title: The Two Fates

sections.desc: Three images of transition — the twilight fading, the night gathering all things in, the moon arriving at fullness — sworn to introduce the surah's thesis: you will travel from stage to stage. The oath passage appears after the judgment scenes, not before them. It is the surah taking a breath before its final word.
sections.title: The Oaths & the Stages

sections.desc: The sky heard and obeyed. These people hear the Quran and do not prostrate. The contrast is structural. Then the savage irony of bashshir — 'give glad tidings' — introducing torment. And the final exception: a reward uninterrupted, ghayru mamnun, for those who believed.
sections.title: The Closing Warning

sectionJourney.subtitle: Cosmic awe → personal reckoning → contemplative wonder → moral urgency

deductiveFunnel.title: The Threshold Sequence

layers.desc: From intact to split. The reflexive form — inshaqqat — means the sky tears itself open from within. Its obedience is not reluctant compliance; it is the only response that makes sense.
layers.label: The Sky's Crossing

layers.desc: From labor to meeting. The word kadih — toil, strain — describes every human life without distinction. The labor is universal. What differs is the meeting.
layers.label: The Human Crossing

layers.desc: Twilight to night to full moon. Three images from the same root w-s-q — gathering and becoming full are two faces of the same process. The cosmos demonstrates the stages the surah names.
layers.label: The Natural Crossings

layers.desc: The thesis-bearing verse. Layer upon layer, stage upon stage. The emphatic la- with the heavy nun makes this one of the Quran's strongest declarations. You are already in transit.
layers.label: The Named Crossing

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: Every element crosses from one state to another — the surah asks whether you recognize your own crossing

content_nodes.concept: Tabaqan 'an tabaq — the stages of existence
Wara'a zahrihi — the record behind the back
Inshiqaq-Infitar pair — two verbs of splitting
Kadih — universal labor toward the meeting

why_this_surah: The sky will split open and obey its Lord — as it must. The earth will flatten and throw out everything inside it — as it must. Then: you too are moving toward your Lord, stage by stage, and you will meet Him. A surah about the fact that everything in creation submits to what's coming, whether it wants to or not — including you.

name: An-Naba
thesis: Forty ayahs structured as a prosecution: the question (what are they asking about?), the evidence (creation's design proves the Designer can resurrect), the scene (the Day arrives, the trumpet sounds, gates open), and the verdict. The surah that introduces the final juz sets the terms for everything that follows.

heart_verse.why: The only human speech in the entire surah. For forty ayahs God has been questioning, describing, warning, offering. At the very end, a single voice breaks through — and all it can say is a wish for nonexistence. The person who refused to believe the earth could give up its dead now wants the earth to swallow him permanently.
heart_verse.arabic: يَوْمَ يَنظُرُ ٱلْمَرْءُ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ وَيَقُولُ ٱلْكَافِرُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى كُنتُ تُرَٰبًۢا
heart_verse.translation: The Day when a person will see what his hands have put forth, and the disbeliever will say, 'Oh, I wish I were dust!'

full_text.arabic: عَمَّ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
full_text.translation: About what are they asking one another?

full_text.arabic: عَنِ ٱلنَّبَإِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ
full_text.translation: About the Great News —

full_text.arabic: ٱلَّذِى هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ
full_text.translation: over which they are in disagreement.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: No! They are going to know.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: Then, no! They are going to know.

full_text.arabic: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلْأَرْضَ مِهَٰدًۭا
full_text.translation: Have We not made the earth a resting place?

full_text.arabic: وَٱلْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًۭا
full_text.translation: And the mountains as stakes?

full_text.arabic: وَخَلَقْنَٰكُمْ أَزْوَٰجًۭا
full_text.translation: And We created you in pairs,

full_text.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا نَوْمَكُمْ سُبَاتًۭا
full_text.translation: and made your sleep a means for rest,

full_text.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلَّيْلَ لِبَاسًۭا
full_text.translation: and made the night as clothing,

full_text.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا ٱلنَّهَارَ مَعَاشًۭا
full_text.translation: and made the day for livelihood,

full_text.arabic: وَبَنَيْنَا فَوْقَكُمْ سَبْعًۭا شِدَادًۭا
full_text.translation: and constructed above you seven strong heavens,

full_text.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا سِرَاجًۭا وَهَّاجًۭا
full_text.translation: and made therein a burning lamp,

full_text.arabic: وَأَنزَلْنَا مِنَ ٱلْمُعْصِرَٰتِ مَآءًۭ ثَجَّاجًۭا
full_text.translation: and sent down from the rain clouds pouring water,

full_text.arabic: لِّنُخْرِجَ بِهِۦ حَبًّۭا وَنَبَاتًۭا
full_text.translation: that We may bring forth thereby grain and vegetation,

full_text.arabic: وَجَنَّٰتٍ أَلْفَافًا
full_text.translation: and gardens of entwined growth.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْفَصْلِ كَانَ مِيقَٰتًۭا
full_text.translation: Indeed, the Day of Decision is an appointed time —

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ يُنفَخُ فِى ٱلصُّورِ فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْوَاجًۭا
full_text.translation: the Day the Horn is blown and you come forth in multitudes,

full_text.arabic: وَفُتِحَتِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ فَكَانَتْ أَبْوَٰبًۭا
full_text.translation: and the heaven is opened and becomes gateways,

full_text.arabic: وَسُيِّرَتِ ٱلْجِبَالُ فَكَانَتْ سَرَابًا
full_text.translation: and the mountains are set in motion and become a mirage.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًۭا
full_text.translation: Indeed, Jahannam has been lying in ambush,

full_text.arabic: لِّلطَّٰغِينَ مَـَٔابًۭا
full_text.translation: for the transgressors, a place of return.

full_text.arabic: لَّٰبِثِينَ فِيهَآ أَحْقَابًۭا
full_text.translation: They will remain therein for ages unending.

full_text.arabic: لَّا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا بَرْدًۭا وَلَا شَرَابًا
full_text.translation: They will not taste therein any coolness or drink,

full_text.arabic: إِلَّا حَمِيمًۭا وَغَسَّاقًۭا
full_text.translation: except scalding water and foul purulence —

full_text.arabic: جَزَآءًۭ وِفَاقًا
full_text.translation: a fitting recompense.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ لَا يَرْجُونَ حِسَابًۭا
full_text.translation: Indeed, they were not expecting an account,

full_text.arabic: وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا كِذَّابًۭا
full_text.translation: and they denied Our signs with emphatic denial.

full_text.arabic: وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ كِتَٰبًۭا
full_text.translation: But all things We have recorded in writing.

full_text.arabic: فَذُوقُوا۟ فَلَن نَّزِيدَكُمْ إِلَّا عَذَابًا
full_text.translation: So taste — for never will We increase you except in torment.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ مَفَازًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, for the God-conscious is attainment —

full_text.arabic: حَدَآئِقَ وَأَعْنَٰبًۭا
full_text.translation: gardens and grapevines,

full_text.arabic: وَكَوَاعِبَ أَتْرَابًۭا
full_text.translation: and companions of equal age,

full_text.arabic: وَكَأْسًۭا دِهَاقًۭا
full_text.translation: and a cup filled to the brim.

full_text.arabic: لَّا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًۭا وَلَا كِذَّٰبًۭا
full_text.translation: No ill speech will they hear therein, nor any falsehood —

full_text.arabic: جَزَآءًۭ مِّن رَّبِّكَ عَطَآءً حِسَابًۭا
full_text.translation: a reward from your Lord, a generous gift made due by account.

full_text.arabic: رَّبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ۖ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَابًۭا
full_text.translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all between them, the Most Merciful. They possess not from Him the right of address.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلرُّوحُ وَٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ صَفًّۭا ۖ لَّا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنُ وَقَالَ صَوَابًۭا
full_text.translation: The Day the Spirit and the angels stand in rows — none shall speak except whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say only what is right.

full_text.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلْحَقُّ ۖ فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ مَـَٔابًا
full_text.translation: That is the True Day. So whoever wills, let him take a path back to his Lord.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّآ أَنذَرْنَٰكُمْ عَذَابًۭا قَرِيبًۭا يَوْمَ يَنظُرُ ٱلْمَرْءُ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ وَيَقُولُ ٱلْكَافِرُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى كُنتُ تُرَٰبًۢا
full_text.translation: Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment — the Day when a person will see what his hands have put forth, and the disbeliever will say, 'Oh, I wish I were dust!'

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No Musa, no Ibrahim, no Thamud. For a Makkan surah, this is striking — the standard warning-by-historical-precedent is set aside entirely. The surah has a different method: evidence from creation, not from history.

No 'pray,' 'give,' 'be patient.' The surah's concern is entirely ontological: what is real, what is coming, what have you already been shown. The audience has a prior problem — they have not yet accepted the reality that would make moral instruction meaningful.

absences.item: No dialogue, no voices — until the last ayah
absences.note: For thirty-nine ayahs, God alone speaks — questioning, describing, warning. The only human voice in the surah is the disbeliever's final cry: 'I wish I were dust.' Forty ayahs of divine prosecution, one line of human response.

No 'O you who believe,' no 'O mankind,' no 'O Messenger.' The surah speaks to no one in particular and therefore to everyone. The prosecution has no named defendant because the indictment is universal.

absences.item: No mercy vocabulary until the close
absences.note: The name al-Rahman appears only in the final section (ayahs 37-38), and even there it is the name that silences the universe. Mercy is present, but it does not soften the prosecution — it presides over the court.

absenceMap.subtitle: An-Naba sets aside the standard Makkan toolkit — every absence is a choice

left.desc: What are they asking about? The Great News — the resurrection they debate and dismiss. They will know.
left.label: The Question

right.desc: That is the True Day. They now know. The wish for dust. No disagreement remains — only the disbeliever's cry.
right.label: The Answer

left.desc: Earth as bed, mountains as pegs, sky as canopy, rain producing gardens — ten signs of divine construction.
left.label: Creation Built

right.desc: Jahannam as ambush for the transgressors; gardens and full cups for the God-conscious. The same gardens, two destinations.
right.label: Creation Fulfilled / Inverted

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: The trumpet, the crowds, the sky becoming gateways, the mountains becoming mirage.
center.note: The fulcrum. Everything before it builds the case. Everything after it lives inside the verdict. The creation signs are undone — the bed shaken, the pegs dissolved, the canopy split.
center.label: The Day of Decision

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah's evidence and consequence form a precise mirror

keywordThread.title: The Return

layers.desc: The transgressors' ma'ab — their place of returning. Jahannam is not a destination they are sent to unwillingly. It is where they were headed all along. The word implies they belong there.
layers.label: Jahannam

layers.desc: Between the two uses of ma'ab lies the entire creation argument: earth, mountains, sleep, rain, gardens. The evidence that should have redirected their return.
layers.label: The Evidence Between

layers.desc: They were not expecting an account and denied the signs with emphatic, persistent denial. The same intensive form kidhdhab returns in ayah 35 — banished from Paradise.
layers.label: The Denial

layers.desc: The listener's ma'ab — 'whoever wills, let him take a path back to his Lord.' The same word, the opposite direction. You are returning somewhere. The only question is where.
layers.label: Return to the Lord
layers.arabic: فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِۦ مَـَٔابًا

keywordThread.subtitle: The word ma'ab — 'place of return' — appears twice, and the entire argument lives between them

sectionJourney.title: The Prosecution

sections.desc: The surah opens in the murmur of the Makkan streets — they keep asking each other about the Great News, the resurrection, unable to settle the matter. The doubled warning (kalla sa-ya'lamun, thumma kalla sa-ya'lamun) converts an intellectual debate into a countdown: they will know once at death, and again at resurrection.
sections.title: The Disputed Question

sections.desc: Ten signs delivered in rapid pairs: earth and mountains, pairs and sleep, night and day, the seven heavens and the blazing lamp, rain clouds and grain, gardens of entwined growth. Each exhibit is something the Makkan listener had direct experience of. The surah turns their daily existence into an argument they cannot escape without denying their own senses.
sections.title: The Evidence from Creation

sections.desc: Yawm al-fasl — the Day of Separation. The trumpet is blown, crowds stream toward judgment, the sky splits into gateways, the mountains dissolve into mirage. The creation signs from the evidence section are systematically undone: the bed shaken, the pegs dissolved, the canopy torn. What proved God's power to create now proves His power to uncreate.
sections.title: The Day of Decision

sections.desc: Jahannam described as mirsad — a predator lying in ambush, waiting with patience. For the transgressors: ages of suffering, no coolness, no drink — only boiling water and festering discharge. The crime named: they were not expecting an account. And every action was being written down anyway.
sections.title: The Ambush

sections.desc: For the God-conscious: gardens, grapevines, a cup filled to the brim, no idle talk and no lying. The word kidhdhab — the same intensive denial that defined the damned in ayah 28 — is the quality banished from Paradise. The reward section is shorter than the punishment: six ayahs to ten. Paradise is offered, not argued for.
sections.title: The Garden

sections.desc: On that Day, no one speaks. The Most Merciful — the name most associated with gentleness — silences the universe. The Spirit and the angels stand in rows. Then: 'That is the True Day.' The surah closes with the only human voice — the disbeliever wishing he were dust. The word turaba circles back to the earth of ayah 6.
sections.title: The Sovereign Silence

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: question → evidence → verdict → sentence

content_nodes.concept: Ma'ab — the two returns
Mirsad — Jahannam as predator in ambush
An-Naba / An-Naziat diptych
Turaba — dust as final word

why_this_surah: The surah that opens Juz 'Amma — the 30th part of the Quran, the part most Muslims memorize first. An-Naba begins with what people are arguing about — the Great News — and builds the case for resurrection through evidence from creation itself: the earth as a bed, mountains as pegs, the night as a cover.

name: Al-Ma’arij
thesis: The surah that holds up a mirror to the anxious, hoarding creature and then, with the patience of a physician, names exactly what would heal it — beginning and ending with prayer.

heart_verse.why: The hinge on which the entire surah turns. Everything before it describes the external reality of judgment. Everything after it describes the internal reality of the creature being judged — its flaws, its potential remedies, and the mockery of those who refuse the remedy. The pivot from cosmology to psychology happens on this single ayah.
heart_verse.arabic: إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا
heart_verse.translation: Indeed, the human being was created anxious —

full_text.arabic: سَأَلَ سَائِلٌ بِعَذَابٍ وَاقِعٍ
full_text.translation: A questioner asked about a punishment that is falling —

full_text.arabic: لِلْكَافِرِينَ لَيْسَ لَهُ دَافِعٌ
full_text.translation: upon the disbelievers — none can repel it —

full_text.arabic: مِنَ اللَّهِ ذِي الْمَعَارِجِ
full_text.translation: from Allah, Lord of the Ascending Stairways.

full_text.arabic: تَعْرُجُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِي يَوْمٍ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ
full_text.translation: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose span is fifty thousand years.

full_text.arabic: فَاصْبِرْ صَبْرًا جَمِيلًا
full_text.translation: So be patient, with a beautiful patience.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهُمْ يَرَوْنَهُ بَعِيدًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, they see it as distant,

full_text.arabic: وَنَرَاهُ قَرِيبًا
full_text.translation: but We see it as near.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السَّمَاءُ كَالْمُهْلِ
full_text.translation: The Day the sky will become like molten metal,

full_text.arabic: وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ
full_text.translation: and the mountains will become like tufts of wool,

full_text.arabic: وَلَا يَسْأَلُ حَمِيمٌ حَمِيمًا
full_text.translation: and no close friend will ask about another.

full_text.arabic: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ ۚ يَوَدُّ الْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِي مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍ بِبَنِيهِ
full_text.translation: They will be made to see one another. The criminal will wish to ransom himself from the punishment of that Day with his own children,

full_text.arabic: وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَأَخِيهِ
full_text.translation: and his wife, and his brother,

full_text.arabic: وَفَصِيلَتِهِ الَّتِي تُؤْوِيهِ
full_text.translation: and his nearest kindred who sheltered him,

full_text.arabic: وَمَن فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
full_text.translation: and everyone on earth — if only it would save him.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا ۛ إِنَّهَا لَظَىٰ
full_text.translation: Never! Indeed, it is the Scorching Fire,

full_text.arabic: نَزَّاعَةً لِلشَّوَىٰ
full_text.translation: a remover of the scalps,

full_text.arabic: تَدْعُو مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
full_text.translation: calling the one who turned his back and turned away,

full_text.arabic: وَجَمَعَ فَأَوْعَىٰ
full_text.translation: and gathered wealth and hoarded it.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الْإِنسَانَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, the human being was created anxious —

full_text.arabic: إِذَا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ جَزُوعًا
full_text.translation: when evil touches him, he is filled with panic,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ الْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا
full_text.translation: and when good touches him, he is withholding —

full_text.arabic: إِلَّا الْمُصَلِّينَ
full_text.translation: except those who pray,

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِهِمْ دَائِمُونَ
full_text.translation: those who are constant in their prayer,

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ فِي أَمْوَالِهِمْ حَقٌّ مَّعْلُومٌ
full_text.translation: and those in whose wealth is a recognized right

full_text.arabic: لِلسَّائِلِ وَالْمَحْرُومِ
full_text.translation: for the beggar and the deprived,

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ يُصَدِّقُونَ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ
full_text.translation: and those who believe in the Day of Judgment,

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ هُم مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِم مُّشْفِقُونَ
full_text.translation: and those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord —

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّهِمْ غَيْرُ مَأْمُونٍ
full_text.translation: indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not a thing from which one is safe —

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِفُرُوجِهِمْ حَافِظُونَ
full_text.translation: and those who guard their private parts,

full_text.arabic: إِلَّا عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ
full_text.translation: except from their spouses or those their right hands possess — they are not blameworthy.

full_text.arabic: فَمَنِ ابْتَغَىٰ وَرَاءَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْعَادُونَ
full_text.translation: But whoever seeks beyond that — they are the transgressors.

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَانَاتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَاعُونَ
full_text.translation: And those who are faithful to their trusts and their covenants,

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ هُم بِشَهَادَاتِهِمْ قَائِمُونَ
full_text.translation: and those who stand by their testimonies,

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِهِمْ يُحَافِظُونَ
full_text.translation: and those who guard their prayers —

full_text.arabic: أُولَٰئِكَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ مُّكْرَمُونَ
full_text.translation: those are in gardens, honored.

full_text.arabic: فَمَالِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قِبَلَكَ مُهْطِعِينَ
full_text.translation: What is wrong with those who disbelieve, rushing toward you,

full_text.arabic: عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَالِ عِزِينَ
full_text.translation: from the right and from the left, in groups?

full_text.arabic: أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ أَن يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍ
full_text.translation: Does each of them aspire to be entered into a Garden of Bliss?

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا ۛ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُم مِّمَّا يَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: Never! Indeed, We created them from what they know.

full_text.arabic: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ الْمَشَارِقِ وَالْمَغَارِبِ
full_text.translation: I swear by the Lord of every sunrise and sunset —

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا لَقَادِرُونَ عَلَىٰ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ خَيْرًا مِّنْهُمْ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ
full_text.translation: We are certainly able to replace them with better — and We are not to be outdone.

full_text.arabic: فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا وَيَلْعَبُوا
full_text.translation: So leave them to plunge and play

full_text.arabic: حَتَّىٰ يُلَاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ
full_text.translation: until they meet their Day which they are promised —

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الْأَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعًا كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍ يُوفِضُونَ خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي كَانُوا يُوعَدُونَ
full_text.translation: The Day they will emerge from the graves rapidly, as though racing toward erected markers — their eyes humbled, humiliation covering them. That is the Day which they were promised.

absenceMap.title: What’s Missing

absences.note: No Musa, no Ibrahim, no destroyed nations. The surah is not interested in history as a warning. Its gaze is fixed on something more elemental: the raw material of the human soul.
No communal legislation, no specific commands beyond the ethical portrait. The surah is a diagnosis and a prescription, not a code of law.
Despite the Makkan context that would support it, no direct comfort is offered. Instead, sabr jamil — beautiful patience — the same phrase spoken by Ya’qub when his sons lied about Yusuf.
No back-and-forth. The questioner asks and the surah answers not with a date but with a mirror — redirecting the gaze from the sky to the soul.
The surah’s portrait of the righteous (22–35) is not a list of beliefs but a list of practices — specific, concrete, and ordered. Faith is rendered as a discipline, not an opinion.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah diagnoses rather than narrates — every absence sharpens the clinical gaze
