why_this_surah: An army with elephants marched on the Ka'ba to destroy it — and God sent birds carrying stones of baked clay that turned them into eaten straw. You don't need to understand the metaphysics. The point is simple: when God protects something, no army on earth can touch it. A surah about divine protection when human protection fails.

name: Al-Muzzammil
thesis: A surah that gave the Prophet his first assignment before his first sermon — stand in the dark, recite slowly, because what is coming is heavy — and then, years later, arrived a single ayah to ease the burden, proving that grace follows discipline, never the reverse.

heart_verse.why: The hinge of the entire surah. Everything before it is command — stand, pray, recite. Everything after it is the reason that command exists. The night prayer is not devotion for its own sake; it is preparation for carrying revelation. The word thaqil radiates through the rest of the surah: the Quran is heavy, the day is heavy, Pharaoh's seizure was heavy, the Day of Judgment turns children gray. Night prayer is the only thing strong enough to bear it.
heart_verse.arabic: إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا
heart_verse.translation: We are going to cast upon you a heavy word.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُزَّمِّلُ
full_text.translation: O you who wraps himself in garments —

full_text.arabic: قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
full_text.translation: stand in prayer through the night, except a little —

full_text.arabic: نِّصْفَهُ أَوِ انقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا
full_text.translation: half of it, or reduce from it slightly —

full_text.arabic: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا
full_text.translation: or add to it, and recite the Quran in slow, measured recitation.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا
full_text.translation: We are going to cast upon you a heavy word.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئًا وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, the rising at night is stronger in impression and more precise in speech.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهَارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, for you during the day is a long stretch of occupation.

full_text.arabic: وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا
full_text.translation: Remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him completely.

full_text.arabic: رَّبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا
full_text.translation: Lord of the East and the West; there is no god but He, so take Him as your trustee.

full_text.arabic: وَاصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَاهْجُرْهُمْ هَجْرًا جَمِيلًا
full_text.translation: And be patient over what they say, and leave them with a graceful departure.

full_text.arabic: وَذَرْنِي وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا
full_text.translation: Leave Me with the deniers of comfort, and give them respite for a little while.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ لَدَيْنَا أَنكَالًا وَجَحِيمًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, with Us are shackles and a blazing fire —

full_text.arabic: وَطَعَامًا ذَا غُصَّةٍ وَعَذَابًا أَلِيمًا
full_text.translation: and food that chokes and a painful punishment —

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ وَكَانَتِ الْجِبَالُ كَثِيبًا مَّهِيلًا
full_text.translation: on the Day the earth and mountains will tremble, and the mountains become a heap of sand pouring down.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولًا شَاهِدًا عَلَيْكُمْ كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, We have sent to you a messenger as a witness over you, just  sent to Pharaoh a messenger.

full_text.arabic: فَعَصَىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْنَاهُ أَخْذًا وَبِيلًا
full_text.translation: But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a terrible seizing.

full_text.arabic: فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِن كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًا يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدَانَ شِيبًا
full_text.translation: How will you protect yourselves, if you disbelieve, from a Day that will turn children gray-haired?

full_text.arabic: السَّمَاءُ مُنفَطِرٌ بِهِ ۚ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ مَفْعُولًا
full_text.translation: The sky will be torn apart by it. His promise is ever fulfilled.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ هَٰذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ ۖ فَمَن شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, this is a reminder; so whoever wills may take a path to his Lord.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَيِ اللَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ وَطَائِفَةٌ مِّنَ الَّذِينَ مَعَكَ ۚ وَاللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ ۚ عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحْصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ
full_text.translation: Your Lord knows that you stand nearly two-thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it, and so does a group of those with you... So recite what is easy for you of the Quran.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.item: No detailed engagement with disbelievers' arguments
absences.note: Other early Makkan surahs debate, challenge, interrogate. Al-Muzzammil barely glances at opposition. Quraysh appears only as a backdrop — people to be patient with. The surah's energy is directed inward, toward the Prophet's spiritual preparation.

absences.item: No stories of previous prophets (except Pharaoh)
absences.note: The Pharaoh reference is compressed into two ayahs — sent a messenger, Pharaoh refused, he was seized. No elaboration, no narrative arc. The pattern is stated, not told.
The surah describes shackles, fire, choking food, mountains dissolving, children turning gray — but never once describes the reward of those who listen. The entire frame is warning and preparation.

absences.item: No mention of community (until the final ayah)
absences.note: For nineteen ayahs the Prophet is alone with his Lord. Only in ayah 20 — the Medinan addition — do others appear: 'a group of those with you.' The private conversation has become a communal reality.

absences.item: No explanation of why the Quran is heavy
absences.note: Ayah 5 announces that the coming word is thaqil — heavy. But it never explains what makes divine speech heavy. The weight is stated as self-evident. The surah trusts the Prophet to discover the meaning through the carrying.

absenceMap.subtitle: Every absence is a window into the surah's purpose

left.desc: Stand through the night except a little — half, or less, or more. Recite the Quran in slow, measured recitation.
left.label: Night Prayer Commanded

right.desc: Your Lord knows you stand two-thirds, half, a third. Recite what is easy for you.
right.label: Night Prayer Eased

left.desc: Rattil al-Qur'ana tartila — give each word its space, its weight, its due.
left.label: The Quran: Recite Slowly

right.desc: Fa-qra'u ma tayassara min al-Qur'an — the relationship has matured from forging to sustaining.
right.label: The Quran: Recite What Is Easy

left.desc: Tabattal ilayhi tabtila — cut off from everything else, dedicate yourself entirely.
left.label: Complete Devotion

right.desc: Establish prayer, give zakah, lend Allah a goodly loan — devotion woven into daily life.
right.label: Prayer & Charity

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Pharaoh refused a messenger and was seized. A Day is coming that turns children gray.
center.note: The center holds the consequence. Everything outside it is preparation and response.
center.label: The Pivot: Pharaoh & the Day

chiasticRing.subtitle: The opening and closing form a precise structural mirror

sectionJourney.title: The Night Forge

sections.desc: Allah addresses His Prophet by his condition — O you wrapped in garments — and commands him to stand through the night, recite the Quran slowly, and devote himself completely. The reason follows: a heavy word is coming, and the night is where the strength to carry it is built.
sections.title: The Command to Rise

sections.desc: The surah turns outward. The Prophet is told to be patient with what people say and to leave them with a graceful departure — hajran jamila. Then the lens turns on the deniers: their comfort is temporary, and a Day is coming that will dissolve the mountains into pouring sand.
sections.title: Patience with the Deniers

sections.desc: In just four ayahs, the entire arc of Pharaoh's refusal and destruction. Then the surah leaps forward: how will you protect yourselves from a Day that turns children gray-haired? The sky itself will be torn apart. The compression is the argument — Pharaoh's story needs no elaboration.
sections.title: The Pharaoh Warning

sections.desc: Years later, a single Medinan ayah arrives. Allah says: I know you have been standing. I watched. Now recite what is easy for you. The easing came after the discipline, and the discipline was real. Grace that follows effort is mercy.
sections.title: The Easing

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: command → patience → warning → easing

deductiveFunnel.title: The Weight

layers.desc: Stand through the night. Recite slowly. The command arrives before the reason — practice before explanation. Allah gave His Prophet a discipline before He gave him a theology.
layers.label: The Command

layers.desc: A heavy word is coming. The verb ulqi — to cast, to hurl upon — suggests revelation is not gently handed over. It lands. The night prayer is the preparation for impact.
layers.label: The Reason

layers.desc: The night hours produce a different quality of alignment between heart and tongue — ashaddu wat'an wa aqwamu qila. The day is long with occupation. The night is where you are most honest.
layers.label: The Alignment
layers.arabic: إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئًا

layers.desc: The easing. After watching them strive, Allah lightens the load. The sequence matters: discipline first, then grace. The standard was set high, the striving was honored, and then mercy arrived to make it sustainable.
layers.label: The Grace

why_this_surah: The surah that established the night prayer — 'Stand in prayer at night, except a little. Half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it' (73:2-4). Revealed early, when the Prophet ﷺ needed spiritual fuel for the mission ahead. The night is when the Quran lands heaviest: 'Indeed, the hours of the night are more effective for training and more suitable for words' (73:6).

name: Ar-Rum
thesis: A sixty-ayah surah that stakes the Quran's credibility on a geopolitical prophecy — then spends the rest proving that reversal is God's signature, written in empires, rain, marriage, and the human life-cycle itself.

heart_verse.why: The structural and theological center. All the external signs — rain, lightning, diversity — point toward something already written inside the human being. The fitrah is the internal sign. The surah's entire argument converges here.
heart_verse.arabic: فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا ۚ فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا
heart_verse.translation: Set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth — the natural disposition of Allah upon which He created people.

full_text.arabic: الم
full_text.translation: Alif, Lam, Mim.

full_text.arabic: غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ
full_text.translation: The Romans have been defeated —

full_text.arabic: فِي أَدْنَى الْأَرْضِ وَهُم مِّن بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ
full_text.translation: in the nearest land. But after their defeat, they will triumph —

full_text.arabic: فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ ۗ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِن قَبْلُ وَمِن بَعْدُ
full_text.translation: within a few years. To Allah belongs the command, before and after.

full_text.arabic: وَعْدَ اللَّهِ ۖ لَا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ
full_text.translation: It is the promise of Allah. Allah does not break His promise.

full_text.arabic: وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا لِّتَسْكُنُوا إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُم مَّوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً
full_text.translation: Among His signs is that He created for you, from yourselves, spouses so you may find rest in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy.

full_text.arabic: وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ خَلْقُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافُ أَلْسِنَتِكُمْ وَأَلْوَانِكُمْ
full_text.translation: Among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your languages and colors.

full_text.arabic: وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا
full_text.translation: Among His signs is that He shows you lightning, inspiring fear and hope.

full_text.arabic: فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا ۚ فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا
full_text.translation: Set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth — the natural disposition of Allah upon which He created people.

full_text.arabic: ظَهَرَ الْفَسَادُ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي النَّاسِ
full_text.translation: Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what people's hands have earned.

full_text.arabic: فَانظُرْ إِلَىٰ آثَارِ رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُحْيِي الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا
full_text.translation: Look at the effects of Allah's mercy — how He gives life to the earth after its death.

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن ضَعْفٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةً ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ ضَعْفًا وَشَيْبَةً
full_text.translation: Allah created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then after strength weakness and gray hair.

full_text.arabic: فَاصْبِرْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ ۖ وَلَا يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ الَّذِينَ لَا يُوقِنُونَ
full_text.translation: So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is true. And let not those who lack certainty make you impatient.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: In sixty ayahs, no prophet's story is told. No Musa, no Ibrahim, no Nuh. The brief reference to destroyed civilizations is exactly that — brief. The surah's argument depends entirely on observable reality.
The surah does not argue for Allah's existence — the Quraysh already affirm it (ayah 61). It argues for the incoherence of affirming Him  while turning to other protectors.
No commands about charity amounts, prayer formats, or social conduct beyond the compressed riba/zakah contrast. The surah is making a case, not issuing a code.
Lightning inspires both fear and hope in the same ayah (24). Rain that saves and storms that destroy are held together. The surah refuses to collapse the duality into a single emotional register.

absences.item: No separation of promise and patience
absences.note: Wa'd Allah opens (ayah 6) and closes (ayah 60) the surah. The promise and the patience are the same frame — conviction does not exempt you from endurance.

absenceMap.subtitle: A surah that builds its case from what you can see — every absence sharpens the argument

left.label: The Prophecy

right.desc: Be patient — wa'd Allah haqq. The same promise that closes the surah. Geopolitical and eschatological promise unified.
right.label: The Patience

left.label: Destroyed Nations

right.desc: Corruption on land and sea echoes the ruin. The surah returns to its opening warning via a structural callback.
right.label: Corruption & Warning

left.desc: Marriage, diversity, lightning, rain — the wa min ayatihi sequence building toward the center.
left.label: Signs: First Cascade

right.desc: Wind, rain, dead earth brought to life — the resurrection-proof cascade returning after the center.
right.label: Signs: Second Cascade

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Set your face toward the religion — the natural disposition upon which He created people.
center.note: All the external signs point toward something already written inside the human being. The fitrah is the internal sign. The rain and wind and diversity of languages are the external signs. They converge on the same truth.
center.label: The Fitrah

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah's chiastic structure centers on the fitrah — the internal sign

sectionJourney.title: The Letter

sections.desc: Rome has been defeated; within a few years they will triumph. History is not random — to Allah belongs the command, before and after. The word wa'd Allah (promise of God) appears here and will return in the final ayah, forming a verbal frame.
sections.title: The Prophecy

sections.desc: A relentless accumulation: prayer-times tied to cosmic cycles, spouses as sakina, the diversity of languages and colors, lightning as fear and hope, rain on dead earth. Each 'wa min ayatihi' places another exhibit before the jury.
sections.title: The Signs Cascade

sections.desc: The structural center. Set your face toward the religion — the natural disposition upon which He created people. Monotheism is the default. Polytheism and sectarian division are the corruption. The internal sign meets the external signs.
sections.title: The Fitrah

sections.desc: Fair-weather faith diagnosed as a species-wide pattern. Corruption on land and sea from human hands. Riba contrasted with zakah. Then the return to wind, rain, and dead earth brought to life — the proof of resurrection in your fields every year.
sections.title: The Human Condition

sections.desc: You cannot make the dead hear. The human life-cycle mirrors the surah's pattern of reversal — weakness, strength, weakness again. The closing command: be patient, the promise is true. Do not let the uncertain unsettle you.
sections.title: The Command to Wait

sectionJourney.subtitle: Five movements: prophecy → signs cascade → fitrah → corruption → patience

deductiveFunnel.title: The Reversal Engine

layers.desc: Rome defeated, then victorious. The largest-scale demonstration of reversal — geopolitical, verifiable, staked as prophecy.
layers.label: Empires

layers.desc: Dead earth brought to life by rain. The same reversal operating at the level of soil and seasons — visible every year.
layers.label: Nature

layers.desc: Weakness, then strength, then weakness again. The reversal pattern written into every human body.
layers.label: Life-cycle
layers.arabic: خَلَقَكُم مِّن ضَعْفٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ ... قُوَّةً ثُمَّ ... ضَعْفًا

layers.desc: Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, you will emerge. The ultimate reversal — death itself reversed by one word.
layers.label: Resurrection
layers.arabic: ثُمَّ إِذَا دَعَاكُمْ دَعْوَةً مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ إِذَا أَنتُمْ تَخْرُجُونَ

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: Every layer demonstrates the same divine pattern: God reverses what seems irreversible

content_nodes.concept: The fitrah verse — monotheism as factory setting
Mawadda in Ar-Rum vs. Al-Ankabut — genuine vs. counterfeit bond
Lightning as dual sign — fear and hope in one image
The rain-resurrection argument across the Quran

why_this_surah: The surah that made a prediction. When the Romans lost to the Persians, the Quran said they would win again within a few years — and they did. But beyond the historical prophecy, this surah is about the idea that God turns things around. What looks like a permanent defeat can reverse. Circumstances change; God's plan doesn't.

name: Al-An'am
thesis: The Quran's longest single breath — a surah revealed whole, escorted by seventy thousand angels, that asks one question across 165 ayahs: by whose authority do you live the way you live? And it will not let you change the subject until you have answered.

heart_verse.why: The same verb — adraka — used in both directions, yielding opposite results. You look for Him and cannot find the edges. He looks at you and misses nothing. The relationship between Creator and created, rendered in eight words.
heart_verse.arabic: لَّا تُدْرِكُهُ ٱلْأَبْصَـٰرُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ ٱلْأَبْصَـٰرَ ۖ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلْخَبِيرُ
heart_verse.translation: Vision cannot grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.

keyAyahs.title: Landmarks

verses.arabic: وَعِندَهُۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلْغَيْبِ لَا يَعْلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَ
verses.context: The density of divine knowledge compressed into a single ayah. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but He knows it. No seed in the darkness of the earth, no wet thing nor dry — all in a clear record.
verses.translation: With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him.

verses.arabic: إِنِّى وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِىَ لِلَّذِى فَطَرَ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ حَنِيفًا
verses.context: Ibrahim's declaration after the stars, moon, and sun all set. What the entire surah has been building toward, given voice by the patriarch who did not inherit his faith but reasoned his way to it.
verses.translation: I have turned my face toward the one who created the heavens and the earth, inclining to truth.

verses.arabic: لَّا تُدْرِكُهُ ٱلْأَبْصَـٰرُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ ٱلْأَبْصَـٰرَ
verses.context: The mirrored verb structure — la tudrikuhu / wa huwa yudriku — among the most precise in the Quran. The divine name that follows, al-Latif (the Subtle), carries a root meaning of present in everything, visible in nothing.
verses.translation: Vision cannot grasp Him, but He grasps all vision.

verses.arabic: قُلْ تَعَالَوْا۟ أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ
verses.context: After 150 ayahs of dismantling false authority, the surah exercises true authority. The Quranic Ten Commandments. Theology becomes ethics. The abstract becomes lived.
verses.translation: Come, let me recite what your Lord has actually prohibited.

verses.arabic: قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِى وَنُسُكِى وَمَحْيَاىَ وَمَمَاتِى لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ
verses.context: The surah's closing personal surrender. The opening was cosmic — God created the heavens and the earth. The closing is a human being giving everything back. The distance between them is the surah's argument.
verses.translation: Say: my prayer and my sacrifice and my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds.

keyAyahs.subtitle: Five verses that define the surah's landscape

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: A Makki surah of this length would be expected to carry warnings through the fates of 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Lut. Al-An'am mentions them only in passing (6:6). It chose argument over warning, evidence over threat. The destroyed nations appear in Al-A'raf, its twin.

Seventy-three ayahs of pure theological argument before the first story. When narrative finally arrives — Ibrahim among the stars — it functions as the argument given human form, not as relief from it.
The most conspicuous structural absence. 150 ayahs of theological argument, then three ayahs of law. The placement is the statement: you do not get the rules until you understand who is giving them.

No 'O you who believe,' no legislation for communal life, no family law, no inheritance. This surah addresses the individual standing before the question of ultimate authority — not the community that will be built after the question is answered.

The surah opens with a total cosmological claim and never relents. There is no parable to ease into, no story to warm up with. The very first ayah announces that God made the heavens and the earth and the darknesses and the light, and the argument begins.

absenceMap.subtitle: What 165 ayahs of sustained argument conspicuously leave out

left.desc: Praise belongs to Allah who created the heavens and earth and made darkness and light. Yet those who disbelieve equate others with their Lord. The surah opens at the largest scale: the act of creation and the immediate human betrayal of it.
left.label: He Created the Heavens and Earth

right.desc: Those who divided their religion into sects — you have nothing to do with them. Whoever brings good will have ten times its like. Allah made you successors on the earth and raised some above others — to test you. The surah closes: creation → test → accountability. The same arc.
right.label: Allah's Knowledge Encompasses All

left.desc: Not one of Allah's signs comes to them but they turn away from it. They ask for angels, they mock, they demand signs. The long catalog of rejection — sign after sign offered, sign after sign dismissed. The preparation for Ibrahim's answer.
left.label: The Signs Dismissed

right.desc: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited: do not associate with Him. Do not kill your children from poverty. Do not approach immorality. This is My straight path, so follow it. The answer to the sign-dismissers: the path is named, the signs now irrelevant.
right.label: The Straight Path

left.desc: Those are the ones Allah has guided — so by their guidance be guided. Noah, Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Yaqub, the prophets — eighteen named at once. Ibrahim's discovery leads to the recognition: he was not alone. The prophets form a chain behind him.
left.label: The Prophetic Chain

right.desc: Say: My Lord has guided me to a straight path — the upright religion, the creed of Ibrahim, a hanif. Say: My prayer, my sacrifice, my life, my death — all for Allah. The mirror: Ibrahim is still the answer. The whole surah was always about returning to him.
right.label: The Nation of Ibrahim

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: When the night darkened over him, he saw a star and said: This is my Lord. Then it set. Then the moon rising. Then the sun. Each one set. Then: I have turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and earth.
center.note: Ibrahim looks at everything the surah's disbelievers worship — the sky, the heavenly bodies — and watches them set. This is the structural center because it is the theological answer: the creation cannot be the Creator. The argument before this center built the case; the argument after it follows from this moment.
center.label: Ibrahim's Discovery

chiasticRing.subtitle: Ibrahim's theological discovery is the structural heart of the surah — everything before it is the argument, everything after is the consequence

sectionJourney.title: The Prosecution

sections.desc: One of five surahs that open with alhamdulillah (1, 6, 18, 34, 35), and the first after Al-Fatiha. The claim is immediate and total: everything that exists was made, and the one who made it deserves exclusive praise. By the second ayah — 'He created you from clay, then decreed a term' — the surah has moved from cosmology to mortality. Darknesses, plural; light, singular. The asymmetry is structural.
sections.title: The Opening Declaration

sections.desc: The surah builds its case through creation. The rain, the gardens, the date palms with clustered fruit hanging low, the olive and the pomegranate — 'similar and dissimilar.' Each thing is named the way a witness names exhibits in a trial. The surah weaves between the ayahs of creation and the ayahs of the Quran itself, making reading the world and reading the Book the same act of attention.
sections.title: The Signs Everywhere

sections.desc: The qul commands multiply — over forty across the surah, more than any other. Muhammad is given his lines for a debate already underway. Every objection is quoted and dismantled: why no miracle, why no angel, why this messenger? Then at ayah 59 — the keys of the unseen. Not a leaf falls but He knows it. The sheer volume of what God tracks makes the Qurayshi claim to independent authority absurd.
sections.title: The Debate Intensifies

sections.desc: After seventy-three ayahs of theological argument, the surah tells a story. Ibrahim looks at a star: this is my Lord. It sets. The moon: this is my Lord. It sets. The sun — the greatest. It sets. Then: 'I have turned my face toward the one who created the heavens and the earth.' The argument from impermanence — whatever is truly God cannot disappear.
sections.title: Ibrahim Among the Stars

sections.desc: Eighteen prophets listed in a single inheritance of guidance — Ishaq, Ya'qub, Nuh, Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa, Harun, Zakariyya, Yahya, 'Isa, Ilyas, Al-Yasa', Yunus, Lut. 'These are the ones God guided, so follow their guidance.' The prophetic project is one project. The guidance is one guidance.
sections.title: The Prophetic Line

sections.desc: The hinge — from the God who creates to the God who speaks. 'They did not give God His true estimate when they said: God has not revealed anything to a human being.' The surah anticipates every objection to its own authority. The word sultan — authority, proof, warrant — recurs: where is your sultan for what you claim?
sections.title: The Quran's Authority

sections.desc: The surah arrives at its namesake. A systematic dismantling of Qurayshi livestock superstitions — the bahirah, the sa'ibah, the wasilah, the ham. 'Who authorized this?' Then, after all the demolition, the surah builds: 'Come, let me recite what your Lord has actually prohibited' (6:151). The Quranic Ten Commandments arrive only after the question of authority has been settled.
sections.title: The Trial of the Cattle

sections.desc: The surah that opened with 'praise belongs to God who created the heavens and the earth' closes with a human being surrendering prayer, sacrifice, life, and death to that same God. The opening was cosmic. The closing is personal. 'Say: my prayer and my sacrifice and my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds.'
sections.title: The Verdict

sectionJourney.subtitle: Seven movements: declaration → signs → debate → Ibrahim → prophets → Quran → cattle trial → verdict

arcs.desc: The surah's argument compressed into two points: He made you, so give yourself back. Creation at the start; surrender at the end. The distance between them is the distance the surah has traveled.
arcs.label: Creation → Surrender
arcs.toLabel: My living & dying are for God

arcs.desc: The legislation arrives only once the question of authority has been settled. After 150 ayahs establishing that God alone has the right to command — only then does He command. Law after theology, command after argument. You do not get the rules until you understand who is giving them.
arcs.label: Theology → Legislation

arcs.desc: The debate passages confront the opposition abstractly. The trial of Qurayshi customs is devastatingly specific — naming the bahirah, the sa'ibah, the wasilah by name. The same argument, two registers: philosophical and then forensic.
arcs.label: Abstract → Specific

structuralArcs.title: The Arcs
structuralArcs.subtitle: Three structural threads that span the surah

content_nodes.concept: Ibrahim's journey through the celestial bodies
6:103 — Vision cannot grasp Him
The Quranic Ten Commandments (6:151–153)
Al-An'am & Al-A'raf — the twin surahs

why_this_surah: Have you ever argued with someone about whether God exists — or argued with yourself? This surah is the Quran's purest case for one God, made entirely through questions: who created the heavens? Who splits the seed? Who brings the living from the dead? No laws, no community rules — just the question of why anything exists at all.

name: Nuh
thesis: Twenty-eight ayahs that give us the most intimate portrait of prophetic exhaustion in revelation — a nine-hundred-and-fifty-year deposition filed by the most patient man in sacred history, in which every method tried is recorded with divine care and the only flood is the one still gathering behind his final prayer.

heart_verse.why: The opening line of Nuh's deposition. With two words — laylan wa naharan — he establishes the surah's defining pattern: exhaustive merism, the listing of opposites to mean 'everything, without exception.' He did not call them sometimes. He called them at every hour. The entire surah that follows is the evidence for this claim.
heart_verse.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِي لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا
heart_verse.translation: He said: 'My Lord, I invited my people night and day.'

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ أَنْ أَنذِرْ قَوْمَكَ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
full_text.translation: Indeed, We sent Nuh to his people: 'Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment.'

full_text.arabic: قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
full_text.translation: He said: 'O my people, I am to you a clear warner.'

full_text.arabic: أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ
full_text.translation: 'Worship Allah, fear Him, and obey me.'

full_text.arabic: يَغْفِرْ لَكُم مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ۚ إِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ إِذَا جَاءَ لَا يُؤَخَّرُ ۖ لَوْ كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: 'He will forgive your sins and delay you until an appointed term. Indeed, the time set by Allah, when it comes, cannot be delayed — if only you knew.'

full_text.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِي لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا
full_text.translation: He said: 'My Lord, I invited my people night and day.'

full_text.arabic: فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ دُعَائِي إِلَّا فِرَارًا
full_text.translation: 'But my calling only increased them in flight.'

full_text.arabic: وَإِنِّي كُلَّمَا دَعَوْتُهُمْ لِتَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ جَعَلُوا أَصَابِعَهُمْ فِي آذَانِهِمْ وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيَابَهُمْ وَأَصَرُّوا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا اسْتِكْبَارًا
full_text.translation: 'Every time I invited them so that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and were arrogant with great arrogance.'

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهَارًا
full_text.translation: 'Then I called them publicly.'

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ إِنِّي أَعْلَنتُ لَهُمْ وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ إِسْرَارًا
full_text.translation: 'Then I announced to them in public and confided to them privately.'

full_text.arabic: فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كَانَ غَفَّارًا
full_text.translation: 'I said: Ask forgiveness of your Lord — indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver.'

full_text.arabic: يُرْسِلِ السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْكُم مِّدْرَارًا
full_text.translation: 'He will send rain upon you in abundance.'

full_text.arabic: وَيُمْدِدْكُم بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ وَيَجْعَل لَّكُمْ أَنْهَارًا
full_text.translation: 'And give you increase in wealth and children, and provide for you gardens and rivers.'

full_text.arabic: مَّا لَكُمْ لَا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارًا
full_text.translation: 'What is the matter with you that you do not attribute to Allah due grandeur?'

full_text.arabic: وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَارًا
full_text.translation: 'While He has created you in stages.'

full_text.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا
full_text.translation: 'Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens in layers?'

full_text.arabic: وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا
full_text.translation: 'And made the moon therein a light and the sun a lamp?'

full_text.arabic: وَاللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا
full_text.translation: 'And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth a progressive growth.'

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا
full_text.translation: 'Then He will return you into it and bring you out in a resurrection.'

full_text.arabic: وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًا
full_text.translation: 'And Allah has made for you the earth a wide expanse.'

full_text.arabic: لِّتَسْلُكُوا مِنْهَا سُبُلًا فِجَاجًا
full_text.translation: 'That you may follow therein roads of passage.'

full_text.arabic: قَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي وَاتَّبَعُوا مَن لَّمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُ وَوَلَدُهُ إِلَّا خَسَارًا
full_text.translation: Nuh said: 'My Lord, they have disobeyed me and followed the one whose wealth and children only increase him in loss.'

full_text.arabic: وَمَكَرُوا مَكْرًا كُبَّارًا
full_text.translation: 'And they devised an immense plan.'

full_text.arabic: وَقَالُوا لَا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا
full_text.translation: 'And they said: Do not leave your gods. Do not leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, nor Ya'uq, nor Nasr.'

full_text.arabic: وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا كَثِيرًا ۖ وَلَا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَالًا
full_text.translation: 'And they have already misled many. And increase the wrongdoers only in error.'

full_text.arabic: مِّمَّا خَطِيئَاتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا فَأُدْخِلُوا نَارًا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا لَهُم مِّن دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنصَارًا
full_text.translation: Because of their sins they were drowned and put into the Fire, and they found no helpers besides Allah.

full_text.arabic: وَقَالَ نُوحٌ رَّبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ دَيَّارًا
full_text.translation: And Nuh said: 'My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any inhabitant from among the disbelievers.'

full_text.arabic: إِنَّكَ إِن تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوا إِلَّا فَاجِرًا كَفَّارًا
full_text.translation: 'Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except every wicked disbeliever.'

full_text.arabic: رَّبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًا
full_text.translation: 'My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and the believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.'

absenceMap.title: What’s Missing

absences.note: The most famous element of Nuh’s story — the ark, the water, the drowning — does not appear. This is a surah about the nine hundred and fifty years before the flood, not the flood itself. It is about the calling, not the catastrophe.

No ‘say to them,’ no ‘do they not see,’ no pivot from Nuh’s story to the present audience. The mirror is held up without commentary. The absence of explicit application makes the application more devastating.

Nuh’s people never speak, never argue back, never offer a counter-position. We hear only his account of their refusal, giving the surah the quality of a deposition — a final testimony delivered before the court of divine justice.

Where other prophet surahs give us dramatic confrontation or divine signs, this one gives us the interior life of a man who kept going long after most would have stopped. The miracle is the persistence itself.

absences.item: No divine consolation within the surah
absences.note: Allah speaks only in the opening commission (ayahs 1–4). After that, He listens. The entire surah is Nuh speaking to God, and God’s response is the surah’s existence — that He considered Nuh’s exhaustion worthy of recording.

absenceMap.subtitle: Every absence in this surah is an argument — what is not narrated shapes the meaning of what is

left.desc: Allah sends Nuh outward, toward a people, with a warning before a painful punishment
left.label: Commission

right.desc: Nuh turns inward, toward Allah, asking for the smallest circle of mercy — himself, his parents, his household
right.label: Final Du‘a

left.desc: Night and day, publicly and privately — every mode of calling, every hour, every strategy
left.label: Da‘wah Methods

right.desc: Because of their sins they were drowned and put into the Fire — the past tense of certainty
right.label: Consequence

left.desc: Forgiveness, rain, wealth, children, gardens — da‘wah calibrated to an agricultural people
left.label: The Promise

right.desc: The same wealth and children now fuel disbelief — the surah’s deepest irony made visible
right.label: The Inversion

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Seven heavens, moon as light, sun as lamp, humanity grown from the earth like plants.
center.note: The surah’s architectural weight rests here — the center of the ring is the center of the tragedy. The signs were the strongest argument, and the thing most catastrophically ignored.
center.label: Cosmic Signs

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah’s opening and closing form a concentric architecture around the cosmic center

sectionJourney.title: The Deposition

sections.desc: Allah frames the mission in His own voice — the only section where He speaks directly. A man was sent with a message and a deadline. The punishment is named before Nuh even begins to speak. Everything that follows lives under this shadow.
sections.title: The Divine Commission

sections.desc: Nuh turns to Allah and reports, method by method, everything he tried. Night and day. Publicly and privately. With promises of rain, wealth, children, gardens. The keyword da‘awtu threads through like a rhythm of persistence meeting refusal. The quality of a man laying evidence before a judge.
sections.title: The Exhaustion Report

sections.desc: The structural center of the surah. Nuh points at the sky — seven heavens in layers, the moon as nur, the sun as siraj, humanity grown from the earth like plants. The signs were his strongest argument, the evidence most deserving of attention, and the thing his people most catastrophically ignored.
sections.title: The Cosmic Evidence

sections.desc: The pivot word ‘asawni (‘they disobeyed me’) crosses from effort to verdict. The same wealth and children offered as blessings in ayah 12 are now the instruments of ruin. Five idol names preserved as fossils of how monotheism decays. Then the most severe prophetic du‘a in the Quran, followed immediately by the most tender.
sections.title: The Collapse & Du‘a

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: commission → exhaustion → evidence → verdict

deductiveFunnel.title: The Catalogue of Refusal

layers.desc: The people bolt from Nuh’s invitation as an animal bolts from danger. The irony is structural: they fled from the one calling them away from the thing they should have been fleeing.
layers.label: Flight

layers.desc: Fingers in ears, garments pulled over heads. The most visceral body language of rejection in the Quran — the physical gestures that express a spiritual closing.
layers.label: Physical Refusal

layers.desc: From passive refusal to active plotting. The word makr — the same word used for the plotting of Quraysh against Muhammad — bridges two moments in prophetic history.
layers.label: Conspiracy

layers.desc: Five idol names preserved nowhere else in the Quran — Wadd, Suwa‘, Yaghuth, Ya‘uq, Nasr. A fossil record of how monotheism decays into idolatry across generations.
layers.label: Fossilized Idolatry

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: Each layer of Nuh’s report reveals a deeper stratum of rejection

content_nodes.concept: Da‘wah as deposition — the forensic voice of prophetic exhaustion
The five idol names — archaeology of shirk
Nuh–Jinn diptych — centuries of refusal vs. a single night of acceptance
The promise–inversion mirror — wealth as blessing and as ruin

why_this_surah: The surah of Nuh — 950 years of calling his people to God, and they covered their ears with their garments. The most detailed account of a prophet's frustration: 'I called them publicly, I called them secretly, I said seek forgiveness and He will send rain.' The surah that shows what a millennium of patience looks like when the answer is still no.

name: An-Najm
thesis: A sixty-two-ayah testimony that begins with a star descending and ends with a forehead touching the ground — ascending to the farthest boundary of creation, returning to demolish every false god by name, establishing that assumption is not knowledge, and commanding the only honest response to both truths: prostrate.

heart_verse.why: Seven Arabic words that compress an entire theology of prophetic reception. At the moment of the greatest vision any human being has ever received — standing at the boundary of creation, in the presence of what covered the Lote Tree — the Prophet's vision held perfectly steady. It did not wander (zagha) and it did not overreach (tagha). Precision, not ecstasy. The eye held its station.
heart_verse.arabic: مَا زَاغَ الْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَىٰ
heart_verse.translation: The eye did not swerve, nor did it transgress.

full_text.arabic: وَالنَّجْمِ إِذَا هَوَىٰ
full_text.translation: By the star when it descends,

full_text.arabic: مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ وَمَا غَوَىٰ
full_text.translation: your companion has not strayed, nor has he been deceived,

full_text.arabic: وَمَا يَنطِقُ عَنِ الْهَوَىٰ
full_text.translation: nor does he speak from his own desire.

full_text.arabic: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا وَحْيٌ يُوحَىٰ
full_text.translation: It is only revelation revealed,

full_text.arabic: عَلَّمَهُ شَدِيدُ الْقُوَىٰ
full_text.translation: taught to him by one mighty in power —

full_text.arabic: ذُو مِرَّةٍ فَاسْتَوَىٰ
full_text.translation: possessor of soundness, and he rose to his true form

full_text.arabic: وَهُوَ بِالْأُفُقِ الْأَعْلَىٰ
full_text.translation: while he was at the highest horizon.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ دَنَا فَتَدَلَّىٰ
full_text.translation: Then he approached and came down,

full_text.arabic: فَكَانَ قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ أَوْ أَدْنَىٰ
full_text.translation: and was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer.

full_text.arabic: فَأَوْحَىٰ إِلَىٰ عَبْدِهِ مَا أَوْحَىٰ
full_text.translation: Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed.

full_text.arabic: مَا كَذَبَ الْفُؤَادُ مَا رَأَىٰ
full_text.translation: The heart did not lie about what it saw.

full_text.arabic: أَفَتُمَارُونَهُ عَلَىٰ مَا يَرَىٰ
full_text.translation: Will you then dispute with him over what he saw?

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ نَزْلَةً أُخْرَىٰ
full_text.translation: And he certainly saw him in another descent,

full_text.arabic: عِندَ سِدْرَةِ الْمُنتَهَىٰ
full_text.translation: at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary,

full_text.arabic: عِندَهَا جَنَّةُ الْمَأْوَىٰ
full_text.translation: near which is the Garden of Refuge —

full_text.arabic: إِذْ يَغْشَى السِّدْرَةَ مَا يَغْشَىٰ
full_text.translation: when there covered the Lote Tree that which covered it.

full_text.arabic: مَا زَاغَ الْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَىٰ
full_text.translation: The eye did not swerve, nor did it transgress.

full_text.arabic: لَقَدْ رَأَىٰ مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِ الْكُبْرَىٰ
full_text.translation: He certainly saw of the greatest signs of his Lord.

full_text.arabic: أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ اللَّاتَ وَالْعُزَّىٰ
full_text.translation: Have you then considered al-Lat and al-Uzza,

full_text.arabic: وَمَنَاةَ الثَّالِثَةَ الْأُخْرَىٰ
full_text.translation: and Manat, the third, the other?

full_text.arabic: أَلَكُمُ الذَّكَرُ وَلَهُ الْأُنثَىٰ
full_text.translation: Is the male for you and the female for Him?

full_text.arabic: تِلْكَ إِذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ
full_text.translation: That, then, is an unjust division.

full_text.arabic: إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا أَسْمَاءٌ سَمَّيْتُمُوهَا أَنتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُم مَّا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلْطَانٍ
full_text.translation: These are nothing but names you yourselves have named — you and your fathers — for which Allah has sent down no authority.

full_text.arabic: إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوَى الْأَنفُسُ ۖ وَلَقَدْ جَاءَهُم مِّن رَّبِّهِمُ الْهُدَىٰ
full_text.translation: They follow nothing but assumption and what their souls desire, even though guidance has come to them from their Lord.

full_text.arabic: أَمْ لِلْإِنسَانِ مَا تَمَنَّىٰ
full_text.translation: Or is there for man whatever he wishes?

full_text.arabic: فَلِلَّهِ الْآخِرَةُ وَالْأُولَىٰ
full_text.translation: To Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first life.

full_text.arabic: وَكَم مِّن مَّلَكٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ لَا تُغْنِي شَفَاعَتُهُمْ شَيْئًا
full_text.translation: How many an angel in the heavens whose intercession avails nothing,

full_text.arabic: إِلَّا مِن بَعْدِ أَن يَأْذَنَ اللَّهُ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيَرْضَىٰ
full_text.translation: except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ الْمَلَائِكَةَ تَسْمِيَةَ الْأُنثَىٰ
full_text.translation: Those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels with female names.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ ۖ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ ۖ وَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا
full_text.translation: They have no knowledge of it. They follow nothing but assumption, and assumption avails nothing against the truth.

full_text.arabic: فَأَعْرِضْ عَن مَّن تَوَلَّىٰ عَن ذِكْرِنَا وَلَمْ يُرِدْ إِلَّا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا
full_text.translation: So turn away from whoever turns his back on Our remembrance and desires only the life of this world.

full_text.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ مَبْلَغُهُم مِّنَ الْعِلْمِ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اهْتَدَىٰ
full_text.translation: That is the extent of their knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays and who is guided.

full_text.arabic: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ لِيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسَاءُوا بِمَا عَمِلُوا وَيَجْزِيَ الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا بِالْحُسْنَى
full_text.translation: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth — that He may recompense those who do evil and reward those who do good with the best.

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَالْفَوَاحِشَ إِلَّا اللَّمَمَ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَاسِعُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ
full_text.translation: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor lapses — indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness.

full_text.arabic: هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ ۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوا أَنفُسَكُمْ ۖ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اتَّقَىٰ
full_text.translation: He knows you best — when He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim purity for yourselves. He knows best who is righteous.

full_text.arabic: أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي تَوَلَّىٰ
full_text.translation: Have you seen the one who turned away —

full_text.arabic: وَأَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلًا وَأَكْدَىٰ
full_text.translation: who gave a little and then stopped?

full_text.arabic: أَعِندَهُ عِلْمُ الْغَيْبِ فَهُوَ يَرَىٰ
full_text.translation: Does he have knowledge of the unseen so he can see?

full_text.arabic: أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ
full_text.translation: Or has he not been informed of what was in the scriptures of Musa,

full_text.arabic: وَإِبْرَاهِيمَ الَّذِي وَفَّىٰ
full_text.translation: and Ibrahim who fulfilled?

full_text.arabic: أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ
full_text.translation: That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another,

full_text.arabic: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
full_text.translation: and that there is nothing for a human being except what he strives for,

full_text.arabic: وَأَنَّ سَعْيَهُ سَوْفَ يُرَىٰ
full_text.translation: and that his striving will soon be seen,

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ يُجْزَاهُ الْجَزَاءَ الْأَوْفَىٰ
full_text.translation: then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense,

full_text.arabic: وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ الْمُنتَهَىٰ
full_text.translation: and that to your Lord is the final return,

full_text.arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَضْحَكَ وَأَبْكَىٰ
full_text.translation: and that He is the one who makes one laugh and makes one weep,

full_text.arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا
full_text.translation: and that He is the one who causes death and gives life,

full_text.arabic: وَأَنَّهُ خَلَقَ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنثَىٰ
full_text.translation: and that He created the two mates, the male and the female,

full_text.arabic: مِن نُّطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَىٰ
full_text.translation: from a sperm-drop when it is emitted,

full_text.arabic: وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ النَّشْأَةَ الْأُخْرَىٰ
full_text.translation: and that upon Him is the second creation,

full_text.arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أَغْنَىٰ وَأَقْنَىٰ
full_text.translation: and that He is the one who enriches and suffices,

full_text.arabic: وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ رَبُّ الشِّعْرَىٰ
full_text.translation: and that He is the Lord of Sirius,

full_text.arabic: وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عَادًا الْأُولَىٰ
full_text.translation: and that He destroyed the first 'Ad,

full_text.arabic: وَثَمُودَ فَمَا أَبْقَىٰ
full_text.translation: and Thamud — He spared none —

full_text.arabic: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِّن قَبْلُ ۖ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا هُمْ أَظْلَمَ وَأَطْغَىٰ
full_text.translation: and the people of Nuh before — they were more unjust and transgressing —

full_text.arabic: وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَةَ أَهْوَىٰ
full_text.translation: and the overturned cities He hurled down,

full_text.arabic: فَغَشَّاهَا مَا غَشَّىٰ
full_text.translation: and covered them with what He covered.

full_text.arabic: فَبِأَيِّ آلَاءِ رَبِّكَ تَتَمَارَىٰ
full_text.translation: So which of the favors of your Lord do you doubt?

full_text.arabic: هَـٰذَا نَذِيرٌ مِّنَ النُّذُرِ الْأُولَىٰ
full_text.translation: This is a warner from among the warners of old.

full_text.arabic: أَزِفَتِ الْآزِفَةُ
full_text.translation: The approaching Hour draws near.

full_text.arabic: لَيْسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ
full_text.translation: There is no remover of it besides Allah.

full_text.arabic: أَفَمِنْ هَـٰذَا الْحَدِيثِ تَعْجَبُونَ ۝ وَتَضْحَكُونَ وَلَا تَبْكُونَ ۝ وَأَنتُمْ سَامِدُونَ ۝ فَاسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ وَاعْبُدُوا ۩
full_text.translation: Do you then wonder at this discourse? And you laugh and do not weep, while you are proudly sporting? So prostrate to Allah and worship.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: Ibrahim and Musa are mentioned as sources — the surah references their scriptures to anchor its ethics — but their stories are not told. An-Najm replaces narrative with direct witness: I saw this with my own eyes.
No commands about prayer, charity, fasting, or conduct — except the final command to prostrate. The surah is establishing something more basic than law: the reality of revelation itself.

absences.item: No description of what was revealed
absences.note: Ayah 10 says 'He revealed to His servant what He revealed' — the content is left unnamed. The surah protects the secret of what passed between them. The channel matters, not the content.

absences.item: No naming of what covered the Lote Tree
absences.note: The repetition 'when there covered it that which covered it' is the Quran choosing not to name what the Prophet saw. Whatever covered the Tree was beyond the capacity of language to hold.
The surah does not debate. It testifies, demolishes, and commands. The only question directed at the audience is: will you dispute with him over what he saw?

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah replaces narrative with testimony — every absence intensifies the directness

right.label: Prostrate and Worship

left.label: Jibreel's Two Visions

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: No soul bears another's burden. There is nothing for a person except what they strive for. To your Lord is the final return.
center.note: The ethical center — what remains when every false support has been stripped away. Your own effort and its consequences.
center.label: The Scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa

chiasticRing.subtitle: The star descends at the opening; the forehead descends at the close

sectionJourney.title: The Testimony

sections.desc: The Prophet sees Jibreel in his true form twice — once on the horizon, once at the Lote Tree at the boundary of all creation. The eye did not swerve, nor did it transgress. He saw the greatest signs of his Lord. The surah opens as testimony, not teaching — someone who has seen something so staggering the courtroom goes silent.
sections.title: The Two Visions

sections.desc: From the highest point any soul has reached, the surah drops without warning to the lowest thing the Quraysh could offer. Al-Lat, al-Uzza, Manat — named and exposed as nothing but names with no authority. After fourteen verses about the boundary of the heavens, the surah says: so tell me about your three stone goddesses.
sections.title: The Three Goddesses

sections.desc: Even the angels cannot intercede without permission. Assumption (zann) avails nothing against truth. Then the ethical center: from the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa — no soul bears another's burden, there is nothing for a person except what they strive for, and to your Lord is the final return.
sections.title: Knowledge vs. Assumption

sections.desc: A rapid litany — He makes you laugh and weep, causes death and life, created the pairs, is Lord of Sirius, destroyed 'Ad and Thamud. The Hour draws near. And then the command that brought even the Quraysh to their knees: prostrate to Allah and worship.
sections.title: The Sovereignty Cascade

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four corridors: vision → demolition → reckoning → prostration

deductiveFunnel.title: The Zann-'Ilm Line

layers.desc: The Prophet's experience is characterized as direct, undistorted witness. The eye held steady. This is 'ilm at its purest — revelation received without a single degree of deviation.
layers.label: Direct Witness

layers.desc: The Quraysh's gods are a vocabulary with no referent — names pointing at nothing. The surah's demolition is linguistic: your gods are a language problem. You invented names and then worshipped the names.
layers.label: Empty Names

layers.desc: Assumption — no matter how confidently held, no matter how culturally reinforced — does not produce a single grain of truth. The surah's most important epistemological statement.
layers.label: Zann Avails Nothing
layers.arabic: وَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ لَا يُغْنِي مِنَ الْحَقِّ شَيْئًا

layers.desc: When zann is cleared away and 'ilm is established, what remains is this: you own only your effort. Sa'y — striving — carries the image of someone walking briskly toward a destination. Not passive hope but movement.
layers.label: Only What You Strive For
layers.arabic: وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَانِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The surah draws a binary between assumption (zann) and knowledge ('ilm) — and places everything on one side or the other
