full_text.arabic: قَالَ لَا تَخْتَصِمُوا لَدَيَّ وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ إِلَيْكُم بِالْوَعِيدِ
full_text.translation: He will say, 'Do not dispute before Me — I had already presented the threat to you.'

full_text.arabic: مَا يُبَدَّلُ الْقَوْلُ لَدَيَّ وَمَا أَنَا بِظَلَّامٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ
full_text.translation: 'The word will not be changed with Me, and I am not unjust to the servants.'

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ امْتَلَأْتِ وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِن مَّزِيدٍ
full_text.translation: On the Day We will say to Hell, 'Are you filled?' and it will say, 'Is there more?'

full_text.arabic: وَأُزْلِفَتِ الْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ
full_text.translation: And Paradise will be brought near to the righteous, not far.

full_text.arabic: هَٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ
full_text.translation: 'This is what you were promised — for every one who constantly returned to Allah and kept His limits.'

full_text.arabic: مَّنْ خَشِيَ الرَّحْمَٰنَ بِالْغَيْبِ وَجَاءَ بِقَلْبٍ مُّنِيبٍ
full_text.translation: 'Who feared the Most Merciful in the unseen and came with a heart turned in devotion.'

full_text.arabic: ادْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَامٍ ۖ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُلُودِ
full_text.translation: 'Enter it in peace. This is the Day of Eternity.'

full_text.arabic: لَهُم مَّا يَشَاءُونَ فِيهَا وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌ
full_text.translation: 'They will have whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more.'

full_text.arabic: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُم بَطْشًا فَنَقَّبُوا فِي الْبِلَادِ هَلْ مِن مَّحِيصٍ
full_text.translation: And how many a generation We destroyed before them who were greater in power and had explored the lands — is there any escape?

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِمَن كَانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ أَوْ أَلْقَى السَّمْعَ وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ
full_text.translation: Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart or who listens while he is present.

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ
full_text.translation: And We created the heavens and earth and what is between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness.

full_text.arabic: فَاصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ
full_text.translation: So be patient over what they say and glorify with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before the setting.

full_text.arabic: وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَارَ السُّجُودِ
full_text.translation: And glorify Him in the night and after prostrations.

full_text.arabic: وَاسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنَادِ الْمُنَادِ مِن مَّكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ
full_text.translation: And listen for the Day when the caller will call from a nearby place.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ الصَّيْحَةَ بِالْحَقِّ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُرُوجِ
full_text.translation: The Day they will hear the blast in truth. That is the Day of Emergence.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْنَا الْمَصِيرُ
full_text.translation: Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the destination.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ الْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعًا ۚ ذَٰلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ
full_text.translation: The Day the earth breaks away from them, and they will be hastening forth. That is a gathering easy for Us.

full_text.arabic: نَّحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَقُولُونَ ۖ وَمَا أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِجَبَّارٍ ۖ فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَن يَخَافُ وَعِيدِ
full_text.translation: We know best what they say, and you are not over them a tyrant. So remind by the Quran whoever fears My threat.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: The destroyed nations in ayahs 12-14 are listed — named and dismissed in a single stroke each. No Musa and Pharaoh, no Yusuf arc, no dialogue between a prophet and his people. The surah refuses dramatic distance. Everything is addressed to you, happening to you, now.

No command to pray, fast, give charity, or maintain any specific practice. The glorification command near the end is devotional, not legal. The surah is pure argument, pure confrontation with reality.

No 'O you who have believed,' no 'O mankind.' The surah speaks to the individual — to the single human soul watched by angels, approached by death, driven to judgment. The second person singular dominates: you, your veil, your sight.

No one speaks on anyone's behalf. The companion devil disclaims responsibility (ayah 27). God's word is settled (ayah 28). There is no negotiation at the stage the surah depicts. The door between worlds swings only one way.

absences.item: No mention of the Prophet's suffering
absences.note: The Prophet is told to be patient and to glorify God, but he is not consoled for any specific hardship. The surah's emotional weight falls entirely on the listener's reckoning with their own mortality and proximity to God.

absenceMap.subtitle: A surah of pure argument — no story, no law, only proximity

left.desc: The sky, the earth, the mountains, the rain, the gardens — laid out as proof that the Creator can create again
left.label: Creation Evidence (detailed)

right.desc: The heavens and earth created in six days without weariness — compressed into a single ayah when you have already been through death and judgment
right.label: Creation Evidence (compressed)

left.desc: Nine peoples named and dismissed. Denial is a pattern, and the pattern always ends the same way.
left.label: Destroyed Nations (catalogue)

right.desc: The catalogue becomes a question: 'Is there any escape?' The movement from statement to question marks the difference between hearing and internalizing.
right.label: Destroyed Nations (question)

left.desc: The intoxication of death, the trumpet, the driver and witness, the veil removed, Hell's insatiable hunger
left.label: Death and Judgment

right.desc: Paradise not far. The awwab and hafiz. A heart turned in devotion. 'And with Us is more' — the same word mazid, now grace instead of hunger.
right.label: Paradise Brought Near

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: We are closer to him than his jugular vein. The two angels record. He does not utter a single word without a watcher ready beside him.
center.note: The architectural heart: everything before builds toward this intimacy, everything after unfolds its consequences. God's closeness is the foundation of all accountability.
center.label: The Jugular Vein

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah opens with creation as evidence and closes with creation compressed into a single ayah

sectionJourney.title: The Four Arcs

sections.desc: The Quraysh dismiss resurrection as absurd — 'a far-off return.' The surah answers by pointing at the sky with no rifts, the spread earth, the mountains, the rain reviving dead land. You have already seen resurrection. You watch it happen every growing season. The denial is not philosophical — it is a failure of observation.
sections.title: Creation

sections.desc: Nine destroyed peoples named in three ayahs — Noah, Rass, Thamud, 'Ad, Pharaoh, Lot, the thicket, Tubba'. No story, no dialogue, no dramatic arc. The names fall like a drumbeat. The pattern always ends the same way.
sections.title: The Catalogue of Denial

sections.desc: The passage that defines the surah. God is closer than the jugular vein. The two recording angels sit on the right and left. Then death arrives — the intoxication that strips away pretense. The trumpet, the driver and witness, the veil removed, the sight made sharp. Hell asks: 'Is there more?'
sections.title: The Intimate Center

sections.desc: Paradise brought near — not far. The righteous defined not by perfection but orientation: a heart that keeps turning back. Then the command to the Prophet: be patient, glorify God at the edges of the day, and remind by the Quran whoever fears the divine threat. The surah closes where it opened — with the Quran itself.
sections.title: The Final Address

sectionJourney.subtitle: Creation as evidence → destroyed nations → the intimate center → the final address

deductiveFunnel.title: The Collapse of Distance

layers.desc: The sky, the earth, the rain. Dead land revived. 'Thus is the emergence.' The distance between rain and resurrection is zero — you have already seen it. The surah begins by collapsing the distance between natural observation and theological truth.
layers.label: Creation → You

layers.desc: Closer than the jugular vein. The distance between God and the human soul is no distance at all. The surveillance is intimacy. The accountability is closeness.
layers.label: God → You
layers.arabic: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ

layers.desc: The intoxication of death arrives with truth — that is what you were trying to avoid. Death is placed at the structural midpoint of the surah because it is at the center of life, not its edge.
layers.label: Death → You

layers.desc: The caller calls from a nearby place — makan qarib. The trumpet sounds from close. The surah's final collapse: even the Day of Judgment is near. Nothing you were afraid of is far. It is all already here.
layers.label: Judgment → You

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The surah systematically destroys every form of distance between you and the inevitable

content_nodes.concept: The jugular vein — habl al-warid (50:16)
Sakrat al-mawt — the intoxication of death (50:19)
Qaf and Ya-Sin — two paths to resurrection
Mazid — surplus as hunger and as grace (50:30, 50:35)

why_this_surah: The Prophet ﷺ recited this surah from the pulpit on Fridays. It opens with the Quran and an oath, and it ends with the reminder: 'We know what the earth takes from them, and with Us is a recording book.' Between those two points, the surah asks one question: can God who created everything really not bring you back?

name: Ali ‘Imran
thesis: A surah that finds you in the rubble, calls the collapse by its right name, refuses to let you blame anyone you shouldn’t or excuse anything you can’t, and then sits with you until you can stand again — and look at the sky — and say: You did not make this for nothing.

heart_verse.why: The pivot on which the entire surah turns. The verb nudawiluhaa — from the root that gives Arabic the word dawla (state, cycle, currency) — compresses a philosophy of history into four syllables. The days of victory and defeat are not random. They are circulated by design. The God who alternates night and day alternates the fortunes of nations by the same principle.
heart_verse.arabic: وتِلْكَ الْأَيَّامُ نُدَاوِلُهَا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ
heart_verse.translation: And these days, We alternate them among the people.

keyAyahs.title: Landmarks

verses.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُّحْكَمَاتٌ
verses.context: The Quran’s only direct statement about its own internal structure. The muhkam/mutashabih distinction maps two postures before ambiguity: the one who chases it to destabilize, and the one who holds it in trust.
verses.translation: It is He who sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are clear and foundational...

verses.arabic: إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَىٰ عِندَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ
verses.context: If miraculous origin proves divinity, then Adam’s claim is stronger — no mother and no father. The miracle points to the Maker. It always pointed to the Maker.
verses.translation: The likeness of Jesus before Allah is the likeness of Adam.

verses.arabic: وتِلْكَ الْأَيَّامُ نُدَاوِلُهَا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ
verses.context: The pivot. The verb nudawiluhaa carries the image of something being handed around like currency. The days of victory and defeat are circulated by design. Defeat is not the absence of God — it is one of the days He circulates.
verses.translation: And these days, We alternate them among the people.

verses.arabic: فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ اللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ
verses.context: Allah addressing the Prophet ﻛ about his conduct after a defeat caused in part by his own followers’ disobedience. The quality that held the community together was not strength — it was softness. Had he hardened, they would have scattered.
verses.translation: By the mercy of Allah, you were lenient with them.

verses.arabic: رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَٰذَا بَاطِلًا سُبْحَانَكَ
verses.context: The du’a of the ulu al-albab. People who have been through the surah — the theology, the narrative, the wound of Uhud — and what remains is a declaration of trust by people who have seen enough to know that trust is the only posture that holds.
verses.translation: Our Lord, You did not create this without purpose. Exalted are You.

keyAyahs.subtitle: Five verses that define the surah’s landscape

absenceMap.title: What’s Missing

absences.note: Al-Baqarah devotes long passages to marriage, divorce, fasting, pilgrimage, inheritance. Ali ‘Imran — of comparable length — offers almost none of that. The community does not need more legislation in this moment. It needs its certainty rebuilt. The absence of law is a diagnosis.

The vivid akhirah imagery of Makki surahs is mostly absent. No extended hellfire tableau, no graphic reckoning scene. The surah’s concern is this world, this wound, this community standing in the aftermath.

Unlike surahs that name Pharaoh, Abu Lahab, or Iblis as focal adversaries, Ali ‘Imran diagnoses communal failure without a villain. The enemy at Uhud is named less than the community’s own internal fractures.

After a military disaster caused partly by his followers’ disobedience, the surah’s address to the Prophet ﻛ is not correction but affirmation: ‘you were gentle with them.’ The absence of blame toward leadership is itself an argument about what kind of authority survives crisis.

The final ayah is not celebration — it is four imperatives: persevere, endure, remain stationed, be conscious of Allah. The surah does not end with arrival. It ends with the instruction to keep standing.

absenceMap.subtitle: 200 ayahs of Madani revelation — and what they conspicuously leave out

left.desc: Allah — no god but Him, Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum. This Book confirms what came before it. Then: the parable of Isa's creation, the admonition of those who twist revelation. The surah opens by establishing what is unmovable.
left.label: The Living, The Sustainer

right.desc: To Allah belongs the kingdom of the heavens and earth. Those with understanding remember Him standing, sitting, lying down. The surah closes where it opened: in the same sovereignty, the same call to hold firm, the same promise.
right.label: Hold to Allah Alone

left.desc: Maryam chosen above the women of the worlds. Isa's birth, his signs, the disciples. Then the long negotiation with Christians and Jews — "Come to a word equal between us." The covenant people confronted with the one they distort.
left.label: Maryam, Isa, and the People of the Book

right.desc: From Badr's victory to Uhud's test — and why the test was necessary. The surah's longest section is the anatomy of a defeat that was not a defeat. Why do you weaken? Those before you also suffered. Patience is the answer to both the story and the question.
right.label: Uhud and Its Lessons

left.desc: The Torah and Gospel were revealed after Ibrahim — so how can he belong to either community? The closest people to Ibrahim are those who follow him. The deepest argument: claim the ancestor by submitting as he submitted.
left.label: Ibrahim — Not Jew, Not Christian

right.desc: Do not take as confidants those who want harm for you. They rejoice at your setbacks and grieve at your successes. Mirror of the Ibrahim argument: do not outsource your allegiance to those who do not share your center.
right.label: Do Not Take as Intimate Friends

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Hold firmly to the rope of Allah, all together, and do not divide. Remember His favor — you were enemies and He joined your hearts. You were on the edge of a pit of fire and He saved you from it.
center.note: The center of Al-Imran is not a theological argument or a narrative — it is a command of unity. Every section before and after it is either the cause of fragmentation (Ahl al-Kitab distorting covenant) or its consequence (Uhud). The rope is the answer to both.
center.label: Hold to the Rope of Allah

chiasticRing.subtitle: A surah that begins with divine sovereignty and ends with it — everything between is the test of holding firm

sectionJourney.title: The Journey

sections.desc: Opens with al-Hayy al-Qayyum — the Living, the Self-Sustaining — the same names that anchor Ayat al-Kursi. Then ayah 7: the muhkam/mutashabih distinction, the Quran’s only direct statement about its own internal structure. Clear verses are the load-bearing walls; ambiguous ones shimmer with more than one meaning. The posture of the firmly rooted is not to chase ambiguity but to hold it: ‘We believe in it. All of it is from our Lord.’
sections.title: The Ground Beneath the Ground

sections.desc: The family of Imran unfolds through escalating impossibilities. Hanna expects a son; she receives a daughter who will become the mother of a prophet. Zakariyya sees Maryam’s miraculous provision and is moved to request his own impossible child. Then Maryam herself: a son without a father. Each miracle builds on the one before. The architecture of the family is the argument. Ayah 59 redirects: the likeness of Isa before Allah is like Adam — the miracle points to the Maker.
sections.title: The House of Miracles

sections.desc: The interfaith argument sharpens. ‘Come to a word that is equitable between us and you’ — kalima sawa’ assumes shared ground before it asks anything. Then ayah 110 defines the Muslim community by a function: commanding good and preventing harm. The Mubahala challenge (ayah 61) marks the outer limit of theological argument — a mutual oath of imprecation that the Najran delegation declined.
sections.title: Common & Contested Ground

sections.desc: The longest sustained battle narrative in the Quran — 55 ayahs of Uhud. The archers left their posts. The rumor spread that the Prophet ﻛ was dead. Three failures named in a single breath: loss of nerve, internal disagreement, disobedience after a clear sign. And yet the quality that held everything together was not strength — it was softness. ‘By the mercy of Allah, you were lenient with them.’ The community survived because its leader refused to harden.
sections.title: The Reckoning

sections.desc: The surah’s most contemplative section. People who remember Allah standing, sitting, lying on their sides. They look at the heavens and earth and say: ‘Our Lord, You did not create this without purpose.’ The final ayah compresses the entire argument into four imperatives: persevere, endure, remain stationed, be conscious of Allah.
sections.title: Those Who Remain

sectionJourney.subtitle: Five movements: theology → narrative → argument → wound → stillness

arcs.desc: The phrase ‘those of innermost understanding’ appears at ayah 7 (responding to textual ambiguity) and returns at ayah 190 (responding to cosmic signs). The surah argues that reading revelation rightly and reading creation rightly require the same posture: willingness to see pattern and purpose in what is not fully explicable.
arcs.label: Ulu al-Albab Envelope

arcs.desc: The divine attribute at the entrance — al-Qayyum, the one who sustains without faltering — becomes an ethical demand at the exit: rabitu, remain stationed. The surah argues that the divine attribute of self-sustaining existence has a corresponding human practice: the refusal to leave your post.
arcs.label: Al-Hayy al-Qayyum → Rabitu

arcs.desc: The family narrative establishes that Allah’s agency is not constrained by expected mechanism. This is exactly what the community needs when it reaches Uhud. The God who produced Isa without biological precedent is the same God who can produce meaning from what looks like ruin.
arcs.label: Miraculous Family → Battlefield Faith

structuralArcs.title: The Arcs
structuralArcs.subtitle: Three structural arguments that span the surah

content_nodes.concept: Muhkam and Mutashabih — the Quran’s self-description
The family of Imran — miracle as architecture
Nudawiluhaa — the circulation of days
Al-Zahrawayn — Al-Baqarah and Ali ‘Imran as a pair

why_this_surah: When you're tested — when things fall apart after you thought you were doing everything right — this surah speaks to that. It came down in the wake of the Battle of Uhud, and it processes the hardest spiritual question: why do bad things happen to people who are trying to be good?

name: At-Talaq
thesis: Twelve ayahs where the rules for ending a marriage and the architecture of seven heavens are governed by the same word, the same command, the same God who counts all things — a surah that placed the cosmos inside a courtroom.

heart_verse.why: The surah's most quoted passage — embedded inside divorce legislation. The most universal promise about divine provision lives inside the most painful domestic reality. The root kh-r-j (to go out) connects the prohibition of expulsion, the divine exit, and the prophetic mission.
heart_verse.arabic: وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مَخْرَجًا وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ
heart_verse.translation: And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ وَأَحْصُوا الْعِدَّةَ ۖ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ رَبَّكُمْ ۖ لَا تُخْرِجُوهُنَّ مِن بُيُوتِهِنَّ وَلَا يَخْرُجْنَ إِلَّا أَن يَأْتِينَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ مُّبَيِّنَةٍ ۚ وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ ۚ وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ ۚ لَا تَدْرِي لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ أَمْرًا
full_text.translation: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period and count the waiting period, and fear Allah your Lord. Do not expel them from their homes, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has wronged himself. You do not know — perhaps Allah will bring about a new situation after that.

full_text.arabic: فَإِذَا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ فَارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ وَأَشْهِدُوا ذَوَيْ عَدْلٍ مِّنكُمْ وَأَقِيمُوا الشَّهَادَةَ لِلَّهِ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمْ يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَن كَانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ ۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مَخْرَجًا
full_text.translation: And when they have reached their term, either retain them honorably or part with them honorably, and bring to witness two just persons from among you and establish the testimony for Allah. That is instructed to whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out.

full_text.arabic: وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَحْتَسِبُ ۚ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَالِغُ أَمْرِهِ ۚ قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْرًا
full_text.translation: And will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah — He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set a measure for everything.

full_text.arabic: وَاللَّائِي يَئِسْنَ مِنَ الْمَحِيضِ مِن نِّسَائِكُمْ إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ وَاللَّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ ۚ وَأُولَاتُ الْأَحْمَالِ أَجَلُهُنَّ أَن يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ ۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْرًا
full_text.translation: And those who no longer menstruate among your women — if you doubt, then their waiting period is three months, and also for those who have not yet menstruated. And for pregnant women, their term is until they deliver. And whoever fears Allah, He will make his affairs easy for him.

full_text.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ أَنزَلَهُ إِلَيْكُمْ ۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يُكَفِّرْ عَنْهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِ وَيُعْظِمْ لَهُ أَجْرًا
full_text.translation: That is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears Allah, He will remove for him his misdeeds and make great for him his reward.

full_text.arabic: أَسْكِنُوهُنَّ مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنتُم مِّن وُجْدِكُمْ وَلَا تُضَارُّوهُنَّ لِتُضَيِّقُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ ۚ وَإِن كُنَّ أُولَاتِ حَمْلٍ فَأَنفِقُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ حَتَّىٰ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ ۚ فَإِنْ أَرْضَعْنَ لَكُمْ فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ ۖ وَأْتَمِرُوا بَيْنَكُم بِمَعْرُوفٍ ۖ وَإِن تَعَاسَرْتُمْ فَسَتُرْضِعُ لَهُ أُخْرَىٰ
full_text.translation: House them where you dwell, according to your means, and do not harm them to make things difficult for them. And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they deliver. And if they nurse for you, give them their wages, and consult together in a fair manner. And if you are in disagreement, then another woman may nurse for him.

full_text.arabic: لِيُنفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِّن سَعَتِهِ ۖ وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ فَلْيُنفِقْ مِمَّا آتَاهُ اللَّهُ ۚ لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا مَا آتَاهَا ۚ سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا
full_text.translation: Let a man of wealth spend according to his wealth, and he whose provision is restricted — let him spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it. Allah will bring, after hardship, ease.

full_text.arabic: وَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ عَتَتْ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهَا وَرُسُلِهِ فَحَاسَبْنَاهَا حِسَابًا شَدِيدًا وَعَذَّبْنَاهَا عَذَابًا نُّكْرًا
full_text.translation: And how many a community defied the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We called it to a severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment.

full_text.arabic: فَذَاقَتْ وَبَالَ أَمْرِهَا وَكَانَ عَاقِبَةُ أَمْرِهَا خُسْرًا
full_text.translation: And it tasted the consequence of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss.

full_text.arabic: أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا ۖ فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَا أُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ۚ قَدْ أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكُمْ ذِكْرًا
full_text.translation: Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment, so fear Allah, O people of understanding who have believed. Allah has sent down to you a reminder.

full_text.arabic: رَّسُولًا يَتْلُو عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ مُبَيِّنَاتٍ لِّيُخْرِجَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ إِلَى النُّورِ
full_text.translation: A Messenger reciting to you the clear signs of Allah, to bring those who believe and do righteous deeds out of darkness into light.

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ وَمِنَ الْأَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ يَتَنَزَّلُ الْأَمْرُ بَيْنَهُنَّ لِتَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أَحَاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا
full_text.translation: Allah is the One who created seven heavens and from the earth that which is similar to them. His command descends through them so that you may know that Allah has power over all things and that Allah encompasses all things in knowledge.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No prophets named. No stories told. The destroyed nations of ayahs 8-10 are unnamed — referenced only as communities who disobeyed. The law stands on its own authority.

The entire surah speaks to the Prophet and through him to husbands and authorities. The women whose rights are being protected are spoken about, not spoken to. Protection operates through obligation placed on the powerful.
No paradise scene, no hellfire. The destroyed nations serve as warning, but the surah's urgency is about how you conduct yourself through dissolution, not what awaits afterward.

absences.item: No separation of law and theology
absences.note: This is what makes the surah unique. There is no 'legal section' followed by a 'spiritual section.' The theology interrupts the legislation. The two are inseparable by design.
Every promise is preceded by a condition of taqwa. The makhraja, the provision, the ease — all require fear of Allah. Grace is not unconditional; it is responsive.

absenceMap.subtitle: A surah of focused intensity — twelve ayahs with no room for anything peripheral

left.desc: La tukhrijuhunna — do not force her out of her home. The legal prohibition. The human act of expulsion.
left.label: Do Not Expel

right.desc: Li-yukhrija — to bring those who believe out of darkness into light. The prophetic mission as divine exit.
right.label: Brought Into Light

left.desc: Perhaps Allah will bring about a new amr — reconciliation as open future
left.label: Amr

right.desc: His amr descends through seven heavens and seven earths — the same word, now universal
right.label: Amr  Reality

chiasticRing.title: The Root Kh-r-j

center.desc: Whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and provide from where he does not expect.
center.note: Between the prohibition of expulsion and the prophetic mission of bringing people out — the divine exit for the one who fears Allah.
center.label: The Makhraja — Way Out

chiasticRing.subtitle: Three uses of the same root — legal, providential, salvific

sectionJourney.title: The Interweave

sections.desc: Divorce procedure and waiting period, then the tawakkul promise: whoever fears Allah, He makes a way out and provides from the unseen. The most quoted verses in this surah, born inside legislation.
sections.title: Procedure & Tawakkul

sections.desc: Post-menopausal women, those who haven't yet menstruated, pregnant women — the law refined. Then: whoever fears Allah, He eases his affairs and magnifies his reward.
sections.title: Specific Cases & Taqwa

sections.desc: Housing, nursing wages, financial support. Then the fusion: Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it. After hardship, ease. The domestic and the cosmic meet.
sections.title: Obligations & Cosmic Promise

sections.desc: Destroyed communities invoked. Disobeying divorce legislation carries the same weight as the defiance that destroyed cities. The word amr threads from domestic hope to civilizational judgment.
sections.title: The Warning

sections.desc: The Messenger brings people from darkness to light. Seven heavens, seven earths, divine command descending through all of them. The God who legislates your divorce governs the universe.
sections.title: Light & Cosmos

sectionJourney.subtitle: Each block of legislation is followed by a theological opening — and the theology escalates

deductiveFunnel.title: Five Taqwa Commands

layers.desc: The first command, opening the surah. Taqwa as the foundation of the entire divorce procedure.
layers.label: Fear Allah, your Lord

layers.desc: The second: whoever fears Allah receives the makhraja. Taqwa and provision are inseparable.
layers.label: A way out
layers.arabic: وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مَخْرَجًا

layers.desc: The third: taqwa brings ease. The pattern is now unmistakable — every block of legislation sealed with a promise.
layers.label: Ease of affairs
layers.arabic: وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْرًا

layers.desc: The fourth: addressed to those who think. The legislative-to-historical arc culminates in a call to those who can see the pattern.
layers.label: O people of understanding

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The word taqwa saturates the surah — every legal instruction is framed as worship

content_nodes.concept: The makhraja promise — divine exit from difficulty
Amr — from domestic hope to cosmic descent
At-Talaq and At-Tahrim diptych
After hardship ease — 65:7 and 94:5-6

why_this_surah: The surah of divorce (al-ṭalāq) — the Quran's detailed legislation on how separation must preserve dignity. Waiting periods, housing rights, financial support, witnesses. The surah that makes the end of a marriage a matter of divine law rather than male whim. 'You do not know — perhaps God will bring about a new situation' (65:1).

name: Al-Ma'idah
thesis: The surah of the last word — a final testament that seals the religion as complete, catalogs every covenant ever broken, and closes with Jesus standing before God demonstrating what a perfectly honored covenant looks like.

heart_verse.why: The single most consequential sentence in the history of revelation. Embedded between rulings on carrion and stone altars, it arrived at Arafat on a Friday. The camel knelt under the weight of revelation. 'Umar wept — because perfection meant the Prophet's mission was drawing to its close.
heart_verse.arabic: ٱلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِى وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلْإِسْلَـٰمَ دِينًا
heart_verse.translation: Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and chosen Islam as your way.

keyAyahs.title: Landmarks

verses.arabic: ٱلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِى
verses.context: The single most momentous declaration in revelation — embedded within food-law rulings. Two distinct completions: akmaltu (perfected in structure) and atmamtu (completed in favor). Everything before this was building. After it, the building is done.
verses.translation: Today I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favor upon you.

verses.arabic: وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ ٱعْدِلُوا۟
verses.context: Justice as covenant obligation — not contingent on who the other party is. The command is repeated for emphasis: 'be just — that is nearer to piety.'
verses.translation: Do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just.

verses.arabic: مَن قَتَلَ نَفْسًا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًا
verses.context: The legislation of the sanctity of life grows directly from the narrative of its first violation. The first broken covenant between human beings was a brother's blood.
verses.translation: Whoever kills a soul — unless for a soul or corruption in the land — it is as if he killed all of humanity.

verses.arabic: وَأَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ بِٱلْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ
verses.context: Muhaymin — watchful protector. The Quran does not replace previous scripture. It guards it. The relationship to earlier revelation defined in a single word.
verses.translation: We revealed to you the Book in truth, confirming what came before it and as a guardian over it.

verses.arabic: إِن تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبَادُكَ ۖ وَإِن تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فَإِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
verses.context: Jesus's final Quranic words. He does not say 'the Merciful, the Forgiving.' He says al-'Aziz al-Hakim — forgiveness as sovereign wisdom, not sentiment. Among the most theologically precise moments in the Quran.
verses.translation: If You punish them, they are Your servants. And if You forgive them, You are the Mighty, the Wise.

keyAyahs.subtitle: Five verses that define the surah's landscape

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.item: No sense of uncertainty about the community's direction
absences.note: The earlier Madani surahs — Al-Baqarah, Ali 'Imran, An-Nisa — are still forming the community, still responding to crises. Al-Ma'idah assumes the infrastructure exists. It is finalizing, not founding.
The community-building register of Al-Baqarah is gone. In its place is something closer to a charge — final instructions given to people who are expected to know, by now, how to carry them.

For a 120-ayah surah, the absence of detailed paradise or hellfire imagery is striking. The surah is concerned with the covenant in this world — how it is honored, how it is broken, and what it looks like in a human being standing before God.

absences.item: No path back from the first murder
absences.note: The brother who kills is not offered repentance within the narrative. He is ashamed that he is less capable than a crow — not remorseful for the killing. The moral collapse is complete, and the surah does not attempt to reverse it.

absences.item: No soft names in Jesus's final words
absences.note: Jesus says al-'Aziz al-Hakim — the Mighty, the Wise — not al-Ghafur al-Rahim. Forgiveness belongs to the One with full authority and full knowledge. The choice of divine names is conspicuously deliberate.

absenceMap.subtitle: What a surah of final instructions conspicuously leaves out

left.desc: O you who believe, fulfill your obligations. Lawful to you is the catch of the sea and its food. Sacred months are sacred. The surah opens with the word 'uqud — contracts, covenants. Everything that follows is either keeping or breaking them.
left.label: Fulfill Your Covenants

right.desc: When I inspired the disciples to believe in Me and My messenger, they said: We believe. The final section of the surah is the disciples taking their own covenant — the same word, the same act — and Isa refusing to claim anything beyond what he was given.
right.label: The Disciples' Covenant

left.desc: Allah took the covenant of the Children of Israel. They broke it. Then the same with the Christians. Then the command: judge by what Allah has revealed. The pattern before the center: covenant given, covenant broken.
left.label: The People of the Book's Betrayal

right.desc: Those who say Allah is the third of three — they have disbelieved. Al-Masih ibn Maryam was only a messenger. The section after the center: what breaking the covenant costs, and what it looks like when a messenger refuses to exceed his station.
right.label: The Punishment for Breaking Covenant

left.desc: They are an abomination from the work of Satan — so avoid it. Satan only wants to cause enmity between you through intoxicants and gambling. A legal ruling placed near the center because its stakes are communal: the covenant community must be lucid to hold together.
left.label: Intoxicants and Games of Chance

right.desc: Send down to us a table laden with food from the sky. Isa warns: whoever disbelieves after this, I will punish them. The table is the last covenant sign in the surah — provision from heaven given on condition of faith, and refused by those who break the condition.
right.label: The Table

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: We revealed to you the Book in truth, confirming what is before it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. Judge between them by what Allah has revealed.
center.note: The center of Al-Maidah is the Quran's own self-description: muhaymin — guardian, criterion, standard over all that came before. This ayah is the axis. Every covenant before it points toward this standard; every betrayal after it is measured against it.
center.label: The Quran as Standard

chiasticRing.subtitle: The last major surah revealed — its covenants frame the whole, its center names the Quran as the standard

sectionJourney.title: The Capstone

sections.desc: The surah opens with a word found nowhere else as a Quranic opening: fulfill your contracts. The word 'uqud sets the key in the first sentence. Immediately: food laws, the verse of completion (5:3), the command to cooperate in righteousness and never let hatred of a people lead you to abandon justice.
sections.title: The Covenant Declared

sections.desc: God took a covenant from the Children of Israel — twelve leaders, divine support — and they broke it. He took a covenant from the Christians, and they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. Partial forgetting is more dangerous than total rejection. The Israelites at the Holy Land refuse to enter: 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We will sit right here.'
sections.title: The Broken Covenants

sections.desc: The surah reaches back to the first human family. Both offered a sacrifice — one accepted, one not. The rejected brother's silence becomes rage, and the rage becomes murder. The accepted brother refuses to mirror the violence: 'I fear God.' A crow teaches the first funeral. From this story: 'Whoever kills a soul, it is as if he killed all of humanity.'
sections.title: The First Murder

sections.desc: The densest legislative passage. Criminal law, the sanctity of life, and the triple declaration: whoever does not judge by what God revealed — they are the disbelievers, the wrongdoers, the transgressors (5:44, 45, 47). The Torah, the Gospel, and the Quran named in sequence as stages of one revelation. The Quran stands as muhaymin — watchful guardian — over all previous scripture.
sections.title: Law, Corruption, and Judgment

sections.desc: The longest sustained section addresses the community's relationship with Jewish and Christian communities. Do not take them as awliya' — governing allies in communal direction, not casual friends. But the surah draws distinctions within communities: some among the Christians, who weep when they hear the Quran, are nearest in affection to the believers (5:82).
sections.title: Navigating the People of the Book

sections.desc: Prohibition of intoxicants, gambling, divination. The Ka'bah named as a standing-place for humanity. The warning against asking for specificity that narrows permissibility (5:101). Then the closing: Jesus's miracles, the table from heaven, and the extraordinary scene where God asks Jesus directly — 'Did you say to the people, take me and my mother as gods?' His answer is prophetic speech at its most transparent.
sections.title: The Final Legislation & Jesus

sectionJourney.subtitle: Six movements: covenant → broken covenants → first murder → law → People of the Book → Jesus & the table

arcs.desc: The opening places the human being inside an obligation. The closing places that obligation inside God's total ownership. Covenants matter because everything belongs to God, and to break your word is to violate the order of a creation you do not own.
arcs.label: Covenant → Sovereignty

arcs.desc: Every broken covenant the surah catalogues — the Israelites who refused, the Christians who forgot — is answered by Jesus's closing speech. He says only what he was commanded. He claims nothing for himself. His final speech is what a perfectly fulfilled covenant looks like.
arcs.label: Broken Covenants → Perfect Covenant

arcs.desc: Three stories of covenants with visible signs: the promised land, the fire that consumed the offering, the table from heaven. In each case, the community's failure comes after the sign. Seeing the evidence is not enough. The table descends, and the covenant can still be broken.
arcs.label: Sign → Obligation → Judgment

structuralArcs.title: The Arcs
structuralArcs.subtitle: Three structural threads that span the surah

content_nodes.concept: 5:3 — The day the religion was perfected
The first murder — Adam's two sons
Muhaymin — the Quran as guardian of scripture
Jesus's closing speech — prophetic self-defense as worship

why_this_surah: The last major surah revealed — God's final word on how to live. It contains the verse where God declares the religion complete. If you want to understand what the Quran considers the final, settled version of its rules on food, justice, and dealing with people of other faiths, this is where to look.

name: Al-Muddaththir
thesis: A surah that pulls the cloak off a trembling man and sends him into a world that will call his message magic — narrating the psychology of denial step by step, turning a number into a diagnostic mirror, and closing by naming the God who sent the warning as the God who forgives.

heart_verse.why: After fifty-five ayahs of warning — the command, the portrait of denial, the fire, the startled donkeys, the closed door of intercession — the final word is forgiveness. Two divine attributes held in a single breath: taqwa and maghfira. The warning exists so that the forgiveness can be reached.
heart_verse.arabic: هُوَ أَهْلُ التَّقْوَىٰ وَأَهْلُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ
heart_verse.translation: He is worthy of being feared and worthy of forgiving.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ
full_text.translation: O you who covers himself —

full_text.arabic: قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ
full_text.translation: arise and warn.

full_text.arabic: وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ
full_text.translation: And magnify your Lord.

full_text.arabic: وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ
full_text.translation: And purify your garments.

full_text.arabic: وَالرُّجْزَ فَاهْجُرْ
full_text.translation: And avoid uncleanliness.

full_text.arabic: وَلَا تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ
full_text.translation: And do not give expecting more in return.

full_text.arabic: وَلِرَبِّكَ فَاصْبِرْ
full_text.translation: And for your Lord, be patient.

full_text.arabic: فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِي النَّاقُورِ
full_text.translation: Then, when the trumpet is blown —

full_text.arabic: فَذَٰلِكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ
full_text.translation: that day will be a difficult day —

full_text.arabic: عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ
full_text.translation: not easy for the disbelievers.

full_text.arabic: ذَرْنِي وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ وَحِيدًا
full_text.translation: Leave Me with the one I created alone.

full_text.arabic: وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مَالًا مَّمْدُودًا
full_text.translation: And I gave him wealth spread out —

full_text.arabic: وَبَنِينَ شُهُودًا
full_text.translation: and sons present at his side —

full_text.arabic: وَمَهَّدتُّ لَهُ تَمْهِيدًا
full_text.translation: and made life smooth for him, ease after ease.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ يَطْمَعُ أَنْ أَزِيدَ
full_text.translation: Then he greedily desires that I give him more.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا ۖ إِنَّهُ كَانَ لِآيَاتِنَا عَنِيدًا
full_text.translation: No! He has been stubbornly resistant to Our signs.

full_text.arabic: سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُودًا
full_text.translation: I will cover him with an arduous climb.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ
full_text.translation: He thought and he calculated —

full_text.arabic: فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ
full_text.translation: may he be destroyed, how he calculated!

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ قُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ
full_text.translation: Then may he be destroyed, how he calculated!

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ
full_text.translation: Then he looked —

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ
full_text.translation: then he frowned and scowled —

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ وَاسْتَكْبَرَ
full_text.translation: then he turned his back and was arrogant —

full_text.arabic: فَقَالَ إِنْ هَٰذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ
full_text.translation: and said, 'This is nothing but magic from the past.'

full_text.arabic: إِنْ هَٰذَا إِلَّا قَوْلُ الْبَشَرِ
full_text.translation: 'This is nothing but the word of a human being.'

full_text.arabic: سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ
full_text.translation: I will drive him into Saqar.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا سَقَرُ
full_text.translation: And what will make you know what Saqar is?

full_text.arabic: لَا تُبْقِي وَلَا تَذَرُ
full_text.translation: It leaves nothing remaining and lets nothing escape.

full_text.arabic: لَوَّاحَةٌ لِّلْبَشَرِ
full_text.translation: It scorches human skin.

full_text.arabic: عَلَيْهَا تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ
full_text.translation: Over it are nineteen.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا جَعَلْنَا أَصْحَابَ النَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَائِكَةً ۙ وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا
full_text.translation: We have made the keepers of the Fire none but angels. And We have made their number a trial for those who disbelieve...

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا وَالْقَمَرِ
full_text.translation: No! By the moon —

full_text.arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ
full_text.translation: and the night when it departs —

full_text.arabic: وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا أَسْفَرَ
full_text.translation: and the morning when it brightens —

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهَا لَإِحْدَى الْكُبَرِ
full_text.translation: indeed, it is one of the greatest things —

full_text.arabic: نَذِيرًا لِّلْبَشَرِ
full_text.translation: a warning for humanity.

full_text.arabic: لِمَن شَاءَ مِنكُمْ أَن يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ
full_text.translation: For whoever among you wishes to advance or stay behind.

full_text.arabic: كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ
full_text.translation: Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned —

full_text.arabic: إِلَّا أَصْحَابَ الْيَمِينِ
full_text.translation: except the people of the right.

full_text.arabic: فِي جَنَّاتٍ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ
full_text.translation: In gardens, questioning —

full_text.arabic: عَنِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ
full_text.translation: about the criminals:

full_text.arabic: مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ
full_text.translation: 'What put you into Saqar?'

full_text.arabic: قَالُوا لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ
full_text.translation: They will say, 'We were not among those who prayed,'

full_text.arabic: وَلَمْ نَكُ نُطْعِمُ الْمِسْكِينَ
full_text.translation: 'and we did not feed the poor,'

full_text.arabic: وَكُنَّا نَخُوضُ مَعَ الْخَائِضِينَ
full_text.translation: 'and we used to engage in falsehood with those who engaged,'

full_text.arabic: وَكُنَّا نُكَذِّبُ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ
full_text.translation: 'and we used to deny the Day of Judgment —'

full_text.arabic: حَتَّىٰ أَتَانَا الْيَقِينُ
full_text.translation: 'until the certainty came to us.'

full_text.arabic: فَمَا تَنفَعُهُمْ شَفَاعَةُ الشَّافِعِينَ
full_text.translation: So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them.

full_text.arabic: فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ
full_text.translation: Then what is wrong with them that they turn away from the reminder —

full_text.arabic: كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُّسْتَنفِرَةٌ
full_text.translation: as if they were alarmed donkeys —

full_text.arabic: فَرَّتْ مِن قَسْوَرَةٍ
full_text.translation: fleeing from a lion?

full_text.arabic: بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفًا مُّنَشَّرَةً
full_text.translation: Rather, each one of them wishes to be given a scripture spread out.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا ۖ بَل لَّا يَخَافُونَ الْآخِرَةَ
full_text.translation: No! They do not fear the Hereafter.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ
full_text.translation: No! Indeed it is a reminder.

full_text.arabic: فَمَن شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ
full_text.translation: So whoever wills may remember it.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا يَذْكُرُونَ إِلَّا أَن يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ ۚ هُوَ أَهْلُ التَّقْوَىٰ وَأَهْلُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ
full_text.translation: And they will not remember unless Allah wills. He is worthy of being feared and worthy of forgiving.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: For a Makkan surah of this length, the absence is striking. The Prophet is being sent out without the comfort of knowing others walked this road before him. He is simply told to rise. The comfort will come later, in other surahs.
No 'Ad, no Thamud, no flood. The consequence is named — Saqar — but the historical precedent is absent. The surah addresses the present and the future, not the past.
The people of the right are mentioned (ayah 39) and placed in gardens (ayah 40), but Paradise receives no description. The surah's energy is spent entirely on warning.
The divine name appears only in the passage about the nineteen and in the closing verses. For most of the surah, the voice speaks without naming itself. The intimacy is such that no name is needed.

absences.item: No elaboration on the five commands
absences.note: Arise, warn, magnify, purify, be patient — each command receives a single verb. No explanation, no context, no qualification. The brevity is the authority.

absenceMap.subtitle: The absences are themselves a statement about the surah's purpose

left.desc: Arise and warn. Five imperatives to a single man hiding under his cloak.
left.label: The Command to Warn

right.desc: They flee the reminder like startled donkeys. The warning meets resistance, and the surah ends on forgiveness.
right.label: The World Flees the Warning

left.desc: When the trumpet is blown, that day will be difficult — 'asir — not easy for the disbelievers.
left.label: The Difficult Day

right.desc: By the moon, the departing night, the brightening dawn. Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned.
right.label: Oaths and Accountability

left.desc: He thought, calculated, frowned, turned away. The gap between effort and conclusion is the surah's indictment.
left.label: The Denier's Deliberation

right.desc: We did not pray. We did not feed the poor. We denied the Day. The certainty we mocked became the certainty we could not escape.
right.label: The Criminals' Confession

chiasticRing.title: The Mirror

center.desc: The fire that leaves nothing. The number that becomes a test. The mirror at the center.
center.note: The number nineteen is a diagnostic. What you do with what you cannot fully explain reveals who you are.
center.label: Saqar and the Nineteen

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah's broad chiastic symmetry

sectionJourney.title: The Commission

sections.desc: A frightened man hiding under his cloak. Five commands in rapid succession: arise, warn, magnify your Lord, purify your garments, be patient. The Prophet's identity is being named — he is a nadhir, a warner. The cloak must come off.
sections.title: The Awakening

sections.desc: The surah narrows to a single human being, created alone with nothing, given everything, still greedy for more. Then the most psychologically detailed portrait of rejection in the Quran: he thought, calculated, looked, frowned, scowled, turned away, was arrogant — and produced the oldest dismissal in the world: it's just magic.
sections.title: The Portrait of the Denier

sections.desc: The fire that leaves nothing and lets nothing escape. Over it are nineteen — and their number is a test. The same information produces certainty in one group, increased faith in another, and mockery in a third. Then the criminals confess: we did not pray, did not feed the poor, indulged in falsehood, denied the Day.
sections.title: Saqar and the Nineteen

sections.desc: Those who flee the reminder like startled donkeys from a lion. Each demands his own personalized scripture. The surah closes on divine sovereignty: no one remembers unless Allah wills. And He is worthy of fear and worthy of forgiving.
sections.title: The Flight from Remembrance

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: awakening → portrait → mirror → confrontation

deductiveFunnel.title: The Staircase of Denial

layers.desc: He thought and he calculated. The rejection does not begin with ignorance — it begins with intelligence. He heard the Quran, recognized its power, and began to deliberate.
layers.label: Thought

layers.desc: Then he looked — surveyed his options, considered the landscape. The pause between thinking and acting, where the choice is still open.
layers.label: Looked

layers.desc: Then he frowned and scowled. The face betrays what the mind has decided. The frown comes after the thinking — meaning the thinking led somewhere he did not want to go.
layers.label: Frowned

layers.desc: Then he turned his back and was arrogant. The body follows the face. Adbara — to turn one's back — and istakbara — to make oneself great. The physical and spiritual movements are one.
layers.label: Turned Away

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: Seven verbs, seven choices, each leading to the next with the inevitability of gravity

content_nodes.concept: The psychology of deliberate denial (74:18–25)
Saqar and the diagnostic number nineteen
Al-Muzzammil – Al-Muddaththir diptych
Kullu nafsin bima kasabat raheena — the soul's mortgage

why_this_surah: The surah of the one wrapped in a cloak — the Prophet ﷺ after his first encounter with Jibril, trembling, asking Khadijah to cover him. Then the command: 'Arise and warn.' This is the moment the private experience of revelation became a public mission. The surah that turns a frightened man into a messenger.

name: At-Takwir
thesis: Twenty-nine ayahs in a single arc: twelve 'when' clauses stacking cosmic dissolution (sun folded, stars scattered, mountains moved, seas boiled), then the question — what have you prepared? — then the oath by the dawn, the night, the breath, establishing that this Quran is the word of a noble messenger.

heart_verse.why: In the middle of cosmic destruction — suns extinguished, mountains moved, oceans boiling — the surah pauses for the smallest and most helpless victim. The question indicts the killer by honoring the victim. In a culture that treated her death as unremarkable, the Quran gives her a voice and a courtroom.
heart_verse.arabic: وَإِذَا الْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ ﴿٨﴾ بِأَيِّ ذَنبٍ قُتِلَتْ
heart_verse.translation: And when the infant girl buried alive is asked — for what sin were you killed?

full_text.arabic: إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ
full_text.translation: When the sun is folded up,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا النُّجُومُ انكَدَرَتْ
full_text.translation: and when the stars fall and scatter,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الْجِبَالُ سُيِّرَتْ
full_text.translation: and when the mountains are set in motion,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ
full_text.translation: and when the pregnant camels are abandoned,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الْوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ
full_text.translation: and when the wild beasts are gathered,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ
full_text.translation: and when the seas are set ablaze,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ
full_text.translation: and when the souls are paired,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ
full_text.translation: and when the infant girl buried alive is asked —

full_text.arabic: بِأَيِّ ذَنبٍ قُتِلَتْ
full_text.translation: for what sin were you killed?

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ
full_text.translation: And when the scrolls are spread open,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ كُشِطَتْ
full_text.translation: and when the sky is stripped away,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ
full_text.translation: and when Hellfire is set ablaze,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا الْجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ
full_text.translation: and when Paradise is brought near —

full_text.arabic: عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّا أَحْضَرَتْ
full_text.translation: every soul will know what it has brought forward.

full_text.arabic: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ
full_text.translation: I swear by the retreating stars —

full_text.arabic: الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ
full_text.translation: those that move and hide —

full_text.arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا عَسْعَسَ
full_text.translation: and by the night as it draws in,

full_text.arabic: وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ
full_text.translation: and by the dawn as it breathes —

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ
full_text.translation: indeed, this is the word of a noble messenger,

full_text.arabic: ذِي قُوَّةٍ عِندَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ مَكِينٍ
full_text.translation: possessing power, secure in rank before the Lord of the Throne,

full_text.arabic: مُّطَاعٍ ثَمَّ أَمِينٍ
full_text.translation: obeyed there, and trustworthy.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا صَاحِبُكُم بِمَجْنُونٍ
full_text.translation: Your companion is not possessed.

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالْأُفُقِ الْمُبِينِ
full_text.translation: He saw him on the clear horizon.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ
full_text.translation: And he is not withholding of the unseen.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَيْطَانٍ رَّجِيمٍ
full_text.translation: And this is not the word of an accursed devil.

full_text.arabic: فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ
full_text.translation: So where are you going?

full_text.arabic: إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ
full_text.translation: It is nothing but a reminder for all creation —

full_text.arabic: لِمَن شَاءَ مِنكُمْ أَن يَسْتَقِيمَ
full_text.translation: for whoever among you wills to walk straight.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ إِلَّا أَن يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ
full_text.translation: But you cannot will unless Allah wills — the Lord of all creation.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No instructions on how to pray, give, or treat others. No legislation, no ethical teaching. The surah does not tell you how to live — it shows you what everything is heading toward and lets that vision do the work on its own.

absences.item: No stories of past prophets or nations
absences.note: No Nuh, no Ad, no Thamud, no destroyed cities. The surah is not interested in precedent. It is interested in what is coming, and the authority of the one who brings the news.

The entire first section is passive constructions — the sun is folded, the stars are scattered, the mountains are moved. No agent named. The doer is so vast that naming Him would diminish the scale of the event.
Nothing is softened. Twelve images of annihilation, no reassurance between them. The surah's gift is not comfort — it is proportion. It recalibrates what is permanent and what is temporary.

absences.item: No middle ground in the closing
absences.note: Human will is real (li-man sha'a). But human will is not sovereign (wa ma tasha'una illa an yasha'a Allah). Both truths held in consecutive ayahs without collapsing either. No resolution offered — you must live inside the tension.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah lets its vision do the moral work — every absence is a deliberate silence

left.desc: Stars fall, seas boil, mountains move — the visible order dismantled
left.label: Cosmic Destruction

right.desc: Stars retreat gracefully, night departs, the dawn breathes — the same created world through a different lens
right.label: Celestial Beauty

left.desc: The smallest victim given a voice and a courtroom amid cosmic annihilation
left.label: The Buried Girl's Trial

right.desc: The man dismissed as mad is defended — he saw Jibreel on the clear horizon
right.label: The Prophet's Defense

left.desc: Deeds spread open, sky stripped, Hellfire and Paradise made present
left.label: Scrolls & Reckoning

right.desc: Jibreel — possessing power, secure in rank, obeyed, trustworthy — the carrier of the message about that reckoning
right.label: Noble Messenger

chiasticRing.title: The Mirror

center.desc: Every soul will know what it has brought forward.
center.note: Twelve suspended conditions resolve into one sentence about personal accountability. The past tense (alimat) conveys certainty — it is so sure to happen it is spoken of as already completed.
center.label: The Arrival

chiasticRing.subtitle: From the largest external image to the most intimate internal reality

sectionJourney.title: The Arc

sections.desc: Six images strip away the familiar world: light (sun), navigation (stars), stability (mountains), wealth (pregnant camels), natural order (wild beasts), elemental boundaries (seas). No commentary between them — each lands before the reader recovers from the last. The form enacts the content: the world is coming apart, and so is your footing.
sections.title: The Cosmic Unraveling

sections.desc: The focus shifts from cosmos to conscience. Souls are paired with their deeds. The buried infant girl is asked — not the killer, but the victim — for what sin she was killed. Scrolls spread open. Sky stripped away. Hellfire ablaze. Paradise brought near. Then the main clause: every soul will know what it has brought forward.
sections.title: The Human Reckoning

sections.desc: After the breathless cascade, something deliberate. Allah swears by retreating stars, departing night, and the dawn as it breathes — one image of gentle life after twelve of destruction. On these oaths: this is the word of a noble messenger (Jibreel), and your companion (Muhammad) is not possessed. The vision of the End is authenticated by the source of the message.
sections.title: The Oath and Testimony

sections.desc: Four ayahs bearing the weight of twenty-five. Fa-ayna tadh'habun — where are you going? A reminder for all creation, for whoever wills to walk straight — but you cannot will unless Allah wills. Human freedom and divine sovereignty held in two consecutive ayahs without collapsing either.
sections.title: The Challenge

sectionJourney.subtitle: Three movements: unraveling → testimony → challenge

deductiveFunnel.title: The Descent

layers.desc: The most visible, most reliable thing in creation — wrapped up and put away like a turban wound at the end of the day. Kuwwirat carries the image of winding cloth until what was visible is concealed.
layers.label: The Sun Folded

layers.desc: From the largest cosmic image to the smallest human victim. The universe is being dismantled, and Allah stops for one murdered child. The structural choice is the theology: injustice against the powerless is what the Day of Judgment was created to answer.
layers.label: The Girl Asked

layers.desc: After twelve images of destruction, one image of gentle life. Tanaffas — the dawn taking its first breath. The root n-f-s (breath, soul, self) transforms in context. Beauty survives even the unraveling.
layers.label: The Dawn Breathes

layers.desc: The entire surah compressed into a single question, carrying the weight of all twenty-five previous ayahs. From cosmos to conscience, from the sun to the soul — now the question is personal. Where are you headed, now that you know what is real?
layers.label: Where Are You Going?

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: From the sun to the soul — the surah's journey inward

content_nodes.concept: The maw'uda — the buried girl's courtroom
Wa al-subhi idha tanaffas — the dawn breathing
Abasa–Takwir diptych — moral blindness and cosmic unraveling
The cosmic oath surahs (81, 82, 84) — architecture of accountability

why_this_surah: When the sun is wrapped up, when the stars fall, when the mountains move, when the pregnant camels are abandoned — the surah stacks image after image of the world ending, then stops and asks: so where are you going? Twelve cosmic events, then one personal question. A surah that makes the Day of Judgment feel like it's already happening.

name: Ar-Ra'd
thesis: A forty-three-ayah argument that the physical world is already saying everything God needs said — thunder doing tasbih, soil preaching, foam vanishing — and the only question left is whether you have the kind of heart that can hear it.

heart_verse.why: Embedded not in a devotional passage but inside the surah's ethical portrait — between people who keep covenants and people who break them. The rest it names is not emotional comfort; it is the settledness of ground after rain. The heart that remembers is like soil that holds water.
heart_verse.arabic: أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ
heart_verse.translation: Truly, in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest.

full_text.arabic: المر ۚ تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ ۗ وَالَّذِي أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ الْحَقُّ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
full_text.translation: Alif Lam Mim Ra. These are the signs of the Book. And what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, but most people do not believe.

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا ۖ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ ۖ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ ۖ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي لِأَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ۚ يُدَبِّرُ الْأَمْرَ يُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُم بِلِقَاءِ رَبِّكُمْ تُوقِنُونَ
full_text.translation: It is Allah who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see, then established Himself above the Throne. He subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. He arranges all affairs and details the signs so that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord.

full_text.arabic: وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ وَأَنْهَارًا ۖ وَمِن كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ جَعَلَ فِيهَا زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ ۖ يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
full_text.translation: And it is He who spread out the earth and placed therein firm mountains and rivers, and from every fruit He made pairs. He covers the night with the day. Indeed, in that are signs for people who reflect.

full_text.arabic: وَفِي الْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُّتَجَاوِرَاتٌ وَجَنَّاتٌ مِّنْ أَعْنَابٍ وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوَانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوَانٍ يُسْقَىٰ بِمَاءٍ وَاحِدٍ وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَهَا عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فِي الْأُكُلِ ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ
full_text.translation: And in the earth are neighboring tracts, and gardens of grapevines and crops and palms, clustered and separate, watered with the same water; yet We make some of them exceed others in fruit. Indeed, in that are signs for people who reason.

full_text.arabic: وَإِن تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ أَإِذَا كُنَّا تُرَابًا أَإِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ ۗ أُولَـٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ ۖ وَأُولَـٰئِكَ الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ ۖ وَأُولَـٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ
full_text.translation: And if you wonder — then wondrous is their saying: 'When we are dust, will we be in a new creation?' Those are the ones who have disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles upon their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.

full_text.arabic: وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِمُ الْمَثُلَاتُ ۗ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِّلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ ظُلْمِهِمْ ۖ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَشَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ
full_text.translation: They ask you to hasten the punishment rather than the good, though examples of punishment have already passed before them. And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in punishment.

full_text.arabic: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلَا أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ ۗ إِنَّمَا أَنتَ مُنذِرٌ ۖ وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هَادٍ
full_text.translation: And those who disbelieve say: 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' You are only a warner, and for every people is a guide.

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنثَىٰ وَمَا تَغِيضُ الْأَرْحَامُ وَمَا تَزْدَادُ ۖ وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِندَهُ بِمِقْدَارٍ
full_text.translation: Allah knows what every female carries, and what the wombs lose and what they gain. And everything with Him is by due measure.

full_text.arabic: عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ الْكَبِيرُ الْمُتَعَالِ
full_text.translation: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Exalted.

full_text.arabic: سَوَاءٌ مِّنكُم مَّنْ أَسَرَّ الْقَوْلَ وَمَن جَهَرَ بِهِ وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍ بِاللَّيْلِ وَسَارِبٌ بِالنَّهَارِ
full_text.translation: It is the same whether any of you conceals his speech or declares it, or hides by night or goes forth by day.

full_text.arabic: لَهُ مُعَقِّبَاتٌ مِّن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُغَيِّرُ مَا بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمْ ۗ وَإِذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ سُوءًا فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُ ۚ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن دُونِهِ مِن وَالٍ
full_text.translation: For each one there are successive angels before and behind him who guard him by Allah's command. Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when Allah intends for a people ill, there is no repelling it. And there is not for them besides Him any protector.

full_text.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا وَيُنشِئُ السَّحَابَ الثِّقَالَ
full_text.translation: It is He who shows you lightning, causing fear and aspiration, and He produces the heavy clouds.

full_text.arabic: وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ مِنْ خِيفَتِهِ وَيُرْسِلُ الصَّوَاعِقَ فَيُصِيبُ بِهَا مَن يَشَاءُ وَهُمْ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي اللَّهِ وَهُوَ شَدِيدُ الْمِحَالِ
full_text.translation: The thunder glorifies His praise, and the angels out of awe of Him. And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes therewith whom He wills while they dispute about Allah — and He is severe in assault.

full_text.arabic: لَهُ دَعْوَةُ الْحَقِّ ۖ وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ لَا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُم بِشَيْءٍ إِلَّا كَبَاسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى الْمَاءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فَاهُ وَمَا هُوَ بِبَالِغِهِ ۚ وَمَا دُعَاءُ الْكَافِرِينَ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَالٍ
full_text.translation: To Him alone is the true call. And those they call upon besides Him do not respond to them at all — except as one who stretches his hands toward water so that it might reach his mouth, but it will never reach him. And the supplication of the disbelievers is nothing but error.

full_text.arabic: وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَن فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا وَظِلَالُهُم بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ ۩
full_text.translation: And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows in the mornings and afternoons.

full_text.arabic: قُلْ مَن رَّبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ ۚ قُلْ أَفَاتَّخَذْتُم مِّن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمْ نَفْعًا وَلَا ضَرًّا ۚ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَىٰ وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُمَاتُ وَالنُّورُ ۗ أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشَابَهَ الْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ قُلِ اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ
full_text.translation: Say: 'Who is Lord of the heavens and the earth?' Say: 'Allah.' Say: 'Have you then taken besides Him allies who do not possess for themselves any benefit or harm?' Say: 'Is the blind equal to the seeing? Or is darkness equal to light? Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created like His creation so that the creation seemed similar to them?' Say: 'Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing.'

full_text.arabic: أَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَسَالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِهَا فَاحْتَمَلَ السَّيْلُ زَبَدًا رَّابِيًا ۚ وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي النَّارِ ابْتِغَاءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتَاعٍ زَبَدٌ مِّثْلُهُ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْحَقَّ وَالْبَاطِلَ ۚ فَأَمَّا الزَّبَدُ فَيَذْهَبُ جُفَاءً ۖ وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ النَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ الْأَمْثَالَ
full_text.translation: He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their capacity. The torrent carries rising foam. And from what they heat in the fire to make ornaments or tools is foam like it. Thus does Allah set forth truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes as refuse; but as for what benefits people, it remains in the earth. Thus does Allah set forth parables.

full_text.arabic: لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجَابُوا لِرَبِّهِمُ الْحُسْنَىٰ ۚ وَالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَهُ لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُم مَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لَافْتَدَوْا بِهِ ۚ أُولَـٰئِكَ لَهُمْ سُوءُ الْحِسَابِ وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ ۖ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ
full_text.translation: For those who answered their Lord is the best reward. But those who did not respond to Him — if they had all that is on the earth and the like of it with it, they would offer it as ransom. Those will have the worst account, and their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.

full_text.arabic: أَفَمَن يَعْلَمُ أَنَّمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ الْحَقُّ كَمَنْ هُوَ أَعْمَىٰ ۚ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ
full_text.translation: Then is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? Only those of understanding will be mindful.

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَنقُضُونَ الْمِيثَاقَ
full_text.translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the pledge.

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ وَيَخَافُونَ سُوءَ الْحِسَابِ
full_text.translation: And those who join what Allah has ordered to be joined, and fear their Lord, and are afraid of the evil of the account.

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِمْ وَأَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَأَنفَقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً وَيَدْرَءُونَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ أُولَـٰئِكَ لَهُمْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ
full_text.translation: And those who are patient, seeking the face of their Lord, and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them secretly and publicly, and repel evil with good — those will have the final home.

full_text.arabic: جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا وَمَن صَلَحَ مِنْ آبَائِهِمْ وَأَزْوَاجِهِمْ وَذُرِّيَّاتِهِمْ ۖ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِم مِّن كُلِّ بَابٍ
full_text.translation: Gardens of perpetual residence — they will enter them with whoever was righteous among their fathers, spouses, and descendants. And the angels will enter upon them from every gate.

full_text.arabic: سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُم بِمَا صَبَرْتُمْ ۚ فَنِعْمَ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ
full_text.translation: 'Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured.' How excellent is the final home!

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ مِيثَاقِهِ وَيَقْطَعُونَ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ ۙ أُولَـٰئِكَ لَهُمُ اللَّعْنَةُ وَلَهُمْ سُوءُ الدَّارِ
full_text.translation: And those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation, and sever what Allah has ordered to be joined, and spread corruption on earth — for them is the curse, and they will have the worst home.

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ ۚ وَفَرِحُوا بِالْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ إِلَّا مَتَاعٌ
full_text.translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it. And they rejoice in the worldly life, while the worldly life is not, compared to the Hereafter, except brief enjoyment.

full_text.arabic: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلَا أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ ۗ قُلْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ أَنَابَ
full_text.translation: And those who disbelieve say: 'Why is a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?' Say: 'Indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back to Him.'

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُم بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ ۗ أَلَا بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ
full_text.translation: Those who believe, and whose hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah — truly, in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest.

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ طُوبَىٰ لَهُمْ وَحُسْنُ مَآبٍ
full_text.translation: Those who believe and do good works — joy is theirs and a beautiful return.

full_text.arabic: كَذَٰلِكَ أَرْسَلْنَاكَ فِي أُمَّةٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهَا أُمَمٌ لِّتَتْلُوَ عَلَيْهِمُ الَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ وَهُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ بِالرَّحْمَـٰنِ ۚ قُلْ هُوَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۖ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ مَتَابِ
full_text.translation: Thus have We sent you to a community before which communities have passed, that you might recite to them what We revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Merciful. Say: 'He is my Lord; there is no god except Him. Upon Him I rely, and to Him is my return.'

full_text.arabic: وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآنًا سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبَالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ الْأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ الْمَوْتَىٰ ۗ بَل لِّلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ جَمِيعًا ۗ أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَن لَّوْ يَشَاءُ اللَّهُ لَهَدَى النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا
full_text.translation: And if there were a Quran by which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be broken apart, or the dead could be spoken to... Rather, the command belongs entirely to Allah. Have the believers not yet realized that if Allah had willed, He could have guided all of humanity?

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ فَأَمْلَيْتُ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُهُمْ ۖ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عِقَابِ
full_text.translation: And messengers before you were mocked, but I gave respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them. And how was My punishment?

full_text.arabic: أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَائِمٌ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ ۗ وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ ۚ أَمْ تُنَبِّئُونَهُ بِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَم بِظَاهِرٍ مِّنَ الْقَوْلِ
full_text.translation: Is He who stands over every soul for what it has earned [not sufficient]? Yet they attribute partners to Allah. Say: 'Name them. Or do you inform Him of something He does not know upon the earth, or is it by apparent speech only?'
