Unlike Thamud or 'Ad, who receive warnings and deadlines, Saba simply turned away and were torn apart. The absence of a prophetic warning in their story makes the parable more terrifying: the signs were the warning, and ignoring signs has no appeal process.

absenceMap.subtitle: Every absence in Saba is a diagnosis — the surah is medicine for one specific disease

left.desc: Al-hamdu lillah — everything belongs to God, who knows what enters the earth and exits the sky. The Hour is certain.
left.label: Divine Knowledge

right.desc: The denial is proven wrong. Faith is reached for too late. A barrier is placed between them and what they desire.
right.label: The Hour Arrives

left.desc: Dawud and Sulayman — iron made soft, mountains singing, jinn laboring. Blessing channeled through worship.
left.label: Blessings: the Grateful

right.desc: False gods own nothing. Wealth is test, not proof. Every intermediary between creature and Creator is removed.
right.label: False Supports Exposed

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Saba — two gardens, good land, a forgiving Lord. They turned away. God sent the flood. He tore them to utter pieces.
center.note: Iblis confirmed his assumption about them. The Saba story is evidence in a trial that has been running since Adam.
center.label: The Ungrateful Nation

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah's opening praise and closing barrier form a precise inversion

sectionJourney.title: The Arithmetic of Blessing

sections.desc: Opens with total praise — al-hamdu lillah — and total divine knowledge, down to sub-atomic detail. Against that backdrop, the deniers say the Hour will never come. The argument is surgical: if God knows every atom, the idea He cannot reassemble a body is not reason but failure of imagination.
sections.title: The Praise & the Denial

sections.desc: Two dynasties blessed by God: Dawud and Sulayman, who channeled blessing through gratitude, and the people of Saba, who received gardens on their right and left and turned away. Same God, same generosity, opposite responses, opposite endings. The pivot: 'few of My servants are truly grateful.'
sections.title: The Parallel Dynasties

sections.desc: Every false support is stripped away. False gods own nothing, share nothing, help nothing. Intercession requires divine permission. Wealth is reframed as test, not proof. The social mechanism of denial is named: the wealthy mock the poor believers, using material status as theological evidence.
sections.title: The Confrontation

sections.desc: Every ally collapses. The single prescription: stand alone before God and reflect. The deniers on Judgment Day reach for faith — tanawush — but the distance has become unbridgeable. A barrier is placed between them and what they desire. Time has run out.
sections.title: The Final Question

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: sovereignty → dynasties → confrontation → reckoning

deductiveFunnel.title: The Distance

layers.desc: God knows every atom in heaven and earth. His knowledge is the premise: if He knows all things, He can do all things, and resurrection is a promise, not a problem.
layers.label: Limitless Knowledge

layers.desc: The command to Dawud's household: work in gratitude. Blessing does not arrive for enjoyment — it arrives to be channeled back into worship. And few of His servants are truly grateful.
layers.label: Gratitude

layers.desc: They turned away. Two words. No catalog of sins, no explanation. The gardens become thorns. The people become a proverb. Mazzaqnahum kulla mumazzaq — torn to utter pieces.
layers.label: The Squandered Garden

layers.desc: The hand reaching for faith from too far away. The desire is sincere. The barrier is absolute. The surah that opened with limitless provision closes with a limitation no power can overcome.
layers.label: The Unreachable

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: Each stage measures the gap that ingratitude creates

content_nodes.concept: Mazzaqnahum — the tearing that became a proverb
Tanawush — reaching for faith too late
Saba-Fatir diptych — paired openings of praise
Sulayman's death and the jinn — appearances masking reality

why_this_surah: The story of Saba' — an entire civilization that had everything (gardens, security, easy travel) and lost it all because they stopped being grateful. If you've ever taken a good thing for granted and only realized its value after it was gone, this surah is a warning about how blessings disappear when gratitude does.

name: Al-Mu'minun
thesis: A surah that tells you the verdict first — the believers have already succeeded — then spends 118 ayahs building the case until the only honest response left is the prayer it places on your lips at the end.

heart_verse.why: The phrase khalqan akhar marks a moment of genuine ontological wonder. What emerges from the embryonic stages is not just a more developed version of what came before — it is something new. The exclamation fa-tabaraka Allah is placed at the point where evidence tips into awe.
heart_verse.arabic: ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ ۚ فَتَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ
heart_verse.translation: Then We produced it as another creation entirely. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.

full_text.arabic: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ
full_text.translation: The believers have already succeeded —

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي صَلَاتِهِمْ خَاشِعُونَ
full_text.translation: those who are humble in their prayer,

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ عَنِ اللَّغْوِ مُعْرِضُونَ
full_text.translation: and those who turn away from idle speech,

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ لِلزَّكَاةِ فَاعِلُونَ
full_text.translation: and those who give the purifying alms,

full_text.arabic: أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْوَارِثُونَ
full_text.translation: Those are the inheritors —

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ يَرِثُونَ الْفِرْدَوْسَ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ
full_text.translation: who will inherit al-Firdaus. They will abide therein eternally.

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنسَانَ مِن سُلَالَةٍ مِّن طِينٍ
full_text.translation: And We created the human being from an extract of clay.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَاهُ خَلْقًا آخَرَ ۚ فَتَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ
full_text.translation: Then We produced it as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.

full_text.arabic: فَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ زُبُرًا ۖ كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ
full_text.translation: But they tore their affair into pieces among themselves, each faction rejoicing in what it had.

full_text.arabic: قُلْ لِّمَنِ الْأَرْضُ وَمَن فِيهَا إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: Say: To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?

full_text.arabic: سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ ۚ قُلْ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
full_text.translation: They will say: 'To Allah.' Say: 'Then will you not remember?'

full_text.arabic: قُلْ مَن بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ يُجِيرُ وَلَا يُجَارُ عَلَيْهِ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: Say: In whose hand is the realm of all things — and He protects while none can protect against Him — if you should know?

full_text.arabic: سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ ۚ قُلْ فَأَنَّىٰ تُسْحَرُونَ
full_text.translation: They will say: 'Allah's.' Say: 'Then how are you deluded?'

full_text.arabic: حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَاءَ أَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ارْجِعُونِ
full_text.translation: Until, when death comes to one of them, he says: 'My Lord, send me back.'

full_text.arabic: فَمَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ
full_text.translation: Those whose scales are heavy — it is they who are the successful.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.

full_text.arabic: وَقُل رَّبِّ اغْفِرْ وَارْحَمْ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الرَّاحِمِينَ
full_text.translation: And say: My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: For a surah of this length, that absence is a design choice. Al-Mu'minun is a surah of demonstration, not instruction. It builds a case rather than issues directives.
Prophets appear in compressed, skeletal strokes — each carrying the same structural beat: messenger arrives, people reject, consequence falls. The pattern is the point, not the drama.
The surah opens by declaring them successful and immediately moves to evidence. Once you see creation, history, and consequence clearly, you will not need to be comforted. You will need only to act.

absences.item: No commands to the Prophet until the end
absences.note: The few imperatives — the qul commands in the triple question sequence — are instruments of cross-examination, not legislation. The surah's voice is prosecutorial, not pastoral.
After 118 ayahs of mounting evidence and unanswerable argument, the surah does not close with victory. It closes on its knees: Rabbi ighfir warham — My Lord, forgive and have mercy.

absenceMap.subtitle: The architecture implies that the case itself is the consolation

left.desc: Qad aflaha al-mu'minun — the believers have already succeeded. Perfect tense. Settled before the qualities are named.
left.label: Already Succeeded

right.desc: Innahu laa yuflih al-kafiroon — the disbelievers will not succeed. Same root f-l-h. Photographic negative.
right.label: Will Not Succeed

left.desc: Humility in prayer, turning from laghw, zakat, guarding private life, honoring trusts — framed by salah
left.label: Seven Qualities

right.desc: Those whose scales are heavy are the muflihun — the successful. Same root completing the circle.
right.label: Heavy Scales

left.desc: From embryo to sky to earth — the most intimate evidence expanding outward concentrically
left.label: Signs in Creation

right.desc: Who owns the earth? The heavens? All things? 'Allah.' Then how are you deluded?
right.label: Triple Question

chiasticRing.title: The Mirror

center.desc: They tore their affair into pieces — each faction rejoicing in what it had.
center.note: The message was always one. The division came from human hands. This is the hinge: everything before it presents the unified truth; everything after confronts the fragmented response.
center.label: The Fracture

chiasticRing.subtitle: Qad aflaha al-mu'minun opens the surah; laa yuflih al-kafirun closes it — same root, opposite verdicts

sectionJourney.title: The Case

sections.desc: Seven qualities of the believer, ascending from inner humility in prayer through avoiding what is vain, giving zakat, guarding private life, honoring trusts — then returning to prayer. The list opens and closes with salah. Everything between is what the container holds. The verdict: they are the inheritors of al-Firdaus.
sections.title: The Portrait

sections.desc: Signs in creation from the embryo outward — dust, fluid, clot, flesh, then khalqan akhar, another creation entirely. The lens pulls to sky, water, gardens, livestock, ships. Then a rapid procession of prophets: Nuh, Musa and Harun, 'Isa and his mother — each carrying the same structural beat: a messenger arrives, the people reject.
sections.title: The Evidence

sections.desc: The message was always one, but people tore it into factions, each rejoicing in what it had. Then the triple question sequence (84–89): three times the audience is asked who owns and governs everything, three times they answer 'Allah,' and three escalating follow-ups — will you not remember? will you not fear? how are you deluded? Correct knowledge coexisting with contradictory living.
sections.title: The Confrontation

sections.desc: The deathbed plea: 'My Lord, send me back.' The answer: kalla. Then the scales — muflihun, from the same root as the surah's opening aflaha. The mirror inversion: the disbelievers will not succeed. And the final word is not triumph but a prayer placed on the Prophet's lips: Rabbi ighfir warham.
sections.title: The Reckoning

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four arcs: portrait → evidence → confrontation → reckoning

deductiveFunnel.title: The Escalation

layers.desc: To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it? They answer: to Allah. The follow-up: then will you not remember? Tatadhakkarun — the gentlest challenge. A nudge.
layers.label: Ownership of the Earth

layers.desc: Who is Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Great Throne? They answer: Allah's. The follow-up: then will you not fear Him? Tattaqun — the challenge sharpens into warning.
layers.label: Lord of the Heavens

layers.desc: In whose hand is the realm of all things — He protects, none can protect against Him? They answer: Allah's. The follow-up: then how are you deluded? Tu'sahoon — passive voice. Not 'why do you delude yourselves' but 'how are you being deluded?' Forces beyond the individual.
layers.label: Realm of All Things

layers.desc: We have brought them the truth, and indeed they are liars. After three correct answers, the gap between their words and their lives is named as a lie. Evidence becomes indictment.
layers.label: The Verdict

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The triple question sequence — three correct answers, three deepening challenges

content_nodes.concept: Qad aflaha — the f-l-h root and what it means to succeed
Khalqan akhar — the moment something new emerges
The triple question sequence and passive-voice delusion
Khushi' in prayer — the root image of softened earth

why_this_surah: Opens with a description of the believers who succeed — and the list is surprisingly practical: they guard their prayers, avoid idle talk, pay their charity, and are faithful to their commitments. If you want a clear picture of what the Quran considers a successful life, this surah defines it in the first eleven ayahs.

name: Al-Ankabut
thesis: A sixty-nine-ayah meditation on what happens to faith when it meets resistance — walking through every prophet's furnace to arrive at a single promise: those who strive for Us, We will guide them to Our ways.

heart_verse.why: The surah's architectural capstone. The word jahadu returns from ayah 6, completing the most precise bookend in the Quran. The striving and the guidance are not sequential — they are simultaneous. The struggle is the guidance arriving.
heart_verse.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا ۚ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
heart_verse.translation: And those who strive for Us — We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with those who do good.

full_text.arabic: الم
full_text.translation: Alif, Lam, Mim.

full_text.arabic: أَحَسِبَ النَّاسُ أَن يُتْرَكُوا أَن يَقُولُوا آمَنَّا وَهُمْ لَا يُفْتَنُونَ
full_text.translation: Do people think they will be left alone because they say 'We believe' and not be tested?

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ ۖ فَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ الْكَاذِبِينَ
full_text.translation: We certainly tested those before them. And Allah will surely distinguish those who are truthful from those who are liars.

full_text.arabic: وَمَن جَاهَدَ فَإِنَّمَا يُجَاهِدُ لِنَفْسِهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعَالَمِينَ
full_text.translation: And whoever strives, strives only for his own soul. Indeed, Allah is free of need from all creation.

full_text.arabic: وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ حُسْنًا
full_text.translation: And We have enjoined upon humanity goodness toward parents.

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًا
full_text.translation: And We certainly sent Nuh to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّمَا اتَّخَذْتُم مِّن دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْثَانًا مَّوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا
full_text.translation: You have taken idols besides Allah only as a bond of affection between you in the life of this world.

full_text.arabic: مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ كَمَثَلِ الْعَنكَبُوتِ اتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتًا
full_text.translation: The example of those who take protectors other than Allah is like that of the spider who takes a home.

full_text.arabic: وَتِلْكَ الْأَمْثَالُ نَضْرِبُهَا لِلنَّاسِ ۖ وَمَا يَعْقِلُهَا إِلَّا الْعَالِمُونَ
full_text.translation: And these examples — We present them to the people, but none will understand them except those of knowledge.

full_text.arabic: اتْلُ مَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ
full_text.translation: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer.

full_text.arabic: وَلَا تُجَادِلُوا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ
full_text.translation: And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best.

full_text.arabic: يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَاعْبُدُونِ
full_text.translation: O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship Me alone.

full_text.arabic: كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ ۖ ثُمَّ إِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ
full_text.translation: Every soul will taste death. Then to Us will you be returned.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا هَـٰذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا لَهْوٌ وَلَعِبٌ
full_text.translation: And this worldly life is nothing but amusement and diversion.

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا فِينَا لَنَهْدِيَنَّهُمْ سُبُلَنَا ۚ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمَعَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
full_text.translation: And those who strive for Us — We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with those who do good.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: Ibrahim's story, told at length in other surahs, is stripped to its bones here. Lut loses nearly all his dramatic scenes. The surah does not want you absorbed in any single story — it wants you to see the pattern running beneath all of them.

No detailed ethical code, no legal instruction. The prescriptions offered are compressed to their essence: pray, recite, argue beautifully, emigrate. The community's need was not rules but psychological architecture.
The Quraysh are confronted but not named. The surah addresses a type, not a tribe — anyone who builds on the wrong foundation.
The surah does not promise ease. It promises that the testing is the point. Every consolation is earned through the prophetic gallery, never offered cheaply.

absences.item: No separation of striving from guidance
absences.note: Jahadu fina / la-nahdiyanna-hum — the struggle is the guidance arriving. The surah refuses to make them sequential. The person inside the test is already on the path.

absenceMap.subtitle: A surah that replaces detail with pattern — every absence serves the argument

left.desc: Faith will be tested; whoever strives, strives for himself. The obligation of striving framed as self-regarding.
left.label: Striving Declared

right.desc: Those who strive for Us will be guided. The same act reframed as relational — a covenant, not just an obligation.
right.label: Striving Fulfilled

left.desc: Parents who pressure against faith. The anguish of domestic opposition.
left.label: Trial of Family

right.desc: Leave if staying means compromising worship. The command to leave what the earlier passage asked you to endure.
right.label: Emigration from Family

left.desc: Every community was tested — the prophetic gallery shows the pattern across all of history.
left.label: Prophets Tested

right.desc: The prescriptive mirror — pray, recite, argue beautifully. The solution to the problem the gallery illustrated.
right.label: How to Endure

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: The image of false security that the entire surah orbits.
center.note: Everything before is evidence: tested prophets, destroyed nations. Everything after is response: how to live, what to recite, where to go. The spider names the error all the narratives illustrated without naming.
center.label: The Spider

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah's opening and closing form a chiastic arc centered on the spider

sectionJourney.title: The Furnace

sections.desc: Faith will be tested. The word yuftanun shares a root with fitna — the smelting of gold. Faith is not a declaration. It is a metallurgical process. The verb jahada appears for the first time — it will return in the final ayah.
sections.title: The Declaration

sections.desc: Before prophets and nations, the surah pauses at the doorstep. Parents who pressure against faith. The same root j-h-d appears — the parent strives against the child's striving. The test lives inside the family.
sections.title: The Trial at Home

sections.desc: The Quran's most compressed archive of prophetic history. Nuh, Ibrahim, Lut, Shu'ayb, 'Ad, Thamud, Qarun, Pharaoh — each story distilled to its crisis point. The word mawadda appears in Ibrahim's speech: the idols are social glue, not conviction.
sections.title: The Prophetic Gallery

sections.desc: The surah's namesake and structural hinge. The spider's web is engineered brilliantly but as a home it is the most vulnerable structure in nature. The pivot from narrative to epistemology: who can read the signs?
sections.title: The Spider

sections.desc: The tools for surviving the test: the Book, the prayer, the beautiful argument — billati hiya ahsan. The Quran itself is declared the sufficient sign. Three forms of evidence, each more immediate than the last.
sections.title: Prescription and Argument

sections.desc: The most direct emigration command: My earth is spacious, so worship Me alone. Framed by death — you will lose everything at death anyway. Whatever you gain through faith is permanent.
sections.title: The Open Earth

sections.desc: This worldly life is amusement and play. The ship in the storm strips pretension. And then the capstone: those who strive for Us, We will guide them. The jahada bookend is complete.
sections.title: The Seal

sectionJourney.subtitle: Seven movements: declaration → trial → gallery → spider → prescription → emigration → promise

deductiveFunnel.title: The Smelting

layers.desc: Do people think they will be left alone? The surah's first substantive word after Alif Lam Mim is ahasiba — did they suppose? Faith as naive assumption.
layers.label: The Question

layers.desc: Every prophet was tested. Nuh for 950 years, Ibrahim thrown into fire, Lut mocked, Shu'ayb denied. The pattern is universal — each nation thought it was different, each nation was the same.
layers.label: The Pattern

layers.desc: The spider's web — intricate, impressive, unable to shelter. The error named in a single metaphor: building entire systems of meaning on something that cannot bear the weight.
layers.label: The Image

layers.desc: From supposition to companionship. The distance between ahasiba and la-ma'a — between naive assumption and hard-won divine companionship — is the argument in miniature.
layers.label: The Promise

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: From the opening question through layers of evidence to the final promise

content_nodes.concept: The spider metaphor — false security named
Mawadda in Al-Ankabut vs. Ar-Rum — counterfeit and original
The jahada bookend — striving as self-regarding and relational
The Alif Lam Mim family — surahs about faith under pressure

why_this_surah: Opens with a direct question: 'Do people think they will be left alone because they say we believe, and not be tested?' If you've ever felt like your faith was being tested and wondered whether that was normal, this surah says yes — that's exactly how it works. Belief without testing is just a claim.

name: As-Sajdah
thesis: A thirty-ayah surah that begins at Allah's throne and ends at the dust of forgotten civilizations — and between those two poles traces the entire arc of existence, funneling everything cosmic toward a single person praying in the dark.

heart_verse.why: The surah's emotional and structural center. The entire cosmological argument — the throne, the six days, the clay, the spirit, the angel of death, the reckoning — funnels into a bedroom in the last third of the night. The verb tatajafa describes the body's refusal to stay comfortable. Something pulls it upward.
heart_verse.arabic: تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا
heart_verse.translation: Their sides forsake their beds; they call upon their Lord in fear and hope.

full_text.arabic: الم
full_text.translation: Alif, Lam, Mim.

full_text.arabic: تَنزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ مِن رَّبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
full_text.translation: The revelation of this Book, about which there is no doubt, is from the Lord of all worlds.

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ
full_text.translation: Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth and all between them in six days.

full_text.arabic: الَّذِي أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ ۖ وَبَدَأَ خَلْقَ الْإِنسَانِ مِن طِينٍ
full_text.translation: He who perfected everything He created, and began the creation of the human being from clay.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ سَوَّاهُ وَنَفَخَ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِهِ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصَارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ
full_text.translation: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him of His spirit, and made for you hearing and sight and hearts.

full_text.arabic: وَقَالُوا أَإِذَا ضَلَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَإِنَّا لَفِي خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ
full_text.translation: And they say: when we are lost in the earth, will we indeed be in a new creation?

full_text.arabic: قُلْ يَتَوَفَّاكُم مَّلَكُ الْمَوْتِ الَّذِي وُكِّلَ بِكُمْ
full_text.translation: Say: the angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take you.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّمَا يُؤْمِنُ بِآيَاتِنَا الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُوا بِهَا خَرُّوا سُجَّدًا
full_text.translation: Only those believe in Our signs who, when reminded of them, fall in prostration.

full_text.arabic: تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا
full_text.translation: Their sides forsake their beds; they call upon their Lord in fear and hope.

full_text.arabic: فَلَا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَّا أُخْفِيَ لَهُم مِّن قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ
full_text.translation: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of the coolness of eyes.

full_text.arabic: وَجَعَلْنَا مِنْهُمْ أَئِمَّةً يَهْدُونَ بِأَمْرِنَا لَمَّا صَبَرُوا وَكَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يُوقِنُونَ
full_text.translation: And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and certain of Our signs.

full_text.arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أَنَّا نَسُوقُ الْمَاءَ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الْجُرُزِ فَنُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعًا
full_text.translation: Have they not seen that We drive water to barren land and bring forth thereby crops?

full_text.arabic: فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ وَانتَظِرْ إِنَّهُم مُّنتَظِرُونَ
full_text.translation: So turn away from them and wait. Indeed, they are waiting.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: Musa appears in one ayah (23). No dramatic scene, no dialogue, no Pharaoh. Where Surah Hud gives you eleven prophets, As-Sajdah gives you the logic that makes all eleven unnecessary: look at the creation inside you and draw the conclusion yourself.

No commands about charity, prayer times, family law. The surah is making an ontological case — about what you are, where you came from, where you are going — and trusts that behavior follows from seeing clearly.

absences.item: No description of Paradise in the hidden reward
absences.note: No gardens, rivers, or thrones. Qurrat a'yun — the cooling of the eyes — is left undefined. The reward is hidden even from the text that announces it.
The ruins are mentioned (ayahs 26-27) but without names or cities. The surah has stripped warning to its most abstract form: you walk through their ruins. That is enough.

Both parties wait (ayah 30). The Prophet waits for Allah's promise. The Quraysh wait for him to fail. Same verb — intazar — opposite meaning. The surah closes on shared posture concealing absolute divergence.

absenceMap.subtitle: A surah that strips narrative to its skeleton — argument replaces story

left.desc: The Quran is from the Lord of all worlds. They say he fabricated it — the surah answers with creation.
left.label: The Book's Origin

right.desc: When will this victory come? Turn away and wait. The opening's certainty (la rayba) inhabits patience (intazir).
right.label: The Challenge & Waiting

left.desc: Heavens, earth, throne, the management of affairs ascending and descending.
left.label: Cosmic Creation

right.desc: Patient leaders, ruined nations, rain on dead land — creation's evidence in history and landscape.
right.label: Historical Signs

left.desc: Clay, water, spirit breathed in, hearing, sight, hearts. The internal Book of the human body.
left.label: Human Creation

right.desc: The external Book of revelation — mirroring the internal one. Both are gifts. Both can be ignored.
right.label: Musa's Book

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Those whose sides forsake their beds, calling on God in fear and hope. The hidden reward.
center.note: The sajdah is the structural center of a surah called 'The Prostration.' The prostration is the lowest physical point a body can reach — and in the surah's architecture, it is the point from which everything ascends.
center.label: The Night Worshippers

chiasticRing.subtitle: A concentric structure that makes its center unmistakable

sectionJourney.title: The Arc

sections.desc: The widest aperture: six days, the throne, the management of affairs. Then the collapse from cosmic to intimate — from heaven to a body made of clay, given water, proportioned, breathed into with God's own spirit. Hearing, sight, hearts. And the quiet indictment: little do you give thanks.
sections.title: Creation: Throne to Clay to Spirit

sections.desc: They say: when we are lost in the earth, will we really be made new? The angel of death answers. Then the devastating scene: the guilty hang their heads — now they are certain, in the one place where certainty can no longer help.
sections.title: Denial and Reckoning

sections.desc: The surah's center. Those whose sides forsake their beds — tatajafa, the body's refusal to stay comfortable. Between fear and hope they call. Their reward has been hidden — ukhfiya — secrecy matched with secrecy. Then the separation: believers and the corrupt are not equal.
sections.title: The Night Worshippers

sections.desc: Musa and the Torah in one ayah. Leaders forged by sabr and yaqin. Ruined nations. Rain on dead land — the proof of resurrection in your fields. The closing command: turn away and wait. Both parties wait, but what they wait for is not the same thing.
sections.title: Precedent and Waiting

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four rooms: creation → denial → prostration → precedent

deductiveFunnel.title: The Collapse

layers.desc: Six days of creation, establishment on the throne, the management of all affairs. The widest possible frame — everything starts at the scale of the cosmos.
layers.label: The Throne

layers.desc: Clay, then water, then spirit breathed in. The cosmos narrows to a single body. The phrase min ruhih — of His spirit — grounds human dignity.
layers.label: The Body

layers.desc: Now they see, now they hear — too late. The certainty they refused in life arrives where it cannot help. The guilty hang their heads.
layers.label: The Reckoning

layers.desc: Everything funnels here. The universe was made, a body was shaped, a spirit was breathed, and the proof that the spirit is real is this: it wakes you at 3 a.m.
layers.label: The Prayer Mat

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: From the widest cosmic aperture to the most intimate human act

content_nodes.concept: Min ruhih — the breathing of the spirit and human dignity
The sajdah-spirit mirror: angels prostrate to Adam, believers prostrate to God
Tatajafa — the body's refusal to stay comfortable
As-Sajdah and Al-Mulk — the Friday night pairing

why_this_surah: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite this surah every Friday at Fajr. It covers everything from the creation of the universe to the creation of the human being to the moment you stand before God. Short enough to read in one sitting, comprehensive enough to reshape how you think about why you exist.

name: Sad
thesis: A surah where every throne in creation — earthly, heavenly, and infernal — is shown to be borrowed, and the only figure who claimed otherwise is the one standing in exile.

heart_verse.why: Seven words in Arabic. The first recorded argument for the superiority of one created being over another based on origin material. The logic that looked at the raw ingredient and refused to see the finished work — the divine breath, the proportioning, the command to honor.
heart_verse.arabic: أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ ۖ خَلَقْتَنِي مِن نَّارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِن طِينٍ
heart_verse.translation: I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: For a surah deeply concerned with justice, there is no specific legislation. It teaches justice through parable — watching a king be corrected — rather than through prescription.

Mountains, rain, livestock, night and day — the nature passages that populate Makkan surahs are absent. Sad uses historical and cosmic evidence: the record of tested kings and the primordial scene that explains why tests exist.

absences.item: No explicit content of Dawud's sin
absences.note: The Quran deliberately leaves a gap between the parable and Dawud's recognition. The classical tradition fills it variously, but the text's silence is the design — what matters is the speed of his repentance.
Dawud does not defend himself. Sulayman does not hesitate. Ayyub does not question. Every servant's first instinct, when tested, is to turn back. No figure in the prophetic sequence argues with God.
Unlike the prophets, Iblis is offered no path back. His exile is permanent. The only creature in the surah who refuses servanthood is the only one for whom the door does not reopen.

absenceMap.subtitle: A surah of thrones and trials — with deliberate silences

left.desc: Pride and fracture. They say: hasten our share before the Day of Account — as a joke
left.label: The Quraysh Mock Judgment

right.desc: Dhikr to the worlds. You will know its truth — after a time. The delay has a terminus
right.label: The Surah's Final Word

left.desc: Two litigants (khasm) scale the wall. The king judges and is judged — falls in sajdah
left.label: Dawud's Earthly Court

right.desc: Leaders and followers in takhasum — the same root. The earthly court and the infernal court mirror each other
right.label: The Quarrel in the Fire

chiasticRing.title: The Ring of Courtrooms

center.desc: The primordial courtroom — Iblis tried, found guilty, sentenced to exile. The origin of every test that came before.
center.note: This scene does not add another story to the sequence. It reveals the source code of every story that preceded it. The delay Iblis was granted is the space in which every human life unfolds.
center.label: The Heavenly Assembly

chiasticRing.subtitle: Every level of the surah stages a trial — and the same root word (kh-s-m) connects them

sectionJourney.title: The Theatre of Thrones

sections.desc: An oath by the Quran of dhikr. The Quraysh's disease named in two words: 'izzah (pride hardened to fracture) and shiqaq (splitting from truth). A rapid roll-call of destroyed nations — Nuh, Ad, Fir'awn of the stakes, Thamud, Lut — each in a single breath. A wall of precedent. They mock the idea of judgment while the single blast approaches.
sections.title: The Diagnosis

sections.desc: Three prophets, each introduced as 'abd — servant. Dawud: given strength and kingdom, tested by litigants who mirror his own story, falls in sajdah mid-sentence. Sulayman: given beauty, chooses dhikr over horses, receives a kingdom without account. Ayyub: tested by suffering, healed by a spring, an oath resolved with soft grass. Each word 'abd builds the architecture of servanthood the surah will set against Iblis.
sections.title: The Tested Kings

sections.desc: Paradise stated briefly. The Fire staged as courtroom drama — leaders and followers cursing each other. The believers they mocked are conspicuously absent from the damned. The word takhasum (quarreling) echoes khasm (litigants) from Dawud's trial — the courtroom imagery binds the prophetic narrative to the afterlife.
sections.title: The Two Destinations

sections.desc: The heavenly assembly before creation. Allah announces Adam. The angels bow. Iblis refuses: 'I am better — fire over clay.' Exile, curse, respite. His vow to mislead all except the sincere (mukhlasin). The surah closes: it is dhikr to the worlds — and you will know its truth after a time.
sections.title: The Origin Story

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: confrontation → tested kings → cosmic courtroom → the Word

deductiveFunnel.title: The Architecture of 'Abd

layers.desc: Our servant Dawud. Introduced by his servanthood before his kingship. Strength and repentance as a single inseparable profile — dha al-ayd, innahu awwab.
layers.label: Dawud

layers.desc: What an excellent servant. Given the greatest earthly kingdom — and the title that matters is still 'abd. His excellence is measured not by what he possesses but by how he holds it.
layers.label: Sulayman

layers.desc: The same words — ni'ma al-'abd. Patience under affliction and gratitude under abundance are the same quality viewed from different angles. The word 'abd unites them.
layers.label: Ayyub

layers.desc: Your sincere servants — the only category beyond Iblis's reach. The word 'abd, built through three case studies, now names the only immunity the surah recognizes.
layers.label: The Sincere

layers.desc: Against the entire chain stands Iblis, who refused servanthood. His refusal to prostrate is, in structural terms, a refusal to occupy the position of 'abd. Fire that will not bow to clay.
layers.label: Iblis: The Refusal

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The surah's most important word — servant — traces a deliberate path through every narrative

content_nodes.concept: Iblis's argument: fire over clay (38:76)
Dawud's sajdah and the velocity of repentance
The handful of grass — Ayyub's oath (38:44)
Khalifah in Al-Baqarah and Sad — the same word, answered

why_this_surah: Dawud made a mistake and immediately fell into prostration and repented. Sulayman was given a kingdom and said 'forgive me.' This surah shows prophets who had power and wealth but never let it make them forget where it came from. If you've ever struggled with whether success and faith can coexist, the answer lives here.

name: Al-Qari'ah
thesis: Eleven ayahs descend from the cosmic to the personal: a name repeated three times, two images of dissolution (moths, wool), then the scales. Heavy scales — satisfaction. Light scales — hāwiya, the abyss, described only as 'a blazing fire.' The surah names the destination but spares no detail on the journey there.

heart_verse.why: The word umm means mother — the place of warmth, return, shelter. To say his mother is Hawiyah is to say the Fire becomes his home, his shelter, the thing that receives him the way a mother's lap receives a child. The inversion is devastating: the place of ultimate safety becomes the place of ultimate torment.
heart_verse.arabic: فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ
heart_verse.translation: His mother is the Abyss.

full_text.arabic: الْقَارِعَةُ
full_text.translation: The Striking Calamity —

full_text.arabic: مَا الْقَارِعَةُ
full_text.translation: What is the Striking Calamity?

full_text.arabic: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْقَارِعَةُ
full_text.translation: And what will make you realize what the Striking Calamity is?

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ
full_text.translation: The Day when people will be like moths scattered about,

full_text.arabic: وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنفُوشِ
full_text.translation: and the mountains will be like carded wool.

full_text.arabic: فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ
full_text.translation: As for the one whose scales are heavy —

full_text.arabic: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ
full_text.translation: they will be in a pleasant life.

full_text.arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ
full_text.translation: And as for the one whose scales are light —

full_text.arabic: فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ
full_text.translation: their mother is the Abyss.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا هِيَهْ
full_text.translation: And what will make you realize what it is?

full_text.arabic: نَارٌ حَامِيَةٌ
full_text.translation: A scorching fire.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: The Quraysh found bodily resurrection physically absurd. The surah offers no evidence, no reasoning. It simply shows you what it looks like — images so vivid they bypass the intellect and land in the body. The Quraysh were not given a theological argument. They were given a vision.

The surah never specifies what makes the scales heavy or light. No list of deeds, no commandments, no prohibited acts. In the economy of that Day, what actually weighs something? The question falls on you.
The closing asks 'what is the Abyss?' and answers with two words. Every other surah using the ma adraka formula expands its answer. This one contracts it. The fire is named and the surah ends.

absences.item: No believers, no prophets, no stories
absences.note: No 'O you who believe,' no Prophetic narrative, no destroyed nation. The surah exists purely as vision — spectacle, sorting, consequence — with no human characters except the anonymous weighed.

No moral instruction, no command to pray or give charity. The surah is pure diagnosis and pure consequence. At-Takathur, which follows immediately, names the distraction that kept you from asking the questions this surah raises.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah builds an entire eschatology in the time it takes to exhale — and leaves out everything else

left.desc: Al-Qari'ah repeated three times, expanding into the ma adraka question — reaching for comprehension that cannot arrive
left.label: The Event Named

right.desc: Ma adraka returns — but the answer contracts to two words: narun hamiyah. Expansion meets compression. The asymmetry is the argument.
right.label: The Fire Named

left.desc: People like scattered moths, mountains like carded wool — the animate and inanimate both lose their form
left.label: Creation Unmade

right.desc: Fa-ummuhu hawiyah — his mother is the plunge. The Fire that receives the way a mother receives.
right.label: The Abyss

chiasticRing.title: The Frame

center.desc: Heavy or light. Pleasant life or the Abyss. The moral reckoning sits at the architectural center of the surah.
center.note: The Event can be shown — moths, wool, scales, a pleasant life. The punishment cannot. It can only be named. The surah puts the weighing at its center and surrounds it with the sensory evidence of its consequences.
center.label: The Scales

chiasticRing.subtitle: Twin towers of incomprehension bracket the moral center

sectionJourney.title: The Three Strikes

sections.desc: The surah opens by hammering its own name three times — al-Qari'ah, al-Qari'ah, al-Qari'ah — each strike deeper than the last. The word qar'a means to strike, to pound, to knock. The percussive rhythm mimics what it describes. Then two images from domestic life: people become scattered moths — al-farash al-mabthuth — swarming, chaotic, drawn toward what they cannot understand. Mountains become carded wool — al-'ihn al-manfush — the hardest thing in the visible world becomes the softest. Not crushed, not blown, but pulled apart fiber by fiber.
sections.title: The Spectacle

sections.desc: The fa-amma...wa amma construction divides humanity into exactly two groups. No spectrum, no ambiguity. Heavy scales earn 'ishatin radiyah — a life of deep satisfaction, from the same root 's pleasure with His servants. Light scales earn something stranger: fa-ummuhu hawiyah — his mother is the Abyss. The place of ultimate safety becomes the place of ultimate torment. The Abyss is where he belongs now. It is home.
sections.title: The Sorting

sections.desc: The ma adraka formula returns — the second time in eleven ayahs. The first asked about the Striking Hour. This one asks about the Abyss. The answer is two words: narun hamiyah — a fire whose heat guards itself, that does not cool, that repels approach. Where the opening expanded through three repetitions, the closing contracts to a single image. The compression is absolute.
sections.title: The Naming

sectionJourney.subtitle: Three movements: spectacle → sorting → consequence

deductiveFunnel.title: The Compression

layers.desc: Three repetitions of the same word, expanding into a question. The surah knocks three times before it opens the door. The rhyme scheme — ah, ah, ah — hammers through the first five ayahs like a heartbeat accelerating. The surah does not explain the Day of Judgment. It recreates the sensation of it arriving.
layers.label: The Name

layers.desc: Two images chosen from domestic life — insects near a lamp, wool in a woman's hands — to describe the end of the world. The mundane becomes the vehicle for the cosmic. The end of the world described in the language of a household task. Not crushed, not blown, not leveled — carded. Pulled apart fiber by fiber.
layers.label: The Vision

layers.desc: The binary that reduces all of human moral life to mass on a scale. The mawazin — plural, suggesting either multiple scales for different categories of deeds or a single scale of such magnitude the plural conveys its weight. The surah does not tell you what makes the scales heavy. The question falls entirely on the listener.
layers.label: The Scales

layers.desc: Two words. Every other surah that uses the ma adraka formula expands its answer. This one contracts it. The fire is named and the surah ends. The closing is so compressed it feels like a door slamming.
layers.label: The Fire

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: From cosmic spectacle to two-word verdict — each layer tighter than the last

content_nodes.concept: Umm  — the mother-abyss inversion
Mountains as carded wool — the unmaking of permanence
Qari'ah-Takathur sequence — scales and what emptied them
Ma adraka — the Quran's formula for incomprehension

why_this_surah: The Striking Hour — the name itself is a question. What is it? The surah answers with images: people scattered like moths, mountains dissolved like wool. Then the scales. Your deeds are weighed. If they're heavy, you're at peace. If they're light — the surah ends with a pit of fire described only as 'and what will make you know what it is?'

name: Az-Zumar
thesis: A seventy-five-ayah argument that sincerity is the only worship that counts — and then, at its structural center, the widest door of mercy ever opened in the Quran, placed there so that the demand does not crush the one who hears it.

heart_verse.why: The most hopeful verse in the Quran, placed at the structural center of the surah that demands the most. The address is 'My servants' — even after transgression, the relationship is not severed. The scope is total: jami'an, all sins, every last one. The surah holds the highest demand and the widest mercy in the same hand.
heart_verse.arabic: قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا مِن رَّحْمَةِ اللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا
heart_verse.translation: Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.

full_text.arabic: تَنزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ
full_text.translation: The revelation of this Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the Wise.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ فَاعْبُدِ اللَّهَ مُخْلِصًا لَّهُ الدِّينَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, making the religion sincerely for Him.

full_text.arabic: أَلَا لِلَّهِ الدِّينُ الْخَالِصُ
full_text.translation: Is pure religion not for Allah alone?

full_text.arabic: لَّوْ أَرَادَ اللَّهُ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا لَّاصْطَفَىٰ مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ ۚ سُبْحَانَهُ
full_text.translation: If Allah had intended to take a son, He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He willed. Exalted is He.

full_text.arabic: خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ ۖ يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهَارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ النَّهَارَ عَلَى اللَّيْلِ
full_text.translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night.

full_text.arabic: خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا
full_text.translation: He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate.

full_text.arabic: إِن تَكْفُرُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنكُمْ
full_text.translation: If you disbelieve, indeed Allah is free from need of you.

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا مَسَّ الْإِنسَانَ ضُرٌّ دَعَا رَبَّهُ مُنِيبًا إِلَيْهِ
full_text.translation: And when adversity touches the human being, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him.

full_text.arabic: أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ سَاجِدًا وَقَائِمًا يَحْذَرُ الْآخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُو رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِ
full_text.translation: Is one who worships devoutly during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]?

full_text.arabic: قُلْ يَا عِبَادِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ
full_text.translation: Say: O My servants who believe, be mindful of your Lord.

full_text.arabic: قُلْ إِنِّي أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ مُخْلِصًا لَّهُ الدِّينَ
full_text.translation: Say: Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, making the religion sincerely for Him.

full_text.arabic: وَأُمِرْتُ لِأَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
full_text.translation: And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims.

full_text.arabic: قُلْ إِنِّي أَخَافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
full_text.translation: Say: Indeed, I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.

full_text.arabic: قُلِ اللَّهَ أَعْبُدُ مُخْلِصًا لَّهُ دِينِي
full_text.translation: Say: Allah I worship, making my religion sincerely for Him.

full_text.arabic: فَاعْبُدُوا مَا شِئْتُم مِّن دُونِهِ
full_text.translation: So worship what you will besides Him.

full_text.arabic: قُلْ إِنَّ الْخَاسِرِينَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
full_text.translation: Say: Indeed, the losers are those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.

full_text.arabic: لَهُم مِّن فَوْقِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ مِّنَ النَّارِ وَمِن تَحْتِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ
full_text.translation: They will have canopies of fire above them and below them, canopies.

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ يَسْتَمِعُونَ الْقَوْلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحْسَنَهُ
full_text.translation: Those who listen to speech and follow the best of it.

full_text.arabic: أَفَمَنْ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةُ الْعَذَابِ أَفَأَنتَ تُنقِذُ مَن فِي النَّارِ
full_text.translation: Is one upon whom the word of punishment has come due [to be rescued]? Can you save one who is in the Fire?

full_text.arabic: لَٰكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ لَهُمْ غُرَفٌ مِّن فَوْقِهَا غُرَفٌ مَّبْنِيَّةٌ
full_text.translation: But those who fear their Lord — for them are chambers, above them chambers built high.

full_text.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَسَلَكَهُ يَنَابِيعَ فِي الْأَرْضِ
full_text.translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky and guides it through springs in the earth?

full_text.arabic: أَفَمَن شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ
full_text.translation: So is one whose chest Allah has opened to Islam, and he is upon a light from his Lord [like one whose heart is hardened]?

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحْسَنَ الْحَدِيثِ كِتَابًا مُّتَشَابِهًا مَّثَانِيَ
full_text.translation: Allah has sent down the best of speech: a Book, consistent, oft-repeated.

full_text.arabic: أَفَمَن يَتَّقِي بِوَجْهِهِ سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
full_text.translation: Is one who shields with his face the worst of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one secure]?

full_text.arabic: كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ فَأَتَاهُمُ الْعَذَابُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
full_text.translation: Those before them denied, and punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.

full_text.arabic: فَأَذَاقَهُمُ اللَّهُ الْخِزْيَ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَلَعَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ
full_text.translation: So Allah made them taste disgrace in worldly life. But the punishment of the Hereafter is greater.

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ ضَرَبْنَا لِلنَّاسِ فِي هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنِ مِن كُلِّ مَثَلٍ لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
full_text.translation: And We have certainly presented in this Quran every kind of example, that they might remember.

full_text.arabic: قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ
full_text.translation: An Arabic Quran, without any crookedness, that they might be mindful.

full_text.arabic: ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَّجُلًا فِيهِ شُرَكَاءُ مُتَشَاكِسُونَ وَرَجُلًا سَلَمًا لِّرَجُلٍ
full_text.translation: Allah presents an example: a man owned by quarreling partners and a man belonging exclusively to one man — are they equal?

full_text.arabic: إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُم مَّيِّتُونَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, you are to die, and indeed, they are to die.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ تَخْتَصِمُونَ
full_text.translation: Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord you will dispute.

full_text.arabic: فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن كَذَبَ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَكَذَّبَ بِالصِّدْقِ إِذْ جَاءَهُ
full_text.translation: Who is more unjust than one who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him?

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِي جَاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ ۙ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُونَ
full_text.translation: And the one who has brought the truth and those who confirm it — those are the righteous.

full_text.arabic: لَهُم مَّا يَشَاءُونَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ جَزَاءُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
full_text.translation: They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.

full_text.arabic: لِيُكَفِّرَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ أَسْوَأَ الَّذِي عَمِلُوا وَيَجْزِيَهُمْ أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ الَّذِي كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ
full_text.translation: That Allah may remove from them the worst of what they did and reward them according to the best of what they used to do.

full_text.arabic: أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهُ
full_text.translation: Is Allah not sufficient for His servant?

full_text.arabic: وَمَن يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِن مُّضِلٍّ ۗ أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِعَزِيزٍ ذِي انتِقَامٍ
full_text.translation: And whoever Allah guides — for him there is no misleader. Is not Allah Almighty, Owner of retribution?

full_text.arabic: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ
full_text.translation: And if you asked them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they would surely say, 'Allah.'

full_text.arabic: قُلْ أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ إِنْ أَرَادَنِيَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ
full_text.translation: Say: Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended for me some harm...

full_text.arabic: قُلْ يَا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُمْ إِنِّي عَامِلٌ ۖ فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: Say: O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. You will know.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ لِلنَّاسِ بِالْحَقِّ
full_text.translation: Indeed, We sent down to you the Book for the people in truth.

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِهَا
full_text.translation: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died, during their sleep.

full_text.arabic: أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ شُفَعَاءَ
full_text.translation: Have they taken intercessors besides Allah?

full_text.arabic: قُل لِّلَّهِ الشَّفَاعَةُ جَمِيعًا
full_text.translation: Say: To Allah belongs all intercession entirely.

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ اشْمَأَزَّتْ قُلُوبُ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ
full_text.translation: When Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter recoil with aversion.

full_text.arabic: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ
full_text.translation: Say: O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.

full_text.arabic: وَلَوْ أَنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ
full_text.translation: And if those who did wrong had all that is on earth and its equivalent with it...

full_text.arabic: وَبَدَا لَهُم مِّنَ اللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يَكُونُوا يَحْتَسِبُونَ
full_text.translation: There will appear to them from Allah what they had not expected.

full_text.arabic: فَإِذَا مَسَّ الْإِنسَانَ ضُرٌّ دَعَانَا
full_text.translation: When adversity touches the human being, he calls upon Us.

full_text.arabic: قَدْ قَالَهَا الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ فَمَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ
full_text.translation: Those before them had already said it, but what they earned did not avail them.

full_text.arabic: فَأَصَابَهُمْ سَيِّئَاتُ مَا كَسَبُوا
full_text.translation: So the evil consequences of what they earned struck them.

full_text.arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ
full_text.translation: Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it?

full_text.arabic: قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا مِن رَّحْمَةِ اللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا
full_text.translation: Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.

full_text.arabic: وَأَنِيبُوا إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ وَأَسْلِمُوا لَهُ
full_text.translation: Turn back to your Lord and submit to Him.

full_text.arabic: وَاتَّبِعُوا أَحْسَنَ مَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ
full_text.translation: And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord.

full_text.arabic: أَن تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ يَا حَسْرَتَا عَلَىٰ مَا فَرَّطتُ فِي جَنبِ اللَّهِ
full_text.translation: Lest a soul should say, 'Oh, how great is my regret over what I neglected in regard to Allah.'

full_text.arabic: أَوْ تَقُولَ لَوْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ هَدَانِي لَكُنتُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ
full_text.translation: Or it should say, 'If only Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.'

full_text.arabic: أَوْ تَقُولَ حِينَ تَرَى الْعَذَابَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِي كَرَّةً فَأَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ
full_text.translation: Or it should say when it sees the punishment, 'If only I had another chance, I would be among the doers of good.'

full_text.arabic: بَلَىٰ قَدْ جَاءَتْكَ آيَاتِي فَكَذَّبْتَ بِهَا وَاسْتَكْبَرْتَ
full_text.translation: But yes, My verses had come to you, and you denied them and were arrogant.

full_text.arabic: وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ تَرَى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهُم مُّسْوَدَّةٌ
full_text.translation: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah, their faces darkened.

full_text.arabic: وَيُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفَازَتِهِمْ
full_text.translation: And Allah will save those who feared Him by their attainment.

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ ۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ
full_text.translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is, over all things, Disposer of affairs.

full_text.arabic: لَّهُ مَقَالِيدُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ
full_text.translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth.

full_text.arabic: قُلْ أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَأْمُرُونِّي أَعْبُدُ أَيُّهَا الْجَاهِلُونَ
full_text.translation: Say: Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكَ لَئِنْ أَشْرَكْتَ لَيَحْبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ
full_text.translation: And it was revealed to you and to those before you: If you associate others with Allah, your deeds would surely become worthless.

full_text.arabic: بَلِ اللَّهَ فَاعْبُدْ وَكُن مِّنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ
full_text.translation: Rather, worship Allah and be among the grateful.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ وَالْأَرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ
full_text.translation: They have not appraised Allah with true appraisal. The entire earth will be within His grip on the Day of Resurrection.

full_text.arabic: وَنُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَن فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا مَن شَاءَ اللَّهُ
full_text.translation: The trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills.

full_text.arabic: وَأَشْرَقَتِ الْأَرْضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّهَا وَوُضِعَ الْكِتَابُ
full_text.translation: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record will be placed.

full_text.arabic: وَوُفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّا عَمِلَتْ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَفْعَلُونَ
full_text.translation: And every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.

full_text.arabic: وَسِيقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ زُمَرًا
full_text.translation: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups.

full_text.arabic: قِيلَ ادْخُلُوا أَبْوَابَ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا ۖ فَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ
full_text.translation: It will be said: Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein. Wretched is the residence of the arrogant.

full_text.arabic: وَسِيقَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ زُمَرًا
full_text.translation: And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups.

full_text.arabic: وَقَالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي صَدَقَنَا وَعْدَهُ وَأَوْرَثَنَا الْأَرْضَ
full_text.translation: And they will say: Praise to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has made us inherit the earth.

full_text.arabic: وَتَرَى الْمَلَائِكَةَ حَافِّينَ مِنْ حَوْلِ الْعَرْشِ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ ۚ وَقِيلَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
full_text.translation: And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, exalting with praise of their Lord. And it will be said: Praise to Allah, Lord of all worlds.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No destroyed nations, no Pharaoh, no 'Ad, no Thamud. In a late Makkan surah where historical destruction is most common, their absence is deliberate. Az-Zumar replaces external warning with an internal one: the soul's own encounter with its sincerity.
Prophets are mentioned only in passing, as recipients of revelation (39:65), never as narrative figures. The surah keeps its gaze fixed on the listener's interior.
The surah's rewards are relational — chambers above chambers, the angels' greeting, the phrase 'you have been good.' The pleasures are about relationship, not consumption.
Ayah 44 forecloses every exit: 'To Allah belongs all intercession entirely.' No one mediates without His permission, and the permission itself belongs to Him. The surah demands direct encounter.

The surah does not dilute its call for sincerity in order to offer mercy. It holds both at full strength — the demand and the door — and insists that this is the only ground on which real worship is possible.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah replaces external warning with internal encounter — every absence is a design choice

left.desc: The command to worship Allah with sincerity — is pure religion not for Allah alone?
left.label: The Demand

right.desc: Two groups driven in processions — those who gave sincerity and those who withheld it — and the final praise
right.label: The Fulfillment

left.desc: The man owned by quarreling partners versus the man belonging to one — the parable of tawhid
left.label: Divided Worship

right.desc: The two zumar: one driven to Hell, one to Paradise — the word appears only here in the entire Quran
right.label: Divided Fates

left.desc: Calls on Allah in hardship, forgets Him in ease — the psychology of inconsistency
left.label: Insincere Heart

right.desc: Three forms of regret catalogued: negligence, wishing for guidance, wishing for another chance
right.label: Too-Late Regret

chiasticRing.title: The Ring of Sincerity

center.desc: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins.
center.note: The structural center of a surah about sincerity is mercy. The demand is real. The mercy is equally real. And between them, the human being finds the only ground on which sincere worship becomes possible.
center.label: The Widest Door

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah's opening demand and closing fulfillment mirror each other around the mercy verse at the center

sectionJourney.title: The Architecture of Sincerity

sections.desc: The surah opens with its non-negotiable demand: sincerity in worship, pure devotion to Allah alone. The phrase mukhlisan lahu al-din appears here for the first time and echoes through the surah like a refrain. The nighttime worshipper — alone, unseen — is the icon of ikhlas.
sections.title: The Declaration

sections.desc: Addressing the believers directly for the first time: patience, spacious earth, and a lifecycle parable — rain to spring to growth to yellowing to debris. Everything you worship besides Allah has this trajectory.
sections.title: The Counsel

sections.desc: The longest movement: the chest opened to Islam, the man owned by quarreling masters versus the man devoted to one, the soul taken in sleep, the heart that recoils when Allah alone is mentioned. Every parable approaches the same truth from a different angle.
sections.title: The Sustained Argument

sections.desc: The mercy verse opens the widest door — then urgency, three forms of too-late regret, the trumpet blast, the earth shining with the light of its Lord, and two processions driven in groups toward two destinations. The final word: al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-'alamin.
sections.title: The Mercy and the Finale

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: demand, counsel, argument, finale

deductiveFunnel.title: The Diagnostic

layers.desc: The surface symptom: calling on Allah in hardship, forgetting Him in ease. Sincerity is what remains when comfort returns.
layers.label: Inconsistency
layers.arabic: وَإِذَا مَسَّ الْإِنسَانَ ضُرٌّ دَعَا رَبَّهُ

layers.desc: The involuntary contraction of the heart when Allah is mentioned alone. The rare verb ishma'azzat describes a physical, visceral shrinking. The test of sincerity is not what you profess but what your heart does.
layers.label: Recoil

layers.desc: The deepest layer: not mere forgetfulness but active self-attribution. 'I was given this because of my knowledge.' The insincere heart takes credit for what Allah gave.
layers.label: Self-Attribution

layers.desc: The root cause of all insincerity: they never measured Allah with His true measure. They never understood how vast He is.
layers.label: Misappraisal

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: Each layer peels back the psychology of insincerity until the root is exposed

content_nodes.concept: The mercy verse — structural center and widest door
The two zumar — processions toward two destinations
Quarreling masters — tawhid as a single image
The soul taken in sleep — consciousness as borrowed gift

why_this_surah: Contains one of the most hopeful verses in the entire Quran: 'Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves — do not despair of the mercy of God. God forgives all sins.' If you've ever felt too far gone, too sinful, too broken to come back — this surah was revealed for you.

name: Al-Fath
thesis: A surah that holds a grieving community in its hands, turns their face toward what they cannot see, and says: the seed is already in the ground — trust the ground.

heart_verse.why: The surah's center of gravity. Allah's pleasure is stated in the past tense — accomplished, definitive, rooted in a specific moment at a specific place. In the very moment they felt most defeated, Allah was most pleased with them. The entire surah pivots on this declaration.
heart_verse.arabic: لَّقَدْ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ
heart_verse.translation: Allah was certainly pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you beneath the tree.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُّبِينًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, We have given you a clear victory —

full_text.arabic: لِّيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللَّهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ مِن ذَنبِكَ وَمَا تَأَخَّرَ وَيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكَ وَيَهْدِيَكَ صِرَاطًا مُّسْتَقِيمًا
full_text.translation: that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will follow, complete His favor upon you, and guide you to a straight path,

full_text.arabic: وَيَنصُرَكَ اللَّهُ نَصْرًا عَزِيزًا
full_text.translation: and that Allah may aid you with a mighty victory.

full_text.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي أَنزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لِيَزْدَادُوا إِيمَانًا مَّعَ إِيمَانِهِمْ ۗ وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا
full_text.translation: He is the One who sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers so that they would increase in faith along with their existing faith. And to Allah belong the armies of the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.

full_text.arabic: لِّيُدْخِلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَيُكَفِّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ
full_text.translation: That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow to abide therein eternally and remove from them their misdeeds —

full_text.arabic: وَيُعَذِّبَ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْمُنَافِقَاتِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَالْمُشْرِكَاتِ الظَّانِّينَ بِاللَّهِ ظَنَّ السَّوْءِ
full_text.translation: and punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and polytheist women — those who assume about Allah an assumption of evil.

full_text.arabic: وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا
full_text.translation: And to Allah belong the armies of the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Almighty and Wise.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ شَاهِدًا وَمُبَشِّرًا وَنَذِيرًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner —

full_text.arabic: لِّتُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وَتُوَقِّرُوهُ وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا
full_text.translation: that you may believe in Allah and His Messenger and honor him and respect him and exalt Him morning and afternoon.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُبَايِعُونَكَ إِنَّمَا يُبَايِعُونَ اللَّهَ يَدُ اللَّهِ فَوْقَ أَيْدِيهِمْ
full_text.translation: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you — they are pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands.

full_text.arabic: سَيَقُولُ لَكَ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ شَغَلَتْنَا أَمْوَالُنَا وَأَهْلُونَا فَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَنَا
full_text.translation: Those who stayed behind of the Bedouin will say to you, 'Our possessions and our families preoccupied us, so ask forgiveness for us.'

full_text.arabic: بَلْ ظَنَنتُمْ أَن لَّن يَنقَلِبَ الرَّسُولُ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِيهِمْ أَبَدًا وَزُيِّنَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَظَنَنتُمْ ظَنَّ السَّوْءِ وَكُنتُمْ قَوْمًا بُورًا
full_text.translation: But you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, and that was made attractive in your hearts. And you assumed an assumption of evil, and you were a people ruined.

full_text.arabic: وَمَن لَّمْ يُؤْمِن بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ فَإِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ سَعِيرًا
full_text.translation: And whoever has not believed in Allah and His Messenger — indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a blaze.

full_text.arabic: وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ يَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَاءُ ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَّحِيمًا
full_text.translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

full_text.arabic: سَيَقُولُ الْمُخَلَّفُونَ إِذَا انطَلَقْتُمْ إِلَىٰ مَغَانِمَ لِتَأْخُذُوهَا ذَرُونَا نَتَّبِعْكُمْ
full_text.translation: Those who stayed behind will say, when you set out toward spoils to take them, 'Let us follow you.'

full_text.arabic: قُل لِّلْمُخَلَّفِينَ مِنَ الْأَعْرَابِ سَتُدْعَوْنَ إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ أُولِي بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ تُقَاتِلُونَهُمْ أَوْ يُسْلِمُونَ
full_text.translation: Say to those who stayed behind of the Bedouin, 'You will be called to a people of great military might; you will fight them, or they will submit.'

full_text.arabic: لَّيْسَ عَلَى الْأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَى الْأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَى الْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ
full_text.translation: There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick.

full_text.arabic: لَّقَدْ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ الشَّجَرَةِ فَعَلِمَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأَنزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَثَابَهُمْ فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا
full_text.translation: Allah was certainly pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you beneath the tree. He knew what was in their hearts, and He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a near victory.

full_text.arabic: وَمَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةً يَأْخُذُونَهَا ۗ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَزِيزًا حَكِيمًا
full_text.translation: And much spoils which they will take. And ever is Allah Almighty and Wise.

full_text.arabic: وَعَدَكُمُ اللَّهُ مَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةً تَأْخُذُونَهَا فَعَجَّلَ لَكُمْ هَٰذِهِ وَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَ النَّاسِ عَنكُمْ
full_text.translation: Allah has promised you much spoils that you will take and has hastened for you this and withheld the hands of people from you —

full_text.arabic: وَأُخْرَىٰ لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهَا قَدْ أَحَاطَ اللَّهُ بِهَا ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرًا
full_text.translation: And other gains are reserved for you that you have not yet attained; Allah has already encompassed them. And ever is Allah over all things competent.

full_text.arabic: وَلَوْ قَاتَلَكُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوَلَّوُا الْأَدْبَارَ ثُمَّ لَا يَجِدُونَ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا
full_text.translation: And if those who disbelieve had fought you, they would have turned their backs; then they would not find a protector or a helper.

full_text.arabic: سُنَّةَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلُ ۖ وَلَن تَجِدَ لِسُنَّةِ اللَّهِ تَبْدِيلًا
full_text.translation: This is the established way of Allah which has occurred before. And never will you find in the way of Allah any change.

full_text.arabic: وَهُوَ الَّذِي كَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُم بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ مِن بَعْدِ أَنْ أَظْفَرَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ
full_text.translation: And He is the One who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca, after He gave you the upper hand over them.

full_text.arabic: هُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَالْهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفًا أَن يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ
full_text.translation: They are the ones who disbelieved and obstructed you from the Sacred Mosque while the offering was prevented from reaching its place of sacrifice.

full_text.arabic: إِذْ جَعَلَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْحَمِيَّةَ حَمِيَّةَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ فَأَنزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِ وَعَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَأَلْزَمَهُمْ كَلِمَةَ التَّقْوَىٰ
full_text.translation: When those who disbelieved had put into their hearts zealotry — the zealotry of the time of ignorance — Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and imposed upon them the word of taqwa.

full_text.arabic: لَّقَدْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ الرُّؤْيَا بِالْحَقِّ ۖ لَتَدْخُلُنَّ الْمَسْجِدَ الْحَرَامَ إِن شَاءَ اللَّهُ آمِنِينَ مُحَلِّقِينَ رُءُوسَكُمْ وَمُقَصِّرِينَ لَا تَخَافُونَ
full_text.translation: Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth: you will enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing, in security, with heads shaved and hair shortened, not fearing.

full_text.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَىٰ وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِاللَّهِ شَهِيدًا
full_text.translation: He is the One who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion. And sufficient is Allah .

full_text.arabic: مُّحَمَّدٌ رَّسُولُ اللَّهِ ۚ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ أَشِدَّاءُ عَلَى الْكُفَّارِ رُحَمَاءُ بَيْنَهُمْ ۖ تَرَاهُمْ رُكَّعًا سُجَّدًا يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوَانًا
full_text.translation: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. You see them bowing and prostrating, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No commands to pray, fast, give charity, or observe any ritual. The surah dearer to the Prophet than anything under the sun does not legislate. It consoles, explains, and reframes. The entire architecture is devoted to opening the eyes before moving the hands.
No story of a previous messenger, no dramatic arc, no dialogue with a rejecting people. The community does not need a mirror from history. It needs someone to tell it what just happened.

Despite being revealed in the aftermath of a military confrontation, not a single ayah describes fighting. The restraint of hands — both theirs and the Quraysh's — is attributed directly to Allah. The surah's victory is not on a battlefield.

No Day of Judgment scene, no trumpet, no scales, no detailed reckoning. Paradise is mentioned briefly (ayah 5) but not described. The surah's horizon is not the afterlife — it is the next two years of history, and the seed that will grow from them.

Unlike Surah Muhammad (47), which diagnoses the community's internal disease, Al-Fath does not rebuke those who came. It rebukes only those who stayed behind. The believers who walked to Hudaybiyyah receive nothing but praise, reassurance, and divine pleasure.

absenceMap.subtitle: A surah that consoles, explains, and reframes — but never legislates
