Taqlid — the creed of inherited tradition

why_this_surah: What happens when faith becomes inherited rather than chosen? When people follow what their parents did without ever asking why? This surah confronts the difference between tradition and truth — and asks whether you believe what you believe because you examined it, or because everyone around you does.

name: Al-Hujurat
thesis: Eighteen ayahs, every one of them a law — the Quran's social constitution, built on the premise that you do not know what God knows about the person standing in front of you.

heart_verse.why: The surah's summit. For the first and only time, the address shifts from 'O you who have believed' to 'O mankind' — the scope expands to the entire human race. Every prohibition that precedes this ayah clears the ground for it. You cannot hear that all human beings are equal before God while you are still laughing at the person next to you.
heart_verse.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَائِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوا ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ
heart_verse.translation: O mankind, We have created you from male and female and made you into peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ۖ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
full_text.translation: O you who have believed, do not put yourselves ahead of Allah and His Messenger, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَرْفَعُوا أَصْوَاتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ وَلَا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ أَن تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَشْعُرُونَ
full_text.translation: O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or speak loudly to him as you speak to one another, lest your deeds become worthless while you do not perceive.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أَصْوَاتَهُمْ عِندَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ
full_text.translation: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah — they are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for taqwa.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنَادُونَكَ مِن وَرَاءِ الْحُجُرَاتِ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, those who call you from behind the private chambers — most of them do not use reason.

full_text.arabic: وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ صَبَرُوا حَتَّىٰ تَخْرُجَ إِلَيْهِمْ لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَّهُمْ ۚ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
full_text.translation: And if they had been patient until you came out to them, it would have been better for them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِن جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أَن تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهَالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلْتُمْ نَادِمِينَ
full_text.translation: O you who have believed, if a corrupt person comes to you with news, verify it, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and then become regretful over what you have done.

full_text.arabic: وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ فِيكُمْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ۚ لَوْ يُطِيعُكُمْ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِّنَ الْأَمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْإِيمَانَ وَزَيَّنَهُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ
full_text.translation: And know that among you is the Messenger of Allah. If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in difficulty, but Allah has made faith beloved to you and beautified it in your hearts.

full_text.arabic: فَضْلًا مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَنِعْمَةً ۚ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ
full_text.translation: A bounty from Allah and a favor. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.

full_text.arabic: وَإِن طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ فَإِن بَغَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَى الْأُخْرَىٰ فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّىٰ تَفِيءَ إِلَىٰ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ
full_text.translation: And if two factions among the believers fight, make peace between them. But if one transgresses against the other, fight the transgressor until it returns to the command of Allah.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
full_text.translation: The believers are but brothers, so make reconciliation between your brothers and have taqwa of Allah, that you may receive mercy.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ عَسَىٰ أَن يَكُونُوا خَيْرًا مِّنْهُمْ وَلَا نِسَاءٌ مِّن نِّسَاءٍ عَسَىٰ أَن يَكُنَّ خَيْرًا مِّنْهُنَّ
full_text.translation: O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule another people; perhaps they may be better than them. Nor let women ridicule other women; perhaps they may be better than them.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِّنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ ۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا
full_text.translation: O you who have believed, avoid much suspicion — indeed, some suspicion is sin. And do not spy, and do not backbite one another.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَائِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوا ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ
full_text.translation: O mankind, We have created you from male and female and made you into peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.

full_text.arabic: قَالَتِ الْأَعْرَابُ آمَنَّا ۖ قُل لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَلَٰكِن قُولُوا أَسْلَمْنَا وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ الْإِيمَانُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ
full_text.translation: The desert Arabs say, 'We have believed.' Say: You have not believed; rather say, 'We have submitted,' for faith has not yet entered your hearts.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتَابُوا وَجَاهَدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الصَّادِقُونَ
full_text.translation: The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and then doubted not, and fought with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah. It is those who are the truthful ones.

full_text.arabic: قُلْ أَتُعَلِّمُونَ اللَّهَ بِدِينِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ
full_text.translation: Say: Would you inform Allah about your religion while Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is Knowing of all things?

full_text.arabic: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُوا ۖ قُل لَّا تَمُنُّوا عَلَيَّ إِسْلَامَكُمْ ۖ بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ هَدَاكُمْ لِلْإِيمَانِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ
full_text.translation: They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islam. Say: Do not consider your Islam a favor to me. Rather, Allah has conferred favor upon you that He has guided you to faith, if you should be truthful.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No paradise is promised for obedience. No hellfire is threatened for violation. The prohibitions against mockery and backbiting carry no eschatological consequence within the surah. The motivation is entirely immediate: perhaps they are better than you.
No story of a previous nation, no destroyed city, no reference to Adam, Ibrahim, Musa, or Isa. The community's own behavior is the only text under examination.

No mention of the sky, the earth, the mountains, the rain, or any of the natural signs the Quran uses elsewhere. The surah has no interest in the external world. Its entire field of vision is the space between human beings.
God is described , Wise, Aware, Seeing — attributes of perception, not power. The surah's God is a witness and a judge of the social order, not a creator displaying His might.

Five times in eighteen ayahs the surah opens with 'O you who have believed' — the highest concentration of this address in the Quran. Each time, another demand follows. The surah treats belief as a promissory note and presents the bill.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah has stripped away everything except the essential legislation

left.desc: Do not put yourselves ahead of God and His Messenger. Have taqwa — God is Hearing and Knowing.
left.label: Conduct Toward the Prophet

right.desc: Do not consider your Islam a favor. God knows the unseen and is Seeing of what you do.
right.label: Conduct Toward God

left.desc: A fasiq brings unverified news — verify before you act. God made faith beloved to your hearts.
left.label: Epistemology

right.desc: True faith defined — belief without doubt, followed by sacrifice. Would you inform God about your religion?
right.label: Epistemology Reversed

left.desc: Believers are brothers — reconcile with justice. The command to make peace.
left.label: Brotherhood

right.desc: The desert Arabs claim brotherhood but faith has not entered their hearts. The claim is tested.
right.label: Brotherhood Examined

chiasticRing.title: The Mirror

center.desc: Do not mock. Do not suspect. Do not spy. Do not backbite. Then: O mankind — the most noble of you is the most righteous.
center.note: The pivot from 'O you who have believed' to 'O mankind.' Everything before addresses the community's internal conduct. Ayah 13 lifts the lens to encompass all of humanity.
center.label: The Declaration

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah's opening and closing face each other across the entire behavioral code

sectionJourney.title: The Social Constitution

sections.desc: How to conduct yourself before God and His Messenger. Do not put yourselves ahead, do not raise your voices, be patient. Your voice reveals the condition of your heart — lowering it is evidence that the heart has already passed a divine examination.
sections.title: The Protocol of the Sacred Presence

sections.desc: If a corrupt person brings you news, verify it — fatabayyanuu. The word legislates epistemology itself. Before you act on information, establish its truth. Then the law of reconciliation: the believers are brothers, so make peace between them with justice.
sections.title: The Verification Principle

sections.desc: The most densely packed ethical legislation in the Quran. Do not mock, do not insult, do not suspect, do not spy, do not backbite. Then the summit: the address shifts from believers to all mankind, and the declaration of human equality sealed by taqwa alone.
sections.title: The Ethical Core

sections.desc: The final distinction: the difference between outward submission and inner faith. The desert Arabs have submitted but faith has not entered their hearts. The surah closes with God's comprehensive knowledge — He is Seeing of what you do.
sections.title: Islam and Iman

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: prophetic protocol → verification → the ethical core → Islam vs. iman

deductiveFunnel.title: The Pathology of Contempt

layers.desc: The visible symptom: ridiculing others. The root yaskhar carries the image of subjugation — pressing someone into service beneath you. Mockery is a claim of superiority, and the surah identifies it as such before prohibiting it.
layers.label: Mockery

layers.desc: Moving from laughter to language: do not insult one another with offensive names. The prohibition targets the weaponization of naming — reducing a person to a label designed to diminish them.
layers.label: Insult

layers.desc: From the external to the internal: avoid much suspicion, for some suspicion is sin. The seed from which spying and backbiting grow. A state of mind that generates investigation.
layers.label: Suspicion

layers.desc: The fruit of suspicion: first you investigate in private, then you speak in absence. The surah seals it with the image of cannibalism — eating the flesh of your dead brother. The revulsion the reader feels is the surah's intended response to gossip.
layers.label: Spying → Backbiting
layers.arabic: وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَعْضًا

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: Ayahs 11-12 trace the entire disease from seed to fruit

content_nodes.concept: Fatabayyanuu — the verification principle (49:6)
Ta'arafu — diversity for the purpose of mutual knowledge
Al-Fath to Al-Hujurat: portrait to protocol
Islam and iman — the distinction and the invitation

why_this_surah: The surah of manners — how to behave with each other. Don't raise your voice over the Prophet's. Don't act on rumor without checking. Don't mock people, spy on each other, or backbite. If someone wrongs you, make peace. The Quran's most concentrated guide to how a community should actually treat one another.

name: Al-Mujadila
thesis: A surah that took a single woman's whispered complaint and drew from it a complete theology of the private — from a husband's cruelty to the cosmic division of loyalties — insisting that every hidden word is already part of the record.

heart_verse.why: The surah's most sweeping statement about divine omniscience. No configuration of private counsel escapes His presence — He is the fourth among three, the sixth among five, present wherever you are. In a surah about whispered conspiracies and hidden loyalties, this verse demolishes the concept of secrecy itself.
heart_verse.arabic: مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجْوَىٰ ثَلَاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ
heart_verse.translation: There is no private conversation among three except that He is the fourth.

full_text.arabic: قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجَادِلُكَ فِي زَوْجِهَا وَتَشْتَكِي إِلَى اللَّهِ
full_text.translation: Allah has certainly heard the speech of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah.

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ يُظَاهِرُونَ مِنكُم مِّن نِّسَائِهِم مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَاتِهِمْ
full_text.translation: Those among you who declare their wives as their mothers — they are not their mothers.

full_text.arabic: مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجْوَىٰ ثَلَاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ
full_text.translation: There is no private conversation among three except that He is the fourth.

full_text.arabic: إِذَا تَنَاجَيْتُمْ فَلَا تَتَنَاجَوْا بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ
full_text.translation: When you converse privately, do not converse in sin and aggression.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوا فِي الْمَجَالِسِ فَافْسَحُوا
full_text.translation: O you who believe, when you are told to make room in gatherings, make room.

full_text.arabic: اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطَانُ فَأَنسَاهُمْ ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ ۚ أُولَـٰئِكَ حِزْبُ الشَّيْطَانِ
full_text.translation: Satan has overcome them and made them forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of Satan.

full_text.arabic: أُولَـٰئِكَ حِزْبُ اللَّهِ ۚ أَلَا إِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ
full_text.translation: Those are the party of Allah. Indeed, the party of Allah — they are the successful.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No stories of previous nations, no references to Musa or Ibrahim or Nuh. The warnings are entirely contemporary — directed at specific behaviors happening in real time.
No painted scenes of hellfire or paradise. The consequences this surah cares about are relational — being on the wrong side of a line you did not realize was being drawn.
The word najwa and its derivatives saturate the middle section. The surah structurally demolishes the concept of secrecy — there is no whispered word that is not already heard.
The surah opens by validating a woman's complaint that every earthly authority had failed to address. The occasion of revelation centers female voice and agency.
Allah appears in every single ayah. In a surah about hidden conversations, God's name is never absent — the acoustic architecture performs the thesis.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah has no interest in history — only in the present moment and the divine gaze upon it

left.desc: A woman's complaint rises to God. Zihar abolished — the most private domestic injustice becomes divine legislation.
left.label: The Plea Upward

right.desc: The party of Satan vs. the party of Allah. Hearts inscribed with faith. The private made cosmic.
right.label: The Loyalty Division

left.desc: God enumerates what they forgot. The record-keeping that comforts the wronged now threatens the wrongdoer.
left.label: Warning to Opposers

right.desc: A charitable gift before consulting the Prophet — sincerity tested, then the requirement eased.
right.label: Private Audience Rules

chiasticRing.title: The Ring of Hearing

center.desc: There is no private conversation among three except that He is the fourth. The surah's gravitational core — divine omniscience meets communal ethics.
center.note: The word Allah appears in every single ayah of this surah — approximately forty times in twenty-two ayahs. In a surah about secrecy, God's name is the most repeated sound.
center.label: God Among Three

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah begins with God listening to a human being and ends with human beings listening to God

sectionJourney.title: From Whisper to Verdict

sections.desc: A woman — Khawla bint Tha'laba — brings a domestic injustice to the Prophet. Her husband declared zihar, freezing her in legal limbo. The Prophet had no answer. So she raised her complaint to Allah, and Allah answered. Qad sami'a — He has certainly heard. The emphatic particle leaves no ambiguity.
sections.title: The Plea That Was Heard

sections.desc: Those who oppose Allah and His Messenger will be humiliated. Allah has enumerated their deeds while they forgot them. The same divine hearing that comforts the wronged now becomes a warning to the wrongdoer.
sections.title: The Warning

sections.desc: The surah's architectural center. God is the fourth among three, the sixth among five — present in every private conversation. The word najwa (secret counsel) becomes the central keyword. Conspiratorial najwa is from Satan. Righteous najwa is permitted. The surah demolishes the concept of a private space above God's hearing.
sections.title: The Anatomy of Secret Counsel

sections.desc: Make room in gatherings — tafassahu. After ten ayahs on invisible architecture, the surah turns to visible architecture: how bodies occupy shared space. A charitable gift before private audience with the Prophet — legislated in one ayah, eased in the next. The disease and the cure use the same Arabic root.
sections.title: The Ethics of Assembly

sections.desc: Those who befriended God's enemies — their oaths used as shields. Satan's party versus Allah's party. The surah's final words: the party of Allah, they are the successful. The arc from a single woman's plea to the cosmic sorting of all loyalties is complete.
sections.title: The Great Division

sectionJourney.subtitle: Five movements: the plea → the warning → secret counsel → assembly ethics → the great division

deductiveFunnel.title: The Expanding Circle

layers.desc: God heard what even Aisha, sitting in the same room, could not fully hear. A single woman's domestic grievance becomes the occasion for divine legislation.
layers.label: One Woman's Plea

layers.desc: Zihar declared an abomination — munkar. The pre-Islamic formula abolished with graduated atonement. The speed of divine response is itself the point.
layers.label: Spousal Ethics

layers.desc: Every private conversation under divine surveillance. The surah moves from one household to every gathering. No space elevated above God's hearing.
layers.label: Community Counsel

layers.desc: The ultimate division — whose party are you in? The domestic and the cosmic are the same question asked at different scales.
layers.label: Cosmic Loyalty

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: From one woman's whispered plea to the cosmic division of all loyalties

content_nodes.concept: Najwa — the anatomy of secret counsel in 58:7-10
Allah in every ayah — the acoustic omniscience of Al-Mujadila
Khawla's plea and Maryam's cry — parallel divine hearings
Hizb Allah — the party of God across the Quran

why_this_surah: A woman came to the Prophet ﷺ to complain about her husband. God heard her from above seven heavens and revealed this surah in response. A private family dispute became revelation. The surah teaches that no injustice is too small for God to address — and that He hears even when no one else will listen.

name: Adh-Dhariyat
thesis: A sixty-ayah prosecution that opens by swearing on invisible forces and closes with the reason you exist — building through cosmic oaths, creation-signs, and a gallery of ruined nations until ayah 56 delivers the verdict: you were made for worship, and the evidence has been surrounding you the entire time.

heart_verse.why: Nine words in Arabic that have defined Islamic theology of purpose for fourteen centuries. The exclusive particle illa narrows the entire scope of human and jinn existence to a single function. Fifty-five ayahs of evidence — cosmic, personal, historical — have been building toward this sentence. The purpose of existence is worship, and the surah presents the entire visible and invisible universe as evidence for why that purpose is inescapable.
heart_verse.arabic: وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ
heart_verse.translation: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.

full_text.arabic: وَالذَّارِيَاتِ ذَرْوًا
full_text.translation: By the scattering winds that scatter —

full_text.arabic: فَالْحَامِلَاتِ وِقْرًا
full_text.translation: and the burden-bearing clouds —

full_text.arabic: فَالْجَارِيَاتِ يُسْرًا
full_text.translation: and the ships that glide with ease —

full_text.arabic: فَالْمُقَسِّمَاتِ أَمْرًا
full_text.translation: and the angels that distribute every command —

full_text.arabic: إِنَّمَا تُوعَدُونَ لَصَادِقٌ
full_text.translation: indeed, what you are promised is true,

full_text.arabic: وَإِنَّ الدِّينَ لَوَاقِعٌ
full_text.translation: and indeed, the recompense will occur.

full_text.arabic: وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الْحُبُكِ
full_text.translation: By the sky full of pathways —

full_text.arabic: إِنَّكُمْ لَفِي قَوْلٍ مُّخْتَلِفٍ
full_text.translation: indeed, you are in contradictory speech.

full_text.arabic: يُؤْفَكُ عَنْهُ مَنْ أُفِكَ
full_text.translation: Turned away from it is whoever is deluded.

full_text.arabic: قُتِلَ الْخَرَّاصُونَ
full_text.translation: Destroyed are the liars —

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي غَمْرَةٍ سَاهُونَ
full_text.translation: those who are in a flood of ignorance, heedless.

full_text.arabic: يَسْأَلُونَ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الدِّينِ
full_text.translation: They ask, 'When is the Day of Recompense?'

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ هُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ يُفْتَنُونَ
full_text.translation: The Day they will be tried over the Fire.

full_text.arabic: ذُوقُوا فِتْنَتَكُمْ هَـٰذَا الَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ
full_text.translation: 'Taste your trial — this is what you wished to hasten.'

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ
full_text.translation: Indeed, the righteous are in gardens and springs,

full_text.arabic: آخِذِينَ مَا آتَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَبْلَ ذَٰلِكَ مُحْسِنِينَ
full_text.translation: receiving what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were doers of good before that.

full_text.arabic: كَانُوا قَلِيلًا مِّنَ اللَّيْلِ مَا يَهْجَعُونَ
full_text.translation: They used to sleep but little of the night,

full_text.arabic: وَبِالْأَسْحَارِ هُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ
full_text.translation: and before dawn they would seek forgiveness,

full_text.arabic: وَفِي أَمْوَالِهِمْ حَقٌّ لِّلسَّائِلِ وَالْمَحْرُومِ
full_text.translation: and in their wealth was a share for the asker and the deprived.

full_text.arabic: وَفِي الْأَرْضِ آيَاتٌ لِّلْمُوقِنِينَ
full_text.translation: And in the earth are signs for those who have certainty,

full_text.arabic: وَفِي أَنفُسِكُمْ ۚ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ
full_text.translation: and in yourselves — do you not see?

full_text.arabic: وَفِي السَّمَاءِ رِزْقُكُمْ وَمَا تُوعَدُونَ
full_text.translation: And in the sky is your provision and what you are promised.

full_text.arabic: فَوَرَبِّ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِّثْلَ مَا أَنَّكُمْ تَنطِقُونَ
full_text.translation: By the Lord of heaven and earth, it is as true as the fact that you speak.

full_text.arabic: هَلْ أَتَاكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيْفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ الْمُكْرَمِينَ
full_text.translation: Has the story of Ibrahim's honored guests reached you?

full_text.arabic: إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَيْهِ فَقَالُوا سَلَامًا ۖ قَالَ سَلَامٌ قَوْمٌ مُّنكَرُونَ
full_text.translation: When they entered upon him and said, 'Peace.' He said, 'Peace — you are an unfamiliar people.'

full_text.arabic: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ فَجَاءَ بِعِجْلٍ سَمِينٍ
full_text.translation: Then he turned to his household and brought a roasted calf.

full_text.arabic: فَقَرَّبَهُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ أَلَا تَأْكُلُونَ
full_text.translation: He placed it before them and said, 'Will you not eat?'

full_text.arabic: فَأَوْجَسَ مِنْهُمْ خِيفَةً ۖ قَالُوا لَا تَخَفْ ۖ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَامٍ عَلِيمٍ
full_text.translation: Then he felt a fear of them. They said, 'Fear not,' and gave him glad tidings of a knowledgeable son.

full_text.arabic: فَأَقْبَلَتِ امْرَأَتُهُ فِي صَرَّةٍ فَصَكَّتْ وَجْهَهَا وَقَالَتْ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ
full_text.translation: His wife came forward with a cry and struck her face, saying, 'A barren old woman!'

full_text.arabic: قَالُوا كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ ۖ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْعَلِيمُ
full_text.translation: They said, 'Thus has your Lord said. He is the Wise, the Knowing.'

full_text.arabic: قَالَ فَمَا خَطْبُكُمْ أَيُّهَا الْمُرْسَلُونَ
full_text.translation: He said, 'Then what is your mission, O messengers?'

full_text.arabic: قَالُوا إِنَّا أُرْسِلْنَا إِلَىٰ قَوْمٍ مُّجْرِمِينَ
full_text.translation: They said, 'We have been sent to a criminal people —'

full_text.arabic: لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجَارَةً مِّن طِينٍ
full_text.translation: 'to send upon them stones of clay,'

full_text.arabic: مُّسَوَّمَةً عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلْمُسْرِفِينَ
full_text.translation: 'marked by your Lord for the transgressors.'

full_text.arabic: فَأَخْرَجْنَا مَن كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
full_text.translation: So We brought out whoever was in it of believers.

full_text.arabic: فَمَا وَجَدْنَا فِيهَا غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِّنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
full_text.translation: But We found not within it other than a single house of Muslims.

full_text.arabic: وَتَرَكْنَا فِيهَا آيَةً لِّلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ الْعَذَابَ الْأَلِيمَ
full_text.translation: And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment.

full_text.arabic: وَفِي مُوسَىٰ إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَاهُ إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ بِسُلْطَانٍ مُّبِينٍ
full_text.translation: And in Musa, when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority.

full_text.arabic: فَتَوَلَّىٰ بِرُكْنِهِ وَقَالَ سَاحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ
full_text.translation: But he turned away with his supporters and said, 'A sorcerer or a madman.'

full_text.arabic: فَأَخَذْنَاهُ وَجُنُودَهُ فَنَبَذْنَاهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ وَهُوَ مُلِيمٌ
full_text.translation: So We seized him and his armies and cast them into the sea, and he was blameworthy.

full_text.arabic: وَفِي عَادٍ إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّيحَ الْعَقِيمَ
full_text.translation: And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind.

full_text.arabic: مَا تَذَرُ مِن شَيْءٍ أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ إِلَّا جَعَلَتْهُ كَالرَّمِيمِ
full_text.translation: It left nothing it came upon but reduced it to ruin.

full_text.arabic: وَفِي ثَمُودَ إِذْ قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَمَتَّعُوا حَتَّىٰ حِينٍ
full_text.translation: And in Thamud, when they were told, 'Enjoy yourselves for a time.'

full_text.arabic: فَعَتَوْا عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ وَهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ
full_text.translation: But they defied their Lord's command, and the thunderbolt seized them while they watched.

full_text.arabic: فَمَا اسْتَطَاعُوا مِن قِيَامٍ وَمَا كَانُوا مُنتَصِرِينَ
full_text.translation: They could neither stand nor defend themselves.

full_text.arabic: وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ مِّن قَبْلُ ۖ إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمًا فَاسِقِينَ
full_text.translation: And the people of Nuh before — they were a defiantly disobedient people.

full_text.arabic: وَالسَّمَاءَ بَنَيْنَاهَا بِأَيْدٍ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ
full_text.translation: And the heaven We built with great power, and We are surely expanding it.

full_text.arabic: وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَاهَا فَنِعْمَ الْمَاهِدُونَ
full_text.translation: And the earth We spread out — and how excellent a spreader.

full_text.arabic: وَمِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ
full_text.translation: And from everything We created pairs, so that you might reflect.

full_text.arabic: فَفِرُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ ۖ إِنِّي لَكُم مِّنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
full_text.translation: So flee to Allah — indeed, I am a clear warner to you from Him.

full_text.arabic: وَلَا تَجْعَلُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَـٰهًا آخَرَ ۖ إِنِّي لَكُم مِّنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُّبِينٌ
full_text.translation: And do not set up with Allah another deity. Indeed, I am a clear warner to you from Him.

full_text.arabic: كَذَٰلِكَ مَا أَتَى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا قَالُوا سَاحِرٌ أَوْ مَجْنُونٌ
full_text.translation: Similarly, no messenger came to those before them except that they said, 'A sorcerer or a madman.'

full_text.arabic: أَتَوَاصَوْا بِهِ ۚ بَلْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طَاغُونَ
full_text.translation: Did they pass this down to one another? No, they are a transgressing people.

full_text.arabic: فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ فَمَا أَنتَ بِمَلُومٍ
full_text.translation: So turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed.

full_text.arabic: وَذَكِّرْ فَإِنَّ الذِّكْرَىٰ تَنفَعُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
full_text.translation: And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ
full_text.translation: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me.

full_text.arabic: مَا أُرِيدُ مِنْهُم مِّن رِّزْقٍ وَمَا أُرِيدُ أَن يُطْعِمُونِ
full_text.translation: I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ
full_text.translation: Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of Power, the Firm.

full_text.arabic: فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ذَنُوبًا مِّثْلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصْحَابِهِمْ فَلَا يَسْتَعْجِلُونِ
full_text.translation: Indeed, for those who wrong is a portion like the portion of their predecessors, so let them not rush Me.

full_text.arabic: فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن يَوْمِهِمُ الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ
full_text.translation: So woe to those who disbelieve from their Day which they are promised.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No dietary laws, no rules of inheritance, no instructions for community organization. Adh-Dhariyat is building the foundation that every commandment elsewhere in the Quran rests upon.

Their objections are characterized in passing — mukhtalif (confused), yu'fakuna (deluded) — but the surah does not pause to argue with them. It argues past them, to the believer who might momentarily waver.
If the question 'why do I exist?' has not been answered, no ethical code can stand on its own. The surah answers that question first.

absences.item: No Ibrahim arguing for Lut's people
absences.note: In Surah Hud, Ibrahim pleads on behalf of Lut's community. Here, he asks the angels' mission and accepts the answer. The Dhariyat version shows submission — acceptance as itself a form of evidence.

absences.item: No urgency in the closing warning
absences.note: The surah tells the wrongdoers not to rush — their portion is coming like the portion of their predecessors. The patience is the confidence. The case has already been won.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah operates at the level of why before it reaches how — every absence is a design choice

right.desc: Woe to the disbelievers from their Day which they are promised — the same root wa-'-da frames the closing
right.label: Final Warning

left.desc: The confused deniers contrasted with the God-conscious who pray before dawn and share their wealth
left.label: Deniers vs. Believers

right.desc: The command to flee to Allah, the purpose of creation, and the self-sufficiency of God who needs no provision
right.label: Flee to God

left.desc: Earth, self, sky — evidence so close it surrounds the listener's own body and consciousness
left.label: Creation-Signs

right.desc: Heaven built with power, earth spread out, pairs created from everything — creation-signs from the divine perspective
right.label: Cosmic Architecture

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Ibrahim's angel-guests, five destroyed nations — history is the surah's primary exhibit.
center.note: The center is where the surah lingers longest. Cosmic signs frame the argument; historical evidence is the argument.
center.label: The Historical Gallery

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah's movements mirror each other around a theological center

sectionJourney.title: The Evidence File

sections.desc: Four oaths sworn on invisible forces — scattering winds, burden-bearing clouds, gliding ships, distributing angels — each one moving further from direct perception. The verdict lands in two emphatic declarations: the promise is true, and the reckoning will occur.
sections.title: The Cosmic Oaths

sections.desc: The deniers are diagnosed as incoherent — mukhtalif, internally contradictory. The muttaqun are described as people who slept little and sought forgiveness before dawn. Then three fields of evidence: the earth, your own selves, the sky. The section seals with an oath: all of this is as certain as the fact that you speak.
sections.title: Conscience and Creation-Signs

sections.desc: Ibrahim's angel-guests deliver joy and ruin at the same table. Then five destructions accelerate in rapid succession — Lut's people, Pharaoh, 'Ad and the barren wind, Thamud and the thunderbolt, the people of Nuh — each shorter than the last, evidence overflowing until even the flood of Nuh needs only one ayah.
sections.title: The Gallery of Ruins

sections.desc: The surah lifts from history to cosmology — heaven built with power, earth spread out, pairs in everything — and then delivers the sentence the entire prosecution has been building toward: 'I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me.' Everything before is evidence. Everything after is consequence.
sections.title: The Purpose

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: cosmic oaths → conscience → historical gallery → the purpose of existence

deductiveFunnel.title: The Provision Arc

layers.desc: The opening oaths swear on forces that carry, distribute, and deliver — unseen agents of provision moving through the cosmos. The winds scatter seeds, the clouds carry rain, the ships carry goods, the angels carry divine commands.
layers.label: Invisible Provision

layers.desc: In the sky is your provision and what you are promised. Rizq appears here as something above you — descending, given, beyond your control. The direction of dependence flows downward from heaven.
layers.label: Provision in the Sky

layers.desc: You were created to worship — not to provide. The verb ya'budun carries the physical image of a path worn smooth by repeated walking. Worship is the beaten track of the soul returning to its source.
layers.label: The Purpose

layers.desc: I do not want from them any provision. The arc completes: God provides everything, God needs nothing. Rizq flows one way — from Creator to created — and never in reverse.
layers.label: God Needs Nothing

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The word rizq (provision) threads through the surah, carrying its argument about the direction of dependence

Ibrahim's hospitality scene — awjasa and concealed fear
Dhariyat–Tur diptych: evidence file and cross-examination
Rizq theology — provision flows one way

why_this_surah: When Ibrahim's guests — angels in disguise — told him and his wife they would have a son, Sarah laughed. She was too old. But the promise was true. This surah is built on the idea that what God scatters (wind, provision, truth) always reaches its destination, even when the delivery seems impossible.

name: At-Tur
thesis: A forty-nine-ayah cross-examination that swears by five cosmic realities, shows you the fire and the garden, dismantles every excuse for denial with fifteen unanswerable questions, and then leaves you standing alone before dawn — glorifying your Lord while the stars retreat.

heart_verse.why: The question that has no answer. If you were not created by anything, you emerged from absolute nothing — and nothing does not produce something. If you created yourselves, you existed before you existed. Both options are impossible. The only remaining possibility is the one the denier refuses to name. This is the hinge of the entire surah — the question everything before has been building toward and everything after radiates from.
heart_verse.arabic: أَمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ الْخَالِقُونَ
heart_verse.translation: Were they created from nothing, or are they themselves the creators?

full_text.arabic: وَالطُّورِ
full_text.translation: By the Mount,

full_text.arabic: وَكِتَابٍ مَّسْطُورٍ
full_text.translation: and a Book inscribed,

full_text.arabic: فِي رَقٍّ مَّنشُورٍ
full_text.translation: in parchment unrolled,

full_text.arabic: وَالْبَيْتِ الْمَعْمُورِ
full_text.translation: and the frequented House,

full_text.arabic: وَالسَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ
full_text.translation: and the raised ceiling,

full_text.arabic: وَالْبَحْرِ الْمَسْجُورِ
full_text.translation: and the sea set aflame —

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ لَوَاقِعٌ
full_text.translation: indeed, the punishment of your Lord will occur.

full_text.arabic: مَّا لَهُ مِن دَافِعٍ
full_text.translation: There is nothing to avert it.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ تَمُورُ السَّمَاءُ مَوْرًا
full_text.translation: The Day the sky will sway with circular motion,

full_text.arabic: وَتَسِيرُ الْجِبَالُ سَيْرًا
full_text.translation: and the mountains will walk with movement.

full_text.arabic: فَوَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
full_text.translation: Woe, that Day, to the deniers —

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ هُمْ فِي خَوْضٍ يَلْعَبُونَ
full_text.translation: those who were in discourse, amusing themselves.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا
full_text.translation: The Day they are thrust toward the fire of Hell with a violent thrust.

full_text.arabic: هَـٰذِهِ النَّارُ الَّتِي كُنتُم بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ
full_text.translation: 'This is the Fire which you used to deny.'

full_text.arabic: أَفَسِحْرٌ هَـٰذَا أَمْ أَنتُمْ لَا تُبْصِرُونَ
full_text.translation: 'Is this magic, or do you not see?'

full_text.arabic: اصْلَوْهَا فَاصْبِرُوا أَوْ لَا تَصْبِرُوا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ إِنَّمَا تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
full_text.translation: 'Burn therein. Be patient or impatient — it is all the same for you. You are only recompensed for what you used to do.'

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَعِيمٍ
full_text.translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and pleasure,

full_text.arabic: فَاكِهِينَ بِمَا آتَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ وَوَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ
full_text.translation: enjoying what their Lord has given them, and their Lord protected them from the punishment of Hellfire.

full_text.arabic: كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
full_text.translation: 'Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you used to do.'

full_text.arabic: مُتَّكِئِينَ عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّصْفُوفَةٍ ۖ وَزَوَّجْنَاهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ
full_text.translation: Reclining on thrones arranged in rows, and We will marry them to fair women with large, beautiful eyes.

full_text.arabic: وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم بِإِيمَانٍ أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَمَا أَلَتْنَاهُم مِّنْ عَمَلِهِم مِّن شَيْءٍ
full_text.translation: And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith — We will join with them their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds.

full_text.arabic: كُلُّ امْرِئٍ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينٌ
full_text.translation: Every person is pledged for what he has earned.

full_text.arabic: وَأَمْدَدْنَاهُم بِفَاكِهَةٍ وَلَحْمٍ مِّمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ
full_text.translation: And We will provide them with fruit and meat from whatever they desire.

full_text.arabic: يَتَنَازَعُونَ فِيهَا كَأْسًا لَّا لَغْوٌ فِيهَا وَلَا تَأْثِيمٌ
full_text.translation: They will exchange a cup in which there is no ill speech and no sin.

full_text.arabic: وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ غِلْمَانٌ لَّهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ لُؤْلُؤٌ مَّكْنُونٌ
full_text.translation: And there will circulate among them young attendants as if they were pearls well-protected.

full_text.arabic: وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ
full_text.translation: And they will turn to one another, asking each other,

full_text.arabic: قَالُوا إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبْلُ فِي أَهْلِنَا مُشْفِقِينَ
full_text.translation: 'Indeed, we were previously among our people, fearful.'

full_text.arabic: فَمَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا وَوَقَانَا عَذَابَ السَّمُومِ
full_text.translation: 'So Allah conferred favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the Scorching Fire.'

full_text.arabic: فَذَكِّرْ فَمَا أَنتَ بِنِعْمَتِ رَبِّكَ بِكَاهِنٍ وَلَا مَجْنُونٍ
full_text.translation: So remind, for you are not, by the favor of your Lord, a soothsayer or a madman.

full_text.arabic: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ شَاعِرٌ نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ
full_text.translation: Or do they say, 'A poet — we await for him a misfortune of time'?

full_text.arabic: قُلْ تَرَبَّصُوا فَإِنِّي مَعَكُم مِّنَ الْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ
full_text.translation: Say, 'Wait, for indeed I am, with you, among those who wait.'

full_text.arabic: أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلَامُهُم بِهَـٰذَا ۚ أَمْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طَاغُونَ
full_text.translation: Or do their minds command them to do this, or are they a transgressing people?

full_text.arabic: أَمْ يَقُولُونَ تَقَوَّلَهُ ۚ بَل لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ
full_text.translation: Or do they say, 'He made it up'? Rather, they do not believe.

full_text.arabic: فَلْيَأْتُوا بِحَدِيثٍ مِّثْلِهِ إِن كَانُوا صَادِقِينَ
full_text.translation: Then let them produce a statement like it, if they are truthful.

full_text.arabic: أَمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ الْخَالِقُونَ
full_text.translation: Or were they created from nothing, or are they themselves the creators?

full_text.arabic: أَمْ خَلَقُوا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۚ بَل لَّا يُوقِنُونَ
full_text.translation: Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain.

full_text.arabic: أَمْ عِندَهُمْ خَزَائِنُ رَبِّكَ أَمْ هُمُ الْمُصَيْطِرُونَ
full_text.translation: Or do they possess the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the controllers?

full_text.arabic: أَمْ لَهُمْ سُلَّمٌ يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ ۖ فَلْيَأْتِ مُسْتَمِعُهُم بِسُلْطَانٍ مُّبِينٍ
full_text.translation: Or do they have a stairway by which they listen? Then let their listener produce a clear authority.

full_text.arabic: أَمْ لَهُ الْبَنَاتُ وَلَكُمُ الْبَنُونَ
full_text.translation: Or does He have daughters while you have sons?

full_text.arabic: أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ أَجْرًا فَهُم مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ
full_text.translation: Or do you ask of them a payment, so they are burdened by debt?

full_text.arabic: أَمْ عِندَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ
full_text.translation: Or do they possess the unseen, so they write it down?

full_text.arabic: أَمْ يُرِيدُونَ كَيْدًا ۖ فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا هُمُ الْمَكِيدُونَ
full_text.translation: Or do they intend a plan? But those who disbelieve — they are the object of a plan.

full_text.arabic: أَمْ لَهُمْ إِلَـٰهٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ ۚ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
full_text.translation: Or do they have a deity other than Allah? Exalted is Allah above whatever they associate with Him.

full_text.arabic: وَإِن يَرَوْا كِسْفًا مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ سَاقِطًا يَقُولُوا سَحَابٌ مَّرْكُومٌ
full_text.translation: And if they see a piece of the sky falling, they would say, 'Clouds heaped up.'

full_text.arabic: فَذَرْهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يُلَاقُوا يَوْمَهُمُ الَّذِي فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ
full_text.translation: So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck insensible.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
full_text.translation: The Day their plan will not avail them at all, nor will they be helped.

full_text.arabic: وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا عَذَابًا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: And indeed, for those who have wronged is a punishment before that, but most of them do not know.

full_text.arabic: وَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا ۖ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
full_text.translation: And be patient for the decision of your Lord, for indeed you are in Our eyes. And exalt with praise of your Lord when you arise.

full_text.arabic: وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَإِدْبَارَ النُّجُومِ
full_text.translation: And in the night glorify Him, and after the setting of the stars.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No prophets named, no destroyed nations recounted, no stories retold. For a Makkan surah of this length, the absence is extraordinary. The surahs around it include prophetic narratives; At-Tur strips all of that away.
The warning comes entirely from cosmic imagery and logical argument. The surah's case rests on the structure of reality itself — no story to hide behind.
No moral instruction, no commands directed at the community about how to live. The surah's only imperative is to the Prophet: be patient, glorify your Lord.

absences.item: No transition between fire and garden
absences.note: The pivot from punishment (ayah 16) to Paradise (ayah 17) is one of the sharpest in the Quran — no bridge, no 'on the other hand.' The surah simply turns.

absences.item: No answer to the central question
absences.note: Ayah 35 — 'Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?' — leaves unstated the only remaining possibility. The listener must complete the syllogism in their own mind.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah strips away everything except argument, consequence, and worship

left.desc: Five oaths building from mountain to sea set aflame — the certainty of punishment, with nothing to avert it
left.label: Cosmic Oaths

right.desc: Even a piece of the sky falling would be rationalized — their denial is not about evidence but will
right.label: Final Warning

left.desc: The sky churns, mountains walk, the deniers are thrust into the Fire — 'Is this magic, or do you not see?'
left.label: Day of Fire

right.desc: You are in Our eyes. Glorify Him when you arise, and after the setting of the stars
right.label: Predawn Worship

left.desc: Gardens, thrones, children reunited, cups without sin — 'We were fearful, and Allah was al-Barr'
left.label: Paradise Reunion

right.desc: Not a soothsayer, not a madman, not a poet — the Prophet asked for nothing and fabricated nothing
right.label: Accusations Dismissed

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Were they created from nothing? Did they create the heavens? Do they have a deity other than Allah?
center.note: Reason sits at the heart of the surah, flanked by consequence and reward. The architecture argues that reason is the corridor from cosmic reality to personal devotion.
center.label: The Unanswerable Questions

chiasticRing.subtitle: Cosmic testimony resolves into personal worship, reason at the center

sectionJourney.title: The Cross-Examination

sections.desc: Five cosmic oaths — mountain, book, frequented house, raised ceiling, sea set aflame — each larger than the last, building until the verdict crashes down: the punishment will occur, and nothing can avert it. The Day itself is compressed to two images: the sky churning, the mountains walking. Then the deniers are shoved into the Fire they called a lie.
sections.title: The Oaths and the Fire

sections.desc: The sharpest pivot in the Quran. Without transition, gardens and pleasure replace fire and ruin. The believers recline on thrones, their children joined to them with no one's reward diminished. Cups are passed without empty talk. And looking back, they say: 'We were previously fearful' — and discover that Allah was al-Barr al-Rahim all along.
sections.title: The Garden and the Reunion

sections.desc: The intellectual core. Fifteen rhetorical questions driven by the particle am — each one removing a floor from beneath the skeptic's position. Were you created from nothing? Did you create the heavens? Do you possess God's treasuries? Do you have a stairway to heaven? The questions accumulate until there is nowhere left to stand.
sections.title: The Fifteen Questions

sections.desc: The confrontation ends. The tone shifts to intimate counsel: be patient, for you are in Our eyes. Glorify your Lord when you arise, and in the night, and after the retreat of the stars. The surah that opened with a mountain closes with one man's worship before dawn.
sections.title: The Predawn Commission

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four waves: cosmic oaths → garden → demolition → predawn worship

deductiveFunnel.title: The Rabb Thread

layers.desc: The punishment of your Lord will occur. Rabb as the sovereign whose judgment is inescapable — the name that means master, sustainer, the one who raises and nourishes.
layers.label: Lord of Punishment

layers.desc: Enjoying what their Lord has given them, and their Lord protected them. Rabb as the source of every good thing in Paradise — the sustainer whose care extends beyond death.
layers.label: Lord of Provision

layers.desc: Do they possess the treasuries of your Lord? Rabb as the owner of all provision, all decree. The question strips the denier of any claim to self-sufficiency.
layers.label: Lord of the Treasuries

layers.desc: Be patient for the decision of your Lord, for you are in Our eyes. Rabb as the intimate guardian — the same name that carried punishment, provision, and sovereignty now carries personal care.
layers.label: Lord of Patience

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The word Rabb (Lord) threads through the surah at every structurally significant point
