full_text.arabic: يَا زَكَرِيَّا إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَامٍ اسْمُهُ يَحْيَىٰ لَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا
full_text.translation: O Zakariyya, We give you good tidings of a son whose name is Yahya — We have given no one this name before.

full_text.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا
full_text.translation: He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?'

full_text.arabic: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِن قَبْلُ وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْئًا
full_text.translation: He said, 'Thus says your Lord: It is easy for Me, and I created you before when you were nothing.'

full_text.arabic: قَالَ رَبِّ اجْعَل لِّي آيَةً ۚ قَالَ آيَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ سَوِيًّا
full_text.translation: He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign.' He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, being sound.'

full_text.arabic: فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ مِنَ الْمِحْرَابِ فَأَوْحَىٰ إِلَيْهِمْ أَن سَبِّحُوا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا
full_text.translation: So he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and signaled to them: glorify in the morning and the evening.

full_text.arabic: يَا يَحْيَىٰ خُذِ الْكِتَابَ بِقُوَّةٍ ۖ وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا
full_text.translation: O Yahya, take the Book with strength. And We gave him wisdom as a child —

full_text.arabic: وَحَنَانًا مِّن لَّدُنَّا وَزَكَاةً ۖ وَكَانَ تَقِيًّا
full_text.translation: and tenderness from Us, and purity. And he was God-conscious —

full_text.arabic: وَبَرًّا بِوَالِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُن جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا
full_text.translation: and good to his parents, and not domineering or rebellious.

full_text.arabic: وَسَلَامٌ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ وُلِدَ وَيَوْمَ يَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ يُبْعَثُ حَيًّا
full_text.translation: And peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive.

full_text.arabic: وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ مَرْيَمَ إِذِ انتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَانًا شَرْقِيًّا
full_text.translation: And mention in the Book, Maryam, when she withdrew from her family to a place in the east —

full_text.arabic: فَاتَّخَذَتْ مِن دُونِهِمْ حِجَابًا فَأَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهَا رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا
full_text.translation: and put a screen between herself and them. Then We sent Our spirit to her, and he appeared before her as a perfectly formed man.

full_text.arabic: قَالَتْ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِالرَّحْمَٰنِ مِنكَ إِن كُنتَ تَقِيًّا
full_text.translation: She said, 'I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-conscious.'

full_text.arabic: قَالَ إِنَّمَا أَنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَامًا زَكِيًّا
full_text.translation: He said, 'I am only the messenger of your Lord, to give you a pure boy.'

full_text.arabic: قَالَتْ أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّا
full_text.translation: She said, 'How can I have a son when no man has touched me, and I have not been unchaste?'

full_text.arabic: قَالَ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ ۖ وَلِنَجْعَلَهُ آيَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَرَحْمَةً مِّنَّا ۚ وَكَانَ أَمْرًا مَّقْضِيًّا
full_text.translation: He said, 'Thus says your Lord: It is easy for Me — and We will make him a sign for the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter already decreed.'

full_text.arabic: فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَانتَبَذَتْ بِهِ مَكَانًا قَصِيًّا
full_text.translation: So she conceived him, and withdrew with him to a far place.

full_text.arabic: فَأَجَاءَهَا الْمَخَاضُ إِلَىٰ جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ قَالَتْ يَا لَيْتَنِي مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَٰذَا وَكُنتُ نَسْيًا مَّنسِيًّا
full_text.translation: The labor pains drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, 'I wish I had died before this and been completely forgotten.'

full_text.arabic: فَنَادَاهَا مِن تَحْتِهَا أَلَّا تَحْزَنِي قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا
full_text.translation: Then he called to her from below her, 'Do not grieve — your Lord has placed beneath you a stream.'

full_text.arabic: وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا
full_text.translation: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree — it will drop fresh, ripe dates upon you.

full_text.arabic: فَكُلِي وَاشْرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا ۖ فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ الْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا فَقُولِي إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنسِيًّا
full_text.translation: So eat and drink and let your eyes be at ease. And if you see any person, say, 'I have pledged a fast of silence to the Most Merciful.'

full_text.arabic: فَأَتَتْ بِهِ قَوْمَهَا تَحْمِلُهُ ۖ قَالُوا يَا مَرْيَمُ لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْئًا فَرِيًّا
full_text.translation: Then she came with him to her people, carrying him. They said, 'O Maryam, you have done something unprecedented.'

full_text.arabic: يَا أُخْتَ هَارُونَ مَا كَانَ أَبُوكِ امْرَأَ سَوْءٍ وَمَا كَانَتْ أُمُّكِ بَغِيًّا
full_text.translation: 'O sister of Harun, your father was not a bad man, and your mother was not unchaste.'

full_text.arabic: فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ ۖ قَالُوا كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَن كَانَ فِي الْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّا
full_text.translation: So she pointed to him. They said, 'How can we speak to one who is a child in the cradle?'

full_text.arabic: قَالَ إِنِّي عَبْدُ اللَّهِ آتَانِيَ الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلَنِي نَبِيًّا
full_text.translation: He said, 'I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet.'

full_text.arabic: وَجَعَلَنِي مُبَارَكًا أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُ وَأَوْصَانِي بِالصَّلَاةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ مَا دُمْتُ حَيًّا
full_text.translation: And He has made me blessed wherever I am, and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long  live —

full_text.arabic: وَبَرًّا بِوَالِدَتِي وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْنِي جَبَّارًا شَقِيًّا
full_text.translation: and good to my mother, and He has not made me domineering or wretched.

full_text.arabic: وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدتُّ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّا
full_text.translation: And peace be upon me the day I was born, the day I die, and the day I am raised alive.

full_text.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ ۚ قَوْلَ الْحَقِّ الَّذِي فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ
full_text.translation: That is Isa son of Maryam — the word of truth about which they dispute.

full_text.arabic: مَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ مِن وَلَدٍ ۖ سُبْحَانَهُ ۚ إِذَا قَضَىٰ أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ
full_text.translation: It is not for Allah to take a son. Glory be to Him. When He decrees a matter, He says to it, 'Be,' and it is.

full_text.arabic: وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ ۚ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ
full_text.translation: And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is a straight path.

full_text.arabic: فَاخْتَلَفَ الْأَحْزَابُ مِن بَيْنِهِمْ ۖ فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن مَّشْهَدِ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
full_text.translation: Then the factions differed among themselves — so woe to those who disbelieved, from the scene of a tremendous Day.

full_text.arabic: أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ يَوْمَ يَأْتُونَنَا ۖ لَٰكِنِ الظَّالِمُونَ الْيَوْمَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُّبِينٍ
full_text.translation: How clearly they will hear and see on the Day they come to Us — but today the wrongdoers are in clear error.

full_text.arabic: وَأَنذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْحَسْرَةِ إِذْ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ وَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
full_text.translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are in heedlessness and do not believe.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَرِثُ الْأَرْضَ وَمَنْ عَلَيْهَا وَإِلَيْنَا يُرْجَعُونَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, We will inherit the earth and everyone on it, and to Us they will be returned.

full_text.arabic: وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَّبِيًّا
full_text.translation: And mention in the Book, Ibrahim. Indeed, he was a man of truth, a prophet.

full_text.arabic: إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَا أَبَتِ لِمَ تَعْبُدُ مَا لَا يَسْمَعُ وَلَا يُبْصِرُ وَلَا يُغْنِي عَنكَ شَيْئًا
full_text.translation: When he said to his father, 'O my dear father, why do you worship what does not hear or see or benefit you at all?'

full_text.arabic: يَا أَبَتِ إِنِّي قَدْ جَاءَنِي مِنَ الْعِلْمِ مَا لَمْ يَأْتِكَ فَاتَّبِعْنِي أَهْدِكَ صِرَاطًا سَوِيًّا
full_text.translation: 'O my dear father, knowledge has come to me that did not come to you, so follow me — I will guide you to a straight path.'

full_text.arabic: يَا أَبَتِ لَا تَعْبُدِ الشَّيْطَانَ ۖ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَصِيًّا
full_text.translation: 'O my dear father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan is ever disobedient to the Most Merciful.'

full_text.arabic: يَا أَبَتِ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَن يَمَسَّكَ عَذَابٌ مِّنَ الرَّحْمَٰنِ فَتَكُونَ لِلشَّيْطَانِ وَلِيًّا
full_text.translation: 'O my dear father, I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, and you will become a companion of Satan.'

full_text.arabic: قَالَ أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنْ آلِهَتِي يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ ۖ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهِ لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ ۖ وَاهْجُرْنِي مَلِيًّا
full_text.translation: He said, 'Are you turning away from my gods, O Ibrahim? If you do not stop, I will stone you. Now leave me alone for a long time.'

full_text.arabic: قَالَ سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكَ ۖ سَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّي ۖ إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِي حَفِيًّا
full_text.translation: He said, 'Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you. He has always been gracious to me.'

full_text.arabic: وَأَعْتَزِلُكُمْ وَمَا تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ وَأَدْعُو رَبِّي عَسَىٰ أَلَّا أَكُونَ بِدُعَاءِ رَبِّي شَقِيًّا
full_text.translation: 'And I will withdraw from you and what you invoke besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord — perhaps I will not be disappointed in calling upon my Lord.'

full_text.arabic: فَلَمَّا اعْتَزَلَهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ وَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ ۖ وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا نَبِيًّا
full_text.translation: So when he had withdrawn from them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We gave him Ishaq and Yaqub, and each of them We made a prophet.

full_text.arabic: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِنَا وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا
full_text.translation: And We gave them of Our mercy, and We made for them a reputation of high truth.

full_text.arabic: وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ مُوسَىٰ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ مُخْلَصًا وَكَانَ رَسُولًا نَّبِيًّا
full_text.translation: And mention in the Book, Musa. He was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet.

full_text.arabic: وَنَادَيْنَاهُ مِن جَانِبِ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنِ وَقَرَّبْنَاهُ نَجِيًّا
full_text.translation: And We called him from the right side of the mountain, and We drew him near, speaking intimately.

full_text.arabic: وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ مِن رَّحْمَتِنَا أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ نَبِيًّا
full_text.translation: And We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun as a prophet.

full_text.arabic: وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ وَكَانَ رَسُولًا نَّبِيًّا
full_text.translation: And mention in the Book, Ismail. He was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.

full_text.arabic: وَكَانَ يَأْمُرُ أَهْلَهُ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَالزَّكَاةِ وَكَانَ عِندَ رَبِّهِ مَرْضِيًّا
full_text.translation: He used to enjoin on his family prayer and zakat, and he was pleasing to his Lord.

full_text.arabic: وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِدْرِيسَ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَّبِيًّا
full_text.translation: And mention in the Book, Idris. He was a man of truth, a prophet.

full_text.arabic: وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا
full_text.translation: And We raised him to a high station.

full_text.arabic: أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِن ذُرِّيَّةِ آدَمَ وَمِمَّنْ حَمَلْنَا مَعَ نُوحٍ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْرَائِيلَ وَمِمَّنْ هَدَيْنَا وَاجْتَبَيْنَا ۚ إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُ الرَّحْمَٰنِ خَرُّوا سُجَّدًا وَبُكِيًّا
full_text.translation: Those were the ones upon whom Allah bestowed favor from among the prophets — from the descendants of Adam, and from those We carried with Nuh, and from the descendants of Ibrahim and Israel, and from those We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down in prostration and in tears.

full_text.arabic: فَخَلَفَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ أَضَاعُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَاتَّبَعُوا الشَّهَوَاتِ ۖ فَسَوْفَ يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا
full_text.translation: But there came after them a generation who lost the prayer and followed desires; so they will meet loss —

full_text.arabic: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَأُولَٰئِكَ يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ وَلَا يُظْلَمُونَ شَيْئًا
full_text.translation: except those who repent and believe and do righteous deeds — they will enter Paradise and will not be wronged at all.

full_text.arabic: جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ الَّتِي وَعَدَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ عِبَادَهُ بِالْغَيْبِ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ مَأْتِيًّا
full_text.translation: Gardens of Eden, which the Most Merciful has promised His servants unseen. His promise will certainly be fulfilled.

full_text.arabic: لَّا يَسْمَعُونَ فِيهَا لَغْوًا إِلَّا سَلَامًا ۖ وَلَهُمْ رِزْقُهُمْ فِيهَا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا
full_text.translation: They will not hear therein any vain talk — only peace. And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening.

full_text.arabic: تِلْكَ الْجَنَّةُ الَّتِي نُورِثُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا مَن كَانَ تَقِيًّا
full_text.translation: That is the Garden We give as inheritance to those of Our servants who are God-conscious.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا نَتَنَزَّلُ إِلَّا بِأَمْرِ رَبِّكَ ۖ لَهُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا وَمَا خَلْفَنَا وَمَا بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ ۚ وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّا
full_text.translation: We descend not except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and behind us and between — and your Lord is never forgetful.

full_text.arabic: رَّبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فَاعْبُدْهُ وَاصْطَبِرْ لِعِبَادَتِهِ ۚ هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيًّا
full_text.translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them — so worship Him and be patient in His worship. Do you know of anyone equal to Him?

full_text.arabic: وَيَقُولُ الْإِنسَانُ أَإِذَا مَا مِتُّ لَسَوْفَ أُخْرَجُ حَيًّا
full_text.translation: And the human being says, 'When I have died, will I really be brought forth alive?'

full_text.arabic: أَوَلَا يَذْكُرُ الْإِنسَانُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُ مِن قَبْلُ وَلَمْ يَكُ شَيْئًا
full_text.translation: Does the human being not remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?

full_text.arabic: فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ وَالشَّيَاطِينَ ثُمَّ لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ حَوْلَ جَهَنَّمَ جِثِيًّا
full_text.translation: So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils, then We will bring them around Hell on their knees.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ لَنَنزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرَّحْمَٰنِ عِتِيًّا
full_text.translation: Then We will extract from every group those who were most defiant against the Most Merciful.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ لَنَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِالَّذِينَ هُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِهَا صِلِيًّا
full_text.translation: Then We know best those who are most deserving of burning therein.

full_text.arabic: وَإِن مِّنكُمْ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَا ۚ كَانَ عَلَىٰ رَبِّكَ حَتْمًا مَّقْضِيًّا
full_text.translation: And there is not one of you who will not pass over it. That is a decree from your Lord, definitively decided.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوا وَّنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ فِيهَا جِثِيًّا
full_text.translation: Then We will save those who had taqwa, and leave the wrongdoers within it, on their knees.

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ قَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَيُّ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ خَيْرٌ مَّقَامًا وَأَحْسَنُ نَدِيًّا
full_text.translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, the disbelievers say to those who believe, 'Which of the two groups is better in position and more impressive in assembly?'

full_text.arabic: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَحْسَنُ أَثَاثًا وَرِئْيًا
full_text.translation: And how many a generation before them have We destroyed who were finer in possessions and appearance!

full_text.arabic: قُلْ مَن كَانَ فِي الضَّلَالَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ لَهُ الرَّحْمَٰنُ مَدًّا ۚ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا رَأَوْا مَا يُوعَدُونَ إِمَّا الْعَذَابَ وَإِمَّا السَّاعَةَ فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ شَرٌّ مَّكَانًا وَأَضْعَفُ جُندًا
full_text.translation: Say, 'Whoever is in error — the Most Merciful will extend for him until, when they see what they were promised — whether punishment or the Hour — they will know who is worst in position and weakest in soldiers.'

full_text.arabic: وَيَزِيدُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا هُدًى ۗ وَالْبَاقِيَاتُ الصَّالِحَاتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًا وَخَيْرٌ مَّرَدًّا
full_text.translation: And Allah increases in guidance those who are guided. And lasting good deeds are better in your Lord's sight in reward and in outcome.

full_text.arabic: أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ بِآيَاتِنَا وَقَالَ لَأُوتَيَنَّ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا
full_text.translation: Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'?

full_text.arabic: أَطَّلَعَ الْغَيْبَ أَمِ اتَّخَذَ عِندَ الرَّحْمَٰنِ عَهْدًا
full_text.translation: Has he seen the unseen, or has he taken a covenant from the Most Merciful?

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا ۚ سَنَكْتُبُ مَا يَقُولُ وَنَمُدُّ لَهُ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ مَدًّا
full_text.translation: Absolutely not. We will record what he says and extend for him from the punishment at length.

full_text.arabic: وَنَرِثُهُ مَا يَقُولُ وَيَأْتِينَا فَرْدًا
full_text.translation: And We will inherit from him what he claims, and he will come to Us alone.

full_text.arabic: وَاتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ آلِهَةً لِّيَكُونُوا لَهُمْ عِزًّا
full_text.translation: And they have taken gods besides Allah, that they might be a source of strength for them.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا ۚ سَيَكْفُرُونَ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدًّا
full_text.translation: Absolutely not. They will deny their worship and become opponents against them.

full_text.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا الشَّيَاطِينَ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ تَؤُزُّهُمْ أَزًّا
full_text.translation: Do you not see that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with incitement?

full_text.arabic: فَلَا تَعْجَلْ عَلَيْهِمْ ۖ إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ عَدًّا
full_text.translation: So do not be impatient over them. We only count out for them a count.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ الْمُتَّقِينَ إِلَى الرَّحْمَٰنِ وَفْدًا
full_text.translation: On the Day We will gather the God-conscious to the Most Merciful as a delegation —

full_text.arabic: وَنَسُوقُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ وِرْدًا
full_text.translation: and drive the sinful to Hell in thirst.

full_text.arabic: لَّا يَمْلِكُونَ الشَّفَاعَةَ إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّخَذَ عِندَ الرَّحْمَٰنِ عَهْدًا
full_text.translation: They will have no power of intercession, except the one who had taken a covenant with the Most Merciful.

full_text.arabic: وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَٰنُ وَلَدًا
full_text.translation: And they say, 'The Most Merciful has taken a son.'

full_text.arabic: لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئًا إِدًّا
full_text.translation: You have brought forth something monstrous —

full_text.arabic: تَكَادُ السَّمَاوَاتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ وَتَنشَقُّ الْأَرْضُ وَتَخِرُّ الْجِبَالُ هَدًّا
full_text.translation: at which the heavens almost shatter, the earth almost splits open, and the mountains almost collapse in ruins —

full_text.arabic: أَن دَعَوْا لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ وَلَدًا
full_text.translation: that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا يَنبَغِي لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا
full_text.translation: It is not fitting for the Most Merciful to take a son.

full_text.arabic: إِن كُلُّ مَن فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِلَّا آتِي الرَّحْمَٰنِ عَبْدًا
full_text.translation: There is not one in the heavens and the earth who will not come to the Most Merciful as a servant.

full_text.arabic: لَّقَدْ أَحْصَاهُمْ وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا
full_text.translation: He has counted them and numbered them precisely.

full_text.arabic: وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَرْدًا
full_text.translation: And every one of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ سَيَجْعَلُ لَهُمُ الرَّحْمَٰنُ وُدًّا
full_text.translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds — the Most Merciful will place love for them.

full_text.arabic: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ الْمُتَّقِينَ وَتُنذِرَ بِهِ قَوْمًا لُّدًّا
full_text.translation: So We have made it easy in your tongue, that you may give glad tidings to the God-conscious and warn therewith a stubborn people.

full_text.arabic: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ ۖ هَلْ تُحِسُّ مِنْهُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَوْ تَسْمَعُ لَهُمْ رِكْزًا
full_text.translation: And how many a generation before them have We destroyed — do you perceive a single one of them, or hear even the faintest sound from them?

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No ethical imperatives, no 'O you who believe,' no instructions about fasting, charity, or prayer. The moral weight is carried entirely by the stories and the contrast between the prophets and those who came after them.

absences.item: No use of the word Masih
absences.note: The most extensive account of Isa outside Al Imran — and the surah never once calls him Christ or Messiah. The choice is deliberate: to show Isa as servant, prophet, child, son, before any title enters the room.

Ibrahim promises to ask forgiveness for his idolatrous father. The surah records no response. The love persists even when the request cannot be fulfilled — and in the silence, something about the nature of loving someone who will not turn around becomes visible.

The correction of the claim about Isa is embedded in the story, not mounted on top of it. Twelve ayahs of portrait before the theological point arrives. The sequencing is the surah's rhetorical genius.

absences.item: No rikz — only once in the Quran
absences.note: The final word — rikz, the faintest possible sound — appears nowhere else in all 114 surahs. The surah gave this word to its ending alone, sealing itself with the silence of erased civilizations.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah trusts the portrait more than the prescription — every absence is a choice

left.desc: Zakariyya calls his Lord nida'an khafiyya — with a secret call in the dark. The quiet of prayer.
left.label: The Whisper

right.desc: Do you perceive a single one of them? Or hear even the faintest sound — rikz? The quiet of obliteration.
right.label: The Silence

left.desc: Zakariyya asks how. The answer: it is easy for Me. Masculine address — rabbuka.
left.label: It Is Easy — rabbuka

right.desc: Maryam asks how. The identical answer with one change: feminine address — rabbuki.
right.label: It Is Easy — rabbuki

left.desc: Yahya's peace — spoken about him by God, in the third person: wa salamun 'alayhi.
left.label: Peace Received

right.desc: Isa's peace — spoken by him from the cradle, in the first person: wa-l-salamu 'alayya.
right.label: Peace Claimed

chiasticRing.title: The Whisper and the Silence

center.desc: When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration and in tears.
center.note: The hinge of the surah. Everything before it builds the prophetic record. Everything after asks: what did you do with that record?
center.label: The Prostration

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah opens with a secret prayer and closes with the absence of even a whisper

sectionJourney.title: Six Rooms

sections.desc: An old man whose bones have gone soft and whose hair has caught fire with age calls out in a whisper — nida'an khafiyya. God answers with an unprecedented child: Yahya. A word used nowhere else in the Quran — hanan, a mother's warmth — is given to this boy alone.
sections.title: The Room of Prayer

sections.desc: Maryam withdraws eastward, puts a screen between herself and the world, and encounters a spirit in the form of a man. Her first instinct is taqwa — she invokes the Most Merciful as a shield. The same divine formula given to Zakariyya returns with a single change: rabbuka becomes rabbuki. Same logic, same ease, different gender.
sections.title: The Annunciation

sections.desc: Maryam in labor, alone, wishing for annihilation. Then water, dates, and a command to be silent. Her child speaks from the cradle — and his first word is 'abd, servant. The theological correction begins from the first syllable.
sections.title: The Palm Tree and the Cradle

sections.desc: Ibrahim and his father — ya abati four times, tenderness persisting through rejection. Musa called to the mountain and drawn near as a confidant. Ismail true to his promise. Idris raised high. Each portrait a single brushstroke, each prophet shown in a moment of isolation.
sections.title: The Gallery of Prophets

sections.desc: The turning point — ayah 58, the verse of prostration. Then the trapdoor opens: after the prophets came a generation that lost the prayer. Two processions emerge — the God-conscious gathered as a delegation, the sinful driven to Hell in thirst.
sections.title: The Rupture

sections.desc: The heavens almost shatter at the claim that God has a son. The creation itself recoils. Then the counter-truth: every being comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has counted them all. And for those who believe — sa-yaj'alu lahumu-l-rahmanu wudda — He will place love.
sections.title: The Declaration

sectionJourney.subtitle: Prayer → miracle → speaking child → gallery → rupture → declaration

deductiveFunnel.title: Seven Uses of Rahma

layers.desc: The surah's first substantive word after the letters: dhikru rahmati rabbika — a mention of the mercy of your Lord. Mercy is the frame before anything begins.
layers.label: The Opening

layers.desc: Hanan — tenderness, a pang of love — given from Us. A word that appears exactly once in the entire Quran, placed here and nowhere else.
layers.label: Yahya's Gift

layers.desc: The child himself is described as a mercy from Us — not merely the recipient of mercy but its embodiment for humanity.
layers.label: Isa

layers.desc: We gave them of Our mercy — Ibrahim, Ishaq, Yaqub. Mercy extends through the prophetic line as inheritance.
layers.label: Ibrahim's Gift

layers.desc: We gave him, out of Our mercy, his brother Harun. A person given as mercy — companionship itself as divine gift.
layers.label: Harun

layers.desc: When the verses of al-Rahman were recited, they fell in prostration. The divine name itself — the Most Merciful — saturates the surah's most pivotal verse.
layers.label: The Prostration

layers.desc: The Most Merciful will place love for them — sa-yaj'alu. Actively. Deliberately. Love as a gift set down by God, not earned by the servant.
layers.label: Love Placed

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The word mercy and its root thread through the surah like a pulse

content_nodes.concept: The hanan hapax — tenderness used once in the Quran
Rabbuka to rabbuki — the mirror formula
Maryam-Kahf-TaHa triptych — survival, mercy, commission
Nasyan mansiyya — the doubled erasure Maryam wished for

why_this_surah: A young woman gives birth alone under a palm tree. An old man begs God for a child he thought he'd never have. A son pleads with his father to stop worshipping idols. This surah is the Quran at its most emotionally raw — the moments where faith costs you something personal, and God meets you in the vulnerability.

name: An-Naml
thesis: A surah that builds the most magnificent kingdom in human history and then names itself after an ant — because the ant could see what the kingdom was for. Power saturated with faith, tested against creatures most kingdoms would never notice.

heart_verse.why: An army of jinn, humans, and birds marching in formation, and one ant stops them. She addresses her community by name, identifies the king, gives tactical instruction, and excuses the army's potential harm — they would do it unknowingly. In a surah filled with palaces, this single sentence names the whole thing.
heart_verse.arabic: قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ لَا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمَانُ وَجُنُودُهُ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
heart_verse.translation: An ant said, 'O ants, enter your dwellings so that Sulayman and his armies do not crush you while they do not perceive.'

full_text.arabic: طس ۚ تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْقُرْآنِ وَكِتَابٍ مُّبِينٍ
full_text.translation: Ta-Sin. These are the verses of the Quran and a clear Book.

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا دَاوُودَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ عِلْمًا
full_text.translation: And We certainly gave Dawud and Sulayman knowledge.

full_text.arabic: قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ
full_text.translation: An ant said, 'O ants, enter your dwellings.'

full_text.arabic: رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ
full_text.translation: My Lord, inspire me to be grateful for Your blessings.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهُ مِن سُلَيْمَانَ وَإِنَّهُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَـٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
full_text.translation: Indeed, it is from Sulayman, and indeed it reads: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

full_text.arabic: أَنَا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَن يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ
full_text.translation: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.

full_text.arabic: أَسْلَمْتُ مَعَ سُلَيْمَانَ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
full_text.translation: I submit with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of all worlds.

full_text.arabic: أَمَّن يُجِيبُ الْمُضْطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ
full_text.translation: Is He not better who answers the desperate when they call upon Him?

full_text.arabic: وَتَرَى الْجِبَالَ تَحْسَبُهَا جَامِدَةً وَهِيَ تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحَابِ
full_text.translation: And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they pass as the passing of clouds.

full_text.arabic: وَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ فَتَعْرِفُونَهَا
full_text.translation: And say: Praise be to Allah. He will show you His signs and you will recognize them.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: Salih's and Lut's destructions are compressed into retrospective summary. The narrative energy, the dialogue and suspense — all reserved for a story that ends in conversion, not destruction. The Queen's submission is center stage; violence is offstage.
No community regulation, no rules for daily life, no dietary laws. The surah is doing something different from warning or legislating — it is displaying. The argument emerges from the display itself.

absences.item: No direct address to the Quraysh
absences.note: The surah builds a portrait of power so much greater, so much more aligned with reality, that Qurayshi prestige shrinks by comparison without ever being named.

absences.item: The only interior basmala in the Quran
absences.note: The formula that frames every surah appears inside Sulayman's letter to the Queen (ayah 30). A king's correspondence carries the same opening as divine revelation — the ordinary becomes extraordinary.

absences.item: Named after an insect that appears for one ayah
absences.note: In a surah filled with kingdoms, palaces, and jinn who move thrones, Allah names the whole thing after the smallest voice in the room — the one who stopped an army with a sentence of concern.

absenceMap.subtitle: An-Naml persuades through spectacle — what it leaves out shapes the argument

left.desc: The Quran declared as guidance and good news for those who act on certainty
left.label: Quran

right.desc: Recite the Quran — whoever is guided is guided for their own benefit. He will show you His signs.
right.label: Quran

left.desc: Musa's nine signs — Pharaoh's people call them sorcery despite recognizing the truth inwardly
left.label: Signs Rejected

right.desc: On that Day, those who denied Allah's signs are gathered and asked: Did you deny without encompassing them in knowledge?
right.label: Signs Judged

left.desc: Dawud and Sulayman receive knowledge — language of birds, armies of three species, the ant's perception
left.label: Knowledge Given

right.desc: The creation questions — gardens, rivers, the desperate answered, darkness navigated. Who does all this?
right.label: Knowledge Displayed

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: My Lord, I have wronged myself, and I submit with Sulayman to Allah, Lord of all worlds.
center.note: The surah's emotional and argumentative peak. A queen who arrived at faith through corrected perception — the glass floor revealed that what she saw was not what was real.
center.label: The Queen's Submission

chiasticRing.subtitle: The Quran's guidance at the opening corresponds to its recitation at the close

sectionJourney.title: The Four Movements

sections.desc: The Quran arrives as guidance. Musa sees a fire and walks into a divine encounter — nine signs for Pharaoh's people, who reject them 'out of injustice and arrogance' even while recognizing the truth inwardly. The pattern is set: undeniable signs, chosen blindness.
sections.title: Light & Encounter

sections.desc: Sulayman inherits a kingdom spanning jinn, humans, and birds. The ant speaks with collective concern. The hoopoe delivers theological analysis of Sheba. The letter carries the only interior basmala in the Quran. The throne crosses continents. The Queen arrives at faith through corrected perception in a palace of glass.
sections.title: The Kingdom of Knowledge

sections.desc: Salih's Thamud — nine conspirators plotting murder in the dark. Lut's people — desire elevated above sight. The negative image of the Sheba story: where the Queen saw signs and submitted, these communities saw signs and refused. The contrast needs no editorial comment.
sections.title: Two Rejections

sections.desc: A cascade of questions — who created, who answers the desperate, who guides through darkness? Five times: 'Is there a god with Allah?' Then the Day of Gathering, the creature that will speak, mountains passing like clouds, and the final command: recite the Quran.
sections.title: The Creation Interrogation

sectionJourney.subtitle: Encounter → kingdom → rejection → interrogation

deductiveFunnel.title: Three Non-Human Witnesses

layers.desc: Speaks to protect her community from approaching power. She sees the danger no one else sees and speaks with clarity and care. The surah bears her name because she could see what the kingdom was for.
layers.label: The Ant

layers.desc: Delivers a theological assessment of Sheba's kingdom that would be sophisticated coming from a human scholar. Identifies sun-worship, names Shaytan as cause, frames it as failure to prostrate. A bird doing theological work.
layers.label: The Hoopoe

layers.desc: The dabbah that will emerge from the earth at the end of time to indict humanity for refusing to believe. Three voices from outside the human world, escalating in scope: a valley, a kingdom, all of creation.
layers.label: The Creature

layers.desc: He will show you His signs and you will recognize them. The natural world sees what humans refuse to see — and one day, the earth itself will testify.
layers.label: The Pattern

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The surah's three voices from outside the human world — each addressing a failure of human perception

content_nodes.concept: The ant's speech — perception and community
The Queen's glass floor — corrected perception as faith
The interior basmala — Sulayman's letter
The Ta-Sin cluster — Ash-Shu'ara, An-Naml, Al-Qasas

why_this_surah: Contains two of the Quran's most memorable scenes: Sulayman and the ant (an entire army halted for one small creature), and Sulayman and the Queen of Sheba (a woman leader who recognizes truth when she sees it). A surah about power used wisely and wisdom that comes from unexpected places.

name: Luqman
thesis: A thirty-four-ayah surah named after a man who was never given prophethood — a father speaking quietly to his son, passing on everything he has learned about God, pride, patience, and how to walk through the world without losing yourself.

heart_verse.why: The ethical hinge of the surah. Everything before establishes tawhid and the parent-child bond. Everything after flows from this: if God sees the mustard seed in the rock, then prayer matters, character matters, the angle of your face when you speak to someone matters.
heart_verse.arabic: يَا بُنَيَّ إِنَّهَا إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ فَتَكُن فِي صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ أَوْ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَأْتِ بِهَا اللَّهُ
heart_verse.translation: O my son, indeed if it be the weight of a mustard seed within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth.

full_text.arabic: الم
full_text.translation: Alif, Lam, Mim.

full_text.arabic: تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ الْحَكِيمِ
full_text.translation: These are the signs of the wise Book —

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا لُقْمَانَ الْحِكْمَةَ أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ
full_text.translation: And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom, saying: 'Be grateful to Allah.'

full_text.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ لُقْمَانُ لِابْنِهِ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُ يَا بُنَيَّ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ
full_text.translation: And when Luqman said to his son while advising him: 'O my son, do not associate anything with Allah.'

full_text.arabic: وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ وَهْنًا عَلَىٰ وَهْنٍ
full_text.translation: And We have enjoined upon man concerning his parents — his mother carried him in weakness upon weakness.

full_text.arabic: يَا بُنَيَّ إِنَّهَا إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ فَتَكُن فِي صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ أَوْ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَأْتِ بِهَا اللَّهُ
full_text.translation: O my son, indeed if it be the weight of a mustard seed within a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth.

full_text.arabic: يَا بُنَيَّ أَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ وَأْمُرْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَانْهَ عَنِ الْمُنكَرِ وَاصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا أَصَابَكَ
full_text.translation: O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you.

full_text.arabic: وَلَا تُصَعِّرْ خَدَّكَ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحًا
full_text.translation: And do not turn your cheek away from people in contempt, and do not walk through the earth with insolence.

full_text.arabic: وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ وَاغْضُضْ مِن صَوْتِكَ ۚ إِنَّ أَنكَرَ الْأَصْوَاتِ لَصَوْتُ الْحَمِيرِ
full_text.translation: Be moderate in your pace and lower your voice. Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys.

full_text.arabic: وَمَن يُسْلِمْ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقَىٰ
full_text.translation: Whoever submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good has grasped the most trustworthy handhold.

full_text.arabic: وَلَوْ أَنَّمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلَامٌ وَالْبَحْرُ يَمُدُّهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ سَبْعَةُ أَبْحُرٍ مَّا نَفِدَتْ كَلِمَاتُ اللَّهِ
full_text.translation: If all the trees on earth were pens and the ocean were ink, replenished by seven more oceans, the words of Allah would not be exhausted.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ وَاخْشَوْا يَوْمًا لَّا يَجْزِي وَالِدٌ عَن وَلَدِهِ
full_text.translation: O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when no father will avail his son.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِندَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي الْأَرْحَامِ
full_text.translation: Indeed, Allah alone has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain. He knows what is in the wombs.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No 'Ad, no Thamud, no people of Lut. For a Makkan surah, this is extraordinary. Luqman replaces warning-by-destruction with warning-by-counsel. The danger is internal: pride, heedlessness, the swaggering gait.

absences.item: No direct address to the Prophet
absences.note: The surah speaks through the Prophet but not to him by name or title. The audience is wider — parents, children, anyone who has been given advice and must decide whether to receive it.

He is a hakim, a wise man — not a prophet. His direct speech is quoted at length as moral instruction, one of the very few non-prophets afforded this treatment in the Quran — the believer of Pharaoh's household (40:28–44) is the other sustained case.
The five unknowables close the surah: the Hour, rain, the wombs, tomorrow, the place of death. Luqman can teach his son how to live. He cannot tell him when or where he will die.

absences.item: No separation of wisdom and gratitude
absences.note: Hikmah is defined as shukr in ayah 12. The double helix of the surah: wisdom is gratitude, ingratitude is disbelief. They cannot be separated.

absenceMap.subtitle: A surah that replaces destruction with counsel — every absence shapes the argument

left.desc: The Quran as al-kitab al-hakim — signs of the wise Book. Creation signs confirm the source.
left.label: The Wise Book

right.desc: God's inexhaustible words, the five unknowables. The closing frame of divine knowledge beyond human reach.
right.label: Cosmic Signs & Unknowables

left.desc: Luqman receives hikmah, defined as gratitude. The accepting response to guidance.
left.label: Wisdom Received

right.desc: Those who follow ancestral custom without thought. The refusing response to guidance.
right.label: Wisdom Rejected

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Tawhid meets parenthood. Luqman speaks, Allah interrupts to honor the mother, then Luqman resumes: the mustard seed, prayer, character, humility.
center.note: The center of the ring is the mother's body (wahnan 'ala wahn). In a surah named after the father, the architectural weight falls on the mother's sacrifice.
center.label: The Father's Counsel

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah layers divine knowledge around the center of a father's counsel

sectionJourney.title: The Counsel

sections.desc: The Quran declared al-hakim — wise. Two kinds of listeners contrasted: one who receives the Book and one who trades in lahw al-hadith, idle speech that displaces. The obstacle to wisdom is not ignorance — it is arrogance (mustakbiran).
sections.title: The Wise Book

sections.desc: A single ayah that changes everything. Luqman is given al-hikmah, and the surah defines it immediately: gratitude. An ushkur lillah. The entire content of wisdom compressed into two words.
sections.title: Wisdom Defined

sections.desc: Tawhid, the mother's sacrifice (wahnan 'ala wahn), God's awareness of the mustard seed, prayer, moral responsibility, patience, the diseases of pride — how you walk, how you speak. Luqman covers the whole person.
sections.title: The Father's Counsel

sections.desc: Those who argue without knowledge. The 'urwa al-wuthqa — the firmest handhold. Then the staggering image: every tree a pen, the ocean ink, seven more oceans — God's words never exhausted. Luqman's few sentences set inside infinite divine speech.
sections.title: The Challenge & the Cosmic

sections.desc: No father will avail his son on that Day. The Hour, the rain, the wombs, tomorrow's provision, the place of your death — five domains of knowledge that belong to God alone. The surah that began with what wisdom can give ends with what wisdom cannot know.
sections.title: The Five Unknowables

sectionJourney.subtitle: Five movements: the wise Book → wisdom defined → the father's counsel → the challenge → the five unknowables

deductiveFunnel.title: The Pedagogy

layers.desc: The foundation. Do not associate anything with Allah. Addressed as ya bunayya — my dear son, my little one. The theological instruction arrives wrapped in tenderness.
layers.label: Tawhid

layers.desc: The ethical hinge. If God sees a mustard seed inside a rock — al-Latif, the Subtle, the one whose awareness reaches into places too small for anyone else. Theology becomes ethics.
layers.label: Awareness
layers.arabic: إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ

layers.desc: Four commands in one ayah. Prayer (vertical), moral responsibility (horizontal), patience (internal). The word 'azm — resolve, backbone — closes the sequence.
layers.label: Practice

layers.desc: Pride is not a doctrine — it is a posture. The sideways turn of the face, the bouncing gait, the raised voice. Luqman reads his son's future body language and warns.
layers.label: Character

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: Luqman's counsel moves from theology to embodied practice in a single arc

content_nodes.concept: Wahnan 'ala wahn — the mother at the center of the father's surah
Al-'urwa al-wuthqa — the firmest handhold in Luqman and Al-Baqarah
The five unknowables and the Hadith of Jibril
Luqman's embodied ethics — pride as posture, not doctrine

why_this_surah: Contains the advice of Luqman to his son — and it reads like the best parenting advice you've ever heard. Don't associate anything with God. Be grateful to your parents. Pray. Encourage good. Be patient with what happens. Don't walk arrogantly. Lower your voice. If you're a parent, or were ever someone's child, this surah speaks to you.

name: Fatir
thesis: A surah that walks you through a gallery of everything God ever originated — wings, rain, oceans, mountains streaked in three colors, the full spectrum of the human heart — and then turns the lights on to show you that the Artist has been watching you look at His work all along.

heart_verse.why: Placed at the summit of a passage about geology and pigmentation — the streaks of red, white, and raven-black in mountains. Knowledge here is the ability to read color as theology. The scholar who trembles is the one who sees a fingerprint of divine will in every shade of stone.
heart_verse.arabic: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ
heart_verse.translation: Only those among His servants who have knowledge truly fear Allah.

full_text.arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ فَاطِرِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ جَاعِلِ الْمَلَائِكَةِ رُسُلًا أُولِي أَجْنِحَةٍ مَّثْنَىٰ وَثُلَاثَ وَرُبَاعَ
full_text.translation: All praise belongs to Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who made the angels messengers having wings in pairs — two, three, and four.

full_text.arabic: مَا يَفْتَحِ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحْمَةٍ فَلَا مُمْسِكَ لَهَا ۖ وَمَا يُمْسِكْ فَلَا مُرْسِلَ لَهُ مِن بَعْدِهِ
full_text.translation: Whatever mercy Allah opens for people, none can withhold it. And whatever He withholds, none can release it after Him.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ ۚ هَلْ مِنْ خَالِقٍ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ يَرْزُقُكُم مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ
full_text.translation: O humanity, remember the blessing of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the sky and the earth?

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَنتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ ۖ وَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ
full_text.translation: O humanity, you are the ones in need of Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.

full_text.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ ثَمَرَاتٍ مُّخْتَلِفًا أَلْوَانُهَا
full_text.translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby fruits of varying colors?

full_text.arabic: وَمِنَ الْجِبَالِ جُدَدٌ بِيضٌ وَحُمْرٌ مُّخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهَا وَغَرَابِيبُ سُودٌ ۝ إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ
full_text.translation: And in the mountains are tracts, white and red of varying shades, and raven-black. Only those among His servants who have knowledge truly fear Allah.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ أَوْرَثْنَا الْكِتَابَ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَيْنَا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا ۖ فَمِنْهُمْ ظَالِمٌ لِّنَفْسِهِ وَمِنْهُم مُّقْتَصِدٌ وَمِنْهُمْ سَابِقٌ بِالْخَيْرَاتِ
full_text.translation: Then We caused those whom We chose to inherit the Book. And among them is he who wrongs himself, the moderate, and the one foremost in good deeds.

full_text.arabic: وَقَالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ
full_text.translation: And they will say: 'Praise to Allah who has removed from us sorrow.'

full_text.arabic: أَوَلَمْ نُعَمِّرْكُم مَّا يَتَذَكَّرُ فِيهِ مَن تَذَكَّرَ وَجَاءَكُمُ النَّذِيرُ
full_text.translation: Did We not give you lives long enough for whoever would reflect to reflect? And the warner came to you.

full_text.arabic: وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِمَا كَسَبُوا مَا تَرَكَ عَلَىٰ ظَهْرِهَا مِن دَابَّةٍ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِ بَصِيرًا
full_text.translation: If Allah were to take people to account for what they have earned, He would not leave upon the earth a single creature. Indeed, Allah is ever, of His servants, Seeing.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: In a Makkan surah of this length, you would expect at least one narrative — Nuh, Hud, Musa. Fatir offers none. Messengers are mentioned only in passing. The entire persuasive weight rests on creation, on what a person can observe without any scripture at all.
Paradise and Hell are stated as consequence, not depicted as experience. No vivid immersive scenes of judgment — unlike neighboring surahs Saba and Ya-Sin. The afterlife is conclusion, not cinema.

No instruction to pray, give charity, or observe specific obligations. The surah is not legislating. It is displaying. The moral argument is made entirely through the evidence of creation and the taxonomy of response.

No Pharaoh, no 'Ad, no Thamud. The antagonist in Fatir is not a person or a nation — it is distraction itself, the inability to see what is already in front of you. The enemy is unnamed because it is universal.

Only two moments address the Prophet directly (ayahs 8, 22). Both are brief. The surah's frustration — quiet but real — is not at persecution but at the gap between evidence and response. The evidence is overwhelming. The refusal continues.

absenceMap.subtitle: Every absence shapes the gallery — what is not on the walls tells you what the curator intends

left.desc: Fatir — Originator of heavens and earth. Angels with varied wings. Mercy opened and closed by Him alone.
left.label: Allah

right.desc: Knower of the unseen. False gods created nothing. The deferral is mercy, and the One deferring is watching. Bassir.
right.label: Allah

left.desc: Warning against worldly deception. Shaytan as the arch-deceiver. The one whose evil deeds are made beautiful to him.
left.label: The Two Paths

right.desc: Not binary but spectrum: the self-wronging, the moderate, the foremost. All three are inheritors. All three were chosen.
right.label: The Three Categories

left.desc: Rain, salt and fresh seas, night and day, sun and moon. Creation as field of provision.
left.label: Cosmic Signs

right.desc: Mountains white, red, raven-black. Creatures of every shade. Knowledge that leads to khashya — trembling awe.
right.label: Color

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: O humanity, you are the ones in need of Allah, and Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
center.note: Everything before it displays the creation and asks: who did this? Everything after it explores the moral consequences of answering that question.
center.label: The Poverty Declaration

chiasticRing.subtitle: The direction of the gaze reverses — from seeing creation to being seen

sectionJourney.title: The Gallery Tour

sections.desc: Opens with praise for al-Fatir — the One who splits open what never existed. Angels with wings in pairs of two, three, and four. Mercy that none can withhold. A direct challenge: is there any creator besides Allah? And a warning against the deception of worldly life.
sections.title: The Originator & His Angels

sections.desc: Rain on dead earth. Two seas — fresh and salt — that never merge. Night turning into day. The surah's prose slows to the pace of observation. Each sign demonstrates a principle: the same rain produces different colors of fruit. Diversity is the evidence of intention.
sections.title: The Gallery of Signs

sections.desc: The hinge: 'O humanity, you are the ones in need of Allah.' Then parables of the blind and seeing, the living and the dead. Mountains streaked white, red, and raven-black. Creatures of every shade. And at the summit: 'Only those who have knowledge truly fear Allah.'
sections.title: Poverty & the Theology of Color

sections.desc: Believers sorted into three categories — the self-wronging, the moderate, the foremost — all called inheritors of the Book. Paradise described as the removal of sorrow. Hell confronted with: 'Did We not give you time?' The final word: Bassir — Seeing. The Artist watches you watch His work.
sections.title: The Three Inheritors & the Final Seeing

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: origination → signs → poverty → reckoning

deductiveFunnel.title: The Gaze

layers.desc: Fatir — the One who splits something open from nothing, who originates without precedent, without model. Diversity is original. Difference is by design. Even the angels do not all have the same number of wings.
layers.label: The Origin

layers.desc: Rain on dead earth, two seas that never merge, night turning into day. The surah does not argue from hidden knowledge or prophetic narrative. It argues from what everyone can already see. The challenge is not 'believe this story' but 'explain what is already in front of you.'
layers.label: The Evidence

layers.desc: The hinge. The word fuqara — utterly destitute — applied to all of humanity without exception. The contrast with al-Ghani al-Hamid is total. There is no middle ground.
layers.label: The Poverty

layers.desc: The final word is Bassir — Seeing. The gallery visitor is also being observed. You began by looking at what He made. You end realizing He has been looking at you the entire time.
layers.label: The Seeing

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The surah reverses who is looking at whom

content_nodes.concept: Innama yakhsha — knowledge that produces trembling
The three inheritors — zalim, muqtasid, sabiq
Saba-Fatir diptych — paired openings of praise
The fly and the raindrop — Al-Hajj 22:73 and Fatir 35:40

why_this_surah: Opens by naming God as the originator of the heavens and the earth, the one who made angels with two, three, and four wings. Then it asks: is there any creator other than God who provides for you? The surah builds the case for God through what He originates — and challenges you to find another explanation.

name: Ya-Sin
thesis: The surah the Prophet called the heart of the Quran — building from a murdered believer's Paradise to the orbits of moons to the dust of bones, and landing on a single syllable of divine power that renders every objection irrelevant.

heart_verse.why: The verse the entire surah funnels toward. Every parable, every cosmic sign, every argument about resurrection converges on this single sentence. The God whose speech warns you is the God whose speech creates worlds.
heart_verse.arabic: إِنَّمَا أَمْرُهُ إِذَا أَرَادَ شَيْئًا أَن يَقُولَ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ
heart_verse.translation: His command, when He wills a thing, is only to say to it: Be — and it is.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: Isa, Musa, Ibrahim, Nuh — all absent. The parable's messengers are anonymous. The warning becomes universal: this is every messenger and every town.
Ad, Thamud, the people of Lut — the destroyed civilizations that populate neighboring surahs are missing. One anonymous parable carries the weight of all of them.
No rules about prayer, fasting, inheritance, or conduct. Ya-Sin is pure argument — evidence, warning, proof — with no legislation.
The Prophet does not speak in this surah. Allah addresses him, affirms him, defends him — but he does not respond within the text. The surah speaks for him.

absences.item: No escape clause for the sealed
absences.note: Ayahs 7–10 describe people with shackles on their necks, barriers before and behind, a covering over their eyes. No remedy is offered within this passage. The sealing is described as complete.

absenceMap.subtitle: Every absence is a design choice — what Ya-Sin leaves out shapes its argument

left.desc: An oath on the Quran to establish: you are a messenger on a straight path, sent to warn a heedless people
left.label: The Prophet Affirmed

right.desc: He is not a poet. The final proof of resurrection. Kun fa-yakun — the speech that warns and the speech that creates
right.label: The Prophet Vindicated

left.desc: Messengers rejected. The believing man killed. The town destroyed by a single blast
left.label: The Parable

right.desc: Signs rejected. The trumpet sounds. Paradise and Fire — the messengers spoke the truth
right.label: The Judgment

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Earth, night, sun, moon, ships — the physical evidence that connects warning to reality.
center.note: The signs of creation are the pivot the entire surah turns on. They are the proof that makes the parable a warning and the trumpet a certainty.
center.label: The Cosmic Signs

chiasticRing.subtitle: Ya-Sin's opening and closing form a deliberate correspondence

sectionJourney.title: The Escalation

sections.desc: An oath on the wise Quran, establishing Muhammad as a messenger on a straight path. A people in shackles they cannot see — barriers before and behind — heedless (ghafilun). The word that opens the surah's diagnosis.
sections.title: The Oath & the Sealed

sections.desc: Three messengers rejected. A man runs from the margins of the city — unnamed, powerless, urgent. His people kill him. He enters Paradise and his first words are grief for his killers. Then one blast, and the town is silenced. Ya hasratan 'ala al-'ibad.
sections.title: The Parable of the Town

sections.desc: Dead earth, living grain. Night peeled from day. Sun and moon in measured orbits — la al-shamsu yanbaghi laha an tudrika al-qamar. Ships on the sea. The pivot of the surah: the physical evidence that connects the parable's warning to the trumpet's reality.
sections.title: The Cosmic Testimony

sections.desc: Every sign met with turning away. Then — sudden — the trumpet. The dead slip from graves. Paradise: God speaks salam. Fire: mouths sealed, limbs testify. The heedlessness that was diagnosed is now judged.
sections.title: The Trumpet & Judgment

sections.desc: He is not a poet. The cattle you ride are evidence you deny. A bone crumbled in mockery is answered by five ayahs of escalating proof — and then the word: kun fa-yakun. The surah lands on a single syllable of omnipotence.
sections.title: The Final Proof

sectionJourney.subtitle: Five movements: oath → parable → cosmos → trumpet → the Word

deductiveFunnel.title: The Closing Proof

layers.desc: He who produced them the first time will give them life. The logic is irresistible — the first creation is harder than the second.
layers.label: First Creation

layers.desc: He made fire from the green tree. Life from what looks dead. Fire from what looks wet. The proof is in the tree you already use.
layers.label: Fire from Green

layers.desc: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? The question scales upward — from bones to trees to the cosmos.
layers.label: Heavens & Earth

layers.desc: Yes, indeed. One word. The shortest and most decisive answer in the Quran's vocabulary.
layers.label: Bala

layers.desc: His command, when He wills a thing, is only to say to it: Be — and it is. The verse the entire surah funnels toward.
layers.label: Kun Fa-Yakun

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: Five ayahs of escalating argument, each layer pressing harder — until the Word

content_nodes.concept: The man from the farthest end of the city
Kun fa-yakun — the creative word
Cosmic adab: the sun, the moon, and yanbaghi
Ya hasratan 'ala al-'ibad — cosmic grief

why_this_surah: Muslims recite this surah more than almost any other — for the dying, at funerals, on Thursday nights. The Quran's core arguments compressed into eighty-three ayahs: a messenger rejected by his own town, the evidence written into creation, the certainty that death is not the end. If you learn one surah beyond Al-Fatiha, many scholars would point you here.

name: Ghafir
thesis: A surah that holds God's mercy and God's severity in the same breath, places a single believing voice at the center of an empire's denial, and asks you to decide which direction you face while the door is still open.

heart_verse.why: After eighty ayahs of argument, counter-argument, historical evidence, and cosmic testimony, the surah arrives at this sentence. One verb. One promise. The entire surah has been building toward the question of whether people will call upon God or upon something else, and here the invitation is issued in its most undressed form.
heart_verse.arabic: وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ
heart_verse.translation: And your Lord said, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.'

full_text.arabic: حم
full_text.translation: Ha. Mim.

full_text.arabic: تَنزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ
full_text.translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Knowing.

full_text.arabic: غَافِرِ الذَّنبِ وَقَابِلِ التَّوْبِ شَدِيدِ الْعِقَابِ ذِي الطَّوْلِ
full_text.translation: Forgiver of sin, Accepter of repentance, Severe in punishment, Owner of abundance.

full_text.arabic: مَا يُجَادِلُ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا
full_text.translation: No one disputes the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve.

full_text.arabic: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَالْأَحْزَابُ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ
full_text.translation: Before them the people of Nuh denied, and the factions after them.

full_text.arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ
full_text.translation: And thus the word of your Lord has come into effect upon those who disbelieved — that they are companions of the Fire.

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ يَحْمِلُونَ الْعَرْشَ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهُ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ وَيُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا
full_text.translation: Those who carry the Throne and those around it exalt with praise of their Lord, believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who have believed.

full_text.arabic: رَبَّنَا وَسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَّحْمَةً وَعِلْمًا فَاغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تَابُوا
full_text.translation: Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented.

full_text.arabic: وَقِهِمُ السَّيِّئَاتِ ۚ وَمَن تَقِ السَّيِّئَاتِ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمْتَهُ
full_text.translation: And protect them from evil deeds. Whoever You protect from evil deeds on that Day — You have shown him mercy.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُنَادَوْنَ لَمَقْتُ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ مِن مَّقْتِكُمْ أَنفُسَكُمْ
full_text.translation: Those who disbelieved will be told: The hatred of Allah for you is greater than your hatred of yourselves.

full_text.arabic: قَالُوا رَبَّنَا أَمَتَّنَا اثْنَتَيْنِ وَأَحْيَيْتَنَا اثْنَتَيْنِ فَاعْتَرَفْنَا بِذُنُوبِنَا
full_text.translation: They say: Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and given us life twice, and we have confessed our sins.

full_text.arabic: ذَٰلِكُم بِأَنَّهُ إِذَا دُعِيَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ كَفَرْتُمْ ۖ وَإِن يُشْرَكْ بِهِ تُؤْمِنُوا
full_text.translation: That is because when Allah alone was called upon, you disbelieved; but when partners were associated with Him, you believed.

full_text.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ وَيُنَزِّلُ لَكُم مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ رِزْقًا
full_text.translation: He is the one who shows you His signs and sends down provision from the sky for you.

full_text.arabic: فَادْعُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكَافِرُونَ
full_text.translation: So call upon Allah, making the religion sincerely for Him, even if the disbelievers dislike it.

full_text.arabic: رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجَاتِ ذُو الْعَرْشِ يُلْقِي الرُّوحَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ
full_text.translation: Exalter of ranks, Owner of the Throne — He places the spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ هُم بَارِزُونَ ۖ لَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْهُمْ شَيْءٌ
full_text.translation: The Day they come forth — nothing of them will be concealed from Allah.

full_text.arabic: لِّمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ ۖ لِلَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ
full_text.translation: To whom belongs the sovereignty this Day? To Allah, the One, the Prevailing.

full_text.arabic: الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ ۚ لَا ظُلْمَ الْيَوْمَ
full_text.translation: This Day every soul will be recompensed for what it earned. No injustice today.

full_text.arabic: يَعْلَمُ خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ وَمَا تُخْفِي الصُّدُورُ
full_text.translation: He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal.

full_text.arabic: وَاللَّهُ يَقْضِي بِالْحَقِّ ۖ وَالَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِهِ لَا يَقْضُونَ بِشَيْءٍ
full_text.translation: Allah judges with truth, and those they call upon besides Him judge nothing at all.

full_text.arabic: أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ كَانُوا مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
full_text.translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen what was the end of those who were before them?

full_text.arabic: كَانُوا هُمْ أَشَدَّ مِنْهُمْ قُوَّةً وَآثَارًا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ
full_text.translation: They were greater in strength and in traces upon the land, but Allah seized them for their sins.

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا مُوسَىٰ بِآيَاتِنَا وَسُلْطَانٍ مُّبِينٍ
full_text.translation: And We sent Musa with Our signs and a clear authority.

full_text.arabic: إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَامَانَ وَقَارُونَ فَقَالُوا سَاحِرٌ كَذَّابٌ
full_text.translation: To Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun — but they said, 'A magician, a great liar.'

full_text.arabic: فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُم بِالْحَقِّ مِنْ عِندِنَا قَالُوا اقْتُلُوا أَبْنَاءَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ
full_text.translation: When he brought them the truth from Us, they said, 'Kill the sons of those who believe with him.'

full_text.arabic: وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ ذَرُونِي أَقْتُلْ مُوسَىٰ وَلْيَدْعُ رَبَّهُ
full_text.translation: Pharaoh said, 'Let me kill Musa, and let him call upon his Lord.'

full_text.arabic: وَقَالَ مُوسَىٰ إِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُم مِّن كُلِّ مُتَكَبِّرٍ
full_text.translation: Musa said, 'I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one.'

full_text.arabic: وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ مُّؤْمِنٌ مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَكْتُمُ إِيمَانَهُ أَتَقْتُلُونَ رَجُلًا أَن يَقُولَ رَبِّيَ اللَّهُ
full_text.translation: A believing man from Pharaoh's family who had concealed his faith said, 'Would you kill a man because he says, My Lord is Allah?'

full_text.arabic: يَا قَوْمِ لَكُمُ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ ظَاهِرِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ
full_text.translation: O my people, sovereignty is yours today, dominant in the land.

full_text.arabic: يَا قَوْمِ إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُم مِّثْلَ يَوْمِ الْأَحْزَابِ
full_text.translation: O my people, I fear for you something like the Day of the Confederates.

full_text.arabic: مِثْلَ دَأْبِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَعَادٍ وَثَمُودَ وَالَّذِينَ مِن بَعْدِهِمْ
full_text.translation: Like the custom of the people of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, and those after them.

full_text.arabic: وَيَا قَوْمِ إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَوْمَ التَّنَادِ
full_text.translation: O my people, I fear for you the Day of Calling Out.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ تُوَلُّونَ مُدْبِرِينَ مَا لَكُم مِّنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ عَاصِمٍ
full_text.translation: A day you will turn your backs fleeing, having no protector from Allah.

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ يُوسُفُ مِن قَبْلُ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ
full_text.translation: And Yusuf had come to you before with clear proofs.

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ سُلْطَانٍ أَتَاهُمْ ۖ كَبُرَ مَقْتًا عِندَ اللَّهِ
full_text.translation: Those who dispute about the signs of Allah without authority — great is hatred of them in the sight of Allah.

full_text.arabic: وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَا هَامَانُ ابْنِ لِي صَرْحًا لَّعَلِّي أَبْلُغُ الْأَسْبَابَ
full_text.translation: Pharaoh said, 'O Haman, build for me a tower that I might reach the pathways.'

full_text.arabic: أَسْبَابَ السَّمَاوَاتِ فَأَطَّلِعَ إِلَىٰ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّي لَأَظُنُّهُ كَاذِبًا
full_text.translation: The pathways into the heavens, and look at the God of Musa, for indeed I think he is a liar.

full_text.arabic: وَقَالَ الَّذِي آمَنَ يَا قَوْمِ اتَّبِعُونِ أَهْدِكُمْ سَبِيلَ الرَّشَادِ
full_text.translation: The one who believed said, 'O my people, follow me, I will guide you to the path of right conduct.'

full_text.arabic: يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّمَا هَٰذِهِ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا مَتَاعٌ
full_text.translation: O my people, this worldly life is only temporary enjoyment.

full_text.arabic: مَنْ عَمِلَ سَيِّئَةً فَلَا يُجْزَىٰ إِلَّا مِثْلَهَا ۖ وَمَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحًا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ
full_text.translation: Whoever does evil will not be recompensed except by the like thereof; and whoever does good, male or female, while being a believer...

full_text.arabic: وَيَا قَوْمِ مَا لِي أَدْعُوكُمْ إِلَى النَّجَاةِ وَتَدْعُونَنِي إِلَى النَّارِ
full_text.translation: O my people, how is it that I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?

full_text.arabic: تَدْعُونَنِي لِأَكْفُرَ بِاللَّهِ وَأُشْرِكَ بِهِ مَا لَيْسَ لِي بِهِ عِلْمٌ
full_text.translation: You call me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge.

full_text.arabic: لَا جَرَمَ أَنَّمَا تَدْعُونَنِي إِلَيْهِ لَيْسَ لَهُ دَعْوَةٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَلَا فِي الْآخِرَةِ
full_text.translation: Assuredly, that to which you call me has no call in this world or in the Hereafter.

full_text.arabic: فَسَتَذْكُرُونَ مَا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ ۚ وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمْرِي إِلَى اللَّهِ
full_text.translation: You will remember what I say to you. And I entrust my affair to Allah.

full_text.arabic: فَوَقَاهُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِ مَا مَكَرُوا ۖ وَحَاقَ بِآلِ فِرْعَوْنَ سُوءُ الْعَذَابِ
full_text.translation: So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted, and a terrible punishment enveloped Pharaoh's people.

full_text.arabic: النَّارُ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا غُدُوًّا وَعَشِيًّا
full_text.translation: The Fire — they are presented to it morning and evening.

full_text.arabic: وَإِذْ يَتَحَاجُّونَ فِي النَّارِ فَيَقُولُ الضُّعَفَاءُ لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا
full_text.translation: And when they argue in the Fire, and the weak say to those who were arrogant...

full_text.arabic: قَالَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَكْبَرُوا إِنَّا كُلٌّ فِيهَا إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ حَكَمَ بَيْنَ الْعِبَادِ
full_text.translation: Those who were arrogant say, 'Indeed, we are all in it. Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants.'

full_text.arabic: وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ فِي النَّارِ لِخَزَنَةِ جَهَنَّمَ ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ يُخَفِّفْ عَنَّا يَوْمًا مِّنَ الْعَذَابِ
full_text.translation: And those in the Fire say to the keepers of Hell, 'Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment.'

full_text.arabic: قَالُوا أَوَلَمْ تَكُ تَأْتِيكُمْ رُسُلُكُم بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ
full_text.translation: They say, 'Did your messengers not come to you with clear proofs?'

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا لَنَنصُرُ رُسُلَنَا وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَيَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْأَشْهَادُ
full_text.translation: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believed during the life of this world and on the Day the witnesses stand.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ الظَّالِمِينَ مَعْذِرَتُهُمْ ۖ وَلَهُمُ اللَّعْنَةُ وَلَهُمْ سُوءُ الدَّارِ
full_text.translation: The Day their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and the worst home.

full_text.arabic: وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْهُدَىٰ وَأَوْرَثْنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ الْكِتَابَ
full_text.translation: And We gave Musa guidance and caused the Children of Israel to inherit the Scripture.

full_text.arabic: هُدًى وَذِكْرَىٰ لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ
full_text.translation: A guidance and a reminder for those of understanding.

full_text.arabic: فَاصْبِرْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لِذَنبِكَ
full_text.translation: So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And seek forgiveness for your sin.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ سُلْطَانٍ أَتَاهُمْ ۙ إِن فِي صُدُورِهِمْ إِلَّا كِبْرٌ
full_text.translation: Those who dispute about the signs of Allah without authority — there is nothing in their chests except grandeur they will never attain.

full_text.arabic: لَخَلْقُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ خَلْقِ النَّاسِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: The creation of the heavens and earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَىٰ وَالْبَصِيرُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَلَا الْمُسِيءُ
full_text.translation: And not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor those who believe and do good and the evildoer.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ لَآتِيَةٌ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهَا وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming — no doubt about it — but most people do not believe.

full_text.arabic: وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ
full_text.translation: And your Lord said, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.'

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِتَسْكُنُوا فِيهِ وَالنَّهَارَ مُبْصِرًا
full_text.translation: Allah is the one who made for you the night for rest and the day for seeing.

full_text.arabic: ذَٰلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ لَّا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ
full_text.translation: That is Allah, your Lord, Creator of all things. There is no god but Him.

full_text.arabic: كَذَٰلِكَ يُؤْفَكُ الَّذِينَ كَانُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ
full_text.translation: Thus are deluded those who used to deny the signs of Allah.

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ قَرَارًا وَالسَّمَاءَ بِنَاءً وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ
full_text.translation: Allah made the earth a stable ground and the sky a structure and formed you and perfected your forms.

full_text.arabic: هُوَ الْحَيُّ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَادْعُوهُ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ
full_text.translation: He is the Living; there is no god but Him. So call upon Him, making the religion sincerely for Him.

full_text.arabic: قُلْ إِنِّي نُهِيتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ
full_text.translation: Say: Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you call upon besides Allah.

full_text.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ
full_text.translation: He is the one who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot.

full_text.arabic: هُوَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ ۖ فَإِذَا قَضَىٰ أَمْرًا فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُن فَيَكُونُ
full_text.translation: He is the one who gives life and causes death. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.

full_text.arabic: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِ اللَّهِ أَنَّىٰ يُصْرَفُونَ
full_text.translation: Have you not seen those who dispute about the signs of Allah — how are they turned away?

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِالْكِتَابِ وَبِمَا أَرْسَلْنَا بِهِ رُسُلَنَا ۖ فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers — they will know.

full_text.arabic: إِذِ الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ وَالسَّلَاسِلُ يُسْحَبُونَ
full_text.translation: When the shackles are around their necks and the chains — they will be dragged.

full_text.arabic: فِي الْحَمِيمِ ثُمَّ فِي النَّارِ يُسْجَرُونَ
full_text.translation: Through boiling water, then in the Fire they will be filled.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ قِيلَ لَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تُشْرِكُونَ
full_text.translation: Then it is said to them, 'Where is what you used to associate?'

full_text.arabic: مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ ۖ قَالُوا ضَلُّوا عَنَّا بَل لَّمْ نَكُن نَّدْعُو مِن قَبْلُ شَيْئًا
full_text.translation: Besides Allah?' They say, 'They have departed from us; rather, we did not used to invoke anything before.'

full_text.arabic: كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ الْكَافِرِينَ
full_text.translation: Thus does Allah lead astray the disbelievers.

full_text.arabic: ذَٰلِكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَفْرَحُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ وَبِمَا كُنتُمْ تَمْرَحُونَ
full_text.translation: That is because you used to rejoice on earth without right, and because you used to behave insolently.

full_text.arabic: ادْخُلُوا أَبْوَابَ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا ۖ فَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ
full_text.translation: Enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein. Wretched is the residence of the arrogant.

full_text.arabic: فَاصْبِرْ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ
full_text.translation: So be patient; indeed, the promise of Allah is truth.

full_text.arabic: فَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ الَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ فَإِلَيْنَا يُرْجَعُونَ
full_text.translation: Whether We show you some of what We promise them or take you in death, to Us they will be returned.

full_text.arabic: اللَّهُ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَنْعَامَ لِتَرْكَبُوا مِنْهَا وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ
full_text.translation: Allah is the one who made for you the livestock — some of them you ride and some of them you eat.

full_text.arabic: وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ وَلِتَبْلُغُوا عَلَيْهَا حَاجَةً فِي صُدُورِكُمْ
full_text.translation: And you have in them benefits, and upon them you reach a need within your breasts.

full_text.arabic: أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ
full_text.translation: Have they not traveled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them?

full_text.arabic: كَانُوا أَكْثَرَ مِنْهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ قُوَّةً وَآثَارًا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَمَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ
full_text.translation: They were more numerous and greater in strength and in traces upon the land, but what they earned did not avail them.

full_text.arabic: فَلَمَّا جَاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُم بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ فَرِحُوا بِمَا عِندَهُم مِّنَ الْعِلْمِ
full_text.translation: When their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what they had of knowledge.

full_text.arabic: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْا بَأْسَنَا قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ وَكَفَرْنَا بِمَا كُنَّا بِهِ مُشْرِكِينَ
full_text.translation: When they saw Our punishment, they said, 'We believe in Allah alone and disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him.'

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No staff thrown, no plagues unleashed, no sea split. The surah skips the entire narrative of confrontation. What interests Ghafir is the argument, the verbal encounter, the moment where one man's speech stands against an empire's consensus.
The rewards described are relational — being entered into gardens, being with righteous family members, being saved from evil deeds. The mercy in this surah is personal, intimate, familial.
He is 'a believing man from Pharaoh's family.' No name, no biography, no backstory. The anonymity makes him a template — not a historical character but a permanent possibility.
The surah says he concealed his faith and then spoke. It does not narrate the transition. The gap between concealment and speech is left for the reader to fill with their own experience.

absences.item: No softening of the temporal condition
absences.note: The surah opens with forgiveness and closes by showing faith at the moment of visible punishment arriving too late. The mercy is infinite. The window is not. The surah holds both truths simultaneously.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah strips the Musa narrative to its rhetorical core — every absence is structural
