why_this_surah: The surah of mutual loss and gain (al-taghābun) — the Day when some gain what others lose. Contains one of the Quran's most balanced statements about family: 'Among your spouses and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon and overlook and forgive, then indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful' (64:14).

name: Al-Ma'un
thesis: Seven ayahs split into a mirror: three on the one who denies religion (pushes the orphan, ignores the hungry), then three on the one who prays (heedless of their prayer, performing for show, withholding small kindnesses). The mirror forces a question: which side are you on?

heart_verse.why: The hinge of the entire surah. Four words that bind cruelty to hollow worship with the conjunction fa — therefore. The people who push away orphans and the people who pray are the same person.
heart_verse.arabic: فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ
heart_verse.translation: So destruction to those who pray.

full_text.arabic: أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ
full_text.translation: Have you seen the one who denies the religion?

full_text.arabic: فَذَٰلِكَ الَّذِي يَدُعُّ الْيَتِيمَ
full_text.translation: That is the one who pushes away the orphan,

full_text.arabic: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ
full_text.translation: and does not encourage the feeding of the poor.

full_text.arabic: فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ
full_text.translation: So destruction to those who pray —

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ
full_text.translation: those who are heedless of their prayer,

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ هُمْ يُرَاءُونَ
full_text.translation: those who make a show,

full_text.arabic: وَيَمْنَعُونَ الْمَاعُونَ
full_text.translation: and withhold small kindnesses.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: The surah contains no imperatives. It does not say 'feed the orphan' or 'pray sincerely.' It diagnoses a disease and walks away.
No descriptions of reward or punishment. Only waylun — destruction — aimed at the worshipper. The weight of the silence is the point.
No story, no historical narrative, no messenger named. Pure portrait — four strokes of a brush that leave no room for evasion.
The surah identifies the separation of worship from compassion and then offers neither remedy nor consolation. The diagnosis is the message.

absenceMap.subtitle: A surah of pure diagnosis — no prescription, no consolation

smallestWord.arc: The distance between these two poles is the surah's thesis: the denial of religion is not a grand philosophical position. It is the pot you did not lend. The meal you did not share. The kindness so trivial it barely registers as a choice.

poles.meaning: The religion — the entire system of faith, reckoning, and way of living
Small kindnesses — a cooking pot, a bucket, a handful of salt, a needle

smallestWord.title: The Smallest Word
smallestWord.subtitle: The surah opens with the largest frame and closes with the smallest object
smallestWord.keyInsight: The entire surah builds toward a word it has not yet said. When al-ma'un arrives — the very last word — it is the smallest word it could possibly be. The cosmic funnels into the domestic.

sectionJourney.title: Two Movements

sections.desc: The surah opens with a question — have you seen the one who denies the din? — then answers it by pointing at cruelty: the orphan pushed away, the poor ignored. Denial is defined not by creed but by conduct.
sections.title: The Anatomy of Denial

sections.desc: Fa-waylun lil-musallin. The conjunction fa makes the logic inescapable: because of the cruelty just described, therefore woe to those who pray. The word al-musallin, honorific everywhere else, arrives here as a verdict.
sections.title: The Hinge

sections.desc: Heedless of prayer (not in it, but away from it), performing worship for a human audience, and withholding ma'un — the smallest acts of human decency. The surah lands on a cooking pot.
sections.title: The Anatomy of Hollow Worship

sectionJourney.subtitle: Anatomy of denial, then anatomy of hollow worship — bound by fa

content_nodes.concept: The preposition 'an vs fi with prayer — a single letter that changes everything
Al-Ma'un and Al-Bayyina — sincerity present vs sincerity drained
The root r-'-y in yura'un — worship as performance for a human audience
Why Al-Ma'un has no commands, no cure, no consolation

why_this_surah: Do you know who really denies the Day of Judgment? The one who pushes away the orphan and doesn't encourage feeding the poor. This surah redefines disbelief — it's not just theology in your head, it's how you treat the most vulnerable people around you. It ends with people who pray but are heedless of their prayer. Faith without compassion is empty.

name: At-Tahrim
thesis: A surah that enters through the bedroom door and exits through the gates of eternity, carrying the same argument the entire way — that faith is the one thing in your life that is entirely, irreducibly yours. No relationship can give it to you. No relationship can take it away.

heart_verse.why: Asiyah's prayer — from inside the palace of the greatest tyrant the Quran describes. She does not ask for Paradise in general terms. She asks for 'indaka — near You. Proximity, not luxury. The earthly house with all its complications is answered by a request for a house that only faith can build.
heart_verse.arabic: رَبِّ ابْنِ لِي عِندَكَ بَيْتًا فِي الْجَنَّةِ
heart_verse.translation: My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكَ ۖ تَبْتَغِي مَرْضَاتَ أَزْوَاجِكَ ۚ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
full_text.translation: O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.

full_text.arabic: قَدْ فَرَضَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ أَيْمَانِكُمْ ۚ وَاللَّهُ مَوْلَاكُمْ ۖ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيمُ الْحَكِيمُ
full_text.translation: Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths. And Allah is your Protector, and He is the Knowing, the Wise.

full_text.arabic: وَإِذْ أَسَرَّ النَّبِيُّ إِلَىٰ بَعْضِ أَزْوَاجِهِ حَدِيثًا فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَتْ بِهِ وَأَظْهَرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهُ وَأَعْرَضَ عَن بَعْضٍ ۖ فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَهَا بِهِ قَالَتْ مَنْ أَنبَأَكَ هَٰذَا ۖ قَالَ نَبَّأَنِيَ الْعَلِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ
full_text.translation: And when the Prophet confided something to one of his wives, and she disclosed it, and Allah informed him of it, he acknowledged part of it and overlooked part. And when he informed her of it, she said, 'Who told you this?' He said, 'I was informed by the Knowing, the Aware.'

full_text.arabic: إِن تَتُوبَا إِلَى اللَّهِ فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا ۖ وَإِن تَظَاهَرَا عَلَيْهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ مَوْلَاهُ وَجِبْرِيلُ وَصَالِحُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ۖ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ
full_text.translation: If you two repent to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined. But if you cooperate against him — then indeed Allah is his Protector, and Jibril and the righteous among the believers, and the angels moreover are his assistants.

full_text.arabic: عَسَىٰ رَبُّهُ إِن طَلَّقَكُنَّ أَن يُبْدِلَهُ أَزْوَاجًا خَيْرًا مِّنكُنَّ مُسْلِمَاتٍ مُّؤْمِنَاتٍ قَانِتَاتٍ تَائِبَاتٍ عَابِدَاتٍ سَائِحَاتٍ ثَيِّبَاتٍ وَأَبْكَارًا
full_text.translation: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorced you, would substitute for him wives better than you — submitting, believing, devoutly obedient, repentant, worshipping, and fasting — previously married or virgins.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًا وَقُودُهَا النَّاسُ وَالْحِجَارَةُ عَلَيْهَا مَلَائِكَةٌ غِلَاظٌ شِدَادٌ لَّا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ مَا أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ
full_text.translation: O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَا تَعْتَذِرُوا الْيَوْمَ ۖ إِنَّمَا تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
full_text.translation: O you who have disbelieved, make no excuses today. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةً نَّصُوحًا عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمْ أَن يُكَفِّرَ عَنكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ يَوْمَ لَا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ ۖ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
full_text.translation: O you who believe, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and on their right; they will say, 'Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things capable.'

full_text.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ جَاهِدِ الْكُفَّارَ وَالْمُنَافِقِينَ وَاغْلُظْ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ وَمَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ ۖ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ
full_text.translation: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.

full_text.arabic: ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا امْرَأَتَ نُوحٍ وَامْرَأَتَ لُوطٍ ۖ كَانَتَا تَحْتَ عَبْدَيْنِ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا صَالِحَيْنِ فَخَانَتَاهُمَا فَلَمْ يُغْنِيَا عَنْهُمَا مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا وَقِيلَ ادْخُلَا النَّارَ مَعَ الدَّاخِلِينَ
full_text.translation: Allah presents as an example for those who disbelieved the wife of Nuh and the wife of Lut. They were under two of Our righteous servants, and they betrayed them. So they did not avail them from Allah at all, and it was said, 'Enter the Fire with those who enter.'

full_text.arabic: وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا امْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ إِذْ قَالَتْ رَبِّ ابْنِ لِي عِندَكَ بَيْتًا فِي الْجَنَّةِ وَنَجِّنِي مِن فِرْعَوْنَ وَعَمَلِهِ وَنَجِّنِي مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ
full_text.translation: And Allah presents as an example for those who believed the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, 'My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people.'

full_text.arabic: وَمَرْيَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرَانَ الَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِنَا وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِمَاتِ رَبِّهَا وَكُتُبِهِ وَكَانَتْ مِنَ الْقَانِتِينَ
full_text.translation: And Maryam, the daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We blew into it of Our spirit, and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures and was of the devoutly obedient.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: The surah begins with a legal matter (the Prophet's oath) but resolves it in a single verse and moves on. It has no interest in the jurisprudence of oaths — it uses the incident as a doorway.

absences.item: No descriptions of Paradise beyond nearness
absences.note: No rivers, no fruit, no physical reward. The one afterlife image that lingers is Asiyah's prayer for a house near God. What she asks for is proximity, not luxury.

absences.item: No engagement with polytheists or Meccans
absences.note: No external adversary. The adversary in At-Tahrim is more subtle: the assumption that your relationships define your spiritual standing.

absences.item: No named prophets in the domestic section
absences.note: The opening is about the Prophet and his wives, but the incident is never fully narrated. The specifics are withheld because the principle matters more than the occasion.

absences.item: No male exemplars in the closing
absences.note: All four archetypes are women. No other surah arranges four female figures as its theological conclusion. The arrangement is deliberate and unprecedented.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah's omissions reveal its design — intimacy without distraction

left.label: Wife of Nuh

right.desc: Married to history's greatest tyrant. Prayed for a house near God. Saved by her own faith from inside the palace of oppression.
right.label: Wife of Pharaoh

left.desc: Married to a prophet of moral isolation. Had daily access to revelation. Betrayed. The prophets could not avail them from Allah at all.
left.label: Wife of Lut

right.desc: Identified by her father, not a husband. Guarded her own chastity. Filled with divine spirit. Faith entirely self-contained.
right.label: Maryam

sectionJourney.title: Bedroom to Eternity

sections.desc: The Prophet's self-imposed prohibition, Allah's correction, the betrayed confidence, the escalating warning to two wives. The most intimate opening in the Quran — a question about something that happened behind closed doors.
sections.title: The Private Sphere

sections.desc: Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire. The single verse that turns from the Prophet's household to every household. If his family requires divine correction, what makes you think yours does not?
sections.title: The Pivot

sections.desc: Disbelievers told to make no excuses. Believers called to sincere repentance — tawbatan nasuha, a phrase unique in the Quran. The vision of light proceeding before the believers on that Day.
sections.title: Judgment & Striving

sections.desc: Two wives of prophets destroyed by their own choices. Asiyah, wife of Pharaoh, saved from inside tyranny. Maryam, belonging to no man's household, complete in her faith. The surah's thesis made visible in four lives.
sections.title: The Four Women

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: domestic incident, communal command, judgment, four archetypes

layers.desc: If you two repent to Allah — dual form, addressed to two specific wives. Repentance as private correction, born in a domestic incident.
layers.label: Private Tawbah

layers.desc: Repent to Allah with sincere repentance — plural, addressed to all believers. The only occurrence of tawbatan nasuha in the Quran. Pure, unmixed, free from self-justification.
layers.label: Communal Tawbah

layers.desc: Their light proceeds before them. Those who repent sincerely walk toward Paradise guided by their own light, praying for it to be perfected even as it shines.
layers.label: Walking in Light

why_this_surah: Opens with God addressing the Prophet ﷺ directly: 'Why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives?' A domestic incident in the Prophet's ﷺ household became revelation — the Quran showing that even the best marriage requires divine mediation. Contains Maryam and Fir'awn's wife as models of faith.

name: Al-Falaq
thesis: Five ayahs descend from the widest evil in creation to the most intimate evil in a human heart, and place one shelter over all of it — the Lord who splits every darkness open.

heart_verse.why: The single declaration that governs the entire surah. The name Rabb al-Falaq — Lord of the Daybreak — appears nowhere else in the Quran. The remedy is named before the disease: the One who splits every darkness open.
heart_verse.arabic: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ
heart_verse.translation: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak.

full_text.arabic: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ
full_text.translation: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak.

full_text.arabic: مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
full_text.translation: From the evil of what He created.

full_text.arabic: وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ
full_text.translation: And from the evil of the darkness when it settles.

full_text.arabic: وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّـٰثَـٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ
full_text.translation: And from the evil of those who blow on knots.

full_text.arabic: وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ
full_text.translation: And from the evil of the envier when he envies.

funnel.title: The Narrowing

sections.desc: Qul a'ūdhu bi-rabb il-falaq — the remedy arrives before the disease. The name Rabb al-Falaq appears nowhere else in the Quran: the Lord of the Daybreak, the one who splits darkness apart. The root f-l-q carries cleaving, breaking open, the first crack of dawn.
sections.title: The Shelter

sections.desc: The widest possible scope. Min sharri mā khalaq — from the evil of everything He created. Before any specific threat is named, the prayer covers all of it.
sections.title: All Created Evil

sections.desc: Ghāsiq idhā waqab — the deep dark when it presses in. A natural phenomenon, impersonal. The night at its thickest, when visibility disappears and the world feels unfamiliar.
sections.title: The Settling Dark

sections.desc: The threshold where evil shifts from nature to human agency. Al-naffāthāt fi'l-'uqad — deliberate, secret, directed harm. Someone is doing something to you, and the method is hidden.
sections.title: Those Who Blow on Knots

sections.desc: Ḥāsid idhā ḥasad — the envier at the moment envy becomes active. The most intimate evil: someone close enough to see your blessings and want them gone. The surah ends here, the prayer still open, still being spoken.
sections.title: The Envier

funnel.subtitle: One shelter named, then four evils — each closer than the last

absenceMap.title: What the Surah Leaves Out

absences.item: The word Allah does not appear
absences.note: Only Rabb — the intimate name, the one that carries a relationship of nurture and care. The surah reaches for closeness when naming the shelter.
The surah ends on the word ḥasad — envy. No return to the refuge, no summation, no āmīn. The prayer hangs open, still in progress.
The Quran's response to being envied is a prayer, a turning. No instruction on how to defeat envy or protect yourself through action — only where to turn when it is aimed at you.
No commands to pray, give charity, or be patient. Everything except the most elemental posture — vulnerability turned toward shelter — has been set aside.

absenceMap.subtitle: Al-Falaq strips prayer to its most elemental form

why_this_surah: You can't see every threat. Darkness falls, envy works in silence, and harm comes from places you didn't expect. This surah teaches you to seek refuge in God from the things you cannot protect yourself against — the evil in creation, the darkness when it settles, and the envy of those who envy. Five ayahs you say every morning and every night.

name: Al-Masad
thesis: Five ayahs where language does double work: tabbat yadā Abī Lahab — 'may the hands of the Father of Flame perish.' The name Abu Lahab, once a compliment about his radiant face, becomes a prophecy of the fire that awaits him. His wife carries firewood — fuel for a fire named after her husband.

heart_verse.why: The only place the Quran uses a man's own curse-word as the verb of his divine sentence. The root ta-ba-ba, the naming of the hands before the person, and the unprecedented act of naming a living opponent all converge in this single opening line.
heart_verse.arabic: تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ
heart_verse.translation: May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.

full_text.arabic: تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ
full_text.translation: May the hands of Abu Lahab be ruined, and ruined is he.

full_text.arabic: مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُ مَالُهُ وَمَا كَسَبَ
full_text.translation: His wealth will not avail him or that which he gained.

full_text.arabic: سَيَصْلَىٰ نَارًا ذَاتَ لَهَبٍ
full_text.translation: He will enter to burn in a Fire of blazing flame.

full_text.arabic: وَامْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ
full_text.translation: And his wife — the carrier of firewood.

full_text.arabic: فِي جِيدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِّن مَّسَدٍ
full_text.translation: Around her neck is a rope of twisted palm fiber.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: Every other Makki condemnation surah leaves a door open — a kalla that implies the possibility of stopping. Al-Masad has no such door. The verdict is complete.
No Rahman, no Rabb, no Ilah. The divine voice speaks entirely through the force of the declaration. The authority is present in the grammar without ever naming itself.
Other surahs use 'if... then...' — warning that implies choice. Here the sentence is already rendered in completed past tense. The case is closed.
Unlike Al-Humaza (104) or Al-Takathur (102) which describe archetypes, this surah names a real, living person — Abu Lahab — by his known epithet. Unique in the entire Quran.

absenceMap.subtitle: Every absence in Al-Masad reshapes how you read the surah

sectionJourney.title: Two Movements

sections.desc: Abu Lahab's hands are ruined. His wealth and earnings will not save him. He will enter a fire of blazing flame. The tense is past — tabbat — placing the ruin in completed time while the man is still alive.
sections.title: The Sentence

sections.desc: Naran dhata lahab — the only future-tense marker (sa-yasla) in the entire surah. Everything else is past or nominal. This single arrow points forward in a surah that otherwise reads like an inscription.
sections.title: The Fire

sections.desc: Umm Jamil is joined to his fate by a single conjunction — wa. She receives her own portrait, her own title, her own punishment. The neck that wore jewels now bears a rope of twisted palm fiber.

why_this_surah: The only surah that names and condemns a specific individual — Abu Lahab, the Prophet's own uncle, who dedicated his life to fighting Islam. His wealth did not save him. His wife carried thorns to throw in the Prophet's path. A surah that stands as permanent proof: family connection means nothing without faith, and opposition to truth has an end.

name: An-Nas
thesis: Three divine names summoned as fortress, then the threat identified — the whisperer who retreats. The Quran that opened with bismi'llāh closes with the human voice turning back toward God, asking for protection from something it cannot fight alone.

heart_verse.why: The pivot of the entire surah. Everything before it is invocation — three divine names summoned as fortress. Everything after it is identification — where the whisperer operates and where it comes from. This verse is the moment prayer becomes diagnosis.
heart_verse.arabic: مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ
heart_verse.translation: From the evil of the retreating whisperer.

full_text.arabic: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ
full_text.translation: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind.

full_text.arabic: مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ
full_text.translation: The King of mankind.

full_text.arabic: إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ
full_text.translation: The God of mankind.

full_text.arabic: مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ
full_text.translation: From the evil of the retreating whisperer,

full_text.arabic: ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ
full_text.translation: Who whispers in the chests of mankind,

full_text.arabic: مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ
full_text.translation: From among jinn and mankind.

absenceMap.title: What the Surah Leaves Out

absences.note: The surah offers no technique for defeating the whisperer — no method, no practice, no behavioral protocol. The medicine is the prayer itself, spoken aloud, breaking the silence in which the whisperer operates.
No paradise, no hellfire, no Day of Judgment. The threat is here, now, in this breath, inside your chest. The surah addresses the present moment.
No Ibrāhīm, no Mūsā, no Quranic episode. The surah assumes you already know the danger and have come to the only door.

absences.item: No description of what the whisperer says
absences.note: The content of the whisper is never specified. The surah identifies the mechanism — whisper, retreat, return — and leaves the content blank, because the content is different for everyone.

absenceMap.subtitle: The Quran's final word is a prayer stripped to its core

twoBreaths.title: Two Breaths

sections.desc: Three divine names in ascending order — Rabb (Lord, the nurturer), Malik (King, the sovereign), Ilāh (God, the one worthy of worship). Each name builds the fortress one wall higher. The grammar is pure calling — arming yourself with names before the threat is spoken.
sections.title: The Invocation

sections.desc: Min sharri'l-waswāsi'l-khannās — from the evil of the retreating whisperer. The temperature changes. The three names suddenly reveal their purpose. Prayer becomes diagnosis. Al-waswās: the one who whispers. Al-khannās: the one who retreats. Two qualities, one being.
sections.title: The Pivot

sections.desc: The enemy is located — fī ṣudūri'l-nās, in the chests of mankind. And its origin: min al-jinnati wa'l-nās, from both jinn and human beings. The God of the entire cosmos has been called upon to protect the innermost chamber of a single heart.
sections.title: The Identification

twoBreaths.subtitle: Three ayahs of invocation, then three ayahs naming the threat — the symmetry is exact
