why_this_surah: The last surah of the Quran — and it ends with a warning about the one enemy you carry with you everywhere: the whisper. It retreats when you remember God and returns when you forget. This surah teaches you to ask God for protection from the voice inside that pulls you away from what you know is right. The final lesson the Quran chose to leave you with.

name: Al-Qalam
thesis: A surah that swears by the instrument of truth, declares the character of the one who carries it, and then shows — through a ruined garden and a returned accusation — what happens to those who dismiss both.

heart_verse.why: The single most important divine testimony about the Prophet's person. The word khuluq is not conduct or behaviour but the deep interior formation of a person. The surah argues that the Prophet's character is itself the refutation of every accusation against him.
heart_verse.arabic: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ
heart_verse.translation: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.

full_text.arabic: نٓ ۚ وَالْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ
full_text.translation: Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.

full_text.arabic: مَا أَنتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ
full_text.translation: You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman.

full_text.arabic: وَإِنَّ لَكَ لَأَجْرًا غَيْرَ مَمْنُونٍ
full_text.translation: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted.

full_text.arabic: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ
full_text.translation: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.

full_text.arabic: فَسَتُبْصِرُ وَيُبْصِرُونَ
full_text.translation: So you will see and they will see —

full_text.arabic: بِأَيِّكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ
full_text.translation: which of you is the one afflicted.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the rightly guided.

full_text.arabic: فَلَا تُطِعِ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ
full_text.translation: So do not obey the deniers.

full_text.arabic: وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ
full_text.translation: They wish that you would soften, and they would soften.

full_text.arabic: وَلَا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ مَّهِينٍ
full_text.translation: And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer,

full_text.arabic: هَمَّازٍ مَّشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ
full_text.translation: scorner, going about with malicious gossip,

full_text.arabic: مَّنَّاعٍ لِّلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ
full_text.translation: a preventer of good, transgressing and sinful,

full_text.arabic: عُتُلٍّ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ زَنِيمٍ
full_text.translation: cruel — and on top of that, of doubtful birth.

full_text.arabic: أَن كَانَ ذَا مَالٍ وَبَنِينَ
full_text.translation: Because he is a possessor of wealth and children,

full_text.arabic: إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا قَالَ أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ
full_text.translation: when Our verses are recited to him, he says: Legends of the ancients.

full_text.arabic: سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ
full_text.translation: We will brand him on the snout.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا بَلَوْنَاهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَا أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, We have tried them  tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to harvest it in the morning —

full_text.arabic: وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ
full_text.translation: and they did not make exception.

full_text.arabic: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَائِفٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَائِمُونَ
full_text.translation: So there came upon it a visitor from your Lord while they slept.

full_text.arabic: فَأَصْبَحَتْ كَالصَّرِيمِ
full_text.translation: And it became as if cut down.

full_text.arabic: فَتَنَادَوْا مُصْبِحِينَ
full_text.translation: And they called one another at morning,

full_text.arabic: أَنِ اغْدُوا عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَارِمِينَ
full_text.translation: saying: Go early to your crop if you would cut the fruit.

full_text.arabic: فَانطَلَقُوا وَهُمْ يَتَخَافَتُونَ
full_text.translation: So they set out, whispering among themselves,

full_text.arabic: أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌ
full_text.translation: that no poor person should enter upon you today.

full_text.arabic: وَغَدَوْا عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍ قَادِرِينَ
full_text.translation: And they went early with determination, able.

full_text.arabic: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهَا قَالُوا إِنَّا لَضَالُّونَ
full_text.translation: But when they saw it, they said: Indeed, we are lost.

full_text.arabic: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ
full_text.translation: Rather, we are deprived.

full_text.arabic: قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ لَوْلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ
full_text.translation: The best among them said: Did I not say to you — why do you not glorify Allah?

full_text.arabic: قَالُوا سُبْحَانَ رَبِّنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ
full_text.translation: They said: Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.

full_text.arabic: فَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَلَاوَمُونَ
full_text.translation: Then they approached one another, blaming each other.

full_text.arabic: قَالُوا يَا وَيْلَنَا إِنَّا كُنَّا طَاغِينَ
full_text.translation: They said: O woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors.

full_text.arabic: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَا أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهَا إِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ
full_text.translation: Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us one better than it. Indeed, to our Lord we are turning.

full_text.arabic: كَذَٰلِكَ الْعَذَابُ ۖ وَلَعَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ ۚ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: Such is the punishment. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ
full_text.translation: Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are Gardens of Pleasure.

full_text.arabic: أَفَنَجْعَلُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كَالْمُجْرِمِينَ
full_text.translation: Shall We then treat the Muslims like the criminals?

full_text.arabic: مَا لَكُمْ كَيْفَ تَحْكُمُونَ
full_text.translation: What is wrong with you? How do you judge?

full_text.arabic: أَمْ لَكُمْ كِتَابٌ فِيهِ تَدْرُسُونَ
full_text.translation: Or do you have a scripture in which you study?

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ لَكُمْ فِيهِ لَمَا تَخَيَّرُونَ
full_text.translation: That indeed for you is whatever you choose?

full_text.arabic: أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمَانٌ عَلَيْنَا بَالِغَةٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ ۙ إِنَّ لَكُمْ لَمَا تَحْكُمُونَ
full_text.translation: Or do you have oaths binding upon Us, reaching until the Day of Resurrection, that indeed for you is whatever you judge?

full_text.arabic: سَلْهُمْ أَيُّهُم بِذَٰلِكَ زَعِيمٌ
full_text.translation: Ask them, which of them will guarantee that.

full_text.arabic: أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَاءُ فَلْيَأْتُوا بِشُرَكَائِهِمْ إِن كَانُوا صَادِقِينَ
full_text.translation: Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners, if they should be truthful.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَن سَاقٍ وَيُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ
full_text.translation: The Day the shin will be uncovered, and they are invited to prostration, but they will not be able.

full_text.arabic: خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ ۖ وَقَدْ كَانُوا يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى السُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَالِمُونَ
full_text.translation: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. And they used to be invited to prostration while they were sound.

full_text.arabic: فَذَرْنِي وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَٰذَا الْحَدِيثِ ۖ سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُم مِّنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
full_text.translation: So leave Me with whoever denies this discourse. We will progressively lead them from where they do not know.

full_text.arabic: وَأُمْلِي لَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ كَيْدِي مَتِينٌ
full_text.translation: And I will give them time. Indeed, My plan is firm.

full_text.arabic: أَمْ تَسْأَلُهُمْ أَجْرًا فَهُم مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ
full_text.translation: Or do you ask of them a payment, so they are burdened by debt?

full_text.arabic: أَمْ عِندَهُمُ الْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ
full_text.translation: Or have they knowledge of the unseen, so they write it down?

full_text.arabic: فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ الْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ
full_text.translation: So be patient for the decision of your Lord and do not be like the companion of the fish when he called out while he was distressed.

full_text.arabic: لَّوْلَا أَن تَدَارَكَهُ نِعْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَرَاءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ
full_text.translation: If not that a favour from his Lord overtook him, he would have been thrown onto the naked shore while he was censured.

full_text.arabic: فَاجْتَبَاهُ رَبُّهُ فَجَعَلَهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ
full_text.translation: But his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous.

full_text.arabic: وَإِن يَكَادُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصَارِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُوا الذِّكْرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُ لَمَجْنُونٌ
full_text.translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the message, and they say: Indeed, he is mad.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ
full_text.translation: And it is nothing but a reminder to the worlds.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No dietary laws, no prayer instructions, no social legislation. The surah does not instruct. It vindicates the Prophet, tells a parable, and dismantles the accusers' position. The entire argument is about character.

No 'Ad, no Thamud, no people of Lot. The usual Makkan catalogue of civilizational destruction is replaced by a story about rich people who didn't share their food. The scale shrinks to make the moral larger.

absences.item: No dramatic sin in the parable
absences.note: The garden owners did not commit violence or worship idols. They adjusted their schedule. They set their alarm earlier. They harvested before the poor arrived. The sin is the quiet engineering of exclusion.

The surah does not refute the accusation of madness at the end. It simply lets the accusers repeat it after fifty ayahs of evidence. The repetition indicts them. Their inability to say anything new is itself the proof.

absences.item: No resolution for the garden owners
absences.note: Their final words contain fragile hope — perhaps our Lord will substitute for us one better. The surah does not say whether this hope was fulfilled. It draws the lesson and moves on.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah operates entirely in the domain of character and consequence

left.desc: Divine oath by the pen, supreme character declared, the accusation of madness refuted
left.label: You Are Not Mad

right.desc: The Yunus warning, patience commanded, the accusation repeated — now exposed as empty
right.label: They Say: He Is Mad

left.desc: Nine qualities of degradation in earthly glory — wealthy, surrounded by sons, morally bankrupt
left.label: The Opponent's Portrait

right.desc: The same type on Judgment Day — eyes humbled, unable to prostrate, progressively led to ruin
right.label: The Day's Portrait

chiasticRing.title: The Frame

center.desc: The garden parable shows the earthly cost of selfishness. The theological section shows the eternal cost. Together: what character costs is the same whether the garden is earthly or heavenly.
center.note: The pivot falls at ayahs 26-27 — the moment the garden owners see the destruction and say: 'We are the deprived.' The people who planned to deprive others discover they have deprived themselves.
center.label: Character and Consequence

chiasticRing.subtitle: The divine declaration and the human accusation bookend the surah — the distance between them is the argument

sectionJourney.title: The Trial

sections.desc: The surah opens with an oath by the pen, declares the Prophet's supreme character, then pivots to paint a devastating portrait of his chief opponent — nine qualities of moral degradation catalogued in staccato rhythm, each landing like a gavel strike. Against the single quality of the Prophet (khuluq azim), the opponent requires nine descriptors.
sections.title: The Defence and the Counter-Portrait

sections.desc: Wealthy garden owners swear to harvest at dawn, deliberately timing their work so the poor will not come asking. They wake to find their garden destroyed overnight. They planned to deprive the poor. They became the deprived. The Arabic mahrum carries the weight of the entire surah's argument.
sections.title: The Parable of the Garden

sections.desc: A cascade of rhetorical questions, each removing one ground for the disbelievers' confidence. You have no book. You have no covenant. You have no guarantor. You have no partners. The earthly garden that was destroyed mirrors the heavenly garden that endures.
sections.title: The Theological Dismantling

sections.desc: The Day arrives — the shin laid bare, the call to prostrate they cannot answer. The Prophet is told to be patient, not to be like the companion of the whale. The accusation of madness returns from ayah 2, now exposed for what it always was. The surah closes on dhikr — remembrance, the deepest form of speech.
sections.title: The Return

sectionJourney.subtitle: Four movements: vindication → parable → dismantling → return

deductiveFunnel.title: From Speech to Silence

layers.desc: The opening is full of speech acts — divine oaths, declarations, commands. The pen is invoked. The Prophet's character is proclaimed. Every word carries cosmic weight.
layers.label: Oaths & Declarations

layers.desc: The opponent is defined by corrupt speech: swearing, slandering, gossiping, dismissing. The garden owners speak constantly: planning, whispering, conspiring to exclude the poor. Speech misused at every level.
layers.label: Slander & Conspiracy

layers.desc: A cascade of unanswerable questions. Each one strips away a false assurance. The questions tighten like a vise until nothing remains but the bare assumption that has already been demolished.
layers.label: Questions & Dismantling

layers.desc: The Prophet is told to be patient — to not speak in frustration. The accusers try to unsettle him with their eyes, not words. The surah ends on dhikr — remembrance directed toward God rather than against people. The pen opened the surah. Remembrance closes it.
layers.label: Patience & Remembrance

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The surah tracks a movement from human noise to divine remembrance

content_nodes.concept: Khuluq 'azim — character as proof of prophethood
The garden parable — engineering exclusion
Al-Mulk–Al-Qalam diptych: cosmos and character
Yunus and the whale — patience under siege

why_this_surah: Opens with an oath by the pen — 'Nūn. By the pen and what they inscribe.' The second revelation after Al-'Alaq, defending the Prophet ﷺ against charges of madness. Contains the parable of the garden owners who planned to harvest secretly and deny the poor — and woke to find their garden destroyed. The pen, the character, the consequence.

name: Al-Haqqah
thesis: A surah that grabs you with a single word repeated three times, marches you past five ruined civilizations and one shattered cosmos, forces you to see yourself holding a book in either your right or your left hand, and then — having shown you everything — turns to the very words you are hearing and says: these, too, are real.

heart_verse.why: The hinge between the cosmic and the personal. Before it, the surah deals in civilizations and landscapes. After it, the surah deals in individuals — one person's right hand, another's left hand. The universe was cleared away so that you could stand visible.
heart_verse.arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ
heart_verse.translation: On that Day you will be exposed — no secret of yours will remain hidden.

full_text.arabic: الْحَاقَّةُ
full_text.translation: The Inevitable Reality.

full_text.arabic: مَا الْحَاقَّةُ
full_text.translation: What is the Inevitable Reality?

full_text.arabic: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا الْحَاقَّةُ
full_text.translation: And what can make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?

full_text.arabic: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ وَعَادٌ بِالْقَارِعَةِ
full_text.translation: Thamud and Ad denied the Striking Calamity.

full_text.arabic: فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ
full_text.translation: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast.

full_text.arabic: وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ
full_text.translation: And as for Ad, they were destroyed by a screaming, violent wind,

full_text.arabic: سَخَّرَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ سَبْعَ لَيَالٍ وَثَمَانِيَةَ أَيَّامٍ حُسُومًا فَتَرَى الْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ
full_text.translation: which He imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days in succession — you would see the people fallen as if they were hollow trunks of palm trees.

full_text.arabic: فَهَلْ تَرَىٰ لَهُم مِّن بَاقِيَةٍ
full_text.translation: Do you see any remnant of them?

full_text.arabic: وَجَاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَن قَبْلَهُ وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَاتُ بِالْخَاطِئَةِ
full_text.translation: And there came Pharaoh, and those before him, and the overturned cities — with sin.

full_text.arabic: فَعَصَوْا رَسُولَ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَهُمْ أَخْذَةً رَّابِيَةً
full_text.translation: They disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a grip that kept tightening.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا لَمَّا طَغَا الْمَاءُ حَمَلْنَاكُمْ فِي الْجَارِيَةِ
full_text.translation: Indeed, when the floodwaters overflowed, We carried you in the sailing vessel,

full_text.arabic: لِنَجْعَلَهَا لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَةً وَتَعِيَهَا أُذُنٌ وَاعِيَةٌ
full_text.translation: so that We might make it a reminder for you, and so that a retaining ear might retain it.

full_text.arabic: فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ
full_text.translation: Then when the trumpet is blown with a single blast,

full_text.arabic: وَحُمِلَتِ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَاحِدَةً
full_text.translation: and the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single blow —

full_text.arabic: فَيَوْمَئِذٍ وَقَعَتِ الْوَاقِعَةُ
full_text.translation: then on that Day, the Occurrence will occur.

full_text.arabic: وَانشَقَّتِ السَّمَاءُ فَهِيَ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَاهِيَةٌ
full_text.translation: And the sky will split apart, for on that Day it will be frail.

full_text.arabic: وَالْمَلَكُ عَلَىٰ أَرْجَائِهَا ۚ وَيَحْمِلُ عَرْشَ رَبِّكَ فَوْقَهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ ثَمَانِيَةٌ
full_text.translation: And the angels will be at its edges, and eight will bear the Throne of your Lord above them on that Day.

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ
full_text.translation: On that Day you will be exposed — no secret of yours will remain hidden.

full_text.arabic: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَيَقُولُ هَاؤُمُ اقْرَءُوا كِتَابِيَهْ
full_text.translation: As for the one given their record in their right hand, they will say: 'Here, read my record!'

full_text.arabic: إِنِّي ظَنَنتُ أَنِّي مُلَاقٍ حِسَابِيَهْ
full_text.translation: 'I knew I would meet my account.'

full_text.arabic: فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ
full_text.translation: So they will be in a pleasant life,

full_text.arabic: فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ
full_text.translation: in a lofty garden,

full_text.arabic: قُطُوفُهَا دَانِيَةٌ
full_text.translation: its fruits hanging within reach.

full_text.arabic: كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا بِمَا أَسْلَفْتُمْ فِي الْأَيَّامِ الْخَالِيَةِ
full_text.translation: 'Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you put forward in the days gone by.'

full_text.arabic: وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِشِمَالِهِ فَيَقُولُ يَا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُوتَ كِتَابِيَهْ
full_text.translation: But as for the one given their record in their left hand, they will say: 'I wish I had never been given my record,'

full_text.arabic: وَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا حِسَابِيَهْ
full_text.translation: 'and had never known what my account was.'

full_text.arabic: يَا لَيْتَهَا كَانَتِ الْقَاضِيَةَ
full_text.translation: 'I wish it had been the end.'

full_text.arabic: مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّي مَالِيَهْ
full_text.translation: 'My wealth has not availed me.'

full_text.arabic: هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطَانِيَهْ
full_text.translation: 'My authority has perished from me.'

full_text.arabic: خُذُوهُ فَغُلُّوهُ
full_text.translation: 'Seize him and shackle him,'

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ الْجَحِيمَ صَلُّوهُ
full_text.translation: 'then drive him into Hellfire,'

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ فِي سِلْسِلَةٍ ذَرْعُهَا سَبْعُونَ ذِرَاعًا فَاسْلُكُوهُ
full_text.translation: 'then insert him into a chain whose length is seventy cubits.'

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهُ كَانَ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ
full_text.translation: Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Magnificent,

full_text.arabic: وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ الْمِسْكِينِ
full_text.translation: and he did not encourage the feeding of the poor.

full_text.arabic: فَلَيْسَ لَهُ الْيَوْمَ هَاهُنَا حَمِيمٌ
full_text.translation: So he has no devoted friend here today,

full_text.arabic: وَلَا طَعَامٌ إِلَّا مِنْ غِسْلِينٍ
full_text.translation: and no food except from the discharge of wounds,

full_text.arabic: لَّا يَأْكُلُهُ إِلَّا الْخَاطِئُونَ
full_text.translation: which none eat except the sinners.

full_text.arabic: فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ
full_text.translation: I swear by what you see

full_text.arabic: وَمَا لَا تُبْصِرُونَ
full_text.translation: and what you do not see —

full_text.arabic: إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ
full_text.translation: it is the word of a noble messenger.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَاعِرٍ ۚ قَلِيلًا مَّا تُؤْمِنُونَ
full_text.translation: It is not the word of a poet — how little you believe!

full_text.arabic: وَلَا بِقَوْلِ كَاهِنٍ ۚ قَلِيلًا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
full_text.translation: And not the word of a soothsayer — how little you reflect!

full_text.arabic: تَنزِيلٌ مِّن رَّبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
full_text.translation: A revelation from the Lord of all worlds.

full_text.arabic: وَلَوْ تَقَوَّلَ عَلَيْنَا بَعْضَ الْأَقَاوِيلِ
full_text.translation: And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings,

full_text.arabic: لَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُ بِالْيَمِينِ
full_text.translation: We would have seized him by the right hand,

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ لَقَطَعْنَا مِنْهُ الْوَتِينَ
full_text.translation: then cut from him the aorta,

full_text.arabic: فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَاجِزِينَ
full_text.translation: and none of you could have shielded him from it.

full_text.arabic: وَإِنَّهُ لَتَذْكِرَةٌ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
full_text.translation: And indeed, it is a reminder for the God-fearing.

full_text.arabic: وَإِنَّا لَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مِنكُم مُّكَذِّبِينَ
full_text.translation: And We know that among you are deniers.

full_text.arabic: وَإِنَّهُ لَحَسْرَةٌ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ
full_text.translation: And it will be a source of agonizing regret for the disbelievers.

full_text.arabic: وَإِنَّهُ لَحَقُّ الْيَقِينِ
full_text.translation: And indeed, it is the truth of certainty.

full_text.arabic: فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ
full_text.translation: So glorify the name of your Lord, the Magnificent.

absenceMap.title: What’s Missing

absences.note: No legislation. No ‘O you who believe’ followed by a directive. No prayer instructions, no fasting rules. The surah has one concern only: establishing what is real and what will happen because it is real.
No back-and-forth between God and a prophet, no conversation between the righteous and the damned. The surah speaks in one direction. It declares.

absences.item: No named prophets in their missions
absences.note: Prophets appear only as historical markers. Musa is not mentioned by name at all, Nuh barely so. The surah is not interested in the messenger’s journey — only in what happened to people who refused the message.
The surah does not invite, does not reason toward a conclusion. It stands in front of you and names what is coming, shows historical proof, then forces you to see what it will look like.

The closing section strips away every label — poet, soothsayer — that the Quraysh invented to dismiss the Quran. The surah is its own evidence, and it refuses to be filed under anything other than revelation.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah declares — every absence sharpens the declaration

left.desc: The Inevitable Reality named three times — a word beyond comprehension
left.label: Al-Haqqah

right.desc: The same root returns: the Quran is haqq al-yaqin, the truth of certainty — and the command to glorify Allah the Magnificent
right.label: Haqq al-Yaqin

left.desc: Five nations destroyed for rejecting their messengers — proof from the past
left.label: Historical Destructions

right.desc: If the Prophet himself were false, he would be destroyed — proof from the present
right.label: Hypothetical Destruction

left.desc: The cosmic scene: trumpet, earth pulverized, sky torn, full exposure
left.label: The Day Arrives

right.desc: Sworn by all reality, visible and invisible — a revelation from the Lord of all worlds
right.label: The Quran’s Authority

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Right hand: joy, a lofty garden, fruit within reach. Left hand: despair, a chain of seventy cubits, no friend and no food.
center.note: Everything before this builds toward the moment of personal reckoning. Everything after argues that the instrument delivering it is trustworthy.
center.label: The Two Fates

chiasticRing.subtitle: Al-Haqqah’s opening and closing mirror each other around the two fates at the center

sectionJourney.title: The Verdict

sections.desc: Three ayahs, one word. The surah names the Inevitable Reality, asks what it is, then asks a deeper question: what could possibly make you know? The formula wa ma adraka signals something beyond human comprehension. The surah opens at the edge of what language can carry.
sections.title: The Triple Invocation

sections.desc: Five destroyed peoples in rapid succession. Thamud by the overwhelming blast. Ad by a screaming wind for seven nights and eight days, their bodies like hollow palm trunks. Pharaoh, the overturned cities, and the floodwaters of Nuh. Each one proof that the Haqqah has come before in smaller forms.
sections.title: The Evidence from History

sections.desc: A single blast on the trumpet. Earth and mountains crushed in one blow. The sky splits and becomes frail. Angels at its edges, eight bearing the Throne. Then the pivot: on that Day you will be exposed. The universe is cleared away so every soul stands visible.
sections.title: The Cosmic Scene

sections.desc: The one given their record in the right hand: radiant, in a lofty garden, fruit within reach. The one given it in the left: three wishes descending into despair, wealth and power named and dismissed, seized and bound in a chain of seventy cubits. The reason: disbelief in Allah the Magnificent, and not encouraging the feeding of the poor.
sections.title: The Two Fates

sections.desc: The Quran places itself on trial. Sworn by all reality visible and invisible, it declares: this is the word of a noble messenger, not a poet, not a soothsayer. If the Prophet had fabricated even one saying, his aorta would be severed. The surah closes by returning haqq to its opening: this is haqq al-yaqin, the truth of certainty.
sections.title: The Quran’s Testimony

sectionJourney.subtitle: Five movements: invocation → history → cosmos → two fates → testimony

deductiveFunnel.title: The Autopsy of Despair

layers.desc: The first wish: I wish I had never been given my record. The evidence itself is unbearable.
layers.label: Reject the Record

layers.desc: The second wish: I wish I had never known what my account was. Consciousness of what was done becomes a torment of its own.
layers.label: Reject the Knowledge

layers.desc: The third wish: I wish death had been the end. The grammar of despair moves inward — from rejecting evidence, to rejecting consciousness, to rejecting existence itself.
layers.label: Reject Existence

layers.desc: Two things that defined this person’s life — wealth and power — named and dismissed in two lines. Halaka: the same word used for the destroyed nations. The personal destruction echoes the historical one.
layers.label: The Verdict
layers.arabic: مَا أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّي مَالِيَهْ ۜ هَلَكَ عَنِّي سُلْطَانِيَهْ

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The condemned person’s response peels back layer after layer

content_nodes.concept: Haqq al-yaqin — the truth of certainty shared with Al-Waqi’ah
Hollow palm trunks — the image shared with Al-Qamar
Yahuddu — not encouraging the feeding of the poor
The severed aorta — the Quran placing itself under existential scrutiny

why_this_surah: The surah of the inevitable reality (al-ḥāqqah) — a name for the Day of Judgment that means 'the thing that must happen.' Opens with three names for the Day, then shows what happened to those who denied it: 'Ad destroyed by a screaming wind for seven nights and eight days, Thamud by a single blast. Then the scene: the earth and mountains lifted and crushed in one blow.

name: Al-Qiyamah
thesis: A forty-ayah surah that places the Day of Resurrection and a single deathbed in the same frame, and shows you they are the same event at different scales.

heart_verse.why: The self-reproaching soul the surah swore by in its opening becomes the self-witnessing soul of the courtroom. No external accuser is needed. The conscience the surah elevated to the rank of an oath is the same conscience that delivers the verdict.
heart_verse.arabic: بَلِ الْإِنسَانُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ
heart_verse.translation: Man is a witness against himself.

full_text.arabic: لَا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ
full_text.translation: I swear by the Day of Resurrection,

full_text.arabic: وَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوَّامَةِ
full_text.translation: and I swear by the self-reproaching soul.

full_text.arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنسَانُ أَلَّن نَّجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُ
full_text.translation: Does man think We will not assemble his bones?

full_text.arabic: بَلَىٰ قَادِرِينَ عَلَىٰ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ
full_text.translation: Yes — We are able to proportion even his fingertips.

full_text.arabic: بَلْ يُرِيدُ الْإِنسَانُ لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ
full_text.translation: But man desires to continue in sin ahead of him.

full_text.arabic: يَسْأَلُ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ
full_text.translation: He asks, 'When is the Day of Resurrection?'

full_text.arabic: فَإِذَا بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ
full_text.translation: When the eye is dazzled,

full_text.arabic: وَخَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ
full_text.translation: and the moon is eclipsed,

full_text.arabic: وَجُمِعَ الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ
full_text.translation: and the sun and moon are joined together —

full_text.arabic: يَقُولُ الْإِنسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ
full_text.translation: man will say that Day, 'Where is the escape?'

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا لَا وَزَرَ
full_text.translation: No! There is no refuge.

full_text.arabic: إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمُسْتَقَرُّ
full_text.translation: To your Lord, that Day, is the settlement.

full_text.arabic: يُنَبَّأُ الْإِنسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ
full_text.translation: Man will be informed that Day of what he sent ahead and what he left behind.

full_text.arabic: بَلِ الْإِنسَانُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ
full_text.translation: Man is a witness against himself,

full_text.arabic: وَلَوْ أَلْقَىٰ مَعَاذِيرَهُ
full_text.translation: even though he throws out his excuses.

full_text.arabic: لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ
full_text.translation: Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ
full_text.translation: Its collection and recitation are upon Us.

full_text.arabic: فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَاهُ فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ
full_text.translation: So when We have recited it, follow its recitation.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا بَيَانَهُ
full_text.translation: Then upon Us is its clarification.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ
full_text.translation: No! But you love the immediate life

full_text.arabic: وَتَذَرُونَ الْآخِرَةَ
full_text.translation: and leave the Hereafter.

full_text.arabic: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ
full_text.translation: Faces that Day will be radiant,

full_text.arabic: إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ
full_text.translation: looking at their Lord.

full_text.arabic: وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَاسِرَةٌ
full_text.translation: And faces that Day will be contorted,

full_text.arabic: تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ
full_text.translation: expecting that something back-breaking is about to be done to them.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا إِذَا بَلَغَتِ التَّرَاقِيَ
full_text.translation: No! When it reaches the collarbones,

full_text.arabic: وَقِيلَ مَنْ ۜ رَاقٍ
full_text.translation: and it is said, 'Who will cure him?'

full_text.arabic: وَظَنَّ أَنَّهُ الْفِرَاقُ
full_text.translation: and he knows it is the parting,

full_text.arabic: وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ
full_text.translation: and the leg is wound around the leg —

full_text.arabic: إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَسَاقُ
full_text.translation: to your Lord, that Day, is the driving.

full_text.arabic: فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّىٰ
full_text.translation: He neither believed nor prayed.

full_text.arabic: وَلَـٰكِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
full_text.translation: But he denied and turned away.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّىٰ
full_text.translation: Then he went to his family, swaggering.

full_text.arabic: أَوْلَىٰ لَكَ فَأَوْلَىٰ
full_text.translation: Woe to you, and woe!

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ أَوْلَىٰ لَكَ فَأَوْلَىٰ
full_text.translation: Then woe to you, and woe!

full_text.arabic: أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنسَانُ أَن يُتْرَكَ سُدًى
full_text.translation: Does man think he will be left without purpose?

full_text.arabic: أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِّن مَّنِيٍّ يُمْنَىٰ
full_text.translation: Was he not a drop of fluid emitted?

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ كَانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ
full_text.translation: Then he became a clinging form, and God created and proportioned him.

full_text.arabic: فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنثَىٰ
full_text.translation: And made from him the two kinds — male and female.

full_text.arabic: أَلَيْسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰ أَن يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتَىٰ
full_text.translation: Is that One not able to give life to the dead?

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: God is referred to only through pronouns and through His creative acts. The surah does not even use the word Allah — forcing the encounter to become personal rather than doctrinal.
No destroyed nations. No Pharaoh, no ʿAd, no Thamud. The surah does not argue through precedent. It argues through the body.
Two faces — radiant and contorted — in two ayahs, and the surah moves on. It refuses the comfort of detailed eschatology.
No ethical instruction, no legal rulings. The surah is not prescribing behavior. It is confronting existence.
No kafiroon, no mushrikoon. The denier is simply al-insan — man, the human being. The category is universal.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah strips away every category and faces the human creature directly

left.desc: Does man think We cannot assemble his bones? Yes — even his fingertips.
left.label: Resurrection Challenge

right.desc: Was he not fluid, then clinging form? Is that One not able to give life to the dead?
right.label: Resurrection Proof

left.desc: Cosmic collapse. Man as self-witness. Excuses cannot cover self-knowledge.
left.label: Day of Judgment

right.desc: Personal death. The soul at the collarbones. The parting known. Legs going still.
right.label: The Deathbed

chiasticRing.title: The Ring

center.desc: Do not hasten your tongue. Its collection and recitation are upon Us.
center.note: The center of the ring is God's gathering of speech — the same root (j-m-ʿ) as gathering bones and gathering the cosmos. If this speech can be gathered, the body is a lesser feat.
center.label: The Gathering of the Word

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah's outer frame asks about resurrection; its center is about how God gathers His word

sectionJourney.title: The Oscillation

sections.desc: God swears by the Day of Resurrection itself and by the self-reproaching soul — the cosmic and the intimate, side by side. The Quraysh mocked the idea of reassembled bones; the surah points to the fingertip, where identity is most particular.
sections.title: The Double Oath

sections.desc: The mocker's question is answered with a scene, not a date. Eyes dazzled, moon eclipsed, sun and moon fused. Man cries 'Where is the escape?' and finds none. Then the courtroom: man is a witness against himself, no matter what excuses he throws.
sections.title: The Day Arrives

sections.desc: The surah stops its own argument to address the Prophet directly — do not hasten your tongue with it. The gathering of the Quran uses the same root (j-m-ʿ) as the gathering of bones and of the cosmos. The quiet center of a relentless surah.
sections.title: The Revelation Pause

sections.desc: The surah descends into a single room. The soul reaches the collarbones. Someone asks 'Who will cure him?' The dying person knows it is the parting. The legs wind around each other. Every detail comes from watching someone die — and the argument becomes somatic.
sections.title: The Deathbed

sections.desc: The denier is stripped bare: he neither believed nor prayed, he denied and swaggered home. Then the surah returns to creation — fluid, clinging form, male and female — and closes on a question that expects only one answer: Is He not able to give life to the dead?
sections.title: The Closed Door

sectionJourney.subtitle: Five movements: oath → Day → revelation → deathbed → confrontation

deductiveFunnel.title: The Gathering Root

layers.desc: Gathering the bones. The resurrection of the body — the smallest scale of divine assembly, and the one the mockers denied.
layers.label: Body

layers.desc: Gathering the sun and moon. Cosmic collapse — the same verb applied to celestial bodies. What God gathers, He gathers at every scale.
layers.label: Cosmos

layers.desc: Gathering the Quran. The preservation of revelation — God who gathers scattered speech into coherent Book can surely gather scattered bones into a body.
layers.label: Scripture

layers.desc: The surah transfers the burden. The truth is no longer something announced to you. It is something you are asked to speak.
layers.label: The Question
layers.arabic: أَلَيْسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰ أَن يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتَىٰ

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The root j-m-ʿ threads through three scales — body, cosmos, scripture

content_nodes.concept: The nafs al-lawwamah — conscience as oath-worthy
The deathbed sequence — soul at the collarbones
The gathering root (j-m-ʿ) across three scales
Fingertip and sawwa — creation as resurrection proof

why_this_surah: The surah of the Day of Resurrection (al-qiyāmah) — 'Does the human being think that We will not reassemble his bones? Yes, We are able to reconstruct even his fingertips' (75:3-4). The Quran's most specific claim about resurrection: God can reconstruct your unique fingerprints. The ayah that anticipated forensic science by thirteen centuries.

name: Al-Insan
thesis: A thirty-one-ayah surah that furnishes Paradise in silver and silk and ginger-flavored springs, then reveals that the key to the door was a single meal given to a hungry stranger with no expectation of thanks.

heart_verse.why: The ethical and theological center of the entire surah. The righteous disclaim every form of return — social, emotional, transactional — in the very act of giving. The eighteen ayahs of Paradise that follow are architecturally downstream of this single declaration of pure intention.
heart_verse.arabic: إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنكُمْ جَزَاءً وَلَا شُكُورًا
heart_verse.translation: We feed you only for the face of Allah. We desire from you neither reward nor thanks.

full_text.arabic: هَلْ أَتَىٰ عَلَى الْإِنسَانِ حِينٌ مِّنَ الدَّهْرِ لَمْ يَكُن شَيْئًا مَّذْكُورًا
full_text.translation: Has there not come upon man a period of time when he was nothing worth mentioning?

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا الْإِنسَانَ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ نَّبْتَلِيهِ فَجَعَلْنَاهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, We created man from a mixed drop to test him; and We made him hearing and seeing.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِرًا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, We guided him to the path — whether he be grateful or ungrateful.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ سَلَاسِلَ وَأَغْلَالًا وَسَعِيرًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles and a blazing fire.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ يَشْرَبُونَ مِن كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُورًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, the righteous will drink from a cup whose mixture is of camphor —

full_text.arabic: عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيرًا
full_text.translation: a spring from which the servants of Allah will drink, making it gush forth abundantly.

full_text.arabic: يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْمًا كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيرًا
full_text.translation: They fulfill their vows and fear a Day whose evil is widespread.

full_text.arabic: وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا
full_text.translation: And they give food, despite their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنكُمْ جَزَاءً وَلَا شُكُورًا
full_text.translation: We feed you only for the face of Allah. We desire from you neither reward nor thanks.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا نَخَافُ مِن رَّبِّنَا يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا قَمْطَرِيرًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressful.

full_text.arabic: فَوَقَاهُمُ اللَّهُ شَرَّ ذَٰلِكَ الْيَوْمِ وَلَقَّاهُمْ نَضْرَةً وَسُرُورًا
full_text.translation: So Allah protected them from the evil of that Day and granted them radiance and joy.

full_text.arabic: وَجَزَاهُم بِمَا صَبَرُوا جَنَّةً وَحَرِيرًا
full_text.translation: And He rewarded them for their patience with a garden and silk.

full_text.arabic: مُّتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ ۖ لَا يَرَوْنَ فِيهَا شَمْسًا وَلَا زَمْهَرِيرًا
full_text.translation: Reclining therein on adorned couches, they will see neither scorching sun nor bitter cold.

full_text.arabic: وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلَالُهَا وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُهَا تَذْلِيلًا
full_text.translation: And near above them are its shades, and its fruit clusters brought within easy reach.

full_text.arabic: وَيُطَافُ عَلَيْهِم بِآنِيَةٍ مِّن فِضَّةٍ وَأَكْوَابٍ كَانَتْ قَوَارِيرَا
full_text.translation: And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and cups of crystal —

full_text.arabic: قَوَارِيرَ مِن فِضَّةٍ قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا
full_text.translation: crystal from silver, which they have determined the measure thereof.

full_text.arabic: وَيُسْقَوْنَ فِيهَا كَأْسًا كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنجَبِيلًا
full_text.translation: And they will be given to drink a cup whose mixture is of ginger —

full_text.arabic: عَيْنًا فِيهَا تُسَمَّىٰ سَلْسَبِيلًا
full_text.translation: a spring therein named Salsabil.

full_text.arabic: وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُّخَلَّدُونَ إِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ حَسِبْتَهُمْ لُؤْلُؤًا مَّنثُورًا
full_text.translation: There will circulate among them young attendants made eternal — when you see them, you would think them scattered pearls.

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيمًا وَمُلْكًا كَبِيرًا
full_text.translation: And when you look there, you will see bliss and a great kingdom.

full_text.arabic: عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُندُسٍ خُضْرٌ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٌ ۖ وَحُلُّوا أَسَاوِرَ مِن فِضَّةٍ وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَرَابًا طَهُورًا
full_text.translation: Upon them will be garments of green silk and brocade. They will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a purifying drink.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ هَـٰذَا كَانَ لَكُمْ جَزَاءً وَكَانَ سَعْيُكُم مَّشْكُورًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, this is for you a reward, and your striving has been appreciated.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ تَنزِيلًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, it is We who have sent down to you the Quran progressively.

full_text.arabic: فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ آثِمًا أَوْ كَفُورًا
full_text.translation: So be patient for the ruling of your Lord, and do not obey among them any sinner or ungrateful one.

full_text.arabic: وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا
full_text.translation: And mention the name of your Lord morning and evening.

full_text.arabic: وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَاسْجُدْ لَهُ وَسَبِّحْهُ لَيْلًا طَوِيلًا
full_text.translation: And during the night prostrate to Him and exalt Him a long part of the night.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ هَـٰؤُلَاءِ يُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ وَيَذَرُونَ وَرَاءَهُمْ يَوْمًا ثَقِيلًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, these people love the immediate life and leave behind them a heavy Day.

full_text.arabic: نَّحْنُ خَلَقْنَاهُمْ وَشَدَدْنَا أَسْرَهُمْ ۖ وَإِذَا شِئْنَا بَدَّلْنَا أَمْثَالَهُمْ تَبْدِيلًا
full_text.translation: We created them and strengthened their forms. And when We will, We can replace them with others like them.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ هَـٰذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ ۖ فَمَن شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا
full_text.translation: Indeed, this is a reminder. So whoever wills may take to his Lord a path.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ إِلَّا أَن يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا
full_text.translation: And you do not will except that Allah wills. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.

full_text.arabic: يُدْخِلُ مَن يَشَاءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ ۚ وَالظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا
full_text.translation: He admits whom He wills into His mercy; but the wrongdoers — He has prepared for them a painful punishment.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No Pharaoh, no ʿAd, no Thamud. The surah does not warn through history. It draws through the promise of what generosity earns.
No narrative of any messenger. The surah speaks directly about the righteous as a type — unnamed, unlocated, defined only by their deeds and their intention.
Their arguments are never cited, never refuted. Punishment is dispatched in one ayah and left behind. The surah has chosen its audience: those who might be drawn, not those who must be warned.
One ayah of chains and fire (76:4), then silence. The surah devotes roughly five times as much space to reward as to punishment. The design choice is unmistakable.

absences.item: No mention of rahma as a word (until the last ayah)
absences.note: The word 'mercy' appears only in 76:31, at the very end. The entire surah performs mercy without naming it — until the closing frame reveals that everything described was an expression of it.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah draws through desire, not through fear — and its absences prove it

left.desc: You were absent from existence — no one spoke your name, no one knew you were coming
left.label: Nothing Worth Mentioning

right.desc: He admits whom He wills into mercy. Your existence was a grant; your return is under His will
right.label: Divine Sovereignty

left.desc: Shakir and kafur — the fork that governs everything that follows
left.label: Grateful or Ungrateful

right.desc: Mashkura — your striving is recognized. The thanks you refused from people, Allah gives Himself
right.label: Appreciated

chiasticRing.title: The Echo

center.desc: They give food despite their love for it. We feed you only for the face of Allah.
center.note: The ethical center: one act of feeding, performed with complete sincerity, generates eighteen ayahs of divine response. The quantity of the deed is not what earns Paradise — the quality of intention is.
center.label: The Pure Intention

chiasticRing.subtitle: Grateful/ungrateful at the opening mirrors mercy/punishment at the close

sectionJourney.title: The Gift Unwrapped

sections.desc: You were nothing worth mentioning. Then fluid, then hearing and sight, then the path — grateful or ungrateful. Two words set up everything: shakir and kafur.
sections.title: The Question of Origin

sections.desc: Punishment dispatched in a single ayah — chains, shackles, fire. Then the door opens to the righteous: a cup mixed with camphor, a spring that responds to their will. The surah has no interest in lingering with punishment.
sections.title: The Fork

sections.desc: They fulfill vows. They feed the poor, the orphan, the captive — despite loving the food. Their motive, spoken in the first person: 'We feed you only for the face of Allah.' This is the pivot on which the entire Paradise rests.
sections.title: The Deed That Earned It

sections.desc: Eighteen ayahs of unbroken reward. Radiance and joy. Silk and shade. Silver vessels, crystal cups. Camphor, ginger, Salsabil. Attendants like scattered pearls. And the final gift: a purifying drink from their Lord's own hand.
sections.title: The Garden Unfurled

sections.desc: Direct address to the Prophet — patience, worship, refusal to obey the sinful. Then the widest frame: creation, divine will, the reminder that choice operates within permission. Mercy and punishment, both under Allah's sovereign decision.
sections.title: The Return to Sovereignty

sectionJourney.subtitle: Five movements: nothingness → fork → deed → garden → sovereignty

deductiveFunnel.title: The Three Drinks

layers.desc: Cool, fragrant, soothing. The first taste of Paradise — described by its ingredient. A hapax legomenon: kafur appears only here in the entire Quran.
layers.label: Camphor

layers.desc: Warm, stimulating, invigorating. Described by its source — a spring named Salsabil. Another hapax legomenon: zanjabil appears only here. The surah alternates coolness and warmth.
layers.label: Ginger

layers.desc: Described not by ingredient or source, but by its giver — their Lord Himself. Tahur means both purifying and pure. After all physical luxury, the final gift cleanses whatever remains of earthly residue.
layers.label: The Purifying Drink

layers.desc: The face sought in 76:9 becomes, in 76:21, the Lord who personally serves the drink. The seeker of Allah's face finds Allah facing them.
layers.label: The Seeker Finds

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: A journey inward from a public spring to a cup from the hand of Allah

content_nodes.concept: Li-wajhillah — feeding for the face of Allah
The three drinks — camphor, ginger, purifying
Shakir-kafur to mashkura — the gratitude arc
Al-Qiyamah to Al-Insan — courtroom then garden

why_this_surah: The Prophet ﷺ recited it in the second raka'ah of Fajr every Friday, paired with As-Sajdah (32). 'Has there come upon the human being a period of time when he was nothing worth mentioning?' (76:1). The surah traces the human from non-existence through creation, testing, and ultimate destination — grateful or ungrateful.

name: Abasa
thesis: Forty-two ayahs in two halves: the correction (the blind man had more right to your attention than the powerful who feel self-sufficient), then the evidence for resurrection (look at your food, your rain, your crops — the One who grew all that can raise the dead). The surah links social blindness to spiritual blindness.

heart_verse.why: The most startling opening in scripture: God rebukes His own Messenger in revelation that will be recited until the end of time. The blind man could not see the frown. Allah saw it anyway. The correction came not in private counsel but in permanent text.
heart_verse.arabic: عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ ﴿١﴾ أَن جَاءَهُ الْأَعْمَىٰ
heart_verse.translation: He frowned and turned away — because the blind man came to him.

full_text.arabic: عَبَسَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
full_text.translation: He frowned and turned away —

full_text.arabic: أَن جَاءَهُ الْأَعْمَىٰ
full_text.translation: because the blind man came to him.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّهُ يَزَّكَّىٰ
full_text.translation: And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself,

full_text.arabic: أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ الذِّكْرَىٰ
full_text.translation: or be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him.

full_text.arabic: أَمَّا مَنِ اسْتَغْنَىٰ
full_text.translation: As for the one who considers himself self-sufficient —

full_text.arabic: فَأَنتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّىٰ
full_text.translation: to him you give your attention.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا عَلَيْكَ أَلَّا يَزَّكَّىٰ
full_text.translation: Though it is not upon you if he does not purify himself.

full_text.arabic: وَأَمَّا مَن جَاءَكَ يَسْعَىٰ
full_text.translation: But as for the one who came to you striving —

full_text.arabic: وَهُوَ يَخْشَىٰ
full_text.translation: while he fears Allah —

full_text.arabic: فَأَنتَ عَنْهُ تَلَهَّىٰ
full_text.translation: from him you are distracted.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ
full_text.translation: No indeed! This is a reminder —

full_text.arabic: فَمَن شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ
full_text.translation: so whoever wills may take heed.

full_text.arabic: فِي صُحُفٍ مُّكَرَّمَةٍ
full_text.translation: In honored pages,

full_text.arabic: مَّرْفُوعَةٍ مُّطَهَّرَةٍ
full_text.translation: exalted and purified,

full_text.arabic: بِأَيْدِي سَفَرَةٍ
full_text.translation: carried by the hands of scribes —

full_text.arabic: كِرَامٍ بَرَرَةٍ
full_text.translation: noble and dutiful.

full_text.arabic: قُتِلَ الْإِنسَانُ مَا أَكْفَرَهُ
full_text.translation: Destroyed is the human being — how ungrateful he is!

full_text.arabic: مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ
full_text.translation: From what thing did He create him?

full_text.arabic: مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ
full_text.translation: From a drop of fluid He created him and determined his path,

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ
full_text.translation: then made the way easy for him,

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُ فَأَقْبَرَهُ
full_text.translation: then caused him to die and had him buried,

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ إِذَا شَاءَ أَنشَرَهُ
full_text.translation: then when He wills, He will raise him.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا لَمَّا يَقْضِ مَا أَمَرَهُ
full_text.translation: No — he has not yet accomplished what He commanded him.

full_text.arabic: فَلْيَنظُرِ الْإِنسَانُ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِهِ
full_text.translation: Let the human being look at his food —

full_text.arabic: أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا
full_text.translation: how We poured water in abundance,

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا
full_text.translation: then split the earth in fragments,

full_text.arabic: فَأَنبَتْنَا فِيهَا حَبًّا
full_text.translation: and caused grain to grow within it,

full_text.arabic: وَعِنَبًا وَقَضْبًا
full_text.translation: and grapes and fresh vegetation,

full_text.arabic: وَزَيْتُونًا وَنَخْلًا
full_text.translation: and olive trees and date palms,

full_text.arabic: وَحَدَائِقَ غُلْبًا
full_text.translation: and dense gardens,

full_text.arabic: وَفَاكِهَةً وَأَبًّا
full_text.translation: and fruits and grasses —

full_text.arabic: مَّتَاعًا لَّكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ
full_text.translation: provision for you and your livestock.

full_text.arabic: فَإِذَا جَاءَتِ الصَّاخَّةُ
full_text.translation: When the Deafening Blast comes —

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ الْمَرْءُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ
full_text.translation: the Day a man will flee from his brother,

full_text.arabic: وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ
full_text.translation: and his mother and his father,

full_text.arabic: وَصَاحِبَتِهِ وَبَنِيهِ
full_text.translation: and his wife and his children —

full_text.arabic: لِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مِّنْهُمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ شَأْنٌ يُغْنِيهِ
full_text.translation: every one of them, that Day, will have enough concern to occupy him.

full_text.arabic: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ مُّسْفِرَةٌ
full_text.translation: Faces that Day will be bright,

full_text.arabic: ضَاحِكَةٌ مُّسْتَبْشِرَةٌ
full_text.translation: laughing, rejoicing.

full_text.arabic: وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ
full_text.translation: And faces that Day will have dust upon them,

full_text.arabic: تَرْهَقُهَا قَتَرَةٌ
full_text.translation: covered in darkness —

full_text.arabic: أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ
full_text.translation: those are the disbelievers, the wicked ones.

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: Most Makkan surahs argue against idolatry. Abasa spends no time on the disbelievers' worldview. The elite are mentioned only to be set aside — the surah is more interested in the blind man they would have ignored.

absences.item: No direct address to the mushrikun
absences.note: The real audience is the Prophet and, through him, every person who will carry the message. The correction is internal. It is about the hearts of the believers, not the arguments of the deniers.
The rebuke is real but exists within a relationship intimate enough to bear it. A stranger does not correct you this way. A parent does. The feeling is being lovingly but firmly redirected.

absences.item: No path to repentance for the elite
absences.note: The self-sufficient man is not offered guidance within the surah's frame. The surah is not interested in converting him — it is interested in redirecting the Prophet's attention away from him.
Neither the Prophet nor Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum nor the Qurayshi leader is named. The anonymity makes the pattern universal — a verdict on a tendency, not a person.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah's silences are as precise as its words — every absence is a theological statement

left.desc: A face contracts — abasa — expressing a judgment about who is worth the Prophet's time
left.label: The Frown

right.desc: Faces bright with laughter or covered in dust — the eternal version of the momentary frown
right.label: The Faces

left.desc: The blind man who came striving and fearing is turned away in favor of the self-sufficient
left.label: The Seeker Ignored

right.desc: Each person so consumed by their own reckoning that no one has capacity for anyone else — yughnihi echoes istaghna
right.label: The Flight

left.desc: Honored pages, purified scribes — what God has given spiritually
left.label: Revelation's Nobility

right.desc: Rain, grain, gardens, fruit — what God has given materially
right.label: Creation's Provision

chiasticRing.title: The Mirror

center.desc: Destroyed is the human being — how ungrateful he is! From a drop of fluid to a grave to resurrection, and he has still not fulfilled his purpose.
center.note: The gravitational core: the raw fact of human dependency that makes both social arrogance and spiritual indifference incoherent.
center.label: The Drop

chiasticRing.subtitle: The surah's opening and closing form a precise inversion — faces bookend the entire structure

sectionJourney.title: The Redirect

sections.desc: Allah narrates the Prophet's own action back to him in third person — a grammatical distancing that is the rebuke itself. The blind man who came striving in reverence is contrasted with the self-sufficient leader who felt no need. The ascending list of the blind man's spiritual qualities (purification, remembrance, awe) makes the inversion devastating.
sections.title: The Frown

sections.desc: Kalla pivots the surah from correction to declaration. The revelation itself is described as inherently noble — on honored pages, carried by purified angelic scribes. A message this dignified should not be withheld from anyone who seeks it. The dignity belongs to the message and to whoever desires it.
sections.title: The Noble Record

sections.desc: Without transition, the surah drops to the raw material of human existence. From a drop of fluid to a path to death to a grave to resurrection — the entire arc compressed into seven ayahs. The man who considers himself self-sufficient was a drop of fluid. He has not yet fulfilled his purpose.
sections.title: The Ingrate

sections.desc: Let the human being look at his food. Rain poured, earth split, grain grown, grapes, olives, date palms, dense gardens — a chain of provision the self-sufficient man did not author. Everything that sustains him is authored by the One he ignored.
sections.title: The Provision

sections.desc: The Deafening Blast — al-sakhkha, a word found only here in the Quran. A man flees from brother, mother, father, wife, children. Each bond closer than the last. Two kinds of faces: bright and laughing, or dust-covered and dark. The surah that opened with a face ends with faces.
sections.title: The Shattering

sectionJourney.subtitle: Five movements: correction → revelation → origin → provision → reckoning

deductiveFunnel.title: The Thread

layers.desc: Istaghna — the Qurayshi elite considers himself self-sufficient, above needing guidance. This is the disease named in the abstract in Al-Alaq (96:7) and shown in real time here.
layers.label: Social Arrogance

layers.desc: The self-sufficient man was a drop of fluid. Every stage of his journey — creation, path, death, burial, resurrection — is measured and decided by another.
layers.label: Illusory Independence

layers.desc: Look at your food. You did not send the rain. You did not split the earth. Your self-sufficiency is an illusion sustained by provision you did not author.
layers.label: Unearned Provision

layers.desc: Yughnihi — same root as istaghna. On that Day, each person is self-sufficient in the worst sense: so consumed by their own reckoning that they flee from everyone they love. The word that described worldly arrogance now describes eschatological isolation.
layers.label: Terrible Self-Sufficiency

deductiveFunnel.subtitle: The root gh-n-y (self-sufficiency) connects the opening rebuke to the final reckoning

The two kalla pivots (ayahs 11 and 23)
Abasa–Takwir diptych — moral blindness and cosmic unraveling
Istaghna in Al-Alaq and Abasa — the same diagnosis

why_this_surah: The surah where God corrects His own Prophet ﷺ. A blind man came seeking guidance while the Prophet was speaking with Quraysh leaders. The Prophet frowned and turned away. This surah opens: 'He frowned and turned away because the blind man came to him.' No other scripture corrects its own messenger this directly.

name: Al-Mutaffifin
thesis: Thirty-six ayahs built on a scale metaphor: those who cheat the scales, the sealed register of the wicked (Sijjīn), then the sealed register of the righteous ('Illiyyīn), then the reversal — the righteous laugh at the disbelievers as the disbelievers once laughed at them. The cosmic scales correct the commercial ones.

heart_verse.why: The surah's turning point. Everything before it describes the crime and its record. Everything after describes the alternative. The word rana — rust, a stain that accumulates layer upon layer — explains how a person moves from cheating a scale to being inscribed in Sijjin: one daily deposit at a time. Not a single dramatic sin, but the slow patina of small compromises.
heart_verse.arabic: كَلَّا ۖ بَلْ ۜ رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم مَّا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ
heart_verse.translation: No! Rather, their hearts have been covered over by what they used to earn.

full_text.arabic: وَيْلٌ لِّلْمُطَفِّفِينَ
full_text.translation: Ruin to the defrauders —

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ إِذَا اكْتَالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ
full_text.translation: those who, when they take a measure from people, take in full,

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَو وَّزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ
full_text.translation: but when they give by measure or weight to them, they give less.

full_text.arabic: أَلَا يَظُنُّ أُولَٰئِكَ أَنَّهُم مَّبْعُوثُونَ
full_text.translation: Do these people not think that they will be resurrected

full_text.arabic: لِيَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
full_text.translation: for a tremendous Day —

full_text.arabic: يَوْمَ يَقُومُ النَّاسُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
full_text.translation: a Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds?

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتَابَ الْفُجَّارِ لَفِي سِجِّينٍ
full_text.translation: No indeed! The record of the wicked is in Sijjin.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا سِجِّينٌ
full_text.translation: And what could make you know what Sijjin is?

full_text.arabic: كِتَابٌ مَّرْقُومٌ
full_text.translation: A written register.

full_text.arabic: وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
full_text.translation: Ruin that Day to the deniers —

full_text.arabic: الَّذِينَ يُكَذِّبُونَ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ
full_text.translation: those who deny the Day of Recompense.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا يُكَذِّبُ بِهِ إِلَّا كُلُّ مُعْتَدٍ أَثِيمٍ
full_text.translation: And none deny it except every sinful transgressor.

full_text.arabic: إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ آيَاتُنَا قَالَ أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ
full_text.translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'Tales of the ancients.'

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا ۖ بَلْ ۜ رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِم مَّا كَانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ
full_text.translation: No! Rather, their hearts have been covered over by what they used to earn.

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَن رَّبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَّمَحْجُوبُونَ
full_text.translation: No indeed! On that Day they will be veiled from their Lord.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ لَصَالُو الْجَحِيمِ
full_text.translation: Then they will enter the Hellfire.

full_text.arabic: ثُمَّ يُقَالُ هَٰذَا الَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ
full_text.translation: Then it will be said, 'This is what you used to deny.'

full_text.arabic: كَلَّا إِنَّ كِتَابَ الْأَبْرَارِ لَفِي عِلِّيِّينَ
full_text.translation: No indeed! The record of the righteous is in Illiyyun.

full_text.arabic: وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا عِلِّيُّونَ
full_text.translation: And what could make you know what Illiyyun is?

full_text.arabic: كِتَابٌ مَّرْقُومٌ
full_text.translation: A written register,

full_text.arabic: يَشْهَدُهُ الْمُقَرَّبُونَ
full_text.translation: witnessed by those brought near.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ لَفِي نَعِيمٍ
full_text.translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss,

full_text.arabic: عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنظُرُونَ
full_text.translation: on adorned couches, gazing.

full_text.arabic: تَعْرِفُ فِي وُجُوهِهِمْ نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ
full_text.translation: You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss.

full_text.arabic: يُسْقَوْنَ مِن رَّحِيقٍ مَّخْتُومٍ
full_text.translation: They are given to drink a sealed wine,

full_text.arabic: خِتَامُهُ مِسْكٌ ۚ وَفِي ذَٰلِكَ فَلْيَتَنَافَسِ الْمُتَنَافِسُونَ
full_text.translation: its seal is musk — so for this, let the competitors compete.

full_text.arabic: وَمِزَاجُهُ مِن تَسْنِيمٍ
full_text.translation: And its mixture is of Tasnim —

full_text.arabic: عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا الْمُقَرَّبُونَ
full_text.translation: a spring from which those nearest to Allah drink.

full_text.arabic: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا كَانُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يَضْحَكُونَ
full_text.translation: Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed.

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِهِمْ يَتَغَامَزُونَ
full_text.translation: And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another.

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا انقَلَبُوا إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِمُ انقَلَبُوا فَكِهِينَ
full_text.translation: And when they returned to their people, they returned jesting.

full_text.arabic: وَإِذَا رَأَوْهُمْ قَالُوا إِنَّ هَٰؤُلَاءِ لَضَالُّونَ
full_text.translation: And when they saw them, they said, 'These people are truly lost.'

full_text.arabic: وَمَا أُرْسِلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ حَافِظِينَ
full_text.translation: But they were not sent as guardians over them.

full_text.arabic: فَالْيَوْمَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنَ الْكُفَّارِ يَضْحَكُونَ
full_text.translation: So today, those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers,

full_text.arabic: عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنظُرُونَ
full_text.translation: on adorned couches, gazing.

full_text.arabic: هَلْ ثُوِّبَ الْكُفَّارُ مَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ
full_text.translation: Have the disbelievers been repaid for what they used to do?

absenceMap.title: What's Missing

absences.note: No prophetic stories, no destroyed nations, no historical examples. The surah's only example is the reader's own behavior — the daily transactions you already know.

No legislative instructions, no prohibitions, no direct address to the Prophet. The surah is not telling you what to do. It is showing you what is already true about the unseen architecture of accountability.

absences.item: No explanation of how Sijjin and Illiyyun work
absences.note: Both records are named but not described beyond 'a written register.' The surah trusts the names themselves — prison below, elevation above — to carry the meaning.

absences.item: No defense offered to the mockers
absences.note: Ayah 33 notes they were 'not sent as guardians' — they appointed themselves judges with no authority. The surah strips them of their one assumed power: the right to evaluate.

absences.item: No transition between market and cosmos
absences.note: The surah moves from a trader's fraud to the Lord of the worlds in six ayahs with no bridge. The absence of explanation is the argument: the connection is self-evident to anyone who believes in accountability.

absenceMap.subtitle: The surah speaks entirely through contrast — every absence forces a mirror

left.label: The Rigged Scale

right.desc: Have they been repaid? The universe does not defraud — thuwwiba returns the exact measure
right.label: The Balanced Scale

left.desc: The record of the wicked: confined, named, inscribed — kitabun marqum
left.label: Sijjin — The Prison Record

right.desc: The record of the righteous: elevated, witnessed by those brought near — same phrase, opposite destination
right.label: Illiyyun — The Exalted Record

left.desc: The disbelievers laughed at the believers, winked, returned home jesting — habitual cruelty
left.label: Mockers Laugh

right.desc: Today the believers laugh at the disbelievers — same verb, subject and object swapped
right.label: Believers Laugh
